import TCSlib.Complexity.Randomized.PolyExpr

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Probabilistic polynomial-time machines, uniform and non-uniform

The randomized machine model of [PS10, §2.1]: the probabilistic polynomial-time Turing
machine (PPT) [PS10, Definition 23.4] with the worst-case running-time convention
[PS10, Definition 23.5], the notion "computes `f` with probability one"
[PS10, Definition 24.6], and the non-uniform PPT of [PS10, Definition 26.8] in its advice
formulation ("a uniform p.p.t. machine `A` that receives an advice string for each input
length"). One structure, `Complexity.NUPPT`, carries all of them (foundation decisions D3
and D4 of `PassShelatChapter2-4Plan.md`):

* a finite binary machine `M : Turing.FinTM Bool` that halts on **every** input `z` within
  `Ct * (|z| + 1) ^ ct` steps;
* an explicit coin polynomial `coins : PolyExpr` (`coins.eval n` uniform coins at parameter
  `n`) and an advice polynomial `adv : PolyExpr` with an advice function `advice : ℕ → List Bool`
  of length `≤ adv.eval n`;
* the single semantic primitive `output z` (the output tape when the budget expires), which is
  `PolyTimeComputable` (`NUPPT.polyTimeComputable_output`), and conversely every
  `PolyTimeComputable` function is the output of some `NUPPT` (`NUPPT.ofPolyTime`).

The activation at security parameter `n` on argument `y` with coins `r` is
`runAt n y r := output ⟨⟨⟨1^n, y⟩, advice n⟩, r⟩` with `r : Fin (coins.eval n) → Bool`
(pairs are `Turing.pairEncode`, `1^n = List.replicate n true`). The random tape is part of the
input, so the time bound holds for every coin string, which is exactly the worst-case
convention of [PS10, Definition 23.5]; "`A` computes `f` with probability 1"
[PS10, Definition 24.6] is `NUPPT.Computes`: equality for every coin string (on the finite
uniform coin space, probability one is the same as every coin string, see
`TCSlib.Cryptography.Asymptotic.Adversary`). A PPT [PS10, Definition 23.4] is an `NUPPT` with
empty advice (`NUPPT.Uniform`); `Complexity.PPT` is the subtype. `Computes` does not require
`Uniform`: [PS10, Definition 24.6] is about a randomized algorithm, i.e. a PPT, and is the case
`A.Uniform ∧ A.Computes f`; for a non-uniform `A`, `Computes` is the advice analogue and holds
for uncomputable `f` (advice `[h n]` for an arbitrary `h : ℕ → Bool`, read back by the machine).
So `∃ A : NUPPT, A.Computes f` does not say that a PPT computes `f`. Efficient computation of
`f` on the encodings `⟨1^n, y⟩` is `∃ A, A.Uniform ∧ A.Computes f`
(`NUPPT.exists_uniform_computes`, and conversely `NUPPT.Computes.polyTimeComputable` of
`TCSlib.Complexity.Randomized.Closure`, which gives polynomial-time computability of
`z ↦ f ⟨1^{|fst z|}, snd z⟩`). `Computes` says nothing about `f` off those encodings, so it is
not [PS10, Definition 24.6] for an arbitrary `f : {0,1}* → {0,1}*`, which constrains every
input string (gate 03a, round 2, R2-1). The
input-length-indexed activation `A_{|y|}(y)` of [PS10, Definition 26.8] is `NUPPT.runLit`; the
lemmas about it and about uniformity are in `TCSlib.Complexity.Randomized.NonUniform`.

## Deviations (DESIGN.md §5, items 1–2)

1. `NUPPT`: totality on all inputs (behaviour class unchanged via clocking); time in the
   machine-input length; advice and coins indexed by the parameter `n` read from `1^n`.
2. `NUPPT`: Def 26.8's machine-sequence formulation not formalized in the core (optional
   module).

In detail (D3): a machine that is polynomial-time on well-formed inputs can be clocked by
`Turing.timed_universal` into one that halts on every input, so requiring totality does not
change the class of behaviours (the optional lemma `NUPPT.ofPartial` doing this is not needed
by any theorem of chapters 2–4); the time bound is measured in the length of the machine
input `⟨⟨⟨1^n, y⟩, advice n⟩, r⟩`, a polynomial in `n + |y|`, so the classes "polynomial in
`n`" (for `|y|` polynomial in `n`, the only case the experiments produce) and "polynomial in
the machine input" coincide.

**Interdefinability of the `1^n`-indexed and the input-length-indexed forms (D3/D4).** The
text indexes advice and coins by the input length (`A_{|x|}(x)`), while `NUPPT` indexes
them by the parameter `n` read from the unary prefix `1^n`. The two are interdefinable in
every experiment of the text: (i) an `NUPPT` run at `n := |y|` is exactly the text's
`A_{|y|}(y)`, by definition (`NUPPT.runLit`; the prefix `1^{|y|}` carries no information);
(ii) conversely, every experiment of the text hands the adversary strings
whose length is a fixed polynomial `ℓ(n)` of the parameter, and an input-length-indexed
machine at length `ℓ(n)` becomes a `1^n`-indexed one by hard-wiring its advice at `ℓ(n)` and
evaluating its coin polynomial at `ℓ(n)` (`exists_reparam_advice` with `φ := ℓ.eval`); for
injective `ℓ` the converse hard-wires `1^n` into the advice at length `ℓ(n)`. The `1^n`
indexing is what makes one random tape per `n` well-typed for the oracle and interactive
layouts of chapters 3–4, where the machine is activated several times at one parameter on
inputs of varying length. Both forms are kept side by side where the text uses the literal
one (Definitions 26.1 and 69.4) and are related by explicit lemmas, never unified silently.

## Main definitions

* `Complexity.NUPPT` — non-uniform PPT [PS10, Definition 26.8, advice formulation]; a PPT
  [PS10, Definition 23.4] is the case `NUPPT.Uniform` (empty advice).
* `Complexity.NUPPT.output` — the output of the machine on a raw input (the semantic
  primitive); `NUPPT.timeBound`, `NUPPT.coinLen`, `NUPPT.adviceLen`.
* `Complexity.NUPPT.advInput` — the adversary input `⟨1^n, y⟩`; `NUPPT.Coins` — the coin type
  at parameter `n`; `NUPPT.runAt`, `NUPPT.runAtL`, `NUPPT.runLit` — activations.
* `Complexity.NUPPT.Uniform` — no advice (a PPT); `Complexity.PPT` — the subtype.
* `Complexity.NUPPT.Computes` — computes `f` with probability one: [PS10, Definition 24.6] for a
  uniform `A` (`NUPPT.Uniform`), the advice analogue otherwise.
* `Complexity.NUPPT.ofPolyTime`, `Complexity.NUPPT.ofPolyTimeUniform` — the `NUPPT` with a
  given polynomial-time output function, with and without advice.

## Main results

* `Complexity.NUPPT.output_spec`, `NUPPT.computesFunInTime`,
  `NUPPT.polyTimeComputable_output` — the output function is computed by the machine within
  its budget, hence is polynomial-time computable.
* `Complexity.NUPPT.output_eq_of_computesInTime` — determinism: any completed computation of
  the machine names `output`.
* `Complexity.NUPPT.output_ofPolyTime`, `NUPPT.ofPolyTimeUniform_uniform` — the converse
  direction: `ofPolyTime hf` outputs `f`, and `ofPolyTimeUniform` is uniform.
* `Complexity.NUPPT.exists_uniform_computes` — every polynomial-time computable function is
  computed with probability one by a PPT [PS10, Definition 24.6, non-vacuity].
* `Complexity.NUPPT.nonempty` — the class is inhabited.

## References

* [PS10] R. Pass, a. shelat, *A Course in Cryptography*, lecture notes, 3rd ed., January 2010.
  (§2.1: Definitions 23.4, 23.5, 24.6 and 26.8.)
* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (Definition 1.3, time-bounded computation; §6.3, advice.)
-/

namespace Complexity

open Turing

/-- A non-uniform probabilistic polynomial-time machine [PS10, Definition 26.8, advice
formulation]: a finite binary machine halting on **every** input `z` within
`Ct (|z|+1)^ct` steps, the explicit polynomial `coins` giving the number of uniform coins at
parameter `n`, and an advice string of length at most `adv.eval n` per parameter.
A PPT [PS10, Definition 23.4] is the case of empty advice (`Uniform`); the time bound holds
for every coin string, the worst-case convention of [PS10, Definition 23.5].

**Deviation:** `NUPPT`: totality on all inputs (behaviour class unchanged via clocking); time
in the machine-input length; advice and coins indexed by the parameter `n` read from `1^n`.
**Deviation:** `NUPPT`: Def 26.8's machine-sequence formulation not formalized in the core
(optional module). -/
structure NUPPT where
  /-- The underlying deterministic finite machine; coins and advice are input components. -/
  M : FinTM Bool
  /-- Coefficient of the running-time bound `Ct * (|z| + 1) ^ ct`. -/
  Ct : ℕ
  /-- Degree of the running-time bound. -/
  ct : ℕ
  /-- The coin polynomial: `coins.eval n` uniform coins at parameter `n`. -/
  coins : PolyExpr
  /-- The advice polynomial: `|advice n| ≤ adv.eval n`. -/
  adv : PolyExpr
  /-- The advice string per parameter (empty for a uniform machine). -/
  advice : ℕ → List Bool
  /-- The advice is polynomially bounded. -/
  advice_length : ∀ n, (advice n).length ≤ adv.eval n
  /-- The machine halts on every input within its polynomial budget. -/
  halts : ∀ z : List Bool, ∃ out : List Bool, M.ComputesInTime z out (Ct * (z.length + 1) ^ ct)

namespace NUPPT

variable (A : NUPPT)

/-- The running-time budget of `A` on inputs of length `m`: `Ct * (m + 1) ^ ct`. -/
def timeBound (m : ℕ) : ℕ := A.Ct * (m + 1) ^ A.ct

/-- The number of coins of `A` at parameter `n`. -/
def coinLen (n : ℕ) : ℕ := A.coins.eval n

/-- The defining equation of `coinLen`: `A.coinLen n = A.coins.eval n`. -/
theorem coinLen_eq (n : ℕ) : A.coinLen n = A.coins.eval n := rfl

/-- The advice-length bound of `A` at parameter `n`. -/
def adviceLen (n : ℕ) : ℕ := A.adv.eval n

/-- The output of `A` on the raw machine input `z`: the output tape when the budget expires
(the machine has halted by then, `output_spec`). This is the single semantic primitive; all
activations are instances of it. -/
def output (z : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  (A.M.tm.runFrom (A.M.tm.initCfg z) (A.timeBound z.length)).output

/-- The machine halts on `z` within its budget with `output z` on the output tape. -/
theorem output_spec (z : List Bool) : A.M.ComputesInTime z (A.output z) (A.timeBound z.length) := by
  obtain ⟨out, h⟩ := A.halts z
  obtain ⟨hs, -⟩ := (FinTM.computesInTime_iff _ _ _ _).mp h
  exact (FinTM.computesInTime_iff _ _ _ _).mpr ⟨hs, rfl⟩

/-- The machine computes the function `output` within the budget `timeBound`. -/
theorem computesFunInTime : A.M.ComputesFunInTime A.output A.timeBound :=
  fun z => A.output_spec z

/-- The output function of an `NUPPT` is polynomial-time computable: the black box through
which every reduction of the campaign is exhibited as a machine (D2). -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_output : PolyTimeComputable A.output :=
  ⟨A.M, A.Ct, A.ct, A.computesFunInTime⟩

/-- Determinism: any completed computation of the machine on `z` produces `output z`
(`Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime.output_unique`). -/
theorem output_eq_of_computesInTime {z w : List Bool} {t : ℕ} (h : A.M.ComputesInTime z w t) :
    A.output z = w :=
  (A.output_spec z).output_unique h

/-- The output is no longer than the budget (a machine emits at most one symbol per step,
`Turing.MultiTapeTM.output_length_le`). -/
theorem output_length_le (z : List Bool) : (A.output z).length ≤ A.timeBound z.length :=
  A.M.tm.output_length_le z (A.timeBound z.length)

/-- The adversary input `⟨1^n, y⟩`: the unary security parameter paired with the argument,
exactly as the text writes `A(1^n, y)` [PS10, Definition 27.3]. -/
def advInput (n : ℕ) (y : List Bool) : List Bool := pairEncode (List.replicate n true) y

/-- The defining equation of `advInput`: `advInput n y = pairEncode (List.replicate n true) y`
(the pair `⟨1^n, y⟩`). -/
theorem advInput_eq (n : ℕ) (y : List Bool) :
    advInput n y = pairEncode (List.replicate n true) y := rfl

/-- The length of the adversary input `⟨1^n, y⟩` is `2n + 2 + |y|`. -/
theorem length_advInput (n : ℕ) (y : List Bool) : (advInput n y).length = 2 * n + 2 + y.length := by
  simp [advInput, length_pairEncode]

/-- The coin type of `A` at parameter `n`: `coins.eval n` uniform bits
[PS10, Definition 23.4, "each bit of the random tape is uniformly and independently chosen"]. -/
abbrev Coins (n : ℕ) : Type := Fin (A.coinLen n) → Bool

/-- Activation at parameter `n` on argument `y` with coins `r`: machine input
`⟨⟨⟨1^n, y⟩, advice n⟩, r⟩`. The sampler `r ↦ runAt n y r` on the uniform coin type
`Coins n` is the distribution `A(1^n, y)` of the text. -/
def runAt (n : ℕ) (y : List Bool) (r : A.Coins n) : List Bool :=
  A.output (pairEncode (pairEncode (advInput n y) (A.advice n)) (List.ofFn r))

/-- Activation with an untyped coin string (the interactive and oracle layouts of
chapters 3–4 hand the machine a coin string of the right length as a list). -/
def runAtL (n : ℕ) (y r : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  A.output (pairEncode (pairEncode (advInput n y) (A.advice n)) r)

/-- The defining equation of `runAtL`:
`A.runAtL n y r = A.output (pairEncode (pairEncode (advInput n y) (A.advice n)) r)`. -/
theorem runAtL_eq (n : ℕ) (y r : List Bool) :
    A.runAtL n y r = A.output (pairEncode (pairEncode (advInput n y) (A.advice n)) r) := rfl

/-- The typed activation is the untyped one on `List.ofFn r`. -/
theorem runAt_eq (n : ℕ) (y : List Bool) (r : A.Coins n) :
    A.runAt n y r = A.runAtL n y (List.ofFn r) := rfl

/-- **The coins of two machines with the same coin polynomial**: `A.Coins n ≃ B.Coins n` when
`A.coins = B.coins` (`finCongr` on the coin lengths). A construction that keeps the coins of the
machine it is built from publishes its coin identification through it, so that consumers move
between the two coin types without reducing `coinLen` or the construction. -/
def coinsCongr {A B : NUPPT} (h : A.coins = B.coins) (n : ℕ) : A.Coins n ≃ B.Coins n :=
  Equiv.arrowCongr (finCongr (by rw [coinLen_eq, coinLen_eq, h])) (Equiv.refl Bool)

/-- The coin equivalence keeps the coin string: `List.ofFn (coinsCongr h n r) = List.ofFn r`. -/
theorem coinsCongr_ofFn {A B : NUPPT} (h : A.coins = B.coins) (n : ℕ) (r : A.Coins n) :
    List.ofFn (coinsCongr h n r) = List.ofFn r :=
  (List.ofFn_congr (by rw [coinLen_eq, coinLen_eq, h]) r).symm

/-- Running `B` on coins carried over from `A`: `B.runAt n y (coinsCongr h n r) =
B.runAtL n y (List.ofFn r)`. -/
theorem runAt_coinsCongr {A B : NUPPT} (h : A.coins = B.coins) (n : ℕ) (y : List Bool)
    (r : A.Coins n) : B.runAt n y (coinsCongr h n r) = B.runAtL n y (List.ofFn r) := by
  rw [runAt_eq, coinsCongr_ofFn]

/-- **The coins of a machine with a known coin polynomial**: `A.Coins n ≃ {0,1}^{c(n)}` when
`A.coins = c` (`finCongr` on the coin length). The interface through which a statement reads the
coins of a construction as bit strings of the polynomial's length, without reducing `coinLen` or
the construction. -/
def coinsEquivPoly {A : NUPPT} {c : PolyExpr} (h : A.coins = c) (n : ℕ) :
    A.Coins n ≃ (Fin (c.eval n) → Bool) :=
  Equiv.arrowCongr (finCongr (by rw [coinLen_eq, h])) (Equiv.refl Bool)

/-- The coin equivalence keeps the coin string:
`List.ofFn (coinsEquivPoly h n r) = List.ofFn r`. -/
theorem coinsEquivPoly_ofFn {A : NUPPT} {c : PolyExpr} (h : A.coins = c) (n : ℕ) (r : A.Coins n) :
    List.ofFn (coinsEquivPoly h n r) = List.ofFn r :=
  (List.ofFn_congr (by rw [coinLen_eq, h]) r).symm

/-- The inverse coin equivalence keeps the coin string:
`List.ofFn ((coinsEquivPoly h n).symm w) = List.ofFn w`. -/
theorem coinsEquivPoly_symm_ofFn {A : NUPPT} {c : PolyExpr} (h : A.coins = c) (n : ℕ)
    (w : Fin (c.eval n) → Bool) : List.ofFn ((coinsEquivPoly h n).symm w) = List.ofFn w := by
  rw [← coinsEquivPoly_ofFn h n, Equiv.apply_symm_apply]

/-- The input-length-indexed activation `A_{|y|}(y)` of [PS10, Definition 26.8]: the
parameter is the input length (the `1^{|y|}` prefix carries no information). It is the layout
of the literal forms of [PS10, Definition 26.1] and [PS10, Definition 69.4] (D5). -/
def runLit (y : List Bool) (r : A.Coins y.length) : List Bool := A.runAt y.length y r

/-- `A` is *uniform* — a PPT [PS10, Definition 23.4] — when its advice is empty at every
parameter. -/
def Uniform : Prop := ∀ n, A.advice n = []

/-- Uniformity is the conjunction of the advice clauses (definitional unfolding):
`A.Uniform ↔ ∀ n, A.advice n = []`. -/
theorem uniform_iff : A.Uniform ↔ ∀ n, A.advice n = [] := Iff.rfl

/-- A uniform machine has empty advice at every parameter. -/
theorem Uniform.advice_eq {A : NUPPT} (h : A.Uniform) (n : ℕ) : A.advice n = [] := h n

/-- `A` computes `f` with probability one [PS10, Definition 24.6]: at every parameter `n`,
on every argument `y` and for **every** coin string `r`, `A(1^n, y; r) = f(⟨1^n, y⟩)`. On
the finite uniform coin space "probability one" is the same as "every coin string"
(`TCSlib.Cryptography.Asymptotic.Adversary`, `NUPPT.computes_iff_uprob`).

The definition does not require `A.Uniform`. [PS10, Definition 24.6] is about a randomized
algorithm, i.e. a PPT, and is the case `A.Uniform ∧ A.Computes f`. For a non-uniform `A` this
is the advice analogue, which holds for uncomputable functions: with advice `[h n]` at
parameter `n` for an arbitrary `h : ℕ → Bool` (`ofPolyTime` of the advice projection), `A`
computes `w ↦ [h |fst w|]`. So `∃ A : NUPPT, A.Computes f` does **not** mean "a PPT computes
`f`"; where the text means efficient computation, the form is `A.Uniform ∧ A.Computes f`
(`exists_uniform_computes`; conversely `NUPPT.Computes.polyTimeComputable` of
`TCSlib.Complexity.Randomized.Closure`, which assumes `Uniform`).

`Computes f` constrains `f` only on the encodings `advInput n y = ⟨1^n, y⟩`: off them `f` is
arbitrary, even uncomputable, so `A.Uniform ∧ A.Computes f` is efficient computation of `f` on
those encodings, not of `f` on every string (the converse gives polynomial-time computability of
`z ↦ f ⟨1^{|fst z|}, snd z⟩`; gate 03a, round 2, R2-1). -/
def Computes (f : List Bool → List Bool) : Prop :=
  ∀ n y (r : A.Coins n), A.runAt n y r = f (advInput n y)

/-- A machine that computes `f` returns `f ⟨1^n, y⟩` on every activation. -/
theorem Computes.runAt_eq {f : List Bool → List Bool} (h : A.Computes f) (n : ℕ)
    (y : List Bool) (r : A.Coins n) : A.runAt n y r = f (advInput n y) :=
  h n y r

/-- The `NUPPT` whose machine is a polynomial-time machine for `f` (chosen from the
`PolyTimeComputable` witness), with the given coin polynomial and advice. Its output function
is `f` (`output_ofPolyTime`). This is how every reduction of the campaign is packaged: the
reduction is an FP function of the raw input `⟨⟨⟨1^n, y⟩, advice n⟩, r⟩` (D2). -/
noncomputable def ofPolyTime {f : List Bool → List Bool} (hf : PolyTimeComputable f)
    (coins adv : PolyExpr) (advice : ℕ → List Bool)
    (hα : ∀ n, (advice n).length ≤ adv.eval n) : NUPPT where
  M := Classical.choose hf
  Ct := Classical.choose (Classical.choose_spec hf)
  ct := Classical.choose (Classical.choose_spec (Classical.choose_spec hf))
  coins := coins
  adv := adv
  advice := advice
  advice_length := hα
  halts := fun z => ⟨f z, Classical.choose_spec (Classical.choose_spec (Classical.choose_spec hf)) z⟩

/-- The output function of `ofPolyTime hf …` is `f` (determinism of completed outputs). -/
theorem output_ofPolyTime {f : List Bool → List Bool} (hf : PolyTimeComputable f)
    (coins adv : PolyExpr) (advice : ℕ → List Bool) (hα : ∀ n, (advice n).length ≤ adv.eval n) :
    (ofPolyTime hf coins adv advice hα).output = f := by
  funext z
  exact (ofPolyTime hf coins adv advice hα).output_eq_of_computesInTime
    (Classical.choose_spec (Classical.choose_spec (Classical.choose_spec hf)) z)

/-- The coin polynomial of `ofPolyTime hf coins adv advice hα` is `coins`. -/
@[simp] theorem coins_ofPolyTime {f : List Bool → List Bool} (hf : PolyTimeComputable f)
    (coins adv : PolyExpr) (advice : ℕ → List Bool) (hα : ∀ n, (advice n).length ≤ adv.eval n) :
    (ofPolyTime hf coins adv advice hα).coins = coins := rfl

/-- **The coins of `ofPolyTime hf coins …`** are `coins(n)` bits: the published equivalence
`(ofPolyTime hf coins adv advice hα).Coins n ≃ {0,1}^{coins(n)}` (`coinsEquivPoly`). -/
noncomputable def coinsEquiv_ofPolyTime {f : List Bool → List Bool} (hf : PolyTimeComputable f)
    (coins adv : PolyExpr) (advice : ℕ → List Bool) (hα : ∀ n, (advice n).length ≤ adv.eval n)
    (n : ℕ) : (ofPolyTime hf coins adv advice hα).Coins n ≃ (Fin (coins.eval n) → Bool) :=
  coinsEquivPoly (coins_ofPolyTime hf coins adv advice hα) n

/-- The coin equivalence of `ofPolyTime` keeps the coin string. -/
theorem coinsEquiv_ofPolyTime_ofFn {f : List Bool → List Bool} (hf : PolyTimeComputable f)
    (coins adv : PolyExpr) (advice : ℕ → List Bool) (hα : ∀ n, (advice n).length ≤ adv.eval n)
    (n : ℕ) (r : (ofPolyTime hf coins adv advice hα).Coins n) :
    List.ofFn (coinsEquiv_ofPolyTime hf coins adv advice hα n r) = List.ofFn r :=
  coinsEquivPoly_ofFn _ n r

/-- The advice polynomial of `ofPolyTime hf coins adv advice hα` is `adv`. -/
@[simp] theorem adv_ofPolyTime {f : List Bool → List Bool} (hf : PolyTimeComputable f)
    (coins adv : PolyExpr) (advice : ℕ → List Bool) (hα : ∀ n, (advice n).length ≤ adv.eval n) :
    (ofPolyTime hf coins adv advice hα).adv = adv := rfl

/-- The advice of `ofPolyTime hf coins adv advice hα` is `advice`. -/
@[simp] theorem advice_ofPolyTime {f : List Bool → List Bool} (hf : PolyTimeComputable f)
    (coins adv : PolyExpr) (advice : ℕ → List Bool) (hα : ∀ n, (advice n).length ≤ adv.eval n) :
    (ofPolyTime hf coins adv advice hα).advice = advice := rfl

/-- The untyped activation of `ofPolyTime hf …` is `f` on the raw layout. -/
theorem runAtL_ofPolyTime {f : List Bool → List Bool} (hf : PolyTimeComputable f)
    (coins adv : PolyExpr) (advice : ℕ → List Bool) (hα : ∀ n, (advice n).length ≤ adv.eval n)
    (n : ℕ) (y r : List Bool) :
    (ofPolyTime hf coins adv advice hα).runAtL n y r =
      f (pairEncode (pairEncode (advInput n y) (advice n)) r) := by
  simp [runAtL, output_ofPolyTime]

/-- The uniform `NUPPT` with output function `f`: `ofPolyTime` with empty advice. -/
noncomputable def ofPolyTimeUniform {f : List Bool → List Bool} (hf : PolyTimeComputable f)
    (coins : PolyExpr) : NUPPT :=
  ofPolyTime hf coins (.const 0) (fun _ => []) (fun _ => by simp)

/-- `ofPolyTimeUniform hf coins` is uniform. -/
theorem ofPolyTimeUniform_uniform {f : List Bool → List Bool} (hf : PolyTimeComputable f)
    (coins : PolyExpr) : (ofPolyTimeUniform hf coins).Uniform := fun _ => rfl

/-- The output function of `ofPolyTimeUniform hf coins` is `f`. -/
theorem output_ofPolyTimeUniform {f : List Bool → List Bool} (hf : PolyTimeComputable f)
    (coins : PolyExpr) : (ofPolyTimeUniform hf coins).output = f :=
  output_ofPolyTime hf coins (.const 0) (fun _ => []) (fun _ => by simp)

/-- The coin polynomial of `ofPolyTimeUniform hf coins` is `coins`. -/
@[simp] theorem coins_ofPolyTimeUniform {f : List Bool → List Bool} (hf : PolyTimeComputable f)
    (coins : PolyExpr) : (ofPolyTimeUniform hf coins).coins = coins := rfl

/-- **The coins of `ofPolyTimeUniform hf coins`** are `coins(n)` bits: the published equivalence
`(ofPolyTimeUniform hf coins).Coins n ≃ {0,1}^{coins(n)}` (`coinsEquivPoly`). -/
noncomputable def coinsEquiv_ofPolyTimeUniform {f : List Bool → List Bool} (hf : PolyTimeComputable f)
    (coins : PolyExpr) (n : ℕ) : (ofPolyTimeUniform hf coins).Coins n ≃ (Fin (coins.eval n) → Bool) :=
  coinsEquivPoly (coins_ofPolyTimeUniform hf coins) n

/-- The coin equivalence of `ofPolyTimeUniform` keeps the coin string. -/
theorem coinsEquiv_ofPolyTimeUniform_ofFn {f : List Bool → List Bool} (hf : PolyTimeComputable f)
    (coins : PolyExpr) (n : ℕ) (r : (ofPolyTimeUniform hf coins).Coins n) :
    List.ofFn (coinsEquiv_ofPolyTimeUniform hf coins n r) = List.ofFn r :=
  coinsEquivPoly_ofFn _ n r

/-- The untyped activation of `ofPolyTimeUniform hf coins` is `f` on the raw layout with
empty advice. -/
theorem runAtL_ofPolyTimeUniform {f : List Bool → List Bool} (hf : PolyTimeComputable f)
    (coins : PolyExpr) (n : ℕ) (y r : List Bool) :
    (ofPolyTimeUniform hf coins).runAtL n y r =
      f (pairEncode (pairEncode (advInput n y) []) r) := by
  simp [runAtL, ofPolyTimeUniform, output_ofPolyTime]

/-- **Non-vacuity of [PS10, Definition 24.6].** Every polynomial-time computable function
`f` is computed with probability one by a PPT (a uniform `NUPPT`): the machine for
`f ∘ pairFstD ∘ pairFstD` applied to the raw input `⟨⟨⟨1^n, y⟩, []⟩, r⟩` ignores the advice
and the coins and returns `f ⟨1^n, y⟩`. (This is the direction "`PolyTimeComputable f` gives a
PPT computing `f`" of the equivalence behind Deviation 3, `FunFamily.Easy`.) -/
theorem exists_uniform_computes {f : List Bool → List Bool} (hf : PolyTimeComputable f)
    (coins : PolyExpr) : ∃ A : NUPPT, A.Uniform ∧ A.coins = coins ∧ A.Computes f := by
  have hF : PolyTimeComputable fun z => f (pairFstD (pairFstD z)) :=
    hf.comp (polyTimeComputable_pairFstD.comp polyTimeComputable_pairFstD)
  refine ⟨ofPolyTimeUniform hF coins, ofPolyTimeUniform_uniform hF coins, rfl, fun n y r => ?_⟩
  rw [runAt_eq, runAtL_ofPolyTimeUniform]
  simp

end NUPPT

/-- PPT [PS10, Definition 23.4] = non-uniform PPT with empty advice: the subtype of uniform
`NUPPT`s. -/
def PPT : Type 1 := {A : NUPPT // A.Uniform}

/-- Non-vacuity: the class is inhabited (the identity machine with no coins). -/
theorem NUPPT.nonempty : Nonempty NUPPT :=
  ⟨NUPPT.ofPolyTimeUniform polyTimeComputable_id (.const 0)⟩

/-- Non-vacuity: the class of PPTs is inhabited. -/
theorem PPT.nonempty : Nonempty PPT :=
  ⟨⟨NUPPT.ofPolyTimeUniform polyTimeComputable_id (.const 0),
    NUPPT.ofPolyTimeUniform_uniform _ _⟩⟩

end Complexity

import TCSlib.Complexity.ClassNP.NTIME
import TCSlib.Complexity.Randomized.RandomBits

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Probabilistic Turing machines and the classes BPTIME, BPP, RTIME, RP, coRP

The machine-level randomized classes of [AB09, §7.1 and §7.3].  A probabilistic Turing
machine is a binary-choice machine `Turing.FinNDTM Bool` read probabilistically: its coin
tosses are the choice word of `Turing.NDTM.runWith`, and `Pr[M(x) = v]` over `t` coins is
the fraction of length-`t` choice words whose run ends with output `v` (`Randomized.randProb`).

## Main definitions

* `Turing.FinNDTM.RunsInTime` — [AB09, Def 7.1]: halts within `T(|x|)` steps on every branch.
* `Turing.FinNDTM.outputWith`, `Turing.FinNDTM.outputProb` — the output under a coin word and
  the probability of an output over `t` coins.
* `Turing.FinNDTM.BPDecidesInTime`, `Randomized.BPTIME`, `Randomized.BPP_PTM` — [AB09, Def 7.2].
* `Turing.FinNDTM.RDecidesInTime`, `Randomized.RTIME`, `Randomized.RP_PTM` — [AB09, Def 7.6];
  `Randomized.coRP_PTM` — [AB09, §7.3].
* `Turing.NDTM.flipOutput` — negate every emitted output bit.

## Main results

* `Turing.FinNDTM.outputProb_eq_of_haltsWithin` — the acceptance probability does not change
  once every branch has halted.
* `Randomized.BPTIME.mono`, `Randomized.BPTIME_const_mul_subset`, and the `RTIME` analogues.
* `Randomized.compl_mem_BPTIME`, `Randomized.compl_mem_BPP_PTM` — closure under complement.

## Divergences

* Output convention: [AB09] says the machine "only outputs 1 or 0".  `BPDecidesInTime` counts a
  branch as correct iff its output is exactly `[L(x)]` (as `FinNDTM.AcceptsWithin` reads
  `[true]`), so any other output counts as an error.  For `RTIME` the clause
  "`x ∉ L ⇒ Pr[M(x) = 1] = 0`" is stated as "every branch outputs `[false]`", which is the
  book's clause under its 0/1-output convention and makes `RP ⊆ BPP` hold as in the book.
  So `BPDecidesInTime` admits machines with other outputs (counted as errors), and the `RTIME`
  soundness clause is stricter than the literal `Pr[M(x) = 1] = 0` for such machines; that
  the classes coincide with the book's is secured by the equivalence with [AB09, Def 7.3]
  (unit U2).
* As for `Complexity.NTIME`, the constant `c` in `c · T` ranges over `ℕ`; `c = 0` (or
  `T n = 0`) gives the unsatisfiable budget `0`, since no machine is halted at time `0`, and
  contributes nothing.  `BPP`/`RP` use the bounds `n^c + 1` of `Complexity.P`, the `+ 1`
  keeping the budget positive at `n = 0`.
* `Turing.NDTM.flipOutput` is a transition relabelling, defined directly; the general output
  map `Turing.NDTM.mapOutput` (`TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Build.NDCombinators`) is not
  imported here.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009.
-/

namespace Turing

namespace NDTM

variable {k : ℕ} {State : Type*} {input : List Bool}

/-- The machine `tm` with every emitted output bit negated: the transitions of `tm`, with the
output symbol of each action replaced by its negation. -/
def flipOutput (tm : NDTM k Bool State) : NDTM k Bool State :=
  ⟨tm.q₀, fun b q i w => { tm.tr b q i w with output := (tm.tr b q i w).output.map not }⟩

/-- A configuration with its output tape negated bitwise. -/
def flipCfg (cfg : Cfg k Bool State input) : Cfg k Bool State input :=
  { cfg with output := cfg.output.map not }

/-- One step of `flipOutput` on a negated configuration is the negation of one step. -/
theorem flipOutput_stepWith (tm : NDTM k Bool State) (b : Bool) (cfg : Cfg k Bool State input) :
    tm.flipOutput.stepWith b (flipCfg cfg) = flipCfg (tm.stepWith b cfg) := by
  cases h : cfg.state with
  | none =>
    rw [stepWith_of_halt h, stepWith_of_halt (by simpa [flipCfg] using h)]
  | some q =>
    have h' : (flipCfg cfg).state = some q := by simpa [flipCfg] using h
    simp only [stepWith, h, flipOutput, flipCfg, Action.apply, List.map_append,
      Option.toList_map]
    rfl

/-- Running `flipOutput` from a negated configuration gives the negated run. -/
theorem flipOutput_runWith (tm : NDTM k Bool State) (w : List Bool)
    (cfg : Cfg k Bool State input) :
    tm.flipOutput.runWith w (flipCfg cfg) = flipCfg (tm.runWith w cfg) := by
  induction w generalizing cfg with
  | nil => rfl
  | cons b w ih => rw [runWith_cons, runWith_cons, flipOutput_stepWith, ih]

/-- `flipOutput` starts in the negation of the original initial configuration. -/
theorem flipOutput_initCfg (tm : NDTM k Bool State) (x : List Bool) :
    tm.flipOutput.initCfg x = flipCfg (tm.initCfg x) := rfl

end NDTM

namespace FinNDTM

/-- `flipOutput` on the bundled layer: the same tapes and states, output bits negated. -/
def flipOutput (N : FinNDTM Bool) : FinNDTM Bool :=
  ⟨N.k, N.State, N.tm.flipOutput⟩

/-- The PTM `N` *runs in time* `T`: on every input `x` it halts within `T(|x|)` steps whatever
its coin tosses. [AB09, Def 7.1] -/
def RunsInTime (N : FinNDTM Bool) (T : ℕ → ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ x : List Bool, N.tm.HaltsWithin x (T x.length)

/-- The output of `N` on `x` under the coin word `w` (one coin per step). -/
def outputWith (N : FinNDTM Bool) (x w : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  (N.tm.runWith w (N.tm.initCfg x)).output

/-- `Pr[M(x) = v]` over `t` fair coins: the fraction of coin words of length `t` whose run on
`x` ends with output `v`. [AB09, §7.1: "the fraction of branches"] -/
def outputProb (N : FinNDTM Bool) (x : List Bool) (t : ℕ) (v : List Bool) : ℚ :=
  Randomized.randProb t fun w => N.outputWith x w = v

/-- The PTM `N` *decides* `L` in time `T` with bounded error: on every input `x` it halts
within `T(|x|)` steps on every branch, and `Pr[M(x) = L(x)] ≥ 2/3`. [AB09, Def 7.2] -/
def BPDecidesInTime (N : FinNDTM Bool) (L : Language Bool) (T : ℕ → ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ x : List Bool, N.tm.HaltsWithin x (T x.length) ∧
    2/3 ≤ N.outputProb x (T x.length) [MultiTapeTM.indicator (L : Set (List Bool)) x]

/-- The PTM `N` decides `L` in time `T` with one-sided error: every branch halts within
`T(|x|)` steps, members are accepted with probability at least `2/3`, and on non-members every
branch outputs `0`. [AB09, Def 7.6] -/
def RDecidesInTime (N : FinNDTM Bool) (L : Language Bool) (T : ℕ → ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ x : List Bool, N.tm.HaltsWithin x (T x.length) ∧
    (x ∈ L → 2/3 ≤ N.outputProb x (T x.length) [true]) ∧
    (x ∉ L → ∀ w : List Bool, w.length = T x.length → N.outputWith x w = [false])

/-- `BPDecidesInTime` bundles `RunsInTime`. -/
theorem BPDecidesInTime.runsInTime {N : FinNDTM Bool} {L : Language Bool} {T : ℕ → ℕ}
    (h : N.BPDecidesInTime L T) : N.RunsInTime T := fun x => (h x).1

/-- `RDecidesInTime` bundles `RunsInTime`. -/
theorem RDecidesInTime.runsInTime {N : FinNDTM Bool} {L : Language Bool} {T : ℕ → ℕ}
    (h : N.RDecidesInTime L T) : N.RunsInTime T := fun x => (h x).1

/-- Once every branch has halted by time `t`, the run under a longer coin word is the run
under its length-`t` prefix. -/
theorem runWith_eq_runWith_take {N : FinNDTM Bool} {x : List Bool} {t : ℕ}
    (h : N.tm.HaltsWithin x t) {w : List Bool} (hw : t ≤ w.length) :
    N.tm.runWith w (N.tm.initCfg x) = N.tm.runWith (w.take t) (N.tm.initCfg x) := by
  have hhalt := h (w.take t) (List.length_take_of_le hw)
  have hrun := NDTM.runWith_append (tm := N.tm) (w.take t) (w.drop t) (N.tm.initCfg x)
  rw [List.take_append_drop, NDTM.runWith_of_halt _ hhalt] at hrun
  exact hrun

/-- **Coins past the halting time are ignored**: if every branch halts within `t` steps, the
output distribution over `t' ≥ t` coins equals the one over `t` coins. -/
theorem outputProb_eq_of_haltsWithin {N : FinNDTM Bool} {x : List Bool} {t t' : ℕ}
    (h : N.tm.HaltsWithin x t) (hle : t ≤ t') (v : List Bool) :
    N.outputProb x t' v = N.outputProb x t v := by
  unfold outputProb
  rw [← Randomized.randProb_take hle (fun w => N.outputWith x w = v)]
  refine Randomized.randProb_congr fun r => ?_
  have hlen : t ≤ (List.ofFn r).length := by rw [List.length_ofFn]; exact hle
  simp only [outputWith, runWith_eq_runWith_take h hlen]

/-- If every branch of length `t` outputs `v`, then `Pr[M(x) = v] = 1`. -/
theorem outputProb_eq_one {N : FinNDTM Bool} {x : List Bool} {t : ℕ} {v : List Bool}
    (h : ∀ w : List Bool, w.length = t → N.outputWith x w = v) : N.outputProb x t v = 1 := by
  unfold outputProb
  rw [Randomized.randProb_congr (B := fun _ => True) fun r => by
    simp only [h _ (List.length_ofFn)]]
  exact Randomized.randProb_true

/-- An output of positive probability is produced by some branch. -/
theorem exists_outputWith_of_outputProb_pos {N : FinNDTM Bool} {x : List Bool} {t : ℕ}
    {v : List Bool} (h : 0 < N.outputProb x t v) :
    ∃ w : List Bool, w.length = t ∧ N.outputWith x w = v := by
  obtain ⟨r, hr⟩ := Randomized.exists_ofFn_of_randProb_pos h
  exact ⟨List.ofFn r, List.length_ofFn, hr⟩

/-- Bounded-error deciding is monotone in the time bound. -/
theorem BPDecidesInTime.mono {N : FinNDTM Bool} {L : Language Bool} {T₁ T₂ : ℕ → ℕ}
    (h : N.BPDecidesInTime L T₁) (hT : ∀ n, T₁ n ≤ T₂ n) : N.BPDecidesInTime L T₂ := by
  intro x
  obtain ⟨hhalt, hprob⟩ := h x
  refine ⟨hhalt.mono (hT _), ?_⟩
  rw [outputProb_eq_of_haltsWithin hhalt (hT _)]
  exact hprob

/-- One-sided-error deciding is monotone in the time bound. -/
theorem RDecidesInTime.mono {N : FinNDTM Bool} {L : Language Bool} {T₁ T₂ : ℕ → ℕ}
    (h : N.RDecidesInTime L T₁) (hT : ∀ n, T₁ n ≤ T₂ n) : N.RDecidesInTime L T₂ := by
  intro x
  obtain ⟨hhalt, hin, hout⟩ := h x
  refine ⟨hhalt.mono (hT _), fun hx => ?_, fun hx w hw => ?_⟩
  · rw [outputProb_eq_of_haltsWithin hhalt (hT _)]
    exact hin hx
  · have hle : T₁ x.length ≤ w.length := hw ▸ hT _
    unfold outputWith
    rw [runWith_eq_runWith_take hhalt hle]
    exact hout hx _ (List.length_take_of_le hle)

/-- A one-sided-error decider is a bounded-error decider. [AB09, §7.3: `RP ⊆ BPP`] -/
theorem RDecidesInTime.bpDecidesInTime {N : FinNDTM Bool} {L : Language Bool} {T : ℕ → ℕ}
    (h : N.RDecidesInTime L T) : N.BPDecidesInTime L T := by
  classical
  intro x
  obtain ⟨hhalt, hin, hout⟩ := h x
  refine ⟨hhalt, ?_⟩
  by_cases hx : x ∈ L
  · simpa only [MultiTapeTM.indicator, hx, if_true] using hin hx
  · have hone : N.outputProb x (T x.length) [false] = 1 := outputProb_eq_one (hout hx)
    simp only [MultiTapeTM.indicator, hx, if_false, hone]
    norm_num

/-- The negated machine has the same halting behaviour. -/
theorem flipOutput_haltsWithin_iff (N : FinNDTM Bool) (x : List Bool) (t : ℕ) :
    N.flipOutput.tm.HaltsWithin x t ↔ N.tm.HaltsWithin x t := by
  show (∀ w : List Bool, w.length = t →
      (N.tm.flipOutput.runWith w (N.tm.flipOutput.initCfg x)).state = none) ↔ _
  simp only [NDTM.flipOutput_initCfg, NDTM.flipOutput_runWith]
  rfl

/-- The negated machine's output is the bitwise negation of the original output. -/
theorem flipOutput_outputWith (N : FinNDTM Bool) (x w : List Bool) :
    N.flipOutput.outputWith x w = (N.outputWith x w).map not := by
  show (N.tm.flipOutput.runWith w (N.tm.flipOutput.initCfg x)).output = _
  rw [NDTM.flipOutput_initCfg, NDTM.flipOutput_runWith]
  rfl

/-- Negating the output turns a bounded-error decider for `L` into one for `Lᶜ`.
[AB09, p. 136: "`BPP = coBPP`"]

**Proof sketch.** Halting is unchanged, and the negated output equals `[Lᶜ(x)]` exactly when
the original equals `[L(x)]` (bitwise negation is injective), so the two events coincide. -/
theorem BPDecidesInTime.flipOutput {N : FinNDTM Bool} {L : Language Bool} {T : ℕ → ℕ}
    (h : N.BPDecidesInTime L T) : N.flipOutput.BPDecidesInTime Lᶜ T := by
  classical
  intro x
  obtain ⟨hhalt, hprob⟩ := h x
  refine ⟨(N.flipOutput_haltsWithin_iff x _).mpr hhalt, ?_⟩
  have hind : [MultiTapeTM.indicator ((Lᶜ : Language Bool) : Set (List Bool)) x] =
      [MultiTapeTM.indicator (L : Set (List Bool)) x].map not := by
    by_cases hx : x ∈ L
    · have hxc : x ∉ (Lᶜ : Language Bool) := fun h => h hx
      simp [MultiTapeTM.indicator, hx, hxc]
    · have hxc : x ∈ (Lᶜ : Language Bool) := hx
      simp [MultiTapeTM.indicator, hx, hxc]
  unfold outputProb at hprob ⊢
  rw [Randomized.randProb_congr (B := fun w =>
    N.outputWith x w = [MultiTapeTM.indicator (L : Set (List Bool)) x]) fun r => by
      rw [flipOutput_outputWith, hind]
      exact (List.map_injective_iff.mpr fun a b hab => by
        cases a <;> cases b <;> simp_all).eq_iff]
  exact hprob

end FinNDTM

end Turing

namespace Randomized

open Turing

/-- `BPTIME(T)`: the languages decided with bounded error by some PTM in time `c · T` for a
constant `c`. [AB09, Def 7.2] -/
def BPTIME (T : ℕ → ℕ) : Set (Language Bool) :=
  {L | ∃ (c : ℕ) (N : FinNDTM Bool), N.BPDecidesInTime L fun n => c * T n}

/-- `BPP = ⋃_c BPTIME(n^c + 1)`, the PTM form of bounded-error probabilistic polynomial time.
[AB09, Def 7.2] -/
def BPP_PTM : Set (Language Bool) := ⋃ c : ℕ, BPTIME fun n => n ^ c + 1

/-- `RTIME(T)`: the languages decided with one-sided error by some PTM in time `c · T` for a
constant `c`. [AB09, Def 7.6] -/
def RTIME (T : ℕ → ℕ) : Set (Language Bool) :=
  {L | ∃ (c : ℕ) (N : FinNDTM Bool), N.RDecidesInTime L fun n => c * T n}

/-- `RP = ⋃_c RTIME(n^c + 1)`. [AB09, Def 7.6] -/
def RP_PTM : Set (Language Bool) := ⋃ c : ℕ, RTIME fun n => n ^ c + 1

/-- `coRP = {L | Lᶜ ∈ RP}`. [AB09, §7.3] -/
def coRP_PTM : Set (Language Bool) := {L | Lᶜ ∈ RP_PTM}

/-- `BPTIME` is monotone in the time bound. -/
theorem BPTIME.mono {T₁ T₂ : ℕ → ℕ} (h : ∀ n, T₁ n ≤ T₂ n) : BPTIME T₁ ⊆ BPTIME T₂ := by
  rintro L ⟨c, N, hN⟩
  exact ⟨c, N, hN.mono fun n => Nat.mul_le_mul_left c (h n)⟩

/-- `RTIME` is monotone in the time bound. -/
theorem RTIME.mono {T₁ T₂ : ℕ → ℕ} (h : ∀ n, T₁ n ≤ T₂ n) : RTIME T₁ ⊆ RTIME T₂ := by
  rintro L ⟨c, N, hN⟩
  exact ⟨c, N, hN.mono fun n => Nat.mul_le_mul_left c (h n)⟩

/-- Constant factors are absorbed: `BPTIME(a · T) ⊆ BPTIME(T)`. -/
theorem BPTIME_const_mul_subset (a : ℕ) (T : ℕ → ℕ) :
    BPTIME (fun n => a * T n) ⊆ BPTIME T := by
  rintro L ⟨c, N, hN⟩
  exact ⟨c * a, N, by simpa only [Nat.mul_assoc] using hN⟩

/-- Constant factors are absorbed: `RTIME(a · T) ⊆ RTIME(T)`. -/
theorem RTIME_const_mul_subset (a : ℕ) (T : ℕ → ℕ) :
    RTIME (fun n => a * T n) ⊆ RTIME T := by
  rintro L ⟨c, N, hN⟩
  exact ⟨c * a, N, by simpa only [Nat.mul_assoc] using hN⟩

/-- `RTIME(T) ⊆ BPTIME(T)`. [AB09, §7.3] -/
theorem RTIME_subset_BPTIME (T : ℕ → ℕ) : RTIME T ⊆ BPTIME T := by
  rintro L ⟨c, N, hN⟩
  exact ⟨c, N, hN.bpDecidesInTime⟩

/-- `BPTIME(T)` is closed under complement. -/
theorem compl_mem_BPTIME {T : ℕ → ℕ} {L : Language Bool} (h : L ∈ BPTIME T) :
    Lᶜ ∈ BPTIME T := by
  obtain ⟨c, N, hN⟩ := h
  exact ⟨c, N.flipOutput, hN.flipOutput⟩

/-- `BPP` (PTM form) is closed under complement. [AB09, p. 136] -/
theorem compl_mem_BPP_PTM {L : Language Bool} (h : L ∈ BPP_PTM) : Lᶜ ∈ BPP_PTM := by
  obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := Set.mem_iUnion.mp h
  exact Set.mem_iUnion.mpr ⟨c, compl_mem_BPTIME hc⟩

end Randomized

import TCSlib.Complexity.Randomized.Inclusions

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# The two definitions of BPP agree

[AB09, p. 126] gives an alternative definition of `BPP` (Def 7.3): a deterministic
polynomial-time machine reading its coin tosses as an extra input.  We prove that the PTM
classes of [AB09, Def 7.2 and Def 7.6] (`Randomized.BPP_PTM`, `Randomized.RP_PTM`,
`Randomized.coRP_PTM`) coincide with the certificate classes over polynomial-time verifiers
(`Randomized.InBPP polyTimeModel` etc.), and transfer the certificate-form corollaries.

## Main definitions

* `Turing.FinNDTM.BPDecidesInTimeWith`, `Randomized.BPP_PTMWith`, `Randomized.InBPPWith` —
  `BPP` with success threshold `p(|x|)` in place of `2/3`, PTM and certificate forms.
* `Turing.FinNDTM.RDecidesInTimeWith`, `Randomized.RP_PTMWith` — `RP` with acceptance
  threshold `p(|x|)` in place of `2/3` (the PTM side of [AB09, Ex 7.4]).

## Main results

* `Randomized.randProb_maskSelect` — uniform coins push forward to uniform bits under a
  coordinate projection (with `Randomized.randProb_drop_take` for the slice).
* `Randomized.exists_FinNDTM_maskSelect_of_eff`, `Randomized.exists_FinNDTM_of_eff` — a
  polynomial-time verifier as a PTM reading a coordinate projection of its coins, hence with the
  same output distribution (via `Complexity.exists_maskSelect_host`).
* `Randomized.mem_BPP_PTMWith_iff` — PTM and certificate `BPP` agree at every threshold;
  its `2/3` case `Randomized.mem_BPP_PTM_iff` is `L ∈ BPP ↔ InBPP polyTimeModel L`
  [AB09, Def 7.2 ≡ Def 7.3].
* `Randomized.mem_RP_PTM_iff`, `Randomized.mem_coRP_PTM_iff` — the same for `RP`, `coRP`.
* `Randomized.BPP_PTM_subset_EXP`, `Randomized.BPP_PTM_eq_P_of_P_eq_NP`,
  `Randomized.BPP_PTM_subset_PPoly` [AB09, Thm 7.14],
  `Randomized.BPP_PTM_subset_SigmaP_two_inter_PiP_two` [AB09, Thm 7.15],
  `Randomized.BPP_PTM_of_polyTimeReducible`, `Randomized.PH_eq_SigmaP_two_of_SAT3_mem_BPP_PTM`,
  `Randomized.RP_PTMWith_error_reduction` [AB09, Ex 7.4] — PTM-form corollaries.

## Divergences

* The coin word of a PTM has length exactly its time bound `K·(n^e + 1)`, while a certificate
  verifier draws `polyLen a k n = a·(n+1)^k` bits; the translation pads (coins past halting
  are ignored) or projects onto the coordinates the simulating machine reads.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009.
-/

namespace Randomized

open Complexity Turing

/-! ### Coordinate projections preserve the uniform distribution -/

/-- `maskSelect` returns one bit per marked position. -/
theorem length_maskSelect (mask w : List Bool) (hw : w.length = mask.length) :
    (maskSelect mask w).length = (mask.filter id).length := by
  induction mask generalizing w with
  | nil => cases w <;> rfl
  | cons emit mask ih =>
    cases w with
    | nil => simp at hw
    | cons b w =>
      have ht : w.length = mask.length := by simpa using hw
      cases emit <;> simp [maskSelect, ih w ht]

/-- **Projection onto marked coordinates is measure-preserving**: the bits of a uniform word
at the marked positions of `mask` are uniform. -/
theorem randProb_maskSelect (mask : List Bool) (A : List Bool → Prop) [DecidablePred A] :
    randProb mask.length (fun w => A (maskSelect mask w)) =
      randProb (mask.filter id).length A := by
  induction mask generalizing A with
  | nil =>
    refine randProb_congr fun r => ?_
    have h : List.ofFn r = [] := List.eq_nil_of_length_eq_zero (by simp)
    rw [h]
    rfl
  | cons emit mask ih =>
    rw [List.length_cons, randProb_succ]
    cases emit with
    | false =>
      simp only [maskSelect, if_false, List.nil_append, List.filter_cons, id, Bool.false_eq_true]
      rw [ih A]
      ring
    | true =>
      simp only [maskSelect, if_true, List.singleton_append, List.filter_cons, id,
        List.length_cons]
      rw [ih (fun u => A (false :: u)), ih (fun u => A (true :: u)), randProb_succ]

/-- The slice-then-project map `w ↦ maskSelect mask (w[s, s+|mask|))` pushes the uniform
distribution on `m`-bit words to the uniform distribution on `|mask.filter id|`-bit words. -/
theorem randProb_maskSelect_drop_take {s m : ℕ} (mask : List Bool) (h : s + mask.length ≤ m)
    (A : List Bool → Prop) [DecidablePred A] :
    randProb m (fun w => A (maskSelect mask ((w.drop s).take mask.length))) =
      randProb (mask.filter id).length A := by
  rw [randProb_drop_take h (fun v => A (maskSelect mask v)), randProb_maskSelect]

/-! ### Certificate verifiers from PTMs -/

/-- The indicator of `V` is `true` exactly on `V`. -/
theorem indicator_eq_true_iff {V : Language Bool} {y : List Bool} :
    MultiTapeTM.indicator (V : Set (List Bool)) y = true ↔ y ∈ V := by
  classical
  simp [MultiTapeTM.indicator]

/-- The indicator of `V` is `false` exactly off `V`. -/
theorem indicator_eq_false_iff {V : Language Bool} {y : List Bool} :
    MultiTapeTM.indicator (V : Set (List Bool)) y = false ↔ y ∉ V := by
  classical
  simp [MultiTapeTM.indicator]

/-- A Boolean verifier whose test on `⟨x, r⟩` is a polynomial-time computable bit is
efficient for `polyTimeModel`. -/
theorem eff_boolVerifier_of_test {M : List Bool → List Bool → Bool} {t : List Bool → Bool}
    (ht : PolyTimeComputable fun z => [t z]) (hM : ∀ x r, t (pairEncode x r) = M x r) :
    polyTimeModel.Eff (boolVerifier M) := by
  refine ⟨{z | t z = true}, {z | t z = true}ᶜ, mem_P_of_test ht,
    compl_mem_P (mem_P_of_test ht), fun x r => ?_⟩
  show (some (M x r) = some true ↔ t (pairEncode x r) = true) ∧
    (some (M x r) = some false ↔ ¬ t (pairEncode x r) = true)
  rw [hM]
  simp

/-- A verifier of the form `M(x, r) = [x ++ r ∈ V]` with `V ∈ P` is polynomial-time. -/
theorem eff_append_mem {V : Language Bool} (hV : V ∈ P) :
    polyTimeModel.Eff (boolVerifier fun x r => MultiTapeTM.indicator V (x ++ r)) := by
  classical
  have hg : PolyTimeComputable fun z => pairFstD z ++ pairSndD z :=
    polyTimeComputable_pairFstD.append polyTimeComputable_pairSndD
  have h1 : (fun z => pairFstD z ++ pairSndD z) ⁻¹' V ∈ P := preimage_mem_P hV hg
  refine ⟨_, _, h1, compl_mem_P h1, fun x r => ⟨?_, ?_⟩⟩
  · show some (MultiTapeTM.indicator V (x ++ r)) = some true ↔
      pairFstD (Turing.pairEncode x r) ++ pairSndD (Turing.pairEncode x r) ∈ V
    rw [pairFstD_pairEncode, pairSndD_pairEncode, Option.some.injEq, indicator_eq_true_iff]
  · show some (MultiTapeTM.indicator V (x ++ r)) = some false ↔
      ¬ (pairFstD (Turing.pairEncode x r) ++ pairSndD (Turing.pairEncode x r) ∈ V)
    rw [pairFstD_pairEncode, pairSndD_pairEncode, Option.some.injEq, indicator_eq_false_iff]

/-- The choice-word verifier of a PTM `N` halting within `T ≤ Q` steps on `x`: on a `Q`-bit
coin word `r`, it accepts iff `N` outputs `[true]` under the first `T` coins of `r`. -/
theorem append_mem_iff_outputWith_take {N : FinNDTM Bool} {V : Language Bool} {x : List Bool}
    {T Q : ℕ}
    (hV : ∀ u : List Bool, u.length = Q →
      (x ++ u ∈ V ↔ (N.tm.runWith u (N.tm.initCfg x)).state = none ∧
        (N.tm.runWith u (N.tm.initCfg x)).output = [true]))
    (hhalt : N.tm.HaltsWithin x T) (hTQ : T ≤ Q) (r : List Bool) (hr : r.length = Q) :
    x ++ r ∈ V ↔ N.outputWith x (r.take T) = [true] := by
  have hle : T ≤ r.length := hr ▸ hTQ
  rw [hV r hr, FinNDTM.runWith_eq_runWith_take hhalt hle]
  exact ⟨fun h => h.2, fun h => ⟨hhalt _ (List.length_take_of_le hle), h⟩⟩

/-- The acceptance probability of the choice-word verifier is the PTM's. -/
theorem randProb_choiceVerifier {N : FinNDTM Bool} {V : Language Bool} {x : List Bool}
    {T Q : ℕ}
    (hV : ∀ u : List Bool, u.length = Q →
      (x ++ u ∈ V ↔ (N.tm.runWith u (N.tm.initCfg x)).state = none ∧
        (N.tm.runWith u (N.tm.initCfg x)).output = [true]))
    (hhalt : N.tm.HaltsWithin x T) (hTQ : T ≤ Q) :
    (randProb Q fun r => MultiTapeTM.indicator V (x ++ r) = true) = N.outputProb x T [true] := by
  classical
  unfold FinNDTM.outputProb
  rw [← randProb_take hTQ fun w => N.outputWith x w = [true]]
  refine randProb_congr fun r => ?_
  rw [indicator_eq_true_iff]
  exact append_mem_iff_outputWith_take hV hhalt hTQ _ (List.length_ofFn)

end Randomized

/-! ### `BPP` with a general success threshold -/

namespace Turing.FinNDTM

/-- `N` decides `L` in time `T` with success threshold `p(|x|)`: every branch halts within
`T(|x|)` steps and `Pr[N(x) = L(x)] ≥ p(|x|)`. [AB09, Def 7.2 and Lemma 7.9] -/
def BPDecidesInTimeWith (N : FinNDTM Bool) (L : Language Bool) (T : ℕ → ℕ) (p : ℕ → ℚ) :
    Prop :=
  ∀ x : List Bool, N.tm.HaltsWithin x (T x.length) ∧
    p x.length ≤ N.outputProb x (T x.length) [MultiTapeTM.indicator (L : Set (List Bool)) x]

/-- `BPDecidesInTime` is the threshold-`2/3` case. -/
theorem bpDecidesInTime_iff_with {N : FinNDTM Bool} {L : Language Bool} {T : ℕ → ℕ} :
    N.BPDecidesInTime L T ↔ N.BPDecidesInTimeWith L T fun _ => 2/3 := Iff.rfl

end Turing.FinNDTM

namespace Randomized

open Complexity Turing

/-- `BPP` with success threshold `p(|x|)`: bounded-error PTMs in time `K·(n^e + 1)`.
[AB09, Lemma 7.9] -/
def BPP_PTMWith (p : ℕ → ℚ) : Set (Language Bool) :=
  ⋃ e : ℕ, {L | ∃ (K : ℕ) (N : FinNDTM Bool),
    N.BPDecidesInTimeWith L (fun n => K * (n ^ e + 1)) p}

/-- `BPP_PTM` is the threshold-`2/3` case. -/
theorem BPP_PTM_eq_BPP_PTMWith : BPP_PTM = BPP_PTMWith fun _ => 2/3 := rfl

/-- The certificate form of `BPP_PTMWith p` over polynomial-time verifiers. -/
def InBPPWith (p : ℕ → ℚ) (L : Language Bool) : Prop :=
  ∃ (M : List Bool → List Bool → Bool) (a k : ℕ),
    polyTimeModel.Eff (boolVerifier M) ∧
    ∀ x : List Bool,
      (x ∈ L → p x.length ≤ randProb (polyLen a k x.length) fun r => M x r = true) ∧
      (x ∉ L → p x.length ≤ randProb (polyLen a k x.length) fun r => M x r = false)

/-- `InBPP polyTimeModel` is the threshold-`2/3` case. -/
theorem inBPPWith_iff_inBPP (L : Language Bool) :
    InBPPWith (fun _ => 2/3) L ↔ InBPP polyTimeModel L := Iff.rfl

/-- **Def 7.2 ⇒ Def 7.3 at threshold `p`**: a polynomial-time PTM yields a polynomial-time
verifier reading its coins as the random string. [AB09, p. 126]

**Proof sketch.** If `N` runs in time `T(n) = c(n^e + 1)`, take `M(x, r) = [x ++ r ∈ V]` with
`V` the choice-word verifier of `exists_choiceVerifier_mem_P` at length `Q = 2c(n+1)^e ≥ T`
(`choiceBudget_le`).  On a `Q`-bit word, `M` accepts iff `N` outputs `[true]` under its first
`T` coins (`append_mem_iff_outputWith_take`), so `randProb_take` turns `Pr[M = 1]` into
`Pr[N(x) = 1]`, and `Pr[M = 0] ≥ Pr[N(x) = 0]`. -/
theorem inBPPWith_of_mem_BPP_PTMWith {p : ℕ → ℚ} {L : Language Bool}
    (h : L ∈ BPP_PTMWith p) : InBPPWith p L := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨e, c, N, hN⟩ := Set.mem_iUnion.mp h
  obtain ⟨V, hVP, hV⟩ := exists_choiceVerifier_mem_P N (2 * c) e
  refine ⟨fun x r => MultiTapeTM.indicator V (x ++ r), 2 * c, e, eff_append_mem hVP, fun x => ?_⟩
  obtain ⟨hhalt, hprob⟩ := hN x
  have hTQ : c * (x.length ^ e + 1) ≤ polyLen (2 * c) e x.length := choiceBudget_le c e _
  have hVx : ∀ u : List Bool, u.length = polyLen (2 * c) e x.length → _ := fun u => hV x u
  have htrue := randProb_choiceVerifier hVx hhalt hTQ
  refine ⟨fun hx => ?_, fun hx => ?_⟩
  · exact le_of_le_of_eq (by simpa [MultiTapeTM.indicator, hx] using hprob) htrue.symm
  · have hfalse : N.outputProb x (c * (x.length ^ e + 1)) [false] ≤
        randProb (polyLen (2 * c) e x.length)
          fun r => MultiTapeTM.indicator V (x ++ r) = false := by
      unfold FinNDTM.outputProb
      rw [← randProb_take hTQ fun w => N.outputWith x w = [false]]
      refine randProb_mono fun r hr => ?_
      rw [indicator_eq_false_iff,
        append_mem_iff_outputWith_take hVx hhalt hTQ _ List.length_ofFn, hr]
      decide
    refine le_trans ?_ hfalse
    simpa [MultiTapeTM.indicator, hx] using hprob

/-- **Def 7.2 ⇒ Def 7.3** (`BPP`), the threshold-`2/3` case of
`inBPPWith_of_mem_BPP_PTMWith`. [AB09, p. 126] -/
theorem inBPP_of_mem_BPP_PTM {L : Language Bool} (h : L ∈ BPP_PTM) :
    InBPP polyTimeModel L :=
  inBPPWith_of_mem_BPP_PTMWith (p := fun _ => 2/3) h

/-! ### PTMs from certificate verifiers -/

/-- **Def 7.3 ⇒ Def 7.2, the machine structure**: a polynomial-time verifier `M` with
`polyLen a k` random bits is simulated by a PTM running in time `K·(n^e + 1)` whose output on a
coin word `w` is `[M(x, u)]`, `u` the projection of the slice `w[s, s + |mask|)` onto the
`polyLen a k |x|` marked positions of `mask` (so `|u| = polyLen a k |x|`).

**Proof sketch.** Let `V = {y | y = x ++ u, |u| = a(|x|+1)^k, ⟨x, u⟩ ∈ V₁} ∈ P`, recovered by
`computesFunInTime_splitSolve`; `exists_maskSelect_host` gives a PTM whose verdict is `V(x ++ u)`
with `u` such a projection. -/
theorem exists_FinNDTM_maskSelect_of_eff {M : List Bool → List Bool → Bool} {a k : ℕ}
    (hM : polyTimeModel.Eff (boolVerifier M)) :
    ∃ (K e : ℕ) (N : FinNDTM Bool), ∀ x : List Bool, ∃ (s : ℕ) (mask : List Bool),
      (mask.filter id).length = polyLen a k x.length ∧
      s + mask.length ≤ K * (x.length ^ e + 1) ∧
      ∀ w : List Bool, w.length = K * (x.length ^ e + 1) →
        (N.tm.runWith w (N.tm.initCfg x)).state = none ∧
        N.outputWith x w = [M x (maskSelect mask ((w.drop s).take mask.length))] ∧
        (maskSelect mask ((w.drop s).take mask.length)).length = polyLen a k x.length := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨V₁, V₀, hV₁, -, hMV⟩ := hM
  let sp : List Bool → List Bool := fun w => match solveSplit a k w.length with
    | some i => Turing.pairEncode (w.take i) (w.drop i)
    | none => []
  have hsp : PolyTimeComputable sp := by
    obtain ⟨S, c, hS⟩ := FinTM.computesFunInTime_splitSolve a k
    exact ⟨S, c, k + 2, hS⟩
  have hVP : sp ⁻¹' V₁ ∈ P := preimage_mem_P hV₁ hsp
  have hsplit : ∀ x u : List Bool, u.length = polyLen a k x.length →
      MultiTapeTM.indicator (sp ⁻¹' V₁) (x ++ u) = M x u := by
    intro x u hu
    have hs : sp (x ++ u) = Turing.pairEncode x u := by
      simp only [sp, List.length_append, hu, polyLen, Meyer.solveSplit_self', List.take_left',
        List.drop_left']
    have hiff : M x u = true ↔ Turing.pairEncode x u ∈ V₁ := by
      simpa only [boolVerifier, Option.some.injEq] using (hMV x u).1
    cases hb : M x u
    · have : x ++ u ∉ sp ⁻¹' V₁ := by
        rw [Set.mem_preimage, hs, ← hiff, hb]
        decide
      simp [MultiTapeTM.indicator, this]
    · have : x ++ u ∈ sp ⁻¹' V₁ := by rw [Set.mem_preimage, hs, ← hiff, hb]
      simp [MultiTapeTM.indicator, this]
  obtain ⟨K, e, N, hN⟩ := exists_maskSelect_host (sp ⁻¹' V₁) hVP a k
  refine ⟨K, e, N, fun x => ?_⟩
  obtain ⟨s, mask, hcount, hle, hrun⟩ := hN x
  have hsel : ∀ w : List Bool, w.length = K * (x.length ^ e + 1) →
      (maskSelect mask ((w.drop s).take mask.length)).length = polyLen a k x.length := by
    intro w hw
    rw [length_maskSelect _ _ (List.length_take_of_le (by rw [List.length_drop]; omega)),
      hcount]
    rfl
  refine ⟨s, mask, hcount, hle, fun w hw => ⟨(hrun w hw).1, ?_, hsel w hw⟩⟩
  rw [FinNDTM.outputWith, (hrun w hw).2, hsplit x _ (hsel w hw)]

/-- **Def 7.3 ⇒ Def 7.2, the machine**: a polynomial-time verifier `M` with `polyLen a k`
random bits is simulated by a PTM running in time `K·(n^e + 1)` whose output on every branch
is `[M(x, u)]` for a `polyLen a k |x|`-bit word `u`, and whose output distribution is that of
`M(x, ·)`.

**Proof sketch.** The machine of `exists_FinNDTM_maskSelect_of_eff`; a coordinate projection of
a slice of uniform coins is uniform (`randProb_maskSelect_drop_take`). -/
theorem exists_FinNDTM_of_eff {M : List Bool → List Bool → Bool} {a k : ℕ}
    (hM : polyTimeModel.Eff (boolVerifier M)) :
    ∃ (K e : ℕ) (N : FinNDTM Bool), ∀ x : List Bool,
      N.tm.HaltsWithin x (K * (x.length ^ e + 1)) ∧
      (∀ b : Bool, N.outputProb x (K * (x.length ^ e + 1)) [b] =
        randProb (polyLen a k x.length) fun u => M x u = b) ∧
      ∀ w : List Bool, w.length = K * (x.length ^ e + 1) →
        ∃ r : Fin (polyLen a k x.length) → Bool, N.outputWith x w = [M x (List.ofFn r)] := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨K, e, N, hN⟩ := exists_FinNDTM_maskSelect_of_eff (a := a) (k := k) hM
  refine ⟨K, e, N, fun x => ?_⟩
  obtain ⟨s, mask, hcount, hle, hrun⟩ := hN x
  refine ⟨fun w hw => (hrun w hw).1, fun b => ?_, fun w hw => ?_⟩
  · unfold FinNDTM.outputProb
    rw [randProb_congr (B := fun w => M x (maskSelect mask ((w.drop s).take mask.length)) = b)
      fun r => by rw [(hrun _ List.length_ofFn).2.1, List.singleton_inj]]
    refine (randProb_maskSelect_drop_take mask hle (fun u => M x u = b)).trans ?_
    rw [hcount]
  · obtain ⟨r, hr⟩ := exists_ofFn_eq (hrun w hw).2.2
    exact ⟨r, by rw [(hrun w hw).2.1, hr]⟩

/-- **Def 7.3 ⇒ Def 7.2 at threshold `p`.** [AB09, p. 126] -/
theorem mem_BPP_PTMWith_of_inBPPWith {p : ℕ → ℚ} {L : Language Bool}
    (h : InBPPWith p L) : L ∈ BPP_PTMWith p := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨M, a, k, hM, hL⟩ := h
  obtain ⟨K, e, N, hN⟩ := exists_FinNDTM_of_eff (a := a) (k := k) hM
  refine Set.mem_iUnion.mpr ⟨e, K, N, fun x => ⟨(hN x).1, ?_⟩⟩
  rw [(hN x).2.1]
  by_cases hx : x ∈ L
  · simpa [MultiTapeTM.indicator, hx] using (hL x).1 hx
  · simpa [MultiTapeTM.indicator, hx] using (hL x).2 hx

/-- **PTM and certificate `BPP` agree at every threshold.** [AB09, Def 7.2 ≡ Def 7.3] -/
theorem mem_BPP_PTMWith_iff (p : ℕ → ℚ) (L : Language Bool) :
    L ∈ BPP_PTMWith p ↔ InBPPWith p L :=
  ⟨inBPPWith_of_mem_BPP_PTMWith, mem_BPP_PTMWith_of_inBPPWith⟩

/-- **Def 7.3 ⇒ Def 7.2** (`BPP`), the threshold-`2/3` case of
`mem_BPP_PTMWith_of_inBPPWith`. [AB09, p. 126] -/
theorem mem_BPP_PTM_of_inBPP {L : Language Bool} (h : InBPP polyTimeModel L) :
    L ∈ BPP_PTM :=
  mem_BPP_PTMWith_of_inBPPWith (p := fun _ => 2/3) h

/-- **[AB09, Def 7.2 ≡ Def 7.3]**: the PTM class `BPP` is the certificate class over
polynomial-time verifiers. -/
theorem mem_BPP_PTM_iff (L : Language Bool) : L ∈ BPP_PTM ↔ InBPP polyTimeModel L :=
  mem_BPP_PTMWith_iff (fun _ => 2/3) L

/-- `BPP_PTM` as a set of languages. -/
theorem BPP_PTM_eq : BPP_PTM = {L | InBPP polyTimeModel L} :=
  Set.ext mem_BPP_PTM_iff

end Randomized

/-! ### `RP` with a general acceptance threshold -/

namespace Turing.FinNDTM

/-- `N` decides `L` in time `T` with one-sided error and acceptance threshold `p(|x|)`: every
branch halts within `T(|x|)` steps, members are accepted with probability at least `p(|x|)`,
and on non-members every branch outputs `0`. The threshold `p` is meant to be positive (at
`p = 0` every language qualifies). [AB09, Def 7.6 and Ex 7.4] -/
def RDecidesInTimeWith (N : FinNDTM Bool) (L : Language Bool) (T : ℕ → ℕ) (p : ℕ → ℚ) :
    Prop :=
  ∀ x : List Bool, N.tm.HaltsWithin x (T x.length) ∧
    (x ∈ L → p x.length ≤ N.outputProb x (T x.length) [true]) ∧
    (x ∉ L → ∀ w : List Bool, w.length = T x.length → N.outputWith x w = [false])

/-- `RDecidesInTime` is the threshold-`2/3` case. -/
theorem rDecidesInTime_iff {N : FinNDTM Bool} {L : Language Bool} {T : ℕ → ℕ} :
    N.RDecidesInTime L T ↔ N.RDecidesInTimeWith L T fun _ => 2/3 := Iff.rfl

end Turing.FinNDTM

namespace Randomized

open Complexity Turing

/-- `RP` with acceptance threshold `p(|x|)` (meant positive): one-sided-error PTMs in time
`K·(n^e + 1)`. [AB09, Ex 7.4] -/
def RP_PTMWith (p : ℕ → ℚ) : Set (Language Bool) :=
  ⋃ e : ℕ, {L | ∃ (K : ℕ) (N : FinNDTM Bool),
    N.RDecidesInTimeWith L (fun n => K * (n ^ e + 1)) p}

/-- `RP_PTM` is the threshold-`2/3` case. -/
theorem RP_PTM_eq_RP_PTMWith : RP_PTM = RP_PTMWith fun _ => 2/3 := rfl

/-- The certificate form of `RP_PTMWith p` over polynomial-time verifiers. -/
def InRPWith (p : ℕ → ℚ) (L : Language Bool) : Prop :=
  ∃ (M : List Bool → List Bool → Bool) (a k : ℕ),
    polyTimeModel.Eff (boolVerifier M) ∧
    ∀ x : List Bool,
      (x ∈ L → p x.length ≤ randProb (polyLen a k x.length) fun r => M x r = true) ∧
      (x ∉ L → ∀ r : Fin (polyLen a k x.length) → Bool, M x (List.ofFn r) = false)

/-- **PTM and certificate `RP` agree at every threshold.** [AB09, Def 7.6, p. 131]

**Proof sketch.** Forward as `inBPPWith_of_mem_BPP_PTMWith`; a non-member's coin word outputs
`[false]` under its first `T` coins, so the verifier rejects it.  Backward by
`exists_FinNDTM_of_eff`: every branch outputs `[M(x, u)]` for some `polyLen a k |x|`-bit `u`,
which is `0` on non-members, and the acceptance probabilities agree. -/
theorem mem_RP_PTMWith_iff (p : ℕ → ℚ) (L : Language Bool) :
    L ∈ RP_PTMWith p ↔ InRPWith p L := by
  classical
  constructor
  · intro h
    obtain ⟨e, c, N, hN⟩ := Set.mem_iUnion.mp h
    obtain ⟨V, hVP, hV⟩ := exists_choiceVerifier_mem_P N (2 * c) e
    refine ⟨fun x r => MultiTapeTM.indicator V (x ++ r), 2 * c, e, eff_append_mem hVP, fun x => ?_⟩
    obtain ⟨hhalt, hin, hout⟩ := hN x
    have hTQ : c * (x.length ^ e + 1) ≤ polyLen (2 * c) e x.length := choiceBudget_le c e _
    have hVx : ∀ u : List Bool, u.length = polyLen (2 * c) e x.length → _ := fun u => hV x u
    refine ⟨fun hx => le_of_le_of_eq (hin hx) (randProb_choiceVerifier hVx hhalt hTQ).symm,
      fun hx r => ?_⟩
    rw [indicator_eq_false_iff, append_mem_iff_outputWith_take hVx hhalt hTQ _ List.length_ofFn,
      hout hx _ (List.length_take_of_le (by rw [List.length_ofFn]; exact hTQ))]
    decide
  · rintro ⟨M, a, k, hM, hL⟩
    obtain ⟨K, e, N, hN⟩ := exists_FinNDTM_of_eff (a := a) (k := k) hM
    refine Set.mem_iUnion.mpr ⟨e, K, N, fun x => ⟨(hN x).1, fun hx => ?_, fun hx w hw => ?_⟩⟩
    · rw [(hN x).2.1]
      exact (hL x).1 hx
    · obtain ⟨r, hr⟩ := (hN x).2.2 w hw
      rw [hr, (hL x).2 hx r]

/-- **[AB09, Def 7.6]**: the PTM class `RP` is the certificate class over polynomial-time
verifiers. -/
theorem mem_RP_PTM_iff (L : Language Bool) : L ∈ RP_PTM ↔ InRP polyTimeModel L := by
  rw [RP_PTM_eq_RP_PTMWith]
  exact mem_RP_PTMWith_iff _ L

/-- **[AB09, §7.3]**: the PTM class `coRP` is the certificate class over polynomial-time
verifiers. -/
theorem mem_coRP_PTM_iff (L : Language Bool) : L ∈ coRP_PTM ↔ InCoRP polyTimeModel L :=
  mem_RP_PTM_iff Lᶜ

/-! ### PTM-form corollaries -/

/-- **`BPP ⊆ EXP`** (PTM form). [AB09, p. 126] -/
theorem BPP_PTM_subset_EXP : BPP_PTM ⊆ EXP := fun _ h =>
  mem_EXP_of_inBPP_polyTimeModel (inBPP_of_mem_BPP_PTM h)

/-- **`P = NP ⇒ BPP = P`** (PTM form). [AB09, p. 135 and p. 140] -/
theorem BPP_PTM_eq_P_of_P_eq_NP (h : P = NP) : BPP_PTM = P :=
  Set.ext fun L => (mem_BPP_PTM_iff L).trans (inBPP_polyTimeModel_iff_mem_P_of_P_eq_NP h L)

/-- **Adleman: `BPP ⊆ P/poly`** (PTM form). [AB09, Thm 7.14] -/
theorem BPP_PTM_subset_PPoly : BPP_PTM ⊆ BoolCircuit.PPoly := fun L h =>
  (BoolCircuit.mem_PPoly_iff L).mpr (adleman_polyTime (inBPP_of_mem_BPP_PTM h))

/-- **Sipser–Gács: `BPP ⊆ Σ₂ᵖ ∩ Π₂ᵖ`** (PTM form). [AB09, Thm 7.15] -/
theorem BPP_PTM_subset_SigmaP_two_inter_PiP_two : BPP_PTM ⊆ SigmaP 2 ∩ PiP 2 := fun _ h =>
  sipser_gacs_polyTime (inBPP_of_mem_BPP_PTM h)

/-- **`BPP` is closed under `≤ₚ`** (PTM form). -/
theorem BPP_PTM_of_polyTimeReducible {L L' : Language Bool} (hred : L' ≤ₚ L)
    (h : L ∈ BPP_PTM) : L' ∈ BPP_PTM :=
  mem_BPP_PTM_of_inBPP (InBPP.of_polyTimeReducible hred (inBPP_of_mem_BPP_PTM h))

/-- **`3SAT ∈ BPP ⇒ PH = Σ₂ᵖ`** (PTM form). [AB09, p. 135] -/
theorem PH_eq_SigmaP_two_of_SAT3_mem_BPP_PTM (h : SAT3 ∈ BPP_PTM) : PH = SigmaP 2 :=
  PH_eq_SigmaP_two_of_inBPP_SAT3 (inBPP_of_mem_BPP_PTM h)

/-- **Error reduction for `RP`** (PTM form, [AB09, Ex 7.4]): a polynomial-time PTM accepting
members with probability `min (2/3) ((|x|+1)^{-c})` yields one accepting them with probability
`1 − 2^{-((|x|+1)^d + 1)}`. -/
theorem RP_PTMWith_error_reduction (c d : ℕ) :
    RP_PTMWith (fun n => min (2/3) (((n + 1 : ℚ) ^ c)⁻¹)) ⊆
      RP_PTMWith fun n => 1 - (1/2 : ℚ) ^ ((n + 1) ^ d + 1) := fun L h =>
  (mem_RP_PTMWith_iff _ L).mpr
    (rp_error_reduction_polyTime (c := c) ((mem_RP_PTMWith_iff _ L).mp h) d)

end Randomized

import TCSlib.Complexity.ClassNP.PolyTimePairing

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Syntactic polynomials for lengths and budgets

Every length or budget of the Pass–shelat campaign that depends on the security parameter
`n` — the number of coins and of advice bits of a machine, the input and output lengths of
function families and ensembles, the stretch of a generator, query and round budgets,
auxiliary-input bounds — is a *syntactic* polynomial expression `Complexity.PolyExpr`
(constants, the variable, sums, products, powers), never an abstract function `ℕ → ℕ`
with a bound. This is foundation decision D9 of `PassShelatChapter2-4Plan.md`: an abstract
length function can smuggle undecidable information through length arithmetic (the audit
lesson recorded in `TCSlib.Complexity.ClassNP.NP`), while a syntactic expression is
evaluated, substituted, bounded and computed in unary by structural recursion.

Time bounds of machines stay in the normal form `C * (n + 1) ^ c` of
`Complexity.PolyTimeComputable`; `PolyExpr.normal C c` is that normal form as an
expression, and `PolyExpr.eval_le` shows that every expression is majorised by one.

The unary evaluator `x ↦ 1^{p(|x|)}` (`Complexity.polyTimeComputable_unaryPoly`) lives in
`TCSlib.Complexity.Randomized.Primitives`, next to the unary-multiplication machine its
`mul` case needs; the normal-form instance `Complexity.polyTimeComputable_unaryNormal` is
proved here from the library's `Complexity.polyTimeComputable_polyUnary`.

## Main definitions

* `Complexity.PolyExpr` — syntactic polynomial expressions in the parameter `n`.
* `Complexity.PolyExpr.eval` — evaluation at a parameter.
* `Complexity.PolyExpr.subst` — substitution `p[q/n]` (parameter changes `n ↦ q(n)`).
* `Complexity.PolyExpr.normal` — the normal form `C * (n + 1) ^ c` as an expression.

## Main results

* `Complexity.PolyExpr.eval_subst` — evaluation commutes with substitution.
* `Complexity.PolyExpr.eval_mono` — evaluation is monotone in the parameter.
* `Complexity.PolyExpr.eval_le`, `Complexity.PolyExpr.polyBound_eval` — every expression is
  bounded by a normal form `C * (n + 1) ^ c` (the bridge to `Complexity.PolyBound`).
* `Complexity.polyTimeComputable_unaryNormal` — `x ↦ 1^{C(|x|+1)^c}` is polynomial-time
  computable (the normal-form case of the unary evaluator).

## References

* [PS10] R. Pass, a. shelat, *A Course in Cryptography*, lecture notes, 3rd ed., January 2010.
  (§2.1: polynomials `p(n)` as running-time, coin and advice bounds.)
* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§2.2, the function class FP.)
-/

namespace Complexity

open Turing

/-- Syntactic polynomial expressions in the security parameter `n`: every length of the
campaign (coins, advice, input/output lengths, query and round budgets) is one of these,
never an abstract `ℕ → ℕ`. `normal C c` is the campaign normal form `C * (n + 1) ^ c`.
[PS10, §2.1] writes such bounds as "a polynomial `p(n)`"; foundation decision D9 of
`PassShelatChapter2-4Plan.md` fixes the syntactic representation.

Cost of D9: an expression is a polynomial with natural-number coefficients and no
subtraction, so lengths such as `n − 1`, `⌊n/2⌋`, `n(n − 1)/2` or `⌈log₂ n⌉` are not
expressible. A consumer pads to a `PolyExpr` majorant or reparametrizes with
`Complexity.NUPPT.exists_reparam_advice` (an abstract `φ : ℕ → ℕ` with a `PolyExpr`
majorant, the one place such a function appears). -/
inductive PolyExpr : Type
  | const : ℕ → PolyExpr
  | var : PolyExpr
  | add : PolyExpr → PolyExpr → PolyExpr
  | mul : PolyExpr → PolyExpr → PolyExpr
  | pow : PolyExpr → ℕ → PolyExpr
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr

namespace PolyExpr

/-- Evaluation of a syntactic polynomial at the parameter `n`, by structural recursion.

Evaluation is notation (user ruling 2026-11-07, Q1, extending R-04-4): consumers may read typed
lengths such as `Fin ((add p q).eval n)` as `Fin (p.eval n + q.eval n)`. It is kept
semireducible: with `@[reducible]` on this structurally recursive definition `simp` no longer
finds the `eval_*` lemmas (gate 07 record). -/
def eval : PolyExpr → ℕ → ℕ
  | const c, _ => c
  | var, n => n
  | add p q, n => p.eval n + q.eval n
  | mul p q, n => p.eval n * q.eval n
  | pow p c, n => (p.eval n) ^ c

/-- Substitution `p[q/n]`: the expression `p` with every occurrence of the variable
replaced by `q` (parameter changes `n ↦ q(n)`, e.g. the coin polynomial of a machine run
at parameter `p(n)` is `coins.subst p`). -/
def subst : PolyExpr → PolyExpr → PolyExpr
  | const c, _ => const c
  | var, q => q
  | add p p', q => add (p.subst q) (p'.subst q)
  | mul p p', q => mul (p.subst q) (p'.subst q)
  | pow p c, q => pow (p.subst q) c

/-- The campaign normal form `C * (n + 1) ^ c` as a syntactic polynomial: the shape of the
time bounds of `Complexity.PolyTimeComputable`. -/
def normal (C c : ℕ) : PolyExpr := mul (const C) (pow (add var (const 1)) c)

/-- Evaluating a constant. -/
@[simp] theorem eval_const (c n : ℕ) : (const c).eval n = c := rfl

/-- Evaluating the variable. -/
@[simp] theorem eval_var (n : ℕ) : var.eval n = n := rfl

/-- Evaluating a sum. -/
@[simp] theorem eval_add (p q : PolyExpr) (n : ℕ) : (add p q).eval n = p.eval n + q.eval n := rfl

/-- Evaluating a product. -/
@[simp] theorem eval_mul (p q : PolyExpr) (n : ℕ) : (mul p q).eval n = p.eval n * q.eval n := rfl

/-- Evaluating a power. -/
@[simp] theorem eval_pow (p : PolyExpr) (c n : ℕ) : (pow p c).eval n = (p.eval n) ^ c := rfl

/-- The normal form evaluates to `C * (n + 1) ^ c`. -/
theorem eval_normal (C c n : ℕ) : (normal C c).eval n = C * (n + 1) ^ c := rfl

/-- Evaluation commutes with substitution: `(p[q/n])(n) = p(q(n))`. -/
theorem eval_subst (p q : PolyExpr) (n : ℕ) : (p.subst q).eval n = p.eval (q.eval n) := by
  induction p <;> simp_all [subst, eval]

/-- Substituting the variable itself is the identity. -/
theorem subst_var (p : PolyExpr) : p.subst var = p := by
  induction p <;> simp_all [subst]

/-- Evaluation is monotone in the parameter (every coefficient is a natural number). -/
theorem eval_mono (p : PolyExpr) : Monotone p.eval := by
  induction p with
  | const k => intro a b _; exact le_rfl
  | var => intro a b h; exact h
  | add p q hp hq => intro a b h; exact Nat.add_le_add (hp h) (hq h)
  | mul p q hp hq => intro a b h; exact Nat.mul_le_mul (hp h) (hq h)
  | pow p k hp => intro a b h; exact Nat.pow_le_pow_left (hp h) k

/-- Every expression is bounded by a normal form `C * (n + 1) ^ c`: the bridge from syntactic
polynomials to the time bounds of `Complexity.PolyTimeComputable` and to
`Complexity.PolyBound`.

**Proof sketch.** Induction on `p`. Constants and the variable are their own majorants
(`k * (n+1)^0`, `1 * (n+1)^1`). For a sum, raise both degrees to their maximum
(`Nat.pow_le_pow_right`) and add the coefficients; for a product, multiply the coefficients
and add the degrees; for a power, raise the coefficient and multiply the degree
(`Nat.pow_le_pow_left`, `mul_pow`, `pow_mul`). -/
theorem eval_le (p : PolyExpr) : ∃ C c : ℕ, ∀ n, p.eval n ≤ C * (n + 1) ^ c := by
  induction p with
  | const k => exact ⟨k, 0, fun n => by simp⟩
  | var => exact ⟨1, 1, fun n => by simp⟩
  | add p q hp hq =>
    obtain ⟨C₁, c₁, h₁⟩ := hp
    obtain ⟨C₂, c₂, h₂⟩ := hq
    refine ⟨C₁ + C₂, max c₁ c₂, fun n => ?_⟩
    have e1 : (n + 1) ^ c₁ ≤ (n + 1) ^ (max c₁ c₂) :=
      Nat.pow_le_pow_right (Nat.succ_pos n) (le_max_left _ _)
    have e2 : (n + 1) ^ c₂ ≤ (n + 1) ^ (max c₁ c₂) :=
      Nat.pow_le_pow_right (Nat.succ_pos n) (le_max_right _ _)
    calc (add p q).eval n = p.eval n + q.eval n := rfl
      _ ≤ C₁ * (n + 1) ^ c₁ + C₂ * (n + 1) ^ c₂ := Nat.add_le_add (h₁ n) (h₂ n)
      _ ≤ C₁ * (n + 1) ^ (max c₁ c₂) + C₂ * (n + 1) ^ (max c₁ c₂) :=
          Nat.add_le_add (Nat.mul_le_mul_left _ e1) (Nat.mul_le_mul_left _ e2)
      _ = (C₁ + C₂) * (n + 1) ^ (max c₁ c₂) := by ring
  | mul p q hp hq =>
    obtain ⟨C₁, c₁, h₁⟩ := hp
    obtain ⟨C₂, c₂, h₂⟩ := hq
    refine ⟨C₁ * C₂, c₁ + c₂, fun n => ?_⟩
    calc (mul p q).eval n = p.eval n * q.eval n := rfl
      _ ≤ (C₁ * (n + 1) ^ c₁) * (C₂ * (n + 1) ^ c₂) := Nat.mul_le_mul (h₁ n) (h₂ n)
      _ = (C₁ * C₂) * (n + 1) ^ (c₁ + c₂) := by ring
  | pow p k hp =>
    obtain ⟨C, c, h⟩ := hp
    refine ⟨C ^ k, c * k, fun n => ?_⟩
    calc (pow p k).eval n = (p.eval n) ^ k := rfl
      _ ≤ (C * (n + 1) ^ c) ^ k := Nat.pow_le_pow_left (h n) k
      _ = C ^ k * (n + 1) ^ (c * k) := by rw [mul_pow, ← pow_mul]

/-- The evaluation of a syntactic polynomial is a `Complexity.PolyBound` (the library's
numerical majorant predicate), by `eval_le`. -/
theorem polyBound_eval (p : PolyExpr) : PolyBound p.eval := p.eval_le

/-- A syntactic polynomial is bounded by its own normal-form majorant *as an expression*:
there are `C, c` with `p.eval n ≤ (normal C c).eval n` for every `n`. -/
theorem exists_normal_ge (p : PolyExpr) : ∃ C c : ℕ, ∀ n, p.eval n ≤ (normal C c).eval n := by
  obtain ⟨C, c, h⟩ := p.eval_le
  exact ⟨C, c, fun n => by rw [eval_normal]; exact h n⟩

end PolyExpr

/-- The unary evaluator of a normal form is polynomial-time: `x ↦ 1^{C(|x|+1)^c}`, i.e.
`x ↦ 1^{(normal C c)(|x|)}`, is polynomial-time computable (the library's
`Complexity.polyTimeComputable_polyUnary`, restated on `PolyExpr.normal`). This is the
case of `Complexity.polyTimeComputable_unaryPoly` that needs no unary multiplication. -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_unaryNormal (C c : ℕ) :
    PolyTimeComputable fun x => List.replicate ((PolyExpr.normal C c).eval x.length) true :=
  polyTimeComputable_polyUnary C c

end Complexity

/-
