import TCSlib.Complexity.Randomized.SipserGacs
import TCSlib.Complexity.Randomized.Adleman
import TCSlib.Complexity.ClassP.P
import TCSlib.Complexity.ClassNP.PolyTimePrefix
import TCSlib.Complexity.CircuitComplexity.PSubsetPPoly
import TCSlib.Complexity.CircuitComplexity.PairEncode
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Encoding
import TCSlib.Complexity.PolyHierarchy.Defs
import TCSlib.Complexity.PolyHierarchy.Normalize
import TCSlib.Complexity.PolyHierarchy.Collapse

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# The polynomial-time verifier model

The instantiation of `Randomized.VerifierModel` by genuine polynomial-time
Turing machines, now that the Chapter 1–2 development (`Complexity.P`,
`Complexity.PolyTimeComputable`, `Turing.pairEncode`, `Complexity.SigmaP`)
is on `main`.  This connects the abstract Chapter 7 class theorems to the
book's machine-based statements: each `ClosedUnder…` hypothesis becomes a
a result about `P`, and the certificate-style `Σ₂` coincides with
`Complexity.SigmaP 2`.

## Main definitions

* `Randomized.polyTimeModel` — the `VerifierModel` whose efficient verifiers
  are those computed by a `P`-language on the `Turing.pairEncode`d input.

## Main results

* `Randomized.polyTimeModel_closedUnderRace` /
  `…_closedUnderAnswerIs` / `…_closedUnderMajority` / `…_closedUnderAny` /
  `…_closedUnderNot` / `…_closedUnderShiftOr` — the closure hypotheses of
  `Randomized.Classes` and `Randomized.SipserGacs` hold for polynomial time.
* `Randomized.inSigma2_polyTimeModel_iff` — certificate-style `Σ₂` for the
  poly-time model coincides with `Complexity.SigmaP 2`.
* `Randomized.zpp_eq_rp_inter_corp_polyTime`,
  `Randomized.sipser_gacs_polyTime` — [AB09, Thm 7.8] and [AB09, Thm 7.15]
  for polynomial-time machines, with no abstract hypotheses.

## Deviations from the source

None beyond those of `Randomized.Classes`: these declarations *discharge*
the deviations by instantiating the abstract model.  With the library's
`Complexity.P_subset_PPoly` ([AB09, Thm 6.6]) now available, Adleman's
circuit hypothesis is dischargeable too
(`Randomized.polyTimeModel_verifierHasCircuits`), so [AB09, Thm 7.14] is
stated unconditionally as `Randomized.adleman_polyTime`.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009.
-/

namespace Randomized

open Complexity

/-- The polynomial-time verifier model: a verifier is *efficient* when its
output is computed by `P`-languages on the `Turing.pairEncode`d pair of
input and random string (`some true`-set and `some false`-set each in `P`),
and a two-witness predicate is efficient when its truth set, on the nested
pairing used by `Complexity.SigmaP`, is in `P`.  This is "`M` is a
polynomial-time TM" of [AB09, Def 7.3], in the library's encoding
conventions. -/
noncomputable def polyTimeModel : VerifierModel where
  Eff M := ∃ V₁ V₀ : Language Bool, V₁ ∈ P ∧ V₀ ∈ P ∧
    ∀ x r : List Bool,
      (M x r = some true ↔ Turing.pairEncode x r ∈ V₁) ∧
      (M x r = some false ↔ Turing.pairEncode x r ∈ V₀)
  EffTwoWitness N := ∃ V : Language Bool, V ∈ P ∧
    ∀ x u v : List Bool,
      (N x u v = true ↔ Turing.pairEncode (Turing.pairEncode x u) v ∈ V)

/-- A verifier is efficient in the polynomial-time model exactly when its `some true` and
`some false` sets, on encoded input/random-string pairs, are languages in `P`. -/
theorem polyTimeModel_eff_iff (M : List Bool → List Bool → Option Bool) :
    polyTimeModel.Eff M ↔
      ∃ V₁ V₀ : Language Bool, V₁ ∈ P ∧ V₀ ∈ P ∧
        ∀ x r : List Bool,
          (M x r = some true ↔ Turing.pairEncode x r ∈ V₁) ∧
          (M x r = some false ↔ Turing.pairEncode x r ∈ V₀) := Iff.rfl

/-- Keep the input `x` and the first `polyLen a k |x|` bits of the random
string: the pair-level reindexing behind the race and shifted constructions.
On `Turing.pairEncode x r` it returns `Turing.pairEncode x (r.take (polyLen a k |x|))`. -/
def sliceTake (a k : ℕ) (z : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  Turing.pairEncode (pairFstD z) ((pairSndD z).take (polyLen a k (pairFstD z).length))

/-- Keep the input `x` and drop the first `polyLen a k |x|` bits of the random
string.  On `Turing.pairEncode x r` it returns
`Turing.pairEncode x (r.drop (polyLen a k |x|))`. -/
def sliceDrop (a k : ℕ) (z : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  Turing.pairEncode (pairFstD z) ((pairSndD z).drop (polyLen a k (pairFstD z).length))

/-- Take, from the second component of a pair, a prefix as long as the first
component: on `Turing.pairEncode u s` it returns `s.take |u|`.  The
length-gated prefix primitive underlying `sliceTake` (and the block slicing of
the shifted construction); the polynomial `polyLen a k` enters only through the
unary length `u`, so no in-machine exponentiation is needed. -/
def takePrefixByLen (p : List Bool) : List Bool := (pairSndD p).take (pairFstD p).length

/-- Drop, from the second component of a pair, a prefix as long as the first
component: on `Turing.pairEncode u s` it returns `s.drop |u|`. -/
def dropPrefixByLen (p : List Bool) : List Bool := (pairSndD p).drop (pairFstD p).length

/-- `takePrefixByLen` is polynomial-time computable.
**Proof sketch.** A single left-to-right pass (`Complexity.CounterProg`):
mirror `Turing.pairDecode` over the doubled first component, counting its
length `|u|` into a register; at the separator, copy the second component
while the register counts down, truncating once it reaches zero.  Malformed
inputs (`pairDecode = none`) halt with empty output, matching
`pairFstD`/`pairSndD = []`.  The abstract step count is linear in `|p|`, so
`Complexity.CounterProg.polyTimeComputable` applies. -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_takePrefixByLen : PolyTimeComputable takePrefixByLen := by
  simpa only [takePrefixByLen, Complexity.PrefixByLength.take] using
    Complexity.polyTimeComputable_takePrefixByLength

/-- `dropPrefixByLen` is polynomial-time computable.
**Proof sketch.** As `takePrefixByLen`, but the copy phase emits only after the
length register has counted down past the first `|u|` bits of the second
component. -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_dropPrefixByLen : PolyTimeComputable dropPrefixByLen := by
  simpa only [dropPrefixByLen, Complexity.PrefixByLength.drop] using
    Complexity.polyTimeComputable_dropPrefixByLength

/-- `sliceTake a k` is polynomial-time computable.
**Proof.** `polyLen a k |x| = a·(|x|+1)^k` is available as a *unary* string via
`Complexity.polyTimeComputable_polyUnary`; pair it with the random string and
apply `takePrefixByLen`, which truncates to that length without any in-machine
exponentiation. -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_sliceTake (a k : ℕ) :
    PolyTimeComputable (sliceTake a k) := by
  have hu : PolyTimeComputable
      (fun z => List.replicate (polyLen a k (pairFstD z).length) true) :=
    (polyTimeComputable_polyUnary a k).comp polyTimeComputable_pairFstD
  have henc : PolyTimeComputable (fun z => Turing.pairEncode
      (List.replicate (polyLen a k (pairFstD z).length) true) (pairSndD z)) :=
    PolyTimeComputable.pairEncode hu polyTimeComputable_pairSndD
  have hg : PolyTimeComputable
      (fun z => (pairSndD z).take (polyLen a k (pairFstD z).length)) := by
    have heq : (fun z => (pairSndD z).take (polyLen a k (pairFstD z).length)) =
        takePrefixByLen ∘ (fun z => Turing.pairEncode
          (List.replicate (polyLen a k (pairFstD z).length) true) (pairSndD z)) := by
      funext z
      simp only [Function.comp, takePrefixByLen, pairFstD_pairEncode, pairSndD_pairEncode,
        List.length_replicate]
    rw [heq]
    exact polyTimeComputable_takePrefixByLen.comp henc
  exact PolyTimeComputable.pairEncode polyTimeComputable_pairFstD hg

/-- `sliceDrop a k` is polynomial-time computable.
**Proof.** As `sliceTake`, with `dropPrefixByLen` in place of
`takePrefixByLen`. -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_sliceDrop (a k : ℕ) :
    PolyTimeComputable (sliceDrop a k) := by
  have hu : PolyTimeComputable
      (fun z => List.replicate (polyLen a k (pairFstD z).length) true) :=
    (polyTimeComputable_polyUnary a k).comp polyTimeComputable_pairFstD
  have henc : PolyTimeComputable (fun z => Turing.pairEncode
      (List.replicate (polyLen a k (pairFstD z).length) true) (pairSndD z)) :=
    PolyTimeComputable.pairEncode hu polyTimeComputable_pairSndD
  have hg : PolyTimeComputable
      (fun z => (pairSndD z).drop (polyLen a k (pairFstD z).length)) := by
    have heq : (fun z => (pairSndD z).drop (polyLen a k (pairFstD z).length)) =
        dropPrefixByLen ∘ (fun z => Turing.pairEncode
          (List.replicate (polyLen a k (pairFstD z).length) true) (pairSndD z)) := by
      funext z
      simp only [Function.comp, dropPrefixByLen, pairFstD_pairEncode, pairSndD_pairEncode,
        List.length_replicate]
    rw [heq]
    exact polyTimeComputable_dropPrefixByLen.comp henc
  exact PolyTimeComputable.pairEncode polyTimeComputable_pairFstD hg

/-- Polynomial time is closed under the race construction.
**Proof sketch.** The `some true`-set of the race is the preimage of `M₁`'s
`some true`-set `V₁` under `sliceTake a k`, and the `some false`-set is the
intersection of the complement of that preimage with the preimage of `M₂`'s
`some true`-set `V₂` under `sliceDrop a k`; both are in `P` by
`Complexity.preimage_mem_P`, `Complexity.compl_mem_P`, and
`Complexity.inter_mem_P`, once `sliceTake`/`sliceDrop` are polynomial-time
(`polyTimeComputable_sliceTake`/`_sliceDrop`).  The off-pair freedom in the
efficiency notion lets us use these preimages verbatim. -/
theorem polyTimeModel_closedUnderRace : ClosedUnderRace polyTimeModel := by
  rintro M₁ M₂ a k ⟨V₁, _, hV₁, _, hM₁⟩ ⟨V₂, _, hV₂, _, hM₂⟩
  refine ⟨sliceTake a k ⁻¹' V₁,
    {z | z ∈ (sliceTake a k ⁻¹' V₁)ᶜ ∧ z ∈ sliceDrop a k ⁻¹' V₂},
    preimage_mem_P hV₁ (polyTimeComputable_sliceTake a k),
    inter_mem_P (compl_mem_P (preimage_mem_P hV₁ (polyTimeComputable_sliceTake a k)))
      (preimage_mem_P hV₂ (polyTimeComputable_sliceDrop a k)),
    fun x r => ?_⟩
  have hv1 : (Turing.pairEncode x r ∈ sliceTake a k ⁻¹' V₁) ↔
      M₁ x (r.take (polyLen a k x.length)) = true := by
    simp only [Set.mem_preimage, sliceTake, pairFstD_pairEncode, pairSndD_pairEncode]
    have h := (hM₁ x (r.take (polyLen a k x.length))).1
    simp only [boolVerifier, Option.some.injEq] at h
    exact h.symm
  have hv2 : (Turing.pairEncode x r ∈ sliceDrop a k ⁻¹' V₂) ↔
      M₂ x (r.drop (polyLen a k x.length)) = true := by
    simp only [Set.mem_preimage, sliceDrop, pairFstD_pairEncode, pairSndD_pairEncode]
    have h := (hM₂ x (r.drop (polyLen a k x.length))).1
    simp only [boolVerifier, Option.some.injEq] at h
    exact h.symm
  refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
  · rw [hv1]
    cases h1 : M₁ x (r.take (polyLen a k x.length)) <;>
      cases h2 : M₂ x (r.drop (polyLen a k x.length)) <;>
      simp [raceVerifier, h1, h2]
  · rw [Set.mem_setOf_eq, Set.mem_compl_iff, hv1, hv2]
    cases h1 : M₁ x (r.take (polyLen a k x.length)) <;>
      cases h2 : M₂ x (r.drop (polyLen a k x.length)) <;>
      simp [raceVerifier, h1, h2]

/-- Polynomial time is closed under the output-postprocessing construction.
**Proof sketch.** The `some b`-set of `M` is literally one of the two
`P`-languages witnessing `Eff M`, and the `some (!b)`-set of the resulting
Boolean verifier is its complement (`Complexity.compl_mem_P`). -/
theorem polyTimeModel_closedUnderAnswerIs :
    ClosedUnderAnswerIs polyTimeModel := by
  rintro M b ⟨V₁, V₀, hV₁, hV₀, hM⟩
  cases b
  · refine ⟨V₀, V₀ᶜ, hV₀, compl_mem_P hV₀, fun x r => ?_⟩
    have h := (hM x r).2
    constructor
    · show some (decide (M x r = some false)) = some true ↔ _
      simp only [Option.some.injEq, decide_eq_true_eq]
      exact h
    · show some (decide (M x r = some false)) = some false ↔ _
      simp only [Option.some.injEq, decide_eq_false_iff_not]
      rw [h]
      exact Iff.rfl
  · refine ⟨V₁, V₁ᶜ, hV₁, compl_mem_P hV₁, fun x r => ?_⟩
    have h := (hM x r).1
    constructor
    · show some (decide (M x r = some true)) = some true ↔ _
      simp only [Option.some.injEq, decide_eq_true_eq]
      exact h
    · show some (decide (M x r = some true)) = some false ↔ _
      simp only [Option.some.injEq, decide_eq_false_iff_not]
      rw [h]
      exact Iff.rfl

/-- Polynomial time is closed under polynomial majority repetition.
**Proof sketch.** The `some true`-set of the majority verifier is exactly the
block-majority closure `Complexity.mem_P_of_blockMajority` at `M`'s
`some true`-language `V₁` (the vote over block `i` is the indicator of
`sliceTake`-style block `i`, by the efficiency witness), and the `some
false`-set is its complement (`Complexity.compl_mem_P`).  The off-pair
freedom in the efficiency notion lets us use these sets verbatim. -/
theorem polyTimeModel_closedUnderMajority :
    ClosedUnderMajority polyTimeModel := by
  classical
  rintro M a k a' k' ⟨V₁, _, hV₁, _, hM⟩
  have hblock := mem_P_of_blockMajority hV₁ a k a' k'
  refine ⟨_, _, hblock, compl_mem_P hblock, fun x r => ?_⟩
  have hMt : ∀ s : List Bool, M x s = true ↔ Turing.pairEncode x s ∈ V₁ := by
    intro s
    have h := (hM x s).1
    simpa only [boolVerifier, Option.some.injEq] using h
  have hcount : ∀ l : List ℕ,
      l.countP (fun i => Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator V₁
          (Turing.pairEncode x ((r.drop (i * (a * (x.length + 1) ^ k))).take
            (a * (x.length + 1) ^ k)))) =
        l.countP (fun i => M x ((r.drop (i * (a * (x.length + 1) ^ k))).take
          (a * (x.length + 1) ^ k))) := by
    intro l
    apply List.countP_congr
    intro i _
    have hi := hMt ((r.drop (i * (a * (x.length + 1) ^ k))).take (a * (x.length + 1) ^ k))
    by_cases hb : M x ((r.drop (i * (a * (x.length + 1) ^ k))).take
        (a * (x.length + 1) ^ k)) = true
    · simp [Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator, hi.mp hb, hb]
    · have hnot : Turing.pairEncode x ((r.drop (i * (a * (x.length + 1) ^ k))).take
          (a * (x.length + 1) ^ k)) ∉ V₁ := fun hc => hb (hi.mpr hc)
      simp [Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator, hnot, Bool.eq_false_iff.mpr hb]
  have hmem : Turing.pairEncode x r ∈
      {z : List Bool | a' * ((pairFstD z).length + 1) ^ k' <
        2 * (List.range (a' * ((pairFstD z).length + 1) ^ k')).countP
          (fun i => Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator V₁
            (Turing.pairEncode (pairFstD z) (blockAt a k z i)))} ↔
      majorityVerifier M (polyLen a k) (polyLen a' k') x r = true := by
    simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq, pairFstD_pairEncode, pairSndD_pairEncode,
      majorityVerifier, polyLen, blockAt, decide_eq_true_eq]
    rw [hcount]
  constructor
  · constructor
    · intro h
      exact hmem.mpr (by simpa only [boolVerifier, Option.some.injEq] using h)
    · intro hw
      exact congrArg some (hmem.mp hw)
  · constructor
    · intro h hw
      have ht := hmem.mp hw
      have hf : majorityVerifier M (polyLen a k) (polyLen a' k') x r = false := by
        simpa only [boolVerifier, Option.some.injEq] using h
      exact absurd (ht.symm.trans hf) (by decide)
    · intro hc
      cases hb : majorityVerifier M (polyLen a k) (polyLen a' k') x r with
      | false => exact congrArg some hb
      | true => exact absurd (hmem.mpr hb) (fun hw => hc hw)

/-- Polynomial time is closed under polynomial `OR`-repetition.
**Proof sketch.** As for the majority closure, via the block-OR closure
`Complexity.mem_P_of_blockAny`: the `some true`-set of the `OR`-verifier is
the set of pairs some of whose random blocks puts the re-paired input in
`M`'s `some true`-language, and the `some false`-set is its complement. -/
theorem polyTimeModel_closedUnderAny : ClosedUnderAny polyTimeModel := by
  classical
  rintro M a k a' k' ⟨V₁, _, hV₁, _, hM⟩
  have hblock := mem_P_of_blockAny hV₁ a k a' k'
  refine ⟨_, _, hblock, compl_mem_P hblock, fun x r => ?_⟩
  have hMt : ∀ s : List Bool, M x s = true ↔ Turing.pairEncode x s ∈ V₁ := by
    intro s
    have h := (hM x s).1
    simpa only [boolVerifier, Option.some.injEq] using h
  have hmem : Turing.pairEncode x r ∈
      {z : List Bool | ∃ i < a' * ((pairFstD z).length + 1) ^ k',
        Turing.pairEncode (pairFstD z) (blockAt a k z i) ∈ V₁} ↔
      anyVerifier M (polyLen a k) (polyLen a' k') x r = true := by
    simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq, pairFstD_pairEncode, pairSndD_pairEncode,
      anyVerifier, polyLen, blockAt, List.any_eq_true, List.mem_range]
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨i, hi, hv⟩
      exact ⟨i, hi, (hMt _).mpr hv⟩
    · rintro ⟨i, hi, hv⟩
      exact ⟨i, hi, (hMt _).mp hv⟩
  constructor
  · constructor
    · intro h
      exact hmem.mpr (by simpa only [boolVerifier, Option.some.injEq] using h)
    · intro hw
      exact congrArg some (hmem.mp hw)
  · constructor
    · intro h hw
      have ht := hmem.mp hw
      have hf : anyVerifier M (polyLen a k) (polyLen a' k') x r = false := by
        simpa only [boolVerifier, Option.some.injEq] using h
      exact absurd (ht.symm.trans hf) (by decide)
    · intro hc
      cases hb : anyVerifier M (polyLen a k) (polyLen a' k') x r with
      | false => exact congrArg some hb
      | true => exact absurd (hmem.mpr hb) (fun hw => hc hw)

/-- Polynomial time is closed under negating the verifier's answer.
**Proof.** Swap the two witnessing `P`-languages. -/
theorem polyTimeModel_closedUnderNot : ClosedUnderNot polyTimeModel := by
  rintro M ⟨V₁, V₀, hV₁, hV₀, hM⟩
  refine ⟨V₀, V₁, hV₀, hV₁, fun x r => ?_⟩
  have h := hM x r
  simp only [boolVerifier, Option.some.injEq] at h ⊢
  rw [Bool.not_eq_true', Bool.not_eq_false']
  exact ⟨h.2, h.1⟩

/-- Polynomial time recognizes the shifted-OR construction.
**Proof sketch.** Decode the nested pair, slice `u` into its
`polyLen a' k' |x|` shift blocks, and XOR each with `v`.  Here
`shiftOrVerifier` uses `List.zipWith xor v block`, which is poly-time on
lists of *arbitrary* lengths and truncates to the shorter of `|v|` and the
block length; the exact-length witnesses quantified in `InSigma2` (where
`|v|` equals the block length) recover the book's equal-length bitwise XOR.
Run the `P`-verifier on each XORed block and `OR` the results — the
XOR-shifted block-OR closure `Complexity.mem_P_of_blockXorAny` at `M`'s
`some true`-language, on the nested pairing used by `Complexity.SigmaP`. -/
theorem polyTimeModel_closedUnderShiftOr :
    ClosedUnderShiftOr polyTimeModel := by
  classical
  rintro M a k a' k' ⟨V₁, _, hV₁, _, hM⟩
  have hblock := mem_P_of_blockXorAny hV₁ a k a' k'
  refine ⟨_, hblock, fun x u v => ?_⟩
  have hMt : ∀ s : List Bool, M x s = true ↔ Turing.pairEncode x s ∈ V₁ := by
    intro s
    have h := (hM x s).1
    simpa only [boolVerifier, Option.some.injEq] using h
  have hbridge : Turing.pairEncode (Turing.pairEncode x u) v ∈
      {w : List Bool | ∃ i < a' * ((pairFstD (pairFstD w)).length + 1) ^ k',
        Turing.pairEncode (pairFstD (pairFstD w))
          (List.zipWith xor (pairSndD w) (blockAt a k (pairFstD w) i)) ∈ V₁} ↔
      ∃ i < a' * (x.length + 1) ^ k',
        Turing.pairEncode x (List.zipWith xor v
          ((u.drop (i * (a * (x.length + 1) ^ k))).take (a * (x.length + 1) ^ k))) ∈ V₁ := by
    simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq, pairFstD_pairEncode, pairSndD_pairEncode, blockAt]
  have hleft : shiftOrVerifier M (polyLen a k) (polyLen a' k') x u v = true ↔
      ∃ i < a' * (x.length + 1) ^ k',
        Turing.pairEncode x (List.zipWith xor v
          ((u.drop (i * (a * (x.length + 1) ^ k))).take (a * (x.length + 1) ^ k))) ∈ V₁ := by
    simp only [shiftOrVerifier, polyLen, List.any_eq_true, List.mem_range]
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨i, hi, hv⟩
      exact ⟨i, hi, (hMt _).mp hv⟩
    · rintro ⟨i, hi, hv⟩
      exact ⟨i, hi, (hMt _).mpr hv⟩
  exact hleft.trans hbridge.symm

/-- Polynomial-time verifiers have polynomial-size circuits when their
random string is fixed, with one size bound uniform in the random string:
the form of [AB09, Thm 6.6] that Adleman's counting argument consumes.
**Proof sketch.** Apply `Complexity.P_subset_PPoly` to the verifier's paired
acceptance language. For each input length and fixed random string, the
resulting circuit reads the doubled input bits, the separator, and the
random bits. A buffer supplies two distinct copies of each input bit and
constants for the separator and random string. Shifting all old vertex
numbers preserves distinct gate inputs and fan-in at most two.

The buffer adds exactly the number of free input bits to the old circuit
size. The paired length is bounded by a polynomial in the input length,
with coefficients depending only on the original randomness schedule.
Composing this bound with the circuit family's size polynomial gives one
bound uniform in the contents of the fixed random string. -/
theorem polyTimeModel_verifierHasCircuits :
    ∀ M a k, polyTimeModel.Eff (boolVerifier M) →
      VerifierHasCircuits M (polyLen a k) := by
  classical
  rintro M a k ⟨V₁, V₀, hV₁, hV₀, hM⟩
  have hPoly : V₁.InPPoly := Complexity.P_subset_PPoly hV₁
  obtain ⟨b, j, F, hF, hSize, hLanguage⟩ := hPoly
  refine ⟨b * (a + 3) ^ j + 1, (k + 1) * (j + 1), fun n r hr => ?_⟩
  let ell := 2 * n + 2 + r.length
  let C := F.circuit ell
  let D : BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit n := BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.pairEncode r C
  have hD : D.IsFaninTwo :=
    BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.pairEncode_isFaninTwo r C (hF ell)
  refine ⟨D, hD.1, hD, ?_, fun v => ?_⟩
  · -- The paired length is polynomial in n, uniformly in the chosen random string.
    have hN : 0 < n + 1 := Nat.succ_pos n
    have hnPow : n + 1 ≤ (n + 1) ^ (k + 1) :=
      Nat.le_self_pow (Nat.succ_ne_zero k) (n + 1)
    have hkPow : (n + 1) ^ k ≤ (n + 1) ^ (k + 1) :=
      Nat.pow_le_pow_right hN (Nat.le_succ k)
    have hLen : ell + 1 ≤ (a + 3) * (n + 1) ^ (k + 1) := by
      dsimp only [ell]
      rw [hr]
      unfold polyLen
      nlinarith [Nat.mul_le_mul_left a hkPow]
    have hCircuit : C.size ≤
        b * (a + 3) ^ j * (n + 1) ^ ((k + 1) * j) := by
      calc
        C.size ≤ b * (ell + 1) ^ j := hSize ell
        _ ≤ b * ((a + 3) * (n + 1) ^ (k + 1)) ^ j :=
          Nat.mul_le_mul_left b (Nat.pow_le_pow_left hLen j)
        _ = b * (a + 3) ^ j * (n + 1) ^ ((k + 1) * j) := by
          rw [mul_pow, ← pow_mul]
          ring
    have hExponent : (k + 1) * j ≤ (k + 1) * (j + 1) :=
      Nat.mul_le_mul_left (k + 1) (Nat.le_succ j)
    have hCircuit' : C.size ≤
        b * (a + 3) ^ j * (n + 1) ^ ((k + 1) * (j + 1)) :=
      hCircuit.trans (Nat.mul_le_mul_left (b * (a + 3) ^ j)
        (Nat.pow_le_pow_right hN hExponent))
    have hPositive : 0 < (k + 1) * (j + 1) :=
      Nat.mul_pos (Nat.succ_pos k) (Nat.succ_pos j)
    have hnSize : n ≤ (n + 1) ^ ((k + 1) * (j + 1)) :=
      (Nat.le_succ n).trans
        (Nat.le_self_pow (Nat.ne_of_gt hPositive) (n + 1))
    calc
      D.size = n + C.size := BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.pairEncode_size r C
      _ ≤ (n + 1) ^ ((k + 1) * (j + 1)) +
          b * (a + 3) ^ j * (n + 1) ^ ((k + 1) * (j + 1)) :=
        Nat.add_le_add hnSize hCircuit'
      _ = (b * (a + 3) ^ j + 1) *
          (n + 1) ^ ((k + 1) * (j + 1)) := by ring
  · -- The buffer feeds the old circuit exactly the encoded pair (x,r).
    rw [BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.pairEncode_eval r C v]
    have hAccept : C.eval (BoolCircuit.pairEncodeInput r v) = true ↔
        Turing.pairEncode (List.ofFn v) r ∈ V₁ := by
      rw [← hLanguage]
      exact BoolCircuit.DAGCircuitFamily.pairEncode_eval_eq_true_iff F r v
    have hVerifier := (hM (List.ofFn v) r).1
    simp only [boolVerifier, Option.some.injEq] at hVerifier
    have hCorrect := hAccept.trans hVerifier.symm
    cases hC : C.eval (BoolCircuit.pairEncodeInput r v) <;>
      cases hV : M (List.ofFn v) r <;> simp_all

/-- **Adleman's theorem for polynomial-time machines** ([AB09, Thm 7.14],
unconditionally): `BPP ⊆ P/poly`, with both sides the library's own classes
(`InBPP polyTimeModel` and `Language.InPPoly`). -/
theorem adleman_polyTime {L : Language Bool}
    (hL : InBPP polyTimeModel L) : L.InPPoly :=
  adleman polyTimeModel polyTimeModel_closedUnderMajority hL
    polyTimeModel_verifierHasCircuits

/-- Certificate-style `Σ₂` over the polynomial-time model coincides with the
library's `Complexity.SigmaP 2` ([AB09, Definition 5.3]).
**Proof sketch.** Both say: a `P`-predicate of the nested pair
`⟨⟨x, u⟩, v⟩` with `∃ u ∀ v` over blocks of length `C·(|x|+1)^c`.  The two
length normal forms (`polyLen a k` here, `C·(n+1)^c` in `PolyHierarchy`)
are identical, so the translation is a re-bracketing of the quantifiers
plus padding of the two block lengths to a common bound. -/
theorem inSigma2_polyTimeModel_iff (L : Language Bool) :
    InSigma2 polyTimeModel L ↔ L ∈ SigmaP 2 := by
  classical
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨N, a₁, k₁, a₂, k₂, ⟨V, hV, hN⟩, hiff⟩
    have h₁ : PolyHierarchy.UnaryPT
        (fun y : List Bool => polyLen a₁ k₁ y.length) := by
      have h := PolyHierarchy.unaryPT_poly a₁ k₁ polyTimeComputable_id
      simpa [polyLen] using h
    have h₂ : PolyHierarchy.UnaryPT
        (fun y : List Bool => polyLen a₂ k₂ y.length) := by
      have h := PolyHierarchy.unaryPT_poly a₂ k₂ polyTimeComputable_id
      simpa [polyLen] using h
    have hmem := PolyHierarchy.mem_altClass_of_normal (b := true) (i := 1)
      hV polyTimeComputable_id h₁ h₂
    have hkey : L = {y | qStep true (polyLen a₁ k₁ y.length)
        fun U => altQuant V (polyLen a₂ k₂ y.length) false 1
          (id (Turing.pairEncode y U))} := by
      ext y
      rw [Set.mem_setOf_eq, hiff y]
      constructor
      · rintro ⟨u, hu, hall⟩
        refine ⟨u, hu, fun v hv => ?_⟩
        show Turing.pairEncode (Turing.pairEncode y u) v ∈ V
        exact (hN y u v).mp (hall v hv)
      · rintro ⟨u, hu, hall⟩
        refine ⟨u, hu, fun v hv => ?_⟩
        exact (hN y u v).mpr (hall v hv)
    rw [hkey]
    exact hmem
  · intro hL
    obtain ⟨C, c, V, hV, hiff⟩ := mem_SigmaP_two_iff_exists_forall.mp hL
    refine ⟨fun x u v =>
        decide (Turing.pairEncode (Turing.pairEncode x u) v ∈ V),
      C, c, C, c,
      ⟨V, hV, fun x u v => by rw [decide_eq_true_eq]⟩, fun x => ?_⟩
    rw [hiff x]
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨u, hu, hall⟩
      refine ⟨u, hu, fun v hv => ?_⟩
      rw [decide_eq_true_eq]
      exact hall v hv
    · rintro ⟨u, hu, hall⟩
      refine ⟨u, hu, fun v hv => ?_⟩
      have h := hall v hv
      rw [decide_eq_true_eq] at h
      exact h

/-- **`ZPP = RP ∩ coRP` for polynomial-time machines** ([AB09, Thm 7.8],
unconditionally): the abstract theorem at `polyTimeModel`, with every
closure hypothesis discharged. -/
theorem zpp_eq_rp_inter_corp_polyTime (L : Language Bool) :
    InZPP polyTimeModel L ↔ InRP polyTimeModel L ∧ InCoRP polyTimeModel L :=
  inZPP_iff_inRP_and_inCoRP polyTimeModel polyTimeModel_closedUnderRace
    polyTimeModel_closedUnderAnswerIs polyTimeModel_closedUnderAny L

/-- **Sipser–Gács for polynomial-time machines** ([AB09, Thm 7.15],
unconditionally): `BPP ⊆ Σ₂ᵖ ∩ Π₂ᵖ` with the library's own polynomial
hierarchy (`Complexity.SigmaP`/`Complexity.PiP`).

**Proof sketch.** The abstract `sipser_gacs` at `polyTimeModel` with its
closure hypotheses discharged, transported along
`inSigma2_polyTimeModel_iff` (and its complement instance for the `Π₂`
half). -/
theorem sipser_gacs_polyTime {L : Language Bool}
    (hL : InBPP polyTimeModel L) :
    L ∈ SigmaP 2 ∧ L ∈ PiP 2 := by
  obtain ⟨h1, h2⟩ := sipser_gacs polyTimeModel
    polyTimeModel_closedUnderMajority polyTimeModel_closedUnderNot
    polyTimeModel_closedUnderShiftOr hL
  exact ⟨(inSigma2_polyTimeModel_iff L).mp h1,
    (inSigma2_polyTimeModel_iff Lᶜ).mp h2⟩

end Randomized

/-

Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: TCSlib contributors

import TCSlib.Complexity.Randomized.Build.PairSplit
import TCSlib.Complexity.Randomized.Build.UnaryMul
import TCSlib.Complexity.Randomized.PolyExpr

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Two new machine primitives: coin splitting and unary multiplication

The closure calculus of non-uniform PPTs ([PS10, §2.1], implicit in every reduction of
chapters 2–4; inventory item Claim-26.3) needs two string machines that the library's
catalog `TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Build.Primitives` does not provide:

* `Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_pairSplitAt` — `⟨u, b⟩ ↦ ⟨b.take |u|, b.drop |u|⟩`: cut a
  coin string at a unary length (fresh coin segments as independent uniform strings);
* `Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_unaryMul` — `⟨1^a, 1^b⟩ ↦ 1^{ab}`: unary multiplication,
  which makes every syntactic polynomial computable in unary
  (`Complexity.polyTimeComputable_unaryPoly`) without the repetition lemma (D9).

Both are built in the `Build/` style (foundation decision D11): explicit finite machines with
a proved timed contract (`TCSlib.Complexity.Randomized.Build.PairSplit`,
`TCSlib.Complexity.Randomized.Build.UnaryMul`). This file states the two contracts with their
construction sketches (DESIGN.md §2.4) and derives the FP-level consequences the closure
catalogue consumes:
`polyTimeComputable_unaryPoly` (by induction on the expression, the `mul` case being the
only use of `unaryMul`) and the typed cuts `polyTimeComputable_pairTakePoly` /
`polyTimeComputable_pairDropPoly` (`pairSplitAt` applied to `⟨1^{p(|fst z|)}, snd z⟩`).

The unary evaluator is hosted here rather than in `TCSlib.Complexity.Randomized.PolyExpr`
because its `mul` case needs `unaryMul`, while the cuts below need both the evaluator and
`PolyExpr`; this keeps the import graph acyclic.

## Main results

* `Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_pairSplitAt` — coin splitting at a unary length, linear
  time (proved; the machine is `Turing.FinTM.exists_pairSplitTM` in
  `TCSlib.Complexity.Randomized.Build.PairSplit`).
* `Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_unaryMul` — unary multiplication, quadratic time
  (proved; the machine is `Turing.FinTM.exists_unaryMulTM` in
  `TCSlib.Complexity.Randomized.Build.UnaryMul`).
* `Complexity.polyTimeComputable_unaryPoly` — `x ↦ 1^{p(|x|)}` is polynomial-time
  computable for every syntactic polynomial `p` (proved by induction; the `mul` and `pow`
  cases rest on `unaryMul`).
* `Complexity.polyTimeComputable_pairTakePoly`, `Complexity.polyTimeComputable_pairDropPoly`
  — on `⟨u, b⟩`, the first / the remaining `p(|u|)` bits of `b` (proved from `pairSplitAt`).

## Main definitions

None (the primitives are existence statements over `Turing.FinTM Bool`).

## References

* [PS10] R. Pass, a. shelat, *A Course in Cryptography*, lecture notes, 3rd ed., January 2010.
  (§2.1, the closure properties of p.p.t. machines used implicitly throughout.)
* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§1.2–1.3, multi-tape machines and linear-time string
  manipulation.)
-/

namespace Turing.FinTM

/-- **Coin splitting at a unary length** (new primitive): on a pair `⟨u, b⟩` the machine
outputs the pair `⟨b.take |u|, b.drop |u|⟩`; on a malformed word it outputs `[]`. Linear
time. This is how a reduction uses disjoint segments of its coin string as independent
uniform strings [PS10, §2.1, implicit; inventory Claim-26.3(c)].

**Proof sketch (construction, DESIGN.md §2.4; built in
`TCSlib.Complexity.Randomized.Build.PairSplit`).** One work tape. Phase 1 is the buffered
aligned parser of `Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_pairFst`: it reads the doubled prefix of
`u` onto the work tape without emitting anything, and stops at the separator `01` (a
malformed prefix halts with empty output). Phase 2 rewinds the work head. Phase 3 is a copy
scan of `b`: while the work head walks across the stored `u`, each bit `c` of `b` read on
the input tape is emitted doubled as `cc` (the doubled first component of the output pair);
when the stored `u` is exhausted the machine emits the separator `01` and then copies the
remainder of `b` verbatim (if `b` is shorter than `u`, the separator is emitted when the
input ends and the second component is empty). The step ledger gives at most `5 (n + 1)`
steps; the output is `pairEncode (b.take |u|) (b.drop |u|)` by `Turing.pairEncode_eq_dbl`
(`Turing.FinTM.exists_pairSplitTM`, with `c = 5`). -/
theorem computesFunInTime_pairSplitAt :
    ∃ (M : FinTM Bool) (c : ℕ),
      M.ComputesFunInTime
        (fun z => match pairDecode z with
          | some (u, b) => pairEncode (b.take u.length) (b.drop u.length)
          | none => [])
        fun n => c * (n + 1) := by
  obtain ⟨M, hM⟩ := exists_pairSplitTM
  exact ⟨M, 5, hM⟩

/-- **Unary multiplication** (new primitive): on a pair `⟨u, v⟩` the machine outputs
`1^{|u| · |v|}`; on a malformed word it outputs `[]`. Quadratic time. With it every syntactic
polynomial is computable in unary (`Complexity.polyTimeComputable_unaryPoly`), so the lengths
`1^{p(n)}` that reductions need never go through the repetition lemma (D9).

**Proof sketch (construction, DESIGN.md §2.4; built in
`TCSlib.Complexity.Randomized.Build.UnaryMul`).** One work tape. Phase 1 is the buffered
aligned parser of `Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_pairFst`: it undoubles the prefix `u` onto
the work tape without emitting anything (one cell per token of `u`, so the content of `u` is
irrelevant) and validates the separator `01`; a malformed input halts with empty output.
Phase 2 rewinds the work head and then, for each symbol of the second component `v` (read
left to right, its content irrelevant), walks across the stored word emitting one `true`
per cell (`emitAction`-style) and rewinds the work tape; at the end of the input it halts.
**Deviation from the DESIGN.md sketch** (which stores `v` and replays it once per token of
`u`): storing `u` and replaying it once per symbol of `v` needs no input rewind, and the
product `|u| · |v|` is the same. The run takes `|u| + 1 + |v| (2 |u| + 3) + 1` steps after
the parser, at most `(n + 1) ^ 2 + 3 n + 5 ≤ 5 (n + 1) ^ 2` in all (step ledger `mul_run`),
and the output is `List.replicate (|u| * |v|) true` by induction on the symbols of `v`
(`List.replicate_add`, `Nat.mul_succ`) — `Turing.FinTM.exists_unaryMulTM`, with `c = 5`. -/
theorem computesFunInTime_unaryMul :
    ∃ (M : FinTM Bool) (c : ℕ),
      M.ComputesFunInTime
        (fun z => match pairDecode z with
          | some (u, v) => List.replicate (u.length * v.length) true
          | none => [])
        fun n => c * (n + 1) ^ 2 := by
  obtain ⟨M, hM⟩ := exists_unaryMulTM
  exact ⟨M, 5, hM⟩

end Turing.FinTM

namespace Complexity

open Turing

/-- FP-level unary multiplication: if `x ↦ 1^{f x}` and `x ↦ 1^{g x}` are polynomial-time
computable, so is `x ↦ 1^{f x · g x}` (pair the two unary strings with
`PolyTimeComputable.pairEncode` and apply the unary-multiplication machine). -/
private theorem polyTimeComputable_unaryMulFun {f g : List Bool → ℕ}
    (hf : PolyTimeComputable fun x => List.replicate (f x) true)
    (hg : PolyTimeComputable fun x => List.replicate (g x) true) :
    PolyTimeComputable fun x => List.replicate (f x * g x) true := by
  obtain ⟨M, c, hM⟩ := Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_unaryMul
  have hmul : PolyTimeComputable (fun z => match pairDecode z with
      | some (u, v) => List.replicate (u.length * v.length) true
      | none => []) := ⟨M, c, 2, hM⟩
  convert hmul.comp (hf.pairEncode hg) using 1
  funext x
  simp [pairDecode_pairEncode]

/-- **The unary evaluator of a syntactic polynomial is polynomial-time:** for every
`p : PolyExpr`, the map `x ↦ 1^{p(|x|)}` is polynomial-time computable. This is the device by
which a reduction produces every length `1^{p(n)}` it needs (coin cuts, parameter changes,
padding), foundation decision D9; it is never routed through the repetition lemma.

**Proof sketch.** Induction on `p`. `const c`: the constant string `1^c`
(`Complexity.polyTimeComputable_const`). `var`: `x ↦ 1^{|x|}`
(`Complexity.polyTimeComputable_unary`). `add p q`: concatenate the two unary strings
(`Complexity.PolyTimeComputable.append`, `List.replicate_add`). `mul p q`: pair the two unary
strings and apply the unary-multiplication machine `Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_unaryMul`
(the only case that uses the new primitive). `pow p c`: inner induction on `c`, the step
being the `mul` case against `1^{p(|x|)}` (`pow_succ`). -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_unaryPoly (p : PolyExpr) :
    PolyTimeComputable fun x => List.replicate (p.eval x.length) true := by
  induction p with
  | const c => exact polyTimeComputable_const (List.replicate c true)
  | var => exact polyTimeComputable_unary
  | add p q hp hq =>
    simpa only [PolyExpr.eval_add, List.replicate_add] using hp.append hq
  | mul p q hp hq => exact polyTimeComputable_unaryMulFun hp hq
  | pow p c hp =>
    induction c with
    | zero => simpa using polyTimeComputable_const (List.replicate 1 true)
    | succ c ih =>
      simpa only [PolyExpr.eval_pow, pow_succ] using polyTimeComputable_unaryMulFun ih hp

/-- The FP form of the coin-splitting machine: `z ↦ ⟨(snd z).take |fst z|, (snd z).drop |fst z|⟩`
on pairs, `[]` on malformed words. -/
private theorem polyTimeComputable_pairSplitAt :
    PolyTimeComputable fun z => match pairDecode z with
      | some (u, b) => pairEncode (b.take u.length) (b.drop u.length)
      | none => [] := by
  obtain ⟨M, c, hM⟩ := Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_pairSplitAt
  exact polyTimeComputable_of_linear ⟨M, c, hM⟩

/-- The re-pairing `z ↦ ⟨1^{p(|fst z|)}, snd z⟩` is polynomial-time (the unary evaluator on
the first component, paired with the second component). -/
private theorem polyTimeComputable_pairUnaryFst (p : PolyExpr) :
    PolyTimeComputable fun z =>
      pairEncode (List.replicate (p.eval (pairFstD z).length) true) (pairSndD z) :=
  ((polyTimeComputable_unaryPoly p).comp polyTimeComputable_pairFstD).pairEncode
    polyTimeComputable_pairSndD

/-- **Typed coin cut, head:** on `z = ⟨u, b⟩`, the first `p(|u|)` bits of `b` are
polynomial-time computable (`z ↦ (snd z).take (p(|fst z|))`, with the total projections
`Complexity.pairFstD`/`pairSndD`). A reduction run on `⟨1^n, r⟩` thereby reads the first
`p(n)` coins as data [PS10, §2.1, implicit; inventory Claim-26.3(c)].

**Proof sketch.** `pairFstD ∘ pairSplitAt ∘ (z ↦ ⟨1^{p(|fst z|)}, snd z⟩)`: the re-pairing is
`polyTimeComputable_unaryPoly p` on `pairFstD` paired with `pairSndD`
(`PolyTimeComputable.pairEncode`), the split is `Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_pairSplitAt`
via `polyTimeComputable_of_linear`, and the composite equals the claimed function by
`Turing.pairDecode_pairEncode`, `Complexity.pairFstD_pairEncode` and `List.length_replicate`
(`PolyTimeComputable.comp`, `funext`). -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_pairTakePoly (p : PolyExpr) :
    PolyTimeComputable fun z => (pairSndD z).take (p.eval (pairFstD z).length) := by
  convert polyTimeComputable_pairFstD.comp
    (polyTimeComputable_pairSplitAt.comp (polyTimeComputable_pairUnaryFst p)) using 1
  funext z
  simp [pairDecode_pairEncode]

/-- **Typed coin cut, tail:** on `z = ⟨u, b⟩`, the bits of `b` after the first `p(|u|)` are
polynomial-time computable (`z ↦ (snd z).drop (p(|fst z|))`): the remaining coins of a
reduction after the first `p(n)` were consumed.

**Proof sketch.** As `polyTimeComputable_pairTakePoly` with `pairSndD` in place of `pairFstD`
after the split (`Complexity.pairSndD_pairEncode`). -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_pairDropPoly (p : PolyExpr) :
    PolyTimeComputable fun z => (pairSndD z).drop (p.eval (pairFstD z).length) := by
  convert polyTimeComputable_pairSndD.comp
    (polyTimeComputable_pairSplitAt.comp (polyTimeComputable_pairUnaryFst p)) using 1
  funext z
  simp [pairDecode_pairEncode]

end Complexity

## ===== TCSlib/Complexity/Randomized/RandomBits.lean =====

/-

Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: TCSlib Contributors
-/
import Mathlib.Algebra.BigOperators.Field
import Mathlib.Algebra.BigOperators.Fin
import TCSlib.Complexity.Randomized.Classes
import TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.Machines.Bin

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Random strings: conditioning, union bounds, and numbers from random bits

Shared infrastructure for randomized algorithms stated with `Randomized.randProb`:
constant events, conditioning on the first coin or on a prefix of the coins, the union bound,
reading numbers off blocks of fair coins, and the uniformity and independence of those
numbers. No textbook counterpart; used throughout the chapter-7 files ([AB09, Ch. 7]).

## Main definitions

* `Randomized.blockVal` — the number in the `i`-th length-`b` block of a bit string
  (little-endian, via `Complexity.LogProg.bitsVal`).
* `Randomized.bitsEquiv`, `Randomized.blocksEquiv` — bits as numbers, as bijections.

## Main results

* `Randomized.randProb_succ`, `Randomized.randProb_append` — conditioning on the first coin,
  on the first `b` coins; `Randomized.randProb_drop`, `Randomized.randProb_drop_take` —
  events of a slice of the coins.
* `Randomized.randProb_append_ge`, `Randomized.randProb_append_le` — conditioning on a
  prefix (lower and upper bounds).
* `Randomized.exists_ofFn_of_randProb_pos`, `Randomized.exists_forall_not_of_randProb_le` —
  positive probability and the union bound.
* `Randomized.blockCount_add_not` — passing and failing blocks are all the blocks.
* `Randomized.randProb_bitsVal` — `L` coins give a uniform number in `[0, 2^L)`.
* `Randomized.randProb_blocks`, `Randomized.randProb_blocks_piFinset` — `n` blocks give `n`
  independent uniform numbers.
* `Randomized.randProb_forall_blocks` — a property of every block has probability the
  power of the one-block probability.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009.
-/

namespace Randomized

open Finset
open Complexity.LogProg (bitsVal bitsVal_lt_two_pow)

/-! ### Elementary events and conditioning on a prefix -/

/-- A constant event has probability `1` or `0`. -/
theorem randProb_const (n : ℕ) (p : Prop) [Decidable p] :
    randProb n (fun _ => p) = if p then 1 else 0 := by
  by_cases hp : p
  · rw [if_pos hp, ← randProb_true (m := n)]
    exact randProb_congr fun _ => by simp [hp]
  · rw [if_neg hp, ← randProb_false (m := n)]
    exact randProb_congr fun _ => by simp [hp]

/-- An event of positive probability holds of some random string. -/
theorem exists_ofFn_of_randProb_pos {m : ℕ} {A : List Bool → Prop} [DecidablePred A]
    (h : 0 < randProb m A) : ∃ r : Fin m → Bool, A (List.ofFn r) := by
  by_contra hne
  push_neg at hne
  rw [randProb_congr (B := fun _ => False) fun r => by simp only [hne r],
    randProb_false] at h
  exact lt_irrefl _ h

/-- The fair first bit: `1/2` of the words of length one are `[c]`. -/
theorem randProb_one_eq (c : Bool) : randProb 1 (fun r => r = [c]) = 1 / 2 := by
  unfold randProb
  have h : (Finset.univ.filter fun r : Fin 1 → Bool => List.ofFn r = [c]).card = 1 := by
    cases c <;> decide
  rw [h]; norm_num

/-- **Conditioning on the first bit**: the probability over `n + 1` bits is the average of
the probabilities over `n` bits after a first bit `1` and after a first bit `0`.

**Proof sketch.** Split the event by the first coin (`randProb_or_disjoint`); each half is
the product of `Pr[first coin = c] = 1/2` (`randProb_one_eq`) and the probability over the
remaining `n` coins (`randProb_split`). -/
theorem randProb_succ (n : ℕ) (P : List Bool → Prop) [DecidablePred P] :
    randProb (n + 1) P =
      (randProb n (fun u => P (true :: u)) + randProb n (fun u => P (false :: u))) / 2 := by
  rw [show n + 1 = 1 + n from Nat.add_comm n 1]
  have e : ∀ c : Bool, randProb (1 + n) (fun w => w.take 1 = [c] ∧ P (c :: w.drop 1)) =
      1 / 2 * randProb n (fun u => P (c :: u)) := fun c => by
    rw [← randProb_one_eq c]
    exact randProb_split 1 n (fun r => r = [c]) (fun u => P (c :: u))
  calc randProb (1 + n) P
      = randProb (1 + n) (fun w => (w.take 1 = [true] ∧ P (true :: w.drop 1)) ∨
          (w.take 1 = [false] ∧ P (false :: w.drop 1))) := randProb_congr fun r => by
        obtain ⟨a, u, hw⟩ : ∃ a u, List.ofFn r = a :: u := by
          cases h : List.ofFn r with
          | nil => have := congrArg List.length h; simp at this
          | cons a u => exact ⟨a, u, rfl⟩
        rw [hw]; cases a <;> simp
    _ = randProb (1 + n) (fun w => w.take 1 = [true] ∧ P (true :: w.drop 1)) +
        randProb (1 + n) (fun w => w.take 1 = [false] ∧ P (false :: w.drop 1)) :=
        randProb_or_disjoint _ _ fun r h => by
          have := h.1.1.symm.trans h.2.1; simp at this
    _ = _ := by rw [e, e]; ring

/-- An event of the bits after the first `S` has, over `S + n` bits, its probability over
`n` bits. -/
theorem randProb_drop (S n : ℕ) (P : List Bool → Prop) [DecidablePred P] :
    randProb (S + n) (fun w => P (w.drop S)) = randProb n P := by
  calc randProb (S + n) (fun w => P (w.drop S))
      = randProb (S + n) (fun w => (fun _ => True) (w.take S) ∧ P (w.drop S)) :=
        randProb_congr fun r => by simp
    _ = randProb S (fun _ => True) * randProb n P := randProb_split S n (fun _ => True) P
    _ = randProb n P := by rw [randProb_true, one_mul]

/-- A condition on the slice `w[s, s+T)` of a uniform `m`-bit word has the probability of the
condition on a uniform `T`-bit word. -/
theorem randProb_drop_take {s T m : ℕ} (h : s + T ≤ m) (B : List Bool → Prop)
    [DecidablePred B] :
    randProb m (fun w => B ((w.drop s).take T)) = randProb T B := by
  have h1 : randProb m (fun w => B ((w.drop s).take T)) =
      randProb (s + T) (fun w => B ((w.drop s).take T)) := by
    rw [← randProb_take h (fun w => B ((w.drop s).take T))]
    refine randProb_congr fun r => ?_
    rw [List.drop_take, List.take_take, Nat.min_def, if_pos (by omega)]
  have h2 : randProb (s + T) (fun w => True ∧ B ((w.drop s).take T)) =
      randProb s (fun _ => True) * randProb T (fun v => B (v.take T)) := by
    convert randProb_split s T (fun _ => True) (fun v => B (v.take T)) using 1
  rw [h1, randProb_congr (B := fun w => True ∧ B ((w.drop s).take T)) fun r => by simp, h2,
    randProb_true, one_mul]
  refine randProb_congr fun r => ?_
  rw [List.take_of_length_le (by simp)]

/-- Conditioning on the first `b` coins: `Pr_{b+m}[A] = 𝔼_u Pr_m[A(u ++ ·)]`. -/
theorem randProb_append (b m : ℕ) (A : List Bool → Prop) [DecidablePred A] :
    randProb (b + m) A =
      (∑ u : Fin b → Bool, randProb m fun l => A (List.ofFn u ++ l)) / 2 ^ b := by
  unfold randProb
  rw [Finset.natCast_card_filter, ← (Fin.appendEquiv b m).sum_comp, Fintype.sum_prod_type,
    ← Finset.sum_div, div_div, pow_add, mul_comm ((2 : ℚ) ^ b)]
  congr 1
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun u _ => ?_
  rw [Finset.natCast_card_filter]
  exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun v _ =>
    if_congr (by
      show A (List.ofFn (Fin.append u v)) ↔ _
      rw [List.ofFn_fin_append]) rfl rfl

/-! ### Union bounds and block votes -/

/-- **Union bound**: if each of the `2^n` events `Bad v` has probability at most `δ` and
`2^n · δ < 1`, one random string avoids every one of them.

**Proof sketch.** Otherwise the `2^n` bad sets cover all `2^m` strings, so
`2^m ≤ 2^n · δ · 2^m < 2^m` (as in `adleman`). -/
theorem exists_forall_not_of_randProb_le {m n : ℕ} (Bad : (Fin n → Bool) → List Bool → Prop)
    [∀ v, DecidablePred (Bad v)] {δ : ℚ} (h : ∀ v, randProb m (Bad v) ≤ δ)
    (hδ : 2 ^ n * δ < 1) : ∃ r : Fin m → Bool, ∀ v, ¬ Bad v (List.ofFn r) := by
  by_contra hne
  push_neg at hne
  have hcover : (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin m → Bool)) ⊆ Finset.univ.biUnion
      (fun v => Finset.univ.filter fun r : Fin m → Bool => Bad v (List.ofFn r)) := by
    intro r _
    obtain ⟨v, hv⟩ := hne r
    exact Finset.mem_biUnion.mpr
      ⟨v, Finset.mem_univ _, Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_univ _, hv⟩⟩
  have h1 := (Finset.card_le_card hcover).trans Finset.card_biUnion_le
  rw [card_univ_bitstrings] at h1
  have h2 : ((2 : ℚ)) ^ m ≤ ∑ v : Fin n → Bool,
      ((Finset.univ.filter fun r : Fin m → Bool => Bad v (List.ofFn r)).card : ℚ) := by
    exact_mod_cast h1
  have h3 : ∀ v, ((Finset.univ.filter fun r : Fin m → Bool => Bad v (List.ofFn r)).card : ℚ) ≤
      δ * 2 ^ m := fun v => by
    have := h v
    unfold randProb at this
    rwa [div_le_iff₀ (by positivity)] at this
  have h4 := h2.trans (Finset.sum_le_sum fun v _ => h3 v)
  rw [Finset.sum_const, card_univ_bitstrings, nsmul_eq_mul] at h4
  push_cast at h4
  have h5 := mul_lt_mul_of_pos_right hδ (pow_pos (two_pos : (0 : ℚ) < 2) m)
  nlinarith

/-- The blocks passing a test and the blocks failing it are all the blocks. -/
theorem blockCount_add_not (q K : ℕ) (B : List Bool → Bool) (l : List Bool) :
    blockCount q K B l + blockCount q K (fun l => !B l) l = K := by
  induction K generalizing l with
  | zero => simp [blockCount]
  | succ K ih =>
    rw [blockCount_succ, blockCount_succ]
    have := ih (l.drop q)
    cases B (l.take q) <;> simp <;> omega

/-! ### Numbers from random bits -/

/-- The number written in the `i`-th length-`b` block of `r`. -/
def blockVal (b : ℕ) (r : List Bool) (i : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  bitsVal ((r.drop (i * b)).take b)

/-- Every block value is below `2^b`. -/
theorem blockVal_lt (b : ℕ) (r : List Bool) (i : ℕ) : blockVal b r i < 2 ^ b :=
  (bitsVal_lt_two_pow _).trans_le (Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by norm_num) (List.length_take_le _ _))

/-- `bitsVal` of a bit tuple is `∑ⱼ fⱼ·2^j`. -/
theorem bitsVal_ofFn {L : ℕ} (f : Fin L → Bool) :
    bitsVal (List.ofFn f) = ∑ j : Fin L, (f j).toNat * 2 ^ (j : ℕ) := by
  induction L with
  | zero => simp [bitsVal]
  | succ L ih =>
    rw [List.ofFn_succ, bitsVal, ih, Fin.sum_univ_succ, Finset.mul_sum]
    simp only [Fin.val_zero, pow_zero, mul_one, Fin.val_succ, pow_succ]
    congr 1
    exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => by ring

/-- `L` random bits are a uniformly random number in `[0, 2^L)`. -/
def bitsEquiv (L : ℕ) : (Fin L → Bool) ≃ Fin (2 ^ L) :=
  (Equiv.arrowCongr (Equiv.refl _) finTwoEquiv.symm).trans finFunctionFinEquiv

/-- `bitsEquiv` is `bitsVal`. -/
theorem bitsEquiv_apply {L : ℕ} (f : Fin L → Bool) :
    (bitsEquiv L f : ℕ) = bitsVal (List.ofFn f) := by
  rw [bitsVal_ofFn, bitsEquiv, Equiv.trans_apply, finFunctionFinEquiv_apply]
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun j _ => ?_
  have hb : ∀ c : Bool, ((finTwoEquiv.symm c : Fin 2) : ℕ) = c.toNat := by decide
  simp [Equiv.arrowCongr_apply, hb]

/-- The number read off `L` uniform bits is uniform on `[0, 2^L)`.

**Proof sketch.** `r ↦ bitsVal r` is the bijection `bitsEquiv` from `{0,1}^L` onto
`[0, 2^L)`, so it maps the strings satisfying `P ∘ bitsVal` bijectively onto
`{v < 2^L | P v}`. -/
theorem randProb_bitsVal (L : ℕ) (P : ℕ → Prop) [DecidablePred P] :
    randProb L (fun r => P (bitsVal r)) = #{v ∈ range (2 ^ L) | P v} / 2 ^ L := by
  unfold randProb
  congr 2
  refine Finset.card_bij (fun r _ => bitsVal (List.ofFn r)) ?_ ?_ ?_
  · intro r hr
    simp only [mem_filter, mem_univ, true_and] at hr
    simpa [hr] using bitsVal_lt_two_pow (List.ofFn r)
  · intro r _ r' _ h
    simp only at h
    rw [← bitsEquiv_apply, ← bitsEquiv_apply] at h
    exact (bitsEquiv L).injective (Fin.ext h)
  · intro v hv
    simp only [mem_filter, mem_range] at hv
    have hr : bitsVal (List.ofFn ((bitsEquiv L).symm ⟨v, hv.1⟩)) = v := by
      rw [← bitsEquiv_apply, Equiv.apply_symm_apply]
    refine ⟨(bitsEquiv L).symm ⟨v, hv.1⟩, ?_, hr⟩
    simp only [mem_filter, mem_univ, true_and]
    rw [hr]
    exact hv.2

/-- `n·b` random bits, cut into `n` blocks of `b`, as `n` numbers in `[0, 2^b)`. -/
def blocksEquiv (n b : ℕ) : (Fin (n * b) → Bool) ≃ (Fin n → Fin (2 ^ b)) :=
  ((Equiv.arrowCongr finProdFinEquiv.symm (Equiv.refl Bool)).trans
    (Equiv.curry _ _ _)).trans (Equiv.arrowCongr (Equiv.refl _) (bitsEquiv b))

/-- The `i`-th coordinate of `blocksEquiv` is the `i`-th block value. -/
theorem blocksEquiv_apply {n b : ℕ} (r : Fin (n * b) → Bool) (i : Fin n) :
    (blocksEquiv n b r i : ℕ) = blockVal b (List.ofFn r) i := by
  have hlist : ((List.ofFn r).drop (i * b)).take b =
      List.ofFn (fun j : Fin b => r (finProdFinEquiv (i, j))) := by
    have hib : (i : ℕ) * b + b ≤ n * b := by
      have := i.isLt
      nlinarith
    apply List.ext_getElem
    · simp
      omega
    · intro j h1 h2
      simp only [List.getElem_take, List.getElem_drop, List.getElem_ofFn]
      congr 1
      ext
      simp [finProdFinEquiv]
      ring
  rw [blockVal, hlist, ← bitsEquiv_apply]
  rfl

/-- The `n` numbers read off `n` blocks of `b` uniform bits are independent and uniform
on `[0, 2^b)`. -/
theorem randProb_blocks (n b : ℕ) (P : (Fin n → ℕ) → Prop) [DecidablePred P] :
    randProb (n * b) (fun r => P (fun i => blockVal b r i)) =
      #{f : Fin n → Fin (2 ^ b) | P (fun i => f i)} / (2 ^ b) ^ n := by
  unfold randProb
  rw [← pow_mul, mul_comm b n]
  congr 2
  refine Finset.card_equiv (blocksEquiv n b) fun r => ?_
  simp only [mem_filter, mem_univ, true_and]
  exact Iff.of_eq (congrArg P (funext fun i => (blocksEquiv_apply r i).symm))

/-- `randProb_blocks` with the block values ranging over `[0, 2^b)^n` as a `Fintype.piFinset`. -/
theorem randProb_blocks_piFinset (n b : ℕ) (P : (Fin n → ℕ) → Prop) [DecidablePred P] :
    randProb (n * b) (fun r => P fun i => blockVal b r i) =
      (#{f ∈ Fintype.piFinset fun _ : Fin n => range (2 ^ b) | P f} : ℚ) / 2 ^ (n * b) := by
  rw [randProb_blocks, ← pow_mul, mul_comm b n]
  congr 2
  refine Finset.card_bij (fun a _ => fun i => (a i : ℕ)) ?_ ?_ ?_
  · intro a ha
    simp only [mem_filter, mem_univ, true_and] at ha
    simp [ha]
  · intro a _ a' _ h
    funext i
    exact Fin.ext (congrFun h i)
  · intro f hf
    simp only [mem_filter, Fintype.mem_piFinset, mem_range] at hf
    exact ⟨fun i => ⟨f i, hf.1 i⟩, by simpa using hf.2, rfl⟩

/-- The probability that all of `t` blocks of `L` uniform bits satisfy `Q` is the `t`-th
power of the one-block probability. -/
theorem randProb_forall_blocks (t L : ℕ) (Q : ℕ → Prop) [DecidablePred Q] :
    randProb (t * L) (fun s => ∀ j : Fin t, Q (blockVal L s j)) =
      randProb L (fun r => Q (bitsVal r)) ^ t := by
  induction t with
  | zero =>
    rw [pow_zero, ← randProb_true (m := 0 * L)]
    exact randProb_congr fun r => by simp
  | succ t ih =>
    rw [show (t + 1) * L = L + t * L by ring, pow_succ', ← ih, ← randProb_split]
    refine randProb_congr fun r => ?_
    rw [Fin.forall_fin_succ]
    simp only [Fin.val_zero, Fin.val_succ, blockVal, zero_mul, List.drop_zero,
      List.drop_drop, show ∀ j : ℕ, (j + 1) * L = L + j * L from fun j => by ring]

/-! ### Conditioning on a prefix: bounds -/

/-- **Conditioning**: if the first `m₁` bits satisfy `A` with probability `p`, and for each
such prefix `u` the remaining `m₂` bits satisfy `C u` with probability `≥ ε`, then the
whole string satisfies `C` with probability `≥ p·ε`.

**Proof sketch.** Splitting strings by `Fin.append`, the count of good strings is the sum
over prefixes `u` of the count of good suffixes; bound each summand with `u ∈ A` below
by `ε·2^{m₂}` and drop the others. -/
theorem randProb_append_ge (m₁ m₂ : ℕ) (A : List Bool → Prop) [DecidablePred A]
    (C : List Bool → List Bool → Prop) [∀ u, DecidablePred (C u)] {ε : ℚ}
    (h : ∀ u : Fin m₁ → Bool, A (List.ofFn u) → ε ≤ randProb m₂ (C (List.ofFn u))) :
    randProb m₁ A * ε ≤ randProb (m₁ + m₂) (fun r => C (r.take m₁) (r.drop m₁)) := by
  have hcard : #{r : Fin (m₁ + m₂) → Bool | C ((List.ofFn r).take m₁)
      ((List.ofFn r).drop m₁)} = ∑ u : Fin m₁ → Bool,
        #{v : Fin m₂ → Bool | C (List.ofFn u) (List.ofFn v)} := by
    rw [← Finset.card_equiv (Fin.appendEquiv m₁ m₂)
      (s := {uv : (Fin m₁ → Bool) × (Fin m₂ → Bool) |
        C (List.ofFn uv.1) (List.ofFn uv.2)}) fun uv => by
        simp only [mem_filter, mem_univ, true_and]
        change _ ↔ C ((List.ofFn (Fin.append uv.1 uv.2)).take m₁)
          ((List.ofFn (Fin.append uv.1 uv.2)).drop m₁)
        rw [List.ofFn_fin_append, List.take_left' (by simp), List.drop_left' (by simp)]]
    rw [Finset.card_filter, Fintype.sum_prod_type]
    simp only [Finset.card_filter]
  have heq : randProb (m₁ + m₂) (fun r => C (r.take m₁) (r.drop m₁)) =
      (∑ u : Fin m₁ → Bool, randProb m₂ (C (List.ofFn u))) / 2 ^ m₁ := by
    unfold randProb
    rw [hcard, Nat.cast_sum, pow_add, ← Finset.sum_div, div_div, mul_comm]
  rw [heq]
  unfold randProb
  rw [mul_comm, ← mul_div_assoc]
  refine div_le_div_of_nonneg_right ?_ (by positivity)
  calc ε * #{u : Fin m₁ → Bool | A (List.ofFn u)}
      = ∑ u ∈ {u : Fin m₁ → Bool | A (List.ofFn u)}, ε := by
        rw [Finset.sum_const, nsmul_eq_mul, mul_comm]
    _ ≤ ∑ u ∈ {u : Fin m₁ → Bool | A (List.ofFn u)}, randProb m₂ (C (List.ofFn u)) :=
        Finset.sum_le_sum fun u hu => h u (by simpa using hu)
    _ ≤ ∑ u : Fin m₁ → Bool, randProb m₂ (C (List.ofFn u)) :=
        Finset.sum_le_sum_of_subset_of_nonneg (Finset.filter_subset _ _)
          fun _ _ _ => randProb_nonneg

/-- **Conditioning on a prefix, upper bound**: if `C u v` forces `A u`, and for each prefix
`u ∈ A` the suffix event has probability at most `ε`, then `Pr[C] ≤ Pr[A] · ε`.

**Proof sketch.** Bound the complement from below by `randProb_append_ge` twice: on `A` the
suffix misses `C` with probability at least `1 - ε`, off `A` always. -/
theorem randProb_append_le (m₁ m₂ : ℕ) (A : List Bool → Prop) [DecidablePred A]
    (C : List Bool → List Bool → Prop) [∀ u, DecidablePred (C u)] {ε : ℚ}
    (hCA : ∀ u v, C u v → A u)
    (h : ∀ u : Fin m₁ → Bool, A (List.ofFn u) → randProb m₂ (C (List.ofFn u)) ≤ ε) :
    randProb (m₁ + m₂) (fun r => C (r.take m₁) (r.drop m₁)) ≤ randProb m₁ A * ε := by
  have h1 := randProb_append_ge m₁ m₂ A (fun u v => A u ∧ ¬ C u v) (ε := 1 - ε) fun u hu => by
    rw [randProb_congr (B := fun v => ¬ C (List.ofFn u) v) fun r => by simp [hu],
      randProb_not]
    linarith [h u hu]
  have h2 := randProb_append_ge m₁ m₂ (fun u => ¬ A u) (fun u _ => ¬ A u) (ε := 1)
    fun u hu => le_of_eq (by
      rw [randProb_congr (B := fun _ => True) fun r => by simp [hu], randProb_true])
  have hsplit : randProb (m₁ + m₂) (fun r => ¬ C (r.take m₁) (r.drop m₁)) =
      randProb (m₁ + m₂) (fun r => A (r.take m₁) ∧ ¬ C (r.take m₁) (r.drop m₁)) +
        randProb (m₁ + m₂) (fun r => ¬ A (r.take m₁)) := by
    rw [← randProb_or_disjoint (fun r => A (r.take m₁) ∧ ¬ C (r.take m₁) (r.drop m₁))
      (fun r => ¬ A (r.take m₁)) fun r h => h.2 h.1.1]
    refine randProb_congr fun r => ?_
    by_cases hA : A ((List.ofFn r).take m₁)
    · simp [hA]
    · simp only [hA, false_and, not_false_eq_true, or_true, iff_true]
      exact fun hc => hA (hCA _ _ hc)
  have hnot : randProb (m₁ + m₂) (fun r => ¬ C (r.take m₁) (r.drop m₁)) =
      1 - randProb (m₁ + m₂) (fun r => C (r.take m₁) (r.drop m₁)) := randProb_not _
  have hA : randProb m₁ (fun u => ¬ A u) = 1 - randProb m₁ A := randProb_not _
  have h2' : randProb m₁ (fun u => ¬ A u) ≤
      randProb (m₁ + m₂) (fun r => ¬ A (r.take m₁)) := by simpa using h2
  have h1' : randProb m₁ A * (1 - ε) ≤
      randProb (m₁ + m₂) (fun r => A (r.take m₁) ∧ ¬ C (r.take m₁) (r.drop m₁)) := h1
  rw [mul_sub, mul_one] at h1'
  linarith

end Randomized
