import TCSlib.Complexity.Randomized.Build.IterateFind
import TCSlib.Complexity.Randomized.Build.StateLoop
import TCSlib.Complexity.Randomized.Build.StringLoops
import TCSlib.Complexity.Randomized.Primitives

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# The repetition lemma: polynomially many rounds of a polynomial-time step

Every theorem of [PS10, ch. 2–4] that *repeats* an adversary — hardness amplification
[PS10, Theorem 35.1, Algorithm 38.5: `2nm²p(n)` fresh-coin calls returning the first
success], Goldreich–Levin [PS10, Theorem 87.3: `n(2^k − 1)` calls and a majority], the
next-bit predictor, the GGM distinguisher hosting `q(n)` oracle queries, the truncated
simulators of the zero-knowledge chapter (inventory item Inf-4.3: "restart loops with a
bounded number of attempts as strict PPT", Claims 123.d and 128.a), rejection samplers
(D10) — reduces to one machine lemma, `Complexity.polyTimeComputable_iterateFind`: iterate a
polynomial-time step `g` at most `R(|x|)` times on a polynomially bounded orbit and return
the payload `out` of the first orbit point accepted by `acc` (`[]` on exhaustion). The
iteration `polyTimeComputable_iterate`, the concatenating variant
`polyTimeComputable_iterateEmit`, the block map and the string tests `majority`, `pairXor`,
`pairEq` are instances or small machines.

**Admissions policy (D11).** `polyTimeComputable_iterateFind` is the single machine lemma
that may remain admitted at the end of the fill campaign (run 4); every theorem that repeats
an adversary depends on it and on nothing else admitted, and the headline axiom prints
(`audits/pass-shelat/Checks.lean`) list it by name if it is still open. The derived lemmas of
this file are to be closed from it (or by small direct machines), so that the admission stays
a single named one. **Status (run 3b):** `polyTimeComputable_iterateFind` is closed — its
machine is built on the public clean-module host `TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Build.ModuleHost`
(clean modules and the finite host), with its instance in
`TCSlib.Complexity.Randomized.Build.IterateFindHost` (the copier and the host's control) and
the assembly in `TCSlib.Complexity.Randomized.Build.IterateFind` (through
`Turing.FinTM.exists_loopFindTM`), and its axiom print is `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`.
The six derived lemmas are closed too, as instances of one public **state-loop** form
`polyTimeComputable_stateFind` of the repetition lemma (a state word `⟨x, s⟩` retaining the
input, a step on the state, a test firing first at round `N x ≤ R|x|`, an output read off the
final state), whose loop data, orbit closed forms and bounds live in
`TCSlib.Complexity.Randomized.Build.StateLoop` (the form itself and the two iteration loops)
and `TCSlib.Complexity.Randomized.Build.StringLoops` (the four string loops).

**Construction of `iterateFind`, as built (DESIGN.md §2.6, step 1, and its as-built erratum,
which records the departures from the frozen steps 2–5).**

1. *State word carries the input.* The loop state is `⟨x, s⟩` (`pairEncode x s`) from
   `⟨x, x⟩`; the step is the length-guarded `guardedStep g P x`, which advances to `⟨x, g s⟩` if
   the **new** point fits, `|g s| ≤ P|x|`, and otherwise leaves the word unchanged. On the
   orbit, for `i ≤ R|x|`, the guard is never taken (`iterate_guardedStep_eq`), so the loop's
   `find?` is the statement's (`acc_guardedStep_eq`). The pure invariant `LoopInv` is closed
   under the step (`loopInv_guardedStep`); the machine uses the stronger actual-pair invariant
   `∃ s, w = ⟨x, s⟩ ∧ |s| ≤ P|x|`, which bounds the word's length by `2|x| + 2 + P|x|`.
2. *The machine.* `Complexity.IterateFind.polyTimeComputable_find`
   (`TCSlib.Complexity.Randomized.Build.IterateFind`) is an instance of
   `Turing.FinTM.exists_loopFindTM` with the guarded step `IterateFind.step`, the same function
   as `guardedStep` (`IterateFind.step_eq`). Its loop body runs five clean modules in the public
   clean-module host `Turing.ModuleHost.hostTM` (`TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Build.ModuleHost`,
   host H14): the copier, which puts the native input on tape 0 (`IterateFind.copyTM`); the
   startup install `x ↦ ⟨x, x⟩`; the verdict install `w ↦ ⟨[acc (snd w)], w⟩`; the step install;
   and the payload emit `w ↦ out (snd (snd w))`. The installs and the emit come from
   `Turing.ModuleHost.clean_install`/`clean_emit` (a clean-call bridge stopped by a release flag
   and cut at its first halt). The host's control
   (`TCSlib.Complexity.Randomized.Build.IterateFindHost`) has three fresh states: the anchor, which
   dispatches into the verdict module; the branch, which reads the verdict cell of tape 0 and
   dispatches into the payload or the step module; and the halt.
3. *Budget and fuel.* Every request has length at most `2n + 6 + P n`, so every module's
   polynomial budget, and that of the fuel machine `x ↦ Nat.bits (R|x|)`
   (`polyTimeComputable_unaryPoly R` and `computesFunInTime_lengthBits`, so that the `find?` range
   is exactly `R|x| + 1`), fit `T n = A·(2n + 7 + P n)^D`; the loop combinator's bound
   `c (T n + 1)(R n + 2)` is put in normal form by `PolyExpr.eval_le`.
4. *The derived lemmas* are instances of the state-loop form `polyTimeComputable_stateFind`,
   which runs `iterateFind` on the guarded step `StateLoop.gstep` of a state word `⟨x, s⟩`:
   `iterate` threads a unary counter, tested against `1^{R|x|}` by `IterLoop.acc` (`R|x| ≤ |cnt|`);
   `iterateEmit` also threads an accumulator; the string functions consume their input.

## Main definitions

* `Complexity.guardedStep` — the length-guarded step on the state word `⟨x, s⟩`.
* `Complexity.LoopInv` — the loop invariant `fst w = x ∧ |snd w| ≤ P|x|`.

## Main results

* `Complexity.polyTimeComputable_iterateFind` — the load-bearing lemma (proved: the machine
  is built in `TCSlib.Complexity.Randomized.Build.IterateFind`, and the pure facts below
  identify its guarded orbit with `g^[i] x`).
* `Complexity.polyTimeComputable_iterate`, `Complexity.polyTimeComputable_iterateEmit` —
  `R(|x|)`-fold iteration and concatenated emissions (proved; state loops with a unary round
  counter).
* `Complexity.polyTimeComputable_stateFind` — the state-loop form of the repetition lemma, of
  which the six derived lemmas are instances (proved, from `polyTimeComputable_iterateFind`).
* `Complexity.polyTimeComputable_majority`, `polyTimeComputable_pairXor`,
  `polyTimeComputable_pairEq`, `polyTimeComputable_blockMap` — string tests and the block
  map used by the reductions (proved; state loops consuming the input).
* `Complexity.loopInv_init`, `Complexity.loopInv_guardedStep`,
  `Complexity.iterate_guardedStep_eq`, `Complexity.acc_guardedStep_eq` — the pure facts about
  the guarded step (proved; step 1 of the plan).

## References

* [PS10] R. Pass, a. shelat, *A Course in Cryptography*, lecture notes, 3rd ed., January 2010.
  (Algorithm 38.5 and Theorem 35.1; Theorem 87.3; Algorithms 123.4 and 128.7.)
* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§1.2–1.3, time-bounded machines.)
-/

namespace Complexity

open Turing StateLoop

/-! ### The guarded step and its pure theory (step 1 of the plan) -/

/-- The length-guarded step on the state word `w = ⟨x, s⟩`: advance to `⟨x, g s⟩` if the new
orbit point fits the bound `P|x|`, else stay (DESIGN.md §2.6, step 1). The guard makes the
loop invariant `LoopInv` closed under the step for every state word; on the orbit it is
never taken. -/
def guardedStep (g : List Bool → List Bool) (P : PolyExpr) (x w : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  if (g (pairSndD w)).length ≤ P.eval x.length then pairEncode x (g (pairSndD w)) else w

/-- The loop invariant: the state word carries the input `x` in its first component and an
orbit point of length at most `P|x|` in its second. -/
def LoopInv (P : PolyExpr) (x w : List Bool) : Prop :=
  pairFstD w = x ∧ (pairSndD w).length ≤ P.eval x.length

/-- The initial state word `⟨x, x⟩` satisfies the invariant when `|x| ≤ P|x|` (the case `i = 0`
of the orbit bound). -/
theorem loopInv_init (P : PolyExpr) (x : List Bool) (h0 : x.length ≤ P.eval x.length) :
    LoopInv P x (pairEncode x x) := by
  simp [LoopInv, h0]

/-- The invariant is closed under the guarded step, for every state word: if the new orbit
point fits, the new word is `⟨x, g s⟩`; otherwise the word is unchanged. -/
theorem loopInv_guardedStep (g : List Bool → List Bool) (P : PolyExpr) (x w : List Bool)
    (h : LoopInv P x w) : LoopInv P x (guardedStep g P x w) := by
  unfold guardedStep
  split_ifs with hg
  · simp [LoopInv, hg]
  · exact h

/-- On the orbit the guard is never taken: for `i ≤ R|x|`, the `i`-fold guarded step from
`⟨x, x⟩` is `⟨x, g^[i] x⟩` (induction on `i`, using the orbit bound at `i`). -/
theorem iterate_guardedStep_eq (g : List Bool → List Bool) (R P : PolyExpr) (x : List Bool)
    (horbit : ∀ i, i ≤ R.eval x.length → (g^[i] x).length ≤ P.eval x.length)
    (i : ℕ) (hi : i ≤ R.eval x.length) :
    (guardedStep g P x)^[i] (pairEncode x x) = pairEncode x (g^[i] x) := by
  induction i with
  | zero => simp
  | succ i ih =>
    rw [Function.iterate_succ_apply', ih (Nat.le_of_succ_le hi)]
    unfold guardedStep
    have hlen : (g (g^[i] x)).length ≤ P.eval x.length := by
      rw [← Function.iterate_succ_apply' g i x]
      exact horbit (i + 1) hi
    simp [hlen, Function.iterate_succ_apply']

/-- The acceptance tests of the loop agree with those of the statement on the whole range
`0, …, R|x|`: `acc (snd ((stepF x)^[i] ⟨x, x⟩)) = acc (g^[i] x)`. -/
theorem acc_guardedStep_eq (g : List Bool → List Bool) (acc : List Bool → Bool) (R P : PolyExpr)
    (x : List Bool)
    (horbit : ∀ i, i ≤ R.eval x.length → (g^[i] x).length ≤ P.eval x.length)
    (i : ℕ) (hi : i ≤ R.eval x.length) :
    acc (pairSndD ((guardedStep g P x)^[i] (pairEncode x x))) = acc (g^[i] x) := by
  rw [iterate_guardedStep_eq g R P x horbit i hi, pairSndD_pairEncode]

/-! ### The repetition lemma and its instances -/

/-- **The repetition lemma (load-bearing; D11).** Let `g` be a polynomial-time step, `acc` a
polynomial-time acceptance test, `out` a polynomial-time payload map, `R` and `P` syntactic
polynomials such that the orbit `g^[i] x` stays of length `≤ P|x|` for `i ≤ R|x|`. Then the
function "iterate `g` from `x` at most `R|x|` times and return `out` of the first accepted
orbit point, `[]` if none is accepted" is polynomial-time computable. It is the machine
behind every repeated-adversary argument of [PS10]: Algorithm 38.5's `2nm²p(n)` attempts
with first success [PS10, Theorem 35.1], the `n(2^k−1)` calls of Goldreich–Levin
[PS10, Theorem 87.3], rejection sampling (D10), the truncated simulators
[PS10, Algorithms 123.4 and 128.7] (inventory Inf-4.3).

**Proof sketch.** The machine is `Complexity.IterateFind.polyTimeComputable_find`
(`TCSlib.Complexity.Randomized.Build.IterateFind`; its construction is in the module docstring):
it computes `out` of the first accepted point, among the first `R|x| + 1`, of the orbit of
`⟨x, x⟩` under the guarded step `IterateFind.step g P x`, which is `guardedStep g P x`
(`IterateFind.step_eq`). Convert its conclusion to the statement's: for `i ≤ R|x|` the guarded
orbit is `⟨x, g^[i] x⟩` (`iterate_guardedStep_eq`), so the two `find?` predicates agree on the
range (`acc_guardedStep_eq`, `IterateFind.find?_congr_of_mem`), and at the index found the
payloads agree (`iterate_guardedStep_eq`, `pairSndD_pairEncode`). -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_iterateFind {g : List Bool → List Bool} (hg : PolyTimeComputable g)
    {acc : List Bool → Bool} (hacc : PolyTimeComputable fun s => [acc s])
    {out : List Bool → List Bool} (hout : PolyTimeComputable out)
    (R P : PolyExpr)
    (horbit : ∀ (x : List Bool) (i : ℕ), i ≤ R.eval x.length →
      (g^[i] x).length ≤ P.eval x.length) :
    PolyTimeComputable fun x =>
      match (List.range (R.eval x.length + 1)).find? (fun i => acc (g^[i] x)) with
      | some i => out (g^[i] x)
      | none => [] := by
  have h := IterateFind.polyTimeComputable_find hg hacc hout R P horbit
  convert h using 1
  funext x
  have hstep : IterateFind.step g P x = guardedStep g P x := by
    funext w
    rw [IterateFind.step_eq]
    rfl
  have hfind : (List.range (R.eval x.length + 1)).find? (fun i => acc (g^[i] x)) =
      (List.range (R.eval x.length + 1)).find?
        (fun i => acc (pairSndD ((IterateFind.step g P x)^[i] (pairEncode x x)))) := by
    apply IterateFind.find?_congr_of_mem
    intro i hi
    rw [List.mem_range] at hi
    rw [hstep, acc_guardedStep_eq g acc R P x (horbit x) i (by omega)]
  rw [hfind]
  cases hf : (List.range (R.eval x.length + 1)).find?
      (fun i => acc (pairSndD ((IterateFind.step g P x)^[i] (pairEncode x x)))) with
  | none => rfl
  | some i =>
    have hi := List.mem_of_find?_eq_some hf
    rw [List.mem_range] at hi
    simp only [hstep, iterate_guardedStep_eq g R P x (horbit x) i (by omega), pairSndD_pairEncode]

/-! ### State loops: the common form of the derived lemmas -/

/-- **State loops** (the common form of the six derived lemmas; DESIGN.md §2.6, step 7). A
state word `⟨x, s⟩` retains the input `x` and evolves its state from `start x` by
`s ↦ step ⟨x, s⟩` (`Complexity.StateLoop.orbit`); a test `acc` on the state word is `false`
before round `N x` and `true` at round `N x ≤ R|x|`, the states up to that round have length at
most `B|x|`, and `out` reads the answer off the final state word. Then
`x ↦ out ⟨x, orbit x (N x)⟩` is polynomial-time computable.

**Proof sketch.** Instance of `polyTimeComputable_iterateFind` on the length-guarded step
`Complexity.StateLoop.gstep step B` (which refuses to move when the new state would exceed
`B|fst w|`), with `R` as the round polynomial and `StateLoop.gstepBound B = 3n + 2 + B(n)` as
the orbit bound — valid for *every* word by `StateLoop.length_gstep_iterate_le`, which is what
`horbit` demands — pre-composed with `x ↦ ⟨x, start x⟩` (`PolyTimeComputable.pairEncode`). On
the genuine orbit the guard never fires (`StateLoop.gstep_iterate_eq`, from the bound on the
first `N x` states), so the loop's `find?` over `List.range (R|⟨x, start x⟩| + 1)` — a range
containing `N x`, as `R` is monotone (`PolyExpr.eval_mono`) — returns `some (N x)`
(`StateLoop.find?_range_eq_some`), and the payload is `out ⟨x, orbit x (N x)⟩`. -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_stateFind {start step : List Bool → List Bool}
    {acc : List Bool → Bool} {out : List Bool → List Bool}
    (hstart : PolyTimeComputable start) (hstep : PolyTimeComputable step)
    (hacc : PolyTimeComputable fun w => [acc w]) (hout : PolyTimeComputable out)
    (R B : PolyExpr) (N : List Bool → ℕ) (hN : ∀ x, N x ≤ R.eval x.length)
    (hbound : ∀ x i, i ≤ N x → (orbit start step x i).length ≤ B.eval x.length)
    (hfirst : ∀ x i, i < N x → acc (pairEncode x (orbit start step x i)) = false)
    (hlast : ∀ x, acc (pairEncode x (orbit start step x (N x))) = true) :
    PolyTimeComputable fun x => out (pairEncode x (orbit start step x (N x))) := by
  have hF := polyTimeComputable_iterateFind (gstep_poly hstep B) hacc hout R (gstepBound B)
    (fun w i _ => length_gstep_iterate_le step B w i)
  have hpre : PolyTimeComputable fun x => pairEncode x (start x) :=
    polyTimeComputable_id.pairEncode hstart
  convert hF.comp hpre using 1
  funext x
  simp only [Function.comp_apply]
  have horb := gstep_iterate_eq start step B x (N x) (hbound x)
  have hle : N x ≤ R.eval (pairEncode x (start x)).length :=
    (hN x).trans (R.eval_mono (by rw [length_pairEncode]; omega))
  have hfind : (List.range (R.eval (pairEncode x (start x)).length + 1)).find?
      (fun i => acc ((gstep step B)^[i] (pairEncode x (start x)))) = some (N x) := by
    apply find?_range_eq_some hle
    · intro i hi
      rw [horb i hi.le]
      exact hfirst x i hi
    · rw [horb (N x) le_rfl]
      exact hlast x
  rw [hfind]
  exact (congrArg out (horb (N x) le_rfl)).symm

/-- **Polynomially many iterations:** under the orbit bound, `x ↦ g^[R|x|] x` is
polynomial-time computable (the honest `m(n)`-fold evaluations of [PS10, Theorem 35.1]
and the `ℓ(n)`-fold generator expansion of [PS10, Lemma 80.5] are instances).

**Proof sketch.** State loop (`polyTimeComputable_stateFind`, data in
`Complexity.StateLoop.IterLoop`) on the state `⟨1^i, g^[i] x⟩` from `⟨[], x⟩`: the step
appends a token to the unary counter and advances the orbit point (`IterLoop.orbit_eq`);
`acc` is the length test `R|x| ≤ |cnt|` against `1^{R|x|}` of the retained input
(`polyTimeComputable_unaryPoly R`, `polyTimeComputable_lenLe`), `false` below round `R|x|`
and `true` there; `out` projects the orbit point. The states of the first `R|x|` rounds have
length `2i + 2 + |g^[i] x| ≤ 2R|x| + 2 + P|x|` by `horbit`. -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_iterate {g : List Bool → List Bool} (hg : PolyTimeComputable g)
    (R P : PolyExpr)
    (horbit : ∀ (x : List Bool) (i : ℕ), i ≤ R.eval x.length →
      (g^[i] x).length ≤ P.eval x.length) :
    PolyTimeComputable fun x => g^[R.eval x.length] x := by
  have hbound : ∀ x i, i ≤ R.eval x.length →
      (orbit IterLoop.start (IterLoop.step g) x i).length ≤
        (PolyExpr.add (.mul (.const 2) R) (.add (.const 2) P)).eval x.length := by
    intro x i hi
    rw [IterLoop.orbit_eq, length_pairEncode, List.length_replicate]
    have := horbit x i hi
    simp only [PolyExpr.eval_add, PolyExpr.eval_mul, PolyExpr.eval_const]
    omega
  have hfirst : ∀ x i, i < R.eval x.length →
      IterLoop.acc R (pairEncode x (orbit IterLoop.start (IterLoop.step g) x i)) = false := by
    intro x i hi
    rw [IterLoop.orbit_eq]
    simp [IterLoop.acc_eq, hi]
  have hlast : ∀ x, IterLoop.acc R
      (pairEncode x (orbit IterLoop.start (IterLoop.step g) x (R.eval x.length))) = true := by
    intro x
    rw [IterLoop.orbit_eq]
    simp [IterLoop.acc_eq]
  have h := polyTimeComputable_stateFind IterLoop.start_poly (IterLoop.step_poly hg)
    (IterLoop.acc_poly R) IterLoop.out_poly R _ (fun x => R.eval x.length) (fun _ => le_rfl)
    hbound hfirst hlast
  convert h using 1
  funext x
  rw [IterLoop.orbit_eq]
  simp [IterLoop.out_eq]

/-- **Polynomially many iterations with concatenated emissions:** under the orbit bound,
`x ↦ emit x ++ emit (g x) ++ ⋯ ++ emit (g^[R|x|] x)` is polynomial-time computable (the
`m − 1` evaluations of `f` whose outputs form the tuple of Algorithm 38.5, the block
evaluations of `prodFun`, the lazily sampled GGM table).

**Proof sketch.** As `polyTimeComputable_iterate` (state loop, data in
`Complexity.StateLoop.EmitLoop`), with the state `⟨1^i, ⟨g^[i] x, acc_i⟩⟩` where
`acc_i = (List.range i).flatMap (emit ∘ g^[·] x)`: the step appends `emit` of the current
orbit point to the accumulator (`PolyTimeComputable.append`) before advancing
(`EmitLoop.orbit_eq`); the counter test `IterLoop.acc R` fires first at round `R|x|`, where
`out` returns `acc_i ++ emit (g^[i] x)` (`List.range_succ`, `List.flatMap_append`). The
accumulator is bounded by `R|x| · C (P|x| + 1)^c` with `C, c` from `hemit.output_length_le`
(`StateLoop.length_flatMap_range_le`), the `PolyExpr` `R · (normal C c)[P/n]`
(`PolyExpr.eval_subst`). -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_iterateEmit {g emit : List Bool → List Bool}
    (hg : PolyTimeComputable g) (hemit : PolyTimeComputable emit) (R P : PolyExpr)
    (horbit : ∀ (x : List Bool) (i : ℕ), i ≤ R.eval x.length →
      (g^[i] x).length ≤ P.eval x.length) :
    PolyTimeComputable fun x =>
      (List.range (R.eval x.length + 1)).flatMap fun i => emit (g^[i] x) := by
  obtain ⟨Ce, ce, hCe⟩ := hemit.output_length_le
  have hbound : ∀ x i, i ≤ R.eval x.length →
      (orbit EmitLoop.start (EmitLoop.step g emit) x i).length ≤
        (PolyExpr.add (.mul (.const 2) R) (.add (.const 4) (.add (.mul (.const 2) P)
          (.mul R ((PolyExpr.normal Ce ce).subst P))))).eval x.length := by
    intro x i hi
    rw [EmitLoop.orbit_eq, length_pairEncode, length_pairEncode, List.length_replicate]
    have h1 := horbit x i hi
    have hchunk : ∀ j < i, (emit (g^[j] x)).length ≤ Ce * (P.eval x.length + 1) ^ ce := by
      intro j hj
      refine (hCe _).trans (Nat.mul_le_mul_left _ (Nat.pow_le_pow_left ?_ _))
      have := horbit x j (by omega)
      omega
    have h2 := (length_flatMap_range_le _ _ i hchunk).trans (Nat.mul_le_mul_right _ hi)
    simp only [PolyExpr.eval_add, PolyExpr.eval_mul, PolyExpr.eval_const, PolyExpr.eval_subst,
      PolyExpr.eval_normal]
    generalize R.eval x.length * (Ce * (P.eval x.length + 1) ^ ce) = Q at h2
    omega
  have hfirst : ∀ x i, i < R.eval x.length →
      IterLoop.acc R (pairEncode x (orbit EmitLoop.start (EmitLoop.step g emit) x i)) = false := by
    intro x i hi
    rw [EmitLoop.orbit_eq]
    simp [IterLoop.acc_eq, hi]
  have hlast : ∀ x, IterLoop.acc R (pairEncode x
      (orbit EmitLoop.start (EmitLoop.step g emit) x (R.eval x.length))) = true := by
    intro x
    rw [EmitLoop.orbit_eq]
    simp [IterLoop.acc_eq]
  have h := polyTimeComputable_stateFind EmitLoop.start_poly (EmitLoop.step_poly hg hemit)
    (IterLoop.acc_poly R) (EmitLoop.out_poly hemit) R _ (fun x => R.eval x.length)
    (fun _ => le_rfl) hbound hfirst hlast
  convert h using 1
  funext x
  rw [EmitLoop.orbit_eq]
  simp [EmitLoop.out_eq, List.range_succ]

/-- **Majority vote** on a bit string: `w ↦ [decide (|w| < 2 · #true w)]` (strict majority of
`true`) is polynomial-time computable (the vote of the Goldreich–Levin inverter
[PS10, Algorithm 89.6] and of the next-bit predictor).

**Proof sketch.** State loop (`polyTimeComputable_stateFind`, data in
`Complexity.StateLoop.MajLoop`) with `R := var` on the state `⟨rest, ⟨1^{#true}, 1^{#false}⟩⟩`
from `⟨w, ⟨[], []⟩⟩`: each step drops the first bit of `rest` (`StateLoop.tail_poly`) and
appends a token to the counter of its value (`StateLoop.headBit_poly`,
`polyTimeComputable_ite`), so after `i ≤ |w|` rounds the state is
`⟨w.drop i, ⟨1^{#true (w.take i)}, 1^{#false (w.take i)}⟩⟩` (`MajLoop.orbit_eq`); `acc` is the
emptiness test on `rest`, first `true` at round `|w|`; `out` is the length test
`|1 :: 1^{#false}| ≤ |1^{#true}|` (`polyTimeComputable_lenLe`), which is the verdict since
`|w| < 2 #true ↔ #false + 1 ≤ #true` (`List.count_true_add_count_false`). States have length
at most `5|w| + 4`. -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_majority :
    PolyTimeComputable fun w => [decide (w.length < 2 * w.count true)] := by
  have h := polyTimeComputable_stateFind MajLoop.start_poly MajLoop.step_poly MajLoop.acc_poly
    MajLoop.out_poly .var (.add (.mul (.const 5) .var) (.const 4)) List.length (fun _ => le_rfl)
    (fun w i hi => by simpa using MajLoop.orbit_length_le w i hi) MajLoop.acc_orbit_false
    MajLoop.acc_orbit_true
  convert h using 1
  funext w
  exact (MajLoop.out_orbit w).symm

/-- **Bitwise exclusive-or of the two components of a pair** (`List.zipWith xor`) is
polynomial-time computable (the one-time pad of [PS10, Algorithm 92.1 and 99.1] and the
hard-core-bit mask of [PS10, Algorithm 104.3]).

**Proof sketch.** State loop (`polyTimeComputable_stateFind`, data in
`Complexity.StateLoop.XorLoop`) with `R := var` on the state `⟨a', ⟨b', c⟩⟩` from
`⟨fst z, ⟨snd z, []⟩⟩`: each step drops the heads of `a'`, `b'` and appends their xor to `c`
(`StateLoop.tail_poly`, `StateLoop.headBit_poly`, `StateLoop.xor_poly`), so after
`i ≤ min |a| |b|` rounds the state is `⟨a.drop i, ⟨b.drop i, (zipWith xor a b).take i⟩⟩`
(`XorLoop.orbit_eq`, by `List.take_succ` and `List.getElem?_zipWith`); `acc` is "one of `a'`,
`b'` is empty" (`StateLoop.isNil_poly`, `StateLoop.or_poly`), first `true` at round
`min |a| |b| = |zipWith xor a b|` (`List.length_zipWith`), where `out` returns `c`. States have
length at most `5|z| + 4` (`StateLoop.length_pairFstD_add_pairSndD_le`). -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_pairXor :
    PolyTimeComputable fun z => List.zipWith xor (pairFstD z) (pairSndD z) := by
  have hN : ∀ z, XorLoop.rounds z ≤ PolyExpr.var.eval z.length := by
    intro z
    have := length_pairFstD_add_pairSndD_le z
    rw [XorLoop.rounds_eq]
    simp only [PolyExpr.eval_var]
    omega
  have h := polyTimeComputable_stateFind XorLoop.start_poly XorLoop.step_poly XorLoop.acc_poly
    XorLoop.out_poly .var (.add (.mul (.const 5) .var) (.const 4)) XorLoop.rounds hN
    (fun z i hi => by simpa using XorLoop.orbit_length_le z i hi) XorLoop.acc_orbit_false
    XorLoop.acc_orbit_true
  convert h using 1
  funext z
  exact (XorLoop.out_orbit z).symm

/-- **Equality test of the two components of a pair** (`[decide (fst z = snd z)]`) is
polynomial-time computable (the test `f(z_i) = y` of [PS10, Algorithm 38.5] and every
verification step of the reductions).

**Proof sketch.** State loop (`polyTimeComputable_stateFind`, data in
`Complexity.StateLoop.EqLoop`) with `R := var` on the state `⟨a', ⟨b', flag⟩⟩` from
`⟨fst z, ⟨snd z, []⟩⟩`: each step drops the heads of `a'`, `b'` and sets `flag := [true]` if
they differ (`polyTimeComputable_ite` on `StateLoop.xor_poly`), so after `i ≤ min |a| |b|`
rounds the state is `⟨a.drop i, ⟨b.drop i, flag⟩⟩` with `flag = []` iff `a.take i = b.take i`
(`EqLoop.orbit_eq`, `EqLoop.flag_succ`); `acc` is `XorLoop.acc` ("one of `a'`, `b'` is
empty"), first `true` at round `min |a| |b|`, where `out` is the conjunction of the three
emptiness tests `a' = [] ∧ b' = [] ∧ flag = []` (`polyTimeComputable_and`), i.e. `a = b`
(`EqLoop.verdict_eq`: equal lengths and equal prefixes). States have length at most
`5|z| + 5`. -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_pairEq :
    PolyTimeComputable fun z => [decide (pairFstD z = pairSndD z)] := by
  have hN : ∀ z, XorLoop.rounds z ≤ PolyExpr.var.eval z.length := by
    intro z
    have := length_pairFstD_add_pairSndD_le z
    rw [XorLoop.rounds_eq]
    simp only [PolyExpr.eval_var]
    omega
  have h := polyTimeComputable_stateFind XorLoop.start_poly EqLoop.step_poly XorLoop.acc_poly
    EqLoop.out_poly .var (.add (.mul (.const 5) .var) (.const 5)) XorLoop.rounds hN
    (fun z i hi => by simpa using EqLoop.orbit_length_le z i hi) EqLoop.acc_orbit_false
    EqLoop.acc_orbit_true
  convert h using 1
  funext z
  exact (EqLoop.out_orbit z).symm

/-- **Block map:** apply `g` to the consecutive blocks of length `b(|fst z|)` of `snd z` and
concatenate (the first component carries `1^n`; the `⌊|snd z| / b(n)⌋` full blocks are
mapped, a partial last block is dropped). This evaluates `prodFun f q` blockwise
[PS10, Theorem 35.1, Algorithm 38.5] and decodes tuples of `n`-bit strings.

**Proof sketch.** State loop (`polyTimeComputable_stateFind`, data in
`Complexity.StateLoop.BlockMapLoop`) with `R := var` (at most `|z|` blocks) on the state
`⟨rest, c⟩` from `⟨snd z, []⟩`, with `k := b(|fst z|)` read off the retained input: each step
drops `k` bits of `rest` and appends `g (rest.take k)` to `c` (`polyTimeComputable_pairDropPoly b`,
`polyTimeComputable_pairTakePoly b` on `⟨fst z, rest⟩`), so after `i` rounds the state is
`⟨(snd z).drop (i k), g (block 0) ++ ⋯ ++ g (block (i − 1))⟩` (`BlockMapLoop.orbit_eq`,
`List.drop_drop`); `acc` is "`|rest| < k` or `k = 0`" (two length tests against `1^k`), `false`
below round `|snd z| / k` and `true` there (`Nat.le_div_iff_mul_le`, `Nat.lt_mul_div_succ`),
where `out` returns `c`, the statement's `flatMap`. States have length at most
`2|z| + 2 + |z| · C (b(|z|) + 1)^c` with `C, c` from `hg.output_length_le`. -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_blockMap (b : PolyExpr) {g : List Bool → List Bool}
    (hg : PolyTimeComputable g) :
    PolyTimeComputable fun z =>
      (List.range ((pairSndD z).length / b.eval (pairFstD z).length)).flatMap fun i =>
        g (((pairSndD z).drop (i * b.eval (pairFstD z).length)).take (b.eval (pairFstD z).length)) := by
  obtain ⟨C, c, hC⟩ := hg.output_length_le
  have hN : ∀ z, BlockMapLoop.rounds b z ≤ PolyExpr.var.eval z.length := by
    intro z
    have := length_pairFstD_add_pairSndD_le z
    rw [BlockMapLoop.rounds_eq]
    exact (Nat.div_le_self _ _).trans (by simp only [PolyExpr.eval_var]; omega)
  have h := polyTimeComputable_stateFind BlockMapLoop.start_poly (BlockMapLoop.step_poly b hg)
    (BlockMapLoop.acc_poly b) BlockMapLoop.out_poly .var _ (BlockMapLoop.rounds b) hN
    (BlockMapLoop.orbit_length_le b g C c hC) (BlockMapLoop.acc_orbit_false b g)
    (BlockMapLoop.acc_orbit_true b g)
  convert h using 1
  funext z
  rw [BlockMapLoop.out_orbit, BlockMapLoop.rounds_eq]

end Complexity

/-

Authors: TCSlib Contributors

import TCSlib.Complexity.Randomized.Classes

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# The Sipser–Gács theorem: BPP ⊆ Σ₂ ∩ Π₂

Arora–Barak's Theorem 7.15: `BPP` sits in the second level of the polynomial
hierarchy.  The proof shows `BPP ⊆ Σ₂`: after error reduction the set `S_x`
of accepting random strings is either almost all of `{0,1}^m` or a tiny
fraction, and two quantifier alternations — "there exist shifts `u₁,…,u_k`
whose translates of `S_x` cover `{0,1}^m`" — distinguish the two cases.

## Main definitions

* `Randomized.InSigma2`, `Randomized.InPi2` — verifier-style `Σ₂ᵖ` and `Π₂ᵖ`
  (two quantified witness strings over an efficient predicate), the classes
  in which [AB09, Thm 7.15] places `BPP`.
* `Randomized.shiftOrVerifier` — the predicate
  `(u, v) ↦ ⋁_{i ≤ k} M(x, v ⊕ uᵢ)` built from a `BPP` verifier, where `u`
  encodes the `k` shifts `u₁,…,u_k` as one concatenated string.

## Main results

* `Randomized.bpp_subset_sigma2` — `BPP ⊆ Σ₂ᵖ`, the core argument.
* `Randomized.sipser_gacs` — [AB09, Thm 7.15].

## Deviations from the source

`Σ₂ᵖ` is defined here in the same certificate style as the chapter's other
classes (an efficient two-witness predicate with polynomially-bounded
witness lengths), rather than via oracle machines or the book's Chapter 5
definitions; `Π₂ᵖ` is its complement-dual, and `BPP ⊆ Σ₂ᵖ ∩ Π₂ᵖ` becomes
"`L` and `Lᶜ` are both `Σ₂`".  As throughout `Randomized.Classes`,
"polynomial time" is the abstract notion `E`, and the single computability
fact the proof uses — that the shifted-OR predicate built from an efficient
verifier is an efficient two-witness predicate — is the explicit hypothesis
`hShift`.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009.
-/

namespace Randomized

variable (E : VerifierModel)

/-- `L ∈ Σ₂ᵖ`, certificate-style: there is an efficient two-witness
predicate `N` and polynomial witness-length bounds such that
`x ∈ L ↔ ∃ u ∀ v, N(x, u, v)`.  [AB09, Thm 7.15]'s target class, defined in
the style of [AB09, Def 7.3] (see the module docstring's **Deviations**). -/
def InSigma2 (L : Language Bool) : Prop :=
  ∃ (N : List Bool → List Bool → List Bool → Bool) (a₁ k₁ a₂ k₂ : ℕ),
    E.EffTwoWitness N ∧
    ∀ x : List Bool,
      x ∈ L ↔ ∃ u : List Bool, u.length = polyLen a₁ k₁ x.length ∧
        ∀ v : List Bool, v.length = polyLen a₂ k₂ x.length → N x u v = true

/-- `L ∈ Π₂ᵖ` iff its complement is in `Σ₂ᵖ` (equivalently,
`x ∈ L ↔ ∀ u ∃ v, …`). -/
def InPi2 (L : Language Bool) : Prop :=
  InSigma2 E Lᶜ

/-- The two-witness predicate `(u, v) ↦ ⋁_{i < k} M(x, v ⊕ uᵢ)`, where the
first witness `u` is the concatenation of `k` shift strings `u₁,…,u_k` of
length `p(|x|)` each and `⊕` is bitwise XOR: the predicate with which
[AB09, Thm 7.15]'s proof expresses "the translates of the accepting set by
`u₁,…,u_k` cover all random strings `v`". -/
def shiftOrVerifier (M : List Bool → List Bool → Bool) (p k : ℕ → ℕ) :
    List Bool → List Bool → List Bool → Bool := fun x u v =>
  (List.range (k x.length)).any fun i =>
    M x (List.zipWith xor v ((u.drop (i * p x.length)).take (p x.length)))

/-- `E` recognizes the shifted-OR construction: from an efficient Boolean
verifier, the predicate `shiftOrVerifier M p k` is an efficient two-witness
predicate for polynomial block lengths `p` and shift counts `k` (closure of
polynomial time under XOR-shifts and a polynomial OR). -/
def ClosedUnderShiftOr : Prop :=
  ∀ M a k a' k', E.Eff (boolVerifier M) →
    E.EffTwoWitness (shiftOrVerifier M (polyLen a k) (polyLen a' k'))

section Helpers

/-- `zipWith` of two `ofFn` lists is the `ofFn` of the pointwise image. -/
theorem zipWith_ofFn {α β γ : Type*} {m : ℕ} (f : α → β → γ)
    (a : Fin m → α) (b : Fin m → β) :
    List.zipWith f (List.ofFn a) (List.ofFn b) =
      List.ofFn (fun i => f (a i) (b i)) := by
  apply List.ext_getElem
  · simp
  · intro i h1 h2
    simp

/-- XOR-ing the random string with a fixed mask (on the left) preserves
probabilities: the map `r ↦ c ⊕ r` is an involution of `{0,1}^m`.

**Proof sketch.** The two counting sets are matched by
`Finset.card_nbij'` with `r ↦ (i ↦ c i xor r i)` as both the forward and
the inverse map: XOR by a fixed mask undoes itself, checked bitwise by
cases on the two bits, and `zipWith_ofFn` rewrites the list-level event
into the pointwise form the bijection transports. -/
theorem randProb_xor_right {m : ℕ} (c : Fin m → Bool)
    (P : List Bool → Prop) [DecidablePred P] :
    randProb m (fun l => P (List.zipWith xor (List.ofFn c) l)) =
      randProb m P := by
  unfold randProb
  congr 2
  have hinv : ∀ r : Fin m → Bool,
      (fun i => xor (c i) (xor (c i) (r i))) = r := by
    intro r
    funext i
    cases c i <;> cases r i <;> rfl
  refine Finset.card_nbij' (fun r => fun i => xor (c i) (r i))
    (fun r => fun i => xor (c i) (r i)) ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_
  · intro r hr
    simp only [Finset.coe_filter, Set.mem_setOf_eq, Finset.mem_univ,
      true_and] at hr ⊢
    show P (List.ofFn fun i => xor (c i) (r i))
    rw [← zipWith_ofFn]
    exact hr
  · intro r hr
    simp only [Finset.coe_filter, Set.mem_setOf_eq, Finset.mem_univ,
      true_and] at hr ⊢
    show P (List.zipWith xor (List.ofFn c)
      (List.ofFn fun i => xor (c i) (r i)))
    rw [zipWith_ofFn, hinv r]
    exact hr
  · intro r _
    funext i
    show xor (c i) (xor (c i) (r i)) = r i
    cases c i <;> cases r i <;> rfl
  · intro r _
    funext i
    show xor (c i) (xor (c i) (r i)) = r i
    cases c i <;> cases r i <;> rfl

/-- XOR-ing the random string with a fixed mask (on the right) preserves
probabilities. -/
theorem randProb_xor_left {m : ℕ} (c : Fin m → Bool)
    (P : List Bool → Prop) [DecidablePred P] :
    randProb m (fun l => P (List.zipWith xor l (List.ofFn c))) =
      randProb m P := by
  have hswap : ∀ r : Fin m → Bool,
      List.zipWith xor (List.ofFn r) (List.ofFn c) =
        List.zipWith xor (List.ofFn c) (List.ofFn r) := by
    intro r
    rw [zipWith_ofFn, zipWith_ofFn]
    congr 1
    funext i
    cases c i <;> cases r i <;> rfl
  rw [randProb_congr (B := fun l => P (List.zipWith xor (List.ofFn c) l))
    fun r => by rw [hswap r]]
  exact randProb_xor_right c P

/-- The exponential beats the linear shift count:
`(19A+20)·X < 2^{(A+7)·X}` for `X ≥ 1`.  (The book's choice `k = ⌈m/n⌉+1`
needs `k < 2^n`, which fails at small `n`; balancing against the error
exponent instead works at every length.)

**Proof sketch.** Two ingredients: `128·X ≤ 128^X` (induction on `X`) and
`A + 1 ≤ 2^A` (`Nat.lt_two_pow_self`).  Splitting
`2^{(A+7)·X} = (2^A)^X · 128^X`, the chain
`(19A+20)·X < 128(A+1)·X = (A+1)·(128·X) ≤ 2^A·(128·X) ≤ (2^A)^X·128^X`
closes the bound, using `2^A ≤ (2^A)^X` for `X ≥ 1` in the last step. -/
theorem shift_count_lt_two_pow (A X : ℕ) (hX : 1 ≤ X) :
    (19 * A + 20) * X < 2 ^ ((A + 7) * X) := by
  have h128 : 128 * X ≤ 128 ^ X := by
    clear hX
    induction X with
    | zero => omega
    | succ Y ih =>
      rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos Y with rfl | hY'
      · norm_num
      · have h1 : 128 ^ (Y + 1) = 128 ^ Y * 128 := pow_succ 128 Y
        nlinarith
  have hA : A + 1 ≤ 2 ^ A := Nat.lt_two_pow_self
  have hsplit : 2 ^ ((A + 7) * X) = (2 ^ A) ^ X * 128 ^ X := by
    rw [pow_mul, pow_add, mul_pow]
    norm_num
  have h3 : 2 ^ A ≤ (2 ^ A) ^ X := by
    conv_lhs => rw [← pow_one (2 ^ A)]
    exact Nat.pow_le_pow_right Nat.one_le_two_pow hX
  calc (19 * A + 20) * X < (128 * (A + 1)) * X :=
      (Nat.mul_lt_mul_right (by omega)).mpr (by omega)
    _ = (A + 1) * (128 * X) := by ring
    _ ≤ (2 ^ A) * (128 * X) := Nat.mul_le_mul_right _ hA
    _ ≤ (2 ^ A) ^ X * 128 ^ X := Nat.mul_le_mul h3 h128
    _ = 2 ^ ((A + 7) * X) := hsplit.symm

/-- The tail crunch for the constant advantage `1/6`: `(18b+18)·(n+1)^e`
majority repetitions drive the error below `2^{-b(n+1)^e}`.

**Proof sketch.** With `x = 4·(1/6)² = 1/9` the Bernoulli hypothesis
`m·x ≥ 1` holds at `m = 9`, and the exponent
`⌊(18b+18)(n+1)^e/2⌋ = (9b+9)(n+1)^e` dominates `9·(b(n+1)^e + 1)`, so
`one_sub_pow_le_half_pow` bounds the power by `(1/2)^{b(n+1)^e + 1}`; the
leading factor `2` absorbs the extra halving. -/
theorem const_tail_bound (b e n : ℕ) :
    2 * (1 - 4 * (1/6 : ℚ) ^ 2) ^ (polyLen (18 * b + 18) e n / 2) ≤
      (1/2 : ℚ) ^ polyLen b e n := by
  have hx0 : (0:ℚ) ≤ 4 * (1/6 : ℚ) ^ 2 := by norm_num
  have hx1 : 4 * (1/6 : ℚ) ^ 2 ≤ 1 := by norm_num
  have hm : 1 ≤ ((9 : ℕ) : ℚ) * (4 * (1/6 : ℚ) ^ 2) := by norm_num
  have hexp : 9 * (polyLen b e n + 1) ≤ polyLen (18 * b + 18) e n / 2 := by
    unfold polyLen
    have h1 : (18 * b + 18) * (n + 1) ^ e / 2 = (9 * b + 9) * (n + 1) ^ e := by
      rw [show 18 * b + 18 = 2 * (9 * b + 9) from by ring, mul_assoc,
        Nat.mul_div_cancel_left _ (by norm_num)]
    rw [h1]
    have hge : 1 ≤ (n + 1) ^ e := Nat.one_le_pow _ _ (by omega)
    nlinarith
  have hhalf := one_sub_pow_le_half_pow hx0 hx1 hm hexp
  calc 2 * (1 - 4 * (1/6 : ℚ) ^ 2) ^ (polyLen (18 * b + 18) e n / 2)
      ≤ 2 * (1/2 : ℚ) ^ (polyLen b e n + 1) :=
        mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hhalf (by norm_num)
    _ = (1/2 : ℚ) ^ polyLen b e n := by
        rw [pow_succ]
        ring

/-- Error reduction with an explicit error schedule `2^{-b(n+1)^e}` and an
explicit randomness schedule — the form [AB09, Thm 7.15]'s proof consumes:
a `BPP` witness `(M₀, a₀, k₀)` amplified by `(18b+18)·(n+1)^e` majority
repetitions.

**Proof sketch.** The witness is `majorityVerifier M₀` over
`K = (18b+18)·(n+1)^e` blocks of `q = a₀·(n+1)^{k₀}` bits.  In each of the
two symmetric cases the failure event is a vote-count tail: for `x ∈ L`
the *false* votes reach `K/2` (rephrased through the complementary
vote-count identity), for `x ∉ L` the *true* votes do.  A single block
errs with probability `≤ 1/3 = 1/2 − 1/6`, so `randProb_tail_le` bounds
the tail by `2·(1 − 4·(1/6)²)^{⌊K/2⌋}`, which `const_tail_bound` crunches
to `(1/2)^{b(n+1)^e}`. -/
theorem amplify_concrete (hMaj : ClosedUnderMajority E) {L : Language Bool}
    {M₀ : List Bool → List Bool → Bool} {a₀ k₀ : ℕ}
    (hM₀ : E.Eff (boolVerifier M₀))
    (hprop₀ : ∀ x : List Bool,
      (x ∈ L → 2/3 ≤
        randProb (polyLen a₀ k₀ x.length) fun r => M₀ x r = true) ∧
      (x ∉ L → 2/3 ≤
        randProb (polyLen a₀ k₀ x.length) fun r => M₀ x r = false))
    (b e : ℕ) :
    ∃ M : List Bool → List Bool → Bool,
      E.Eff (boolVerifier M) ∧
      ∀ x : List Bool,
        (x ∈ L → 1 - (1/2 : ℚ) ^ polyLen b e x.length ≤
          randProb (polyLen ((18 * b + 18) * a₀) (e + k₀) x.length)
            fun r => M x r = true) ∧
        (x ∉ L → 1 - (1/2 : ℚ) ^ polyLen b e x.length ≤
          randProb (polyLen ((18 * b + 18) * a₀) (e + k₀) x.length)
            fun r => M x r = false) := by
  classical
  refine ⟨majorityVerifier M₀ (polyLen a₀ k₀) (polyLen (18 * b + 18) e),
    hMaj M₀ a₀ k₀ (18 * b + 18) e hM₀, fun x => ?_⟩
  have hqK : polyLen ((18 * b + 18) * a₀) (e + k₀) x.length
      = polyLen (18 * b + 18) e x.length * polyLen a₀ k₀ x.length := by
    unfold polyLen
    ring
  set n := x.length with hn
  set q := polyLen a₀ k₀ n with hq
  set K := polyLen (18 * b + 18) e n with hK
  have hmaj_iff : ∀ l : List Bool,
      majorityVerifier M₀ (polyLen a₀ k₀)
          (polyLen (18 * b + 18) e) x l = true ↔
        K < 2 * blockCount q K (M₀ x) l := by
    intro l
    show decide (K < 2 * blockCount q K (M₀ x) l) = true ↔ _
    rw [decide_eq_true_iff]
  have hcount : ∀ l : List Bool,
      blockCount q K (M₀ x) l +
        blockCount q K (fun l' => !(M₀ x l')) l = K := by
    intro l
    unfold blockCount
    have haux : ∀ (p : ℕ → Bool) (li : List ℕ),
        li.countP p + li.countP (fun i => !(p i)) = li.length := by
      intro p li
      induction li with
      | nil => simp
      | cons hd tl ih =>
        rw [List.countP_cons, List.countP_cons, List.length_cons]
        rcases hp : p hd <;> simp [hp] <;> omega
    rw [haux (fun i => M₀ x ((l.drop (i * q)).take q)) (List.range K)]
    exact List.length_range
  have hs_false : randProb q (fun l => M₀ x l = false)
      = 1 - randProb q (fun l => M₀ x l = true) := randProb_bool_false (M₀ x)
  have hs_not : randProb q (fun l => (!(M₀ x l)) = true)
      = randProb q (fun l => M₀ x l = false) :=
    randProb_congr fun r => by simp
  rw [hqK]
  constructor
  · intro hx
    have hW := (hprop₀ x).1 hx
    have hsf : randProb q (fun l => (!(M₀ x l)) = true) ≤ 1/2 - 1/6 := by
      rw [hs_not, hs_false]
      linarith
    have htail := randProb_tail_le q K (fun l' => !(M₀ x l'))
      (by norm_num : (0:ℚ) ≤ 1/6) hsf
    have hev : randProb (K * q)
        (fun l => ¬ (majorityVerifier M₀ (polyLen a₀ k₀)
          (polyLen (18 * b + 18) e) x l = true))
        = randProb (K * q) (fun l =>
            K ≤ 2 * blockCount q K (fun l' => !(M₀ x l')) l) :=
      randProb_congr fun r => by
        rw [hmaj_iff]
        have := hcount (List.ofFn r)
        constructor
        · intro h
          omega
        · intro h
          omega
    have hnot := randProb_not (m := K * q)
      (fun l => majorityVerifier M₀ (polyLen a₀ k₀)
        (polyLen (18 * b + 18) e) x l = true)
    rw [hev] at hnot
    have hfin : randProb (K * q) (fun l =>
        K ≤ 2 * blockCount q K (fun l' => !(M₀ x l')) l)
        ≤ (1/2 : ℚ) ^ polyLen b e n := le_trans htail (by
      rw [hK]
      exact const_tail_bound b e n)
    linarith
  · intro hx
    have hW := (hprop₀ x).2 hx
    have hst : randProb q (fun l => M₀ x l = true) ≤ 1/2 - 1/6 := by
      have := hs_false
      linarith
    have htail := randProb_tail_le q K (M₀ x)
      (by norm_num : (0:ℚ) ≤ 1/6) hst
    have hmono : randProb (K * q)
        (fun l => ¬ (majorityVerifier M₀ (polyLen a₀ k₀)
          (polyLen (18 * b + 18) e) x l = false))
        ≤ randProb (K * q) (fun l => K ≤ 2 * blockCount q K (M₀ x) l) := by
      refine randProb_mono fun r hr => ?_
      have h1 : majorityVerifier M₀ (polyLen a₀ k₀)
          (polyLen (18 * b + 18) e) x (List.ofFn r) = true := by
        rcases hb : majorityVerifier M₀ (polyLen a₀ k₀)
          (polyLen (18 * b + 18) e) x (List.ofFn r)
        · exact absurd hb hr
        · rfl
      have h2 := (hmaj_iff (List.ofFn r)).mp h1
      omega
    have hnot := randProb_not (m := K * q)
      (fun l => majorityVerifier M₀ (polyLen a₀ k₀)
        (polyLen (18 * b + 18) e) x l = false)
    have hfin : randProb (K * q) (fun l =>
        K ≤ 2 * blockCount q K (M₀ x) l)
        ≤ (1/2 : ℚ) ^ polyLen b e n := le_trans htail (by
      rw [hK]
      exact const_tail_bound b e n)
    linarith

end Helpers

/-- A set smaller than the whole type misses some element. -/
theorem exists_notMem_of_card_lt {α : Type*} [Fintype α]
    {S : Finset α} (h : S.card < Fintype.card α) : ∃ a, a ∉ S := by
  by_contra hall
  push_neg at hall
  have heq : S = Finset.univ := Finset.eq_univ_iff_forall.mpr hall
  rw [heq, Finset.card_univ] at h
  exact absurd h (lt_irrefl _)

/-- **`BPP ⊆ Σ₂ᵖ`**, the core of [AB09, Thm 7.15].

**Proof sketch.** *Setup*: amplify the `BPP` witness (`amplify_concrete`
at `b = a₀ + 7`, `e = k₀`) to error `2^{-T}`, `T = (a₀+7)·(n+1)^{k₀}`, on
`m` random bits; the `Σ₂` predicate is `shiftOrVerifier` with
`ks = (19a₀+20)·(n+1)^{k₀}` shift blocks, and two counting claims are
recorded: `ks < 2^T` (`shift_count_lt_two_pow`) and `m < T·ks`.
*Completeness* (`x ∈ L`, the probabilistic method): for each fixed `v`,
all `ks` independent shift blocks miss `v`'s translate with probability
`(1 − s)^{ks} ≤ 2^{-T·ks}` — the binomial distribution
`randProb_blockCount` at `j = 0` after the XOR-invariance
`randProb_xor_right` — so a union bound over the `2^m` choices of `v`
covers less than the `2^{ks·m}` shift tuples by the second claim, and
some concatenated shift string `u` hits every `v`.  *Soundness*
(`x ∉ L`, counting): each of the `ks` translates of the accepting set
has measure `≤ 2^{-T}` (`randProb_xor_left`), so by the first claim they
cover fewer than `2^m` strings, and `exists_notMem_of_card_lt` exhibits
an uncovered `v'` falsifying the assumed `∀ v` witness. -/
theorem bpp_subset_sigma2 (hMaj : ClosedUnderMajority E)
    (hShift : ClosedUnderShiftOr E) {L : Language Bool} (hL : InBPP E L) :
    InSigma2 E L := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨M₀, a₀, k₀, hM₀, hprop₀⟩ := hL
  obtain ⟨M, hM, hprop⟩ := amplify_concrete E hMaj hM₀ hprop₀ (a₀ + 7) k₀
  refine ⟨shiftOrVerifier M (polyLen ((18 * (a₀ + 7) + 18) * a₀) (k₀ + k₀))
      (polyLen (19 * a₀ + 20) k₀),
    (19 * a₀ + 20) * ((18 * (a₀ + 7) + 18) * a₀), k₀ + (k₀ + k₀),
    (18 * (a₀ + 7) + 18) * a₀, k₀ + k₀,
    hShift M ((18 * (a₀ + 7) + 18) * a₀) (k₀ + k₀) (19 * a₀ + 20) k₀ hM,
    fun x => ?_⟩
  set n := x.length with hn
  set m := polyLen ((18 * (a₀ + 7) + 18) * a₀) (k₀ + k₀) n with hm
  set T := polyLen (a₀ + 7) k₀ n with hT
  set ks := polyLen (19 * a₀ + 20) k₀ n with hks
  have hX1 : 1 ≤ (n + 1) ^ k₀ := Nat.one_le_pow _ _ (by omega)
  have hulen : polyLen ((19 * a₀ + 20) * ((18 * (a₀ + 7) + 18) * a₀))
      (k₀ + (k₀ + k₀)) n = ks * m := by
    rw [hks, hm]
    unfold polyLen
    ring
  have hclaim1 : ((ks : ℕ) : ℚ) < 2 ^ T := by
    rw [hks, hT]
    unfold polyLen
    exact_mod_cast shift_count_lt_two_pow a₀ ((n + 1) ^ k₀) hX1
  have hclaim2 : m < T * ks := by
    rw [hm, hT, hks]
    unfold polyLen
    have hXX : (n + 1) ^ (k₀ + k₀) = (n + 1) ^ k₀ * (n + 1) ^ k₀ :=
      pow_add _ _ _
    rw [hXX]
    have hC : (18 * (a₀ + 7) + 18) * a₀ < (a₀ + 7) * (19 * a₀ + 20) := by
      nlinarith
    calc (18 * (a₀ + 7) + 18) * a₀ * ((n + 1) ^ k₀ * (n + 1) ^ k₀)
        < (a₀ + 7) * (19 * a₀ + 20) * ((n + 1) ^ k₀ * (n + 1) ^ k₀) := by
          have hXp : 0 < (n + 1) ^ k₀ * (n + 1) ^ k₀ := by positivity
          exact (Nat.mul_lt_mul_right hXp).mpr hC
      _ = (a₀ + 7) * (n + 1) ^ k₀ * ((19 * a₀ + 20) * (n + 1) ^ k₀) := by
          ring
  have hacc := hprop x
  rw [← hn, ← hm, ← hT] at hacc
  constructor
  · -- `x ∈ L`: the probabilistic method produces covering shifts
    intro hx
    have haccx := hacc.1 hx
    have hs1 : randProb m (fun l => M x l = true) ≤ 1 := randProb_le_one
    have hfail : 1 - randProb m (fun l => M x l = true) ≤ (1/2 : ℚ) ^ T := by
      linarith
    have hfail0 : (0:ℚ) ≤ 1 - randProb m (fun l => M x l = true) := by
      linarith
    have hbadv : ∀ v : Fin m → Bool,
        ((Finset.univ.filter fun u : Fin (ks * m) → Bool =>
          blockCount m ks (fun w => M x (List.zipWith xor (List.ofFn v) w))
            (List.ofFn u) = 0).card : ℚ)
          ≤ (1/2 : ℚ) ^ (T * ks) * 2 ^ (ks * m) := by
      intro v
      have hsB : randProb m (fun w =>
          M x (List.zipWith xor (List.ofFn v) w) = true)
          = randProb m (fun l => M x l = true) :=
        randProb_xor_right v (fun w => M x w = true)
      have hdist := randProb_blockCount m
        (fun w => M x (List.zipWith xor (List.ofFn v) w)) ks 0
        (Nat.zero_le _)
      rw [hsB] at hdist
      simp only [Nat.choose_zero_right, pow_zero, Nat.cast_one, one_mul,
        Nat.sub_zero] at hdist
      have hle : randProb (ks * m) (fun l =>
          blockCount m ks (fun w => M x (List.zipWith xor (List.ofFn v) w))
            l = 0) ≤ (1/2 : ℚ) ^ (T * ks) := by
        rw [hdist]
        calc (1 - randProb m (fun l => M x l = true)) ^ ks
            ≤ ((1/2 : ℚ) ^ T) ^ ks := pow_le_pow_left₀ hfail0 hfail ks
          _ = (1/2 : ℚ) ^ (T * ks) := by rw [← pow_mul]
      unfold randProb at hle
      rw [div_le_iff₀ (by positivity)] at hle
      exact hle
    have hexists : ∃ u : Fin (ks * m) → Bool, ∀ v : Fin m → Bool,
        blockCount m ks (fun w => M x (List.zipWith xor (List.ofFn v) w))
          (List.ofFn u) ≠ 0 := by
      by_contra hforall
      push_neg at hforall
      have hcover : (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin (ks * m) → Bool)) ⊆
          Finset.univ.biUnion (fun v : Fin m → Bool =>
            Finset.univ.filter fun u : Fin (ks * m) → Bool =>
              blockCount m ks
                (fun w => M x (List.zipWith xor (List.ofFn v) w))
                (List.ofFn u) = 0) := by
        intro u _
        obtain ⟨v, hv⟩ := hforall u
        exact Finset.mem_biUnion.mpr ⟨v, Finset.mem_univ v,
          Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_univ u, hv⟩⟩
      have h1 : (2:ℕ) ^ (ks * m) ≤ (Finset.univ.biUnion
          (fun v : Fin m → Bool =>
            Finset.univ.filter fun u : Fin (ks * m) → Bool =>
              blockCount m ks
                (fun w => M x (List.zipWith xor (List.ofFn v) w))
                (List.ofFn u) = 0)).card := by
        rw [← card_univ_bitstrings (ks * m)]
        exact Finset.card_le_card hcover
      have h2 := Finset.card_biUnion_le
        (s := (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin m → Bool)))
        (t := fun v : Fin m → Bool =>
          Finset.univ.filter fun u : Fin (ks * m) → Bool =>
            blockCount m ks
              (fun w => M x (List.zipWith xor (List.ofFn v) w))
              (List.ofFn u) = 0)
      have h3 : ((2:ℚ)) ^ (ks * m) ≤
          ∑ v : Fin m → Bool, ((Finset.univ.filter
            fun u : Fin (ks * m) → Bool =>
              blockCount m ks
                (fun w => M x (List.zipWith xor (List.ofFn v) w))
                (List.ofFn u) = 0).card : ℚ) := by
        rw [← Nat.cast_sum]
        exact_mod_cast le_trans h1 h2
      have h4 : ((2:ℚ)) ^ (ks * m) ≤
          (2:ℚ) ^ m * ((1/2 : ℚ) ^ (T * ks) * 2 ^ (ks * m)) := by
        calc ((2:ℚ)) ^ (ks * m)
            ≤ ∑ _v : Fin m → Bool, ((1/2 : ℚ) ^ (T * ks) * 2 ^ (ks * m)) :=
              le_trans h3 (Finset.sum_le_sum fun v _ => hbadv v)
          _ = (2:ℚ) ^ m * ((1/2 : ℚ) ^ (T * ks) * 2 ^ (ks * m)) := by
              rw [Finset.sum_const, card_univ_bitstrings, nsmul_eq_mul]
              push_cast
              ring
      have hlt : ((2:ℚ)) ^ m < 2 ^ (T * ks) :=
        pow_lt_pow_right₀ (by norm_num) hclaim2
      have hfrac : (2:ℚ) ^ m * (1/2 : ℚ) ^ (T * ks) < 1 := by
        rw [div_pow, one_pow, mul_one_div, div_lt_one (by positivity)]
        exact hlt
      nlinarith [pow_pos (show (0:ℚ) < 2 by norm_num) (ks * m), h4, hfrac]
    obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := hexists
    refine ⟨List.ofFn u, ?_, ?_⟩
    · rw [List.length_ofFn]
      exact hulen.symm
    · intro v hvlen
      obtain ⟨v', hv'⟩ := exists_ofFn_eq hvlen
      have hbc := hu v'
      have hpos : 0 < blockCount m ks
          (fun w => M x (List.zipWith xor (List.ofFn v') w))
          (List.ofFn u) := Nat.pos_of_ne_zero hbc
      unfold blockCount at hpos
      rw [List.countP_pos_iff] at hpos
      obtain ⟨i, hi_mem, hi⟩ := hpos
      show (List.range ks).any _ = true
      rw [List.any_eq_true]
      refine ⟨i, hi_mem, ?_⟩
      rw [hv']
      exact hi
  · -- `x ∉ L`: no shifts can cover, by counting the accepted strings
    rintro ⟨u, hu_len, hall⟩
    by_contra hx
    have hrej := hacc.2 hx
    have hboolf := randProb_bool_false (m := m) (M x)
    have hst : randProb m (fun l => M x l = true) ≤ (1/2 : ℚ) ^ T := by
      linarith
    rw [hulen] at hu_len
    have hblock_len : ∀ i, i < ks → ((u.drop (i * m)).take m).length = m := by
      intro i hi
      have h1 : (i + 1) * m ≤ ks * m := Nat.mul_le_mul_right m (by omega)
      rw [Nat.succ_mul] at h1
      rw [List.length_take, List.length_drop, hu_len]
      omega
    have hacc_card : ∀ i ∈ Finset.range ks,
        ((Finset.univ.filter fun v : Fin m → Bool =>
          M x (List.zipWith xor (List.ofFn v) ((u.drop (i * m)).take m))
            = true).card : ℚ) ≤ (1/2 : ℚ) ^ T * 2 ^ m := by
      intro i hi
      obtain ⟨ci, hci⟩ := exists_ofFn_eq (hblock_len i (Finset.mem_range.mp hi))
      have hxor : randProb m (fun l =>
          M x (List.zipWith xor l (List.ofFn ci)) = true)
          = randProb m (fun l => M x l = true) :=
        randProb_xor_left ci (fun w => M x w = true)
      have hle : randProb m (fun l =>
          M x (List.zipWith xor l ((u.drop (i * m)).take m)) = true)
          ≤ (1/2 : ℚ) ^ T := by
        rw [show (u.drop (i * m)).take m = List.ofFn ci from hci, hxor]
        exact hst
      unfold randProb at hle
      rw [div_le_iff₀ (by positivity)] at hle
      exact hle
    have hcover : (Finset.univ.filter fun v : Fin m → Bool =>
        ∃ i ∈ Finset.range ks,
          M x (List.zipWith xor (List.ofFn v) ((u.drop (i * m)).take m))
            = true) ⊆
        (Finset.range ks).biUnion (fun i =>
          Finset.univ.filter fun v : Fin m → Bool =>
            M x (List.zipWith xor (List.ofFn v) ((u.drop (i * m)).take m))
              = true) := by
      intro v hv
      rw [Finset.mem_filter] at hv
      obtain ⟨-, i, hi, hMi⟩ := hv
      exact Finset.mem_biUnion.mpr ⟨i, hi,
        Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_univ _, hMi⟩⟩
    have hcard : ((Finset.univ.filter fun v : Fin m → Bool =>
        ∃ i ∈ Finset.range ks,
          M x (List.zipWith xor (List.ofFn v) ((u.drop (i * m)).take m))
            = true).card : ℚ) < 2 ^ m := by
      have h1 := Finset.card_le_card hcover
      have h2 := Finset.card_biUnion_le (s := Finset.range ks)
        (t := fun i => Finset.univ.filter fun v : Fin m → Bool =>
          M x (List.zipWith xor (List.ofFn v) ((u.drop (i * m)).take m))
            = true)
      have h3 : ((Finset.univ.filter fun v : Fin m → Bool =>
          ∃ i ∈ Finset.range ks, M x (List.zipWith xor (List.ofFn v)
            ((u.drop (i * m)).take m)) = true).card : ℚ) ≤
          ∑ i ∈ Finset.range ks, ((Finset.univ.filter
            fun v : Fin m → Bool => M x (List.zipWith xor (List.ofFn v)
              ((u.drop (i * m)).take m)) = true).card : ℚ) := by
        rw [← Nat.cast_sum]
        exact_mod_cast le_trans h1 h2
      have h6 : (ks : ℚ) * ((1/2 : ℚ) ^ T * 2 ^ m) < 2 ^ m := by
        have h7 : (ks : ℚ) * (1/2 : ℚ) ^ T < 1 := by
          rw [div_pow, one_pow, mul_one_div, div_lt_one (by positivity)]
          exact hclaim1
        nlinarith [pow_pos (show (0:ℚ) < 2 by norm_num) m, h7]
      calc ((Finset.univ.filter fun v : Fin m → Bool =>
          ∃ i ∈ Finset.range ks, M x (List.zipWith xor (List.ofFn v)
            ((u.drop (i * m)).take m)) = true).card : ℚ)
          ≤ ∑ i ∈ Finset.range ks, ((Finset.univ.filter
              fun v : Fin m → Bool => M x (List.zipWith xor (List.ofFn v)
                ((u.drop (i * m)).take m)) = true).card : ℚ) := h3
        _ ≤ ∑ _i ∈ Finset.range ks, ((1/2 : ℚ) ^ T * 2 ^ m) :=
            Finset.sum_le_sum hacc_card
        _ = (ks : ℚ) * ((1/2 : ℚ) ^ T * 2 ^ m) := by
            rw [Finset.sum_const, Finset.card_range, nsmul_eq_mul]
        _ < 2 ^ m := h6
    have hcardN : (Finset.univ.filter fun v : Fin m → Bool =>
        ∃ i ∈ Finset.range ks,
          M x (List.zipWith xor (List.ofFn v) ((u.drop (i * m)).take m))
            = true).card < Fintype.card (Fin m → Bool) := by
      have hcardfun : Fintype.card (Fin m → Bool) = 2 ^ m := by
        rw [← card_univ_bitstrings m, Finset.card_univ]
      rw [hcardfun]
      exact_mod_cast hcard
    obtain ⟨v', hv'⟩ := exists_notMem_of_card_lt hcardN
    have hvfalse : ∀ i ∈ List.range ks,
        M x (List.zipWith xor (List.ofFn v')
          ((u.drop (i * m)).take m)) = false := by
      intro i hi
      rw [List.mem_range] at hi
      rcases hb : M x (List.zipWith xor (List.ofFn v')
          ((u.drop (i * m)).take m))
      · rfl
      · exact absurd (Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_univ _,
          ⟨i, Finset.mem_range.mpr hi, hb⟩⟩) hv'
    have hN := hall (List.ofFn v') (by rw [List.length_ofFn])
    have hfalse : shiftOrVerifier M
        (polyLen ((18 * (a₀ + 7) + 18) * a₀) (k₀ + k₀))
        (polyLen (19 * a₀ + 20) k₀) x u (List.ofFn v') = false := by
      show (List.range ks).any _ = false
      rw [List.any_eq_false]
      intro i hi
      show ¬ (M x (List.zipWith xor (List.ofFn v')
        ((u.drop (i * m)).take m)) = true)
      rw [hvfalse i hi]
      simp
    rw [hN] at hfalse
    exact absurd hfalse (by simp)

/-- **Sipser–Gács** ([AB09, Thm 7.15]): `BPP ⊆ Σ₂ᵖ ∩ Π₂ᵖ` — relative to the
efficiency notion `E`, under the closure hypotheses the proof uses.

**Proof.** It suffices to prove `BPP ⊆ Σ₂ᵖ` (`bpp_subset_sigma2`) and
apply it to `Lᶜ` as well, since `BPP` is closed under complementation
(`InBPP.compl`, which is where the hypothesis `hNot` is used).  Given
`L ∈ BPP` with witness `(M₀, a₀, k₀)`, amplify by majority
(`amplify_concrete`, using `hMaj`) to error `2^{−T(n)}` with
`T(n) = (a₀+7)(n+1)^{k₀}`; the amplified verifier uses
`m(n) = (18(a₀+7)+18)·a₀·(n+1)^{2k₀}` random bits.  Take
`k(n) = (19a₀+20)(n+1)^{k₀}` shifts — a `polyLen` schedule, as the
`shiftOrVerifier` closure (`hShift`) requires.  The two counting claims
are balanced against `T` rather than the book's `n` (whose choice
`k = ⌈m/n⌉ + 1` needs `k < 2^n` and fails at small `n`):
(Claim 1) `k(n) < 2^{T(n)}` (`shift_count_lt_two_pow`), so for `x ∉ L`
the `k` translates of the accepting set, each of measure `≤ 2^{−T}`,
cannot cover `{0,1}^m`; a union bound exhibits an uncovered `v` for
every `u`.  (Claim 2) `m(n) < T(n)·k(n)`, so for `x ∈ L` the probability
that `k` random shifts miss some `v` is at most `2^m·2^{−Tk} < 1`
(the vote-count distribution `randProb_blockCount` at `j = 0` and the
XOR-invariance `randProb_xor_right`), and the probabilistic method
yields covering shifts.  Hence
`x ∈ L ↔ ∃ u₁,…,u_k ∀ v, ⋁ᵢ M(x, v ⊕ uᵢ)`, the `Σ₂`-shape
`shiftOrVerifier` expresses; all the lengths involved are `polyLen`
schedules. -/
theorem sipser_gacs (hMaj : ClosedUnderMajority E)
    (hNot : ClosedUnderNot E) (hShift : ClosedUnderShiftOr E)
    {L : Language Bool} (hL : InBPP E L) :
    InSigma2 E L ∧ InPi2 E L :=
  ⟨bpp_subset_sigma2 E hMaj hShift hL,
    bpp_subset_sigma2 E hMaj hShift (InBPP.compl E hNot hL)⟩

end Randomized

## ===== TCSlib/Complexity/SpaceComplexity/Machines/Bin.lean =====

import Mathlib.Data.Nat.Size
import Mathlib.Data.Nat.Log
import Mathlib.Tactic.Ring

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Binary counters as words

Register-tape programs keep counters in little-endian binary, as the words `Nat.bits n`
(least significant bit first, no redundant zeros). This file collects the word-level facts the
counter machines need: the value of a word, injectivity of `Nat.bits`, the carry rule of
the increment (`Complexity.LogProg.bits_succ`), and length bounds.

## Main definitions

* `Complexity.LogProg.bitsVal` — the value of a little-endian word.
* `Complexity.LogProg.incW` — the increment of a little-endian word (carry propagation).

## Main results

* `Complexity.LogProg.bitsVal_bits`, `Complexity.LogProg.bits_injective`.
* `Complexity.LogProg.bitsVal_lt_two_pow`, `Complexity.LogProg.eq_of_bitsVal_eq` — a word's
  value is below `2^{length}` and determines the word among words of its length.
* `Complexity.LogProg.bits_succ` — `Nat.bits (n + 1) = incW (Nat.bits n)`.
* `Complexity.LogProg.length_bits_le` — `|Nat.bits n| ≤ m` when `n < 2^m`;
  `Complexity.LogProg.length_bits_mono` — `|Nat.bits n|` is monotone in `n`.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§4.1: counters in logarithmic space.)
-/

namespace Complexity.LogProg

/-- The value of a little-endian binary word. (Duplicates `BoolCircuit.bitsVal` of
`TCSlib.Complexity.CircuitComplexity.Adder`; to be unified.) -/
def bitsVal : List Bool → ℕ
  | [] => 0
  | b :: w => b.toNat + 2 * bitsVal w

/-- The increment of a little-endian binary word: flip the leading `1`s to `0` and the
first `0` (or the end) to `1`. -/
def incW : List Bool → List Bool
  | [] => [true]
  | false :: w => true :: w
  | true :: w => false :: incW w

/-- `Nat.bits` of an even and an odd number. -/
lemma bits_two_mul_add (n : ℕ) (b : Bool) (h : n = 0 → b = true) :
    Nat.bits (2 * n + b.toNat) = b :: Nat.bits n := by
  cases b with
  | false =>
    have hn : n ≠ 0 := fun h0 => by simpa using h h0
    simpa using Nat.bit0_bits n hn
  | true => simp

/-- The value of `Nat.bits n` is `n`. -/
lemma bitsVal_bits (n : ℕ) : bitsVal (Nat.bits n) = n := by
  induction n using Nat.strong_induction_on with
  | _ n ih =>
    rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos n with rfl | hn
    · simp [bitsVal, Nat.zero_bits]
    · have hdecomp : n = 2 * (n / 2) + (decide (n % 2 = 1)).toNat := by
        rcases Nat.mod_two_eq_zero_or_one n with h | h <;> simp [h] <;> omega
      have hb : n / 2 = 0 → decide (n % 2 = 1) = true := by
        intro h0; simp; omega
      rw [hdecomp, bits_two_mul_add _ _ hb]
      simp only [bitsVal]
      rw [ih (n / 2) (by omega)]
      rcases Nat.mod_two_eq_zero_or_one n with h | h <;> simp [h]; omega

/-- `Nat.bits` is injective. -/
lemma bits_injective : Function.Injective Nat.bits := fun a b h => by
  rw [← bitsVal_bits a, ← bitsVal_bits b, h]

/-- A word of `L` letters has value below `2 ^ L`. -/
lemma bitsVal_lt_two_pow (w : List Bool) : bitsVal w < 2 ^ w.length := by
  induction w with
  | nil => simp [bitsVal]
  | cons b w ih => cases b <;> simp [bitsVal, pow_succ] <;> omega

/-- Words of equal length and equal value are equal. -/
lemma eq_of_bitsVal_eq : ∀ {a b : List Bool}, a.length = b.length →
    bitsVal a = bitsVal b → a = b
  | [], [], _, _ => rfl
  | x :: a, y :: b, hl, hv => by
    simp only [bitsVal] at hv
    have hx : x = y := by
      have := congrArg (· % 2) hv
      cases x <;> cases y <;> simp_all <;> omega
    subst hx
    exact congrArg _ (eq_of_bitsVal_eq (by simpa using hl) (by omega))

/-- **The carry rule**: the binary word of `n + 1` is the increment of that of `n`. -/
lemma bits_succ (n : ℕ) : Nat.bits (n + 1) = incW (Nat.bits n) := by
  induction n using Nat.strong_induction_on with
  | _ n ih =>
    rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos n with rfl | hn
    · simp [Nat.zero_bits, Nat.one_bits, incW]
    · rcases Nat.mod_two_eq_zero_or_one n with h | h
      · -- `n = 2m`, `m ≠ 0`
        obtain ⟨m, rfl⟩ : ∃ m, n = 2 * m := ⟨n / 2, by omega⟩
        have hm : m ≠ 0 := by omega
        rw [Nat.bit0_bits m hm, show 2 * m + 1 = 2 * m + (true).toNat by rfl,
          bits_two_mul_add m true (fun _ => rfl)]
        rfl
      · -- `n = 2m + 1`
        obtain ⟨m, rfl⟩ : ∃ m, n = 2 * m + 1 := ⟨n / 2, by omega⟩
        rw [Nat.bit1_bits, show 2 * m + 1 + 1 = 2 * (m + 1) + (false).toNat by simp; ring,
          bits_two_mul_add (m + 1) false (by omega), ih m (by omega)]
        rfl

/-- The binary word of `n` has at most `m` letters when `n < 2^m`. -/
lemma length_bits_le {n m : ℕ} (h : n < 2 ^ m) : (Nat.bits n).length ≤ m := by
  rw [Nat.size_eq_bits_len]
  exact Nat.size_le.mpr h

/-- Binary words of larger numbers are not shorter. -/
lemma length_bits_mono {a b : ℕ} (h : a ≤ b) : (Nat.bits a).length ≤ (Nat.bits b).length := by
  rw [Nat.size_eq_bits_len, Nat.size_eq_bits_len]; exact Nat.size_le_size h

/-- The binary word of `n` has at most `⌊log₂ n⌋ + 1` letters. -/
lemma length_bits_le_log (n : ℕ) : (Nat.bits n).length ≤ Nat.log 2 n + 1 :=
  length_bits_le (Nat.lt_pow_succ_log_self (by norm_num) n)

/-- Every letter of `Nat.bits n` is followed by more letters or is a `1`: the word has no
trailing `0`. (The last letter is `true`.) -/
lemma bits_getLast (n : ℕ) (h : Nat.bits n ≠ []) : (Nat.bits n).getLast h = true := by
  induction n using Nat.strong_induction_on with
  | _ n ih =>
    rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos n with rfl | hn
    · simp [Nat.zero_bits] at h
    · have hdecomp : n = 2 * (n / 2) + (decide (n % 2 = 1)).toNat := by
        rcases Nat.mod_two_eq_zero_or_one n with h | h <;> simp [h] <;> omega
      have hb : n / 2 = 0 → decide (n % 2 = 1) = true := by
        intro h0; simp; omega
      have e := bits_two_mul_add (n / 2) _ hb
      rw [← hdecomp] at e
      simp only [e]
      by_cases h0 : Nat.bits (n / 2) = []
      · simp only [h0, List.getLast_singleton]
        have : n / 2 = 0 := by
          have := bitsVal_bits (n / 2); rw [h0] at this; simp [bitsVal] at this; omega
        exact hb this
      · rw [List.getLast_cons h0]
        exact ih (n / 2) (by omega) h0

end Complexity.LogProg

namespace Complexity.LogProg

/-- `n + 1 ≤ 2^(⌊log₂ n⌋ + 1)`. -/
lemma succ_le_two_pow_log (n : ℕ) : n + 1 ≤ 2 ^ (Nat.log 2 n + 1) :=
  Nat.lt_pow_succ_log_self (by norm_num) n

/-- **Logarithms of polynomials are logarithmic**: `⌊log₂ (A (n+1)^c + B)⌋ + 1` is at most a
constant times `⌊log₂ n⌋ + 1`.

**Proof sketch.** With `L = ⌊log₂ n⌋`, `n + 1 ≤ 2^{L+1}`, `A < 2^A` and `B < 2^B`, so
`A (n+1)^c + B < 2^{A + B + c(L+1) + 1}`; take `K = A + B + c + 2`. -/
lemma log_poly_bound (A c B : ℕ) :
    ∃ K, ∀ n, Nat.log 2 (A * (n + 1) ^ c + B) + 1 ≤ K * (Nat.log 2 n + 1) := by
  refine ⟨A + B + c + 2, fun n => ?_⟩
  set L := Nat.log 2 n
  have h1 : (n + 1) ^ c ≤ 2 ^ (c * (L + 1)) := by
    rw [pow_mul']; exact Nat.pow_le_pow_left (succ_le_two_pow_log n) c
  have hA : A < 2 ^ A := Nat.lt_two_pow_self
  have hB : B < 2 ^ B := Nat.lt_two_pow_self
  have hy : A * (n + 1) ^ c + B < 2 ^ (A + B + c * (L + 1) + 1) := by
    have e1 : A * (n + 1) ^ c ≤ 2 ^ A * 2 ^ (c * (L + 1)) :=
      Nat.mul_le_mul hA.le h1
    have e2 : 2 ^ A * 2 ^ (c * (L + 1)) ≤ 2 ^ (A + B + c * (L + 1)) := by
      rw [← pow_add]; exact Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by norm_num) (by omega)
    have e3 : 2 ^ B ≤ 2 ^ (A + B + c * (L + 1)) := Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by norm_num) (by omega)
    rw [pow_succ]; omega
  have hlog : Nat.log 2 (A * (n + 1) ^ c + B) < A + B + c * (L + 1) + 1 := by
    rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos (A * (n + 1) ^ c + B) with h | h
    · rw [h]; simp
    · exact Nat.log_lt_of_lt_pow (by omega) hy
  have hle : A + B + 2 ≤ (A + B + 2) * (L + 1) := Nat.le_mul_of_pos_right _ (by omega)
  have heq : (A + B + c + 2) * (L + 1) = (A + B + 2) * (L + 1) + c * (L + 1) := by ring
  rw [heq]
  generalize c * (L + 1) = P at hlog ⊢
  generalize (A + B + 2) * (L + 1) = Q at hle ⊢
  omega

end Complexity.LogProg

## ===== TCSlib/Complexity/TuringMachine/Build/Convention.lean =====

/-

Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: Seyoon Ragavan
-/
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Simulation

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Machine-construction library: the calling convention

The vocabulary module of the machine-construction library
(`machine-library-design.md`, design frozen 2026-10-03): the single seam
notion that the library's control combinators speak, plus the pure list/
arithmetic functions that the primitive contracts in
`TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Build.Primitives` are stated against.

**Status: proved.** This module is fully proved (definitions, two glue
lemmas, and the two `incFixed` laws promoted at CH34-D4), and the sibling
`Build` modules' contracts stated against
it are now all proved as well (library fill batches and the emitter
increment; zero sorries). The `Build` surface was new Chapter-1 growth,
audited in the shared infrastructure and emitter rounds
(`audits/ch1-infra-*`, `audits/emitter-*`).

## The seam notion

The model already gives *whole* machines a clean boundary: read-only input,
blank work tapes, append-only output, start at `Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg`.
The library therefore needs a configuration discipline only where a
construction crosses an *internal* seam — the round boundary of the loop
combinator and the entry of a wrapped subroutine. `Turing.Cfg.ofWords` is
that discipline: control at a designated anchor, input head at its initial
position, every work tape holding one word from the origin
(`Turing.FinTM.bufferTape`) with its head at the origin, output empty. A
loop body's contract is "`ofWords` in, `ofWords` out", and — per the frozen
design decision — the body *restores its own scratch to blank* (its scratch
words are `[]` on both sides of the contract) rather than relying on a
generic clearing pass.

## Main definitions

* `Turing.Cfg.ofWords` — the canonical seam configuration: anchor state,
  input head at 1, work tape `i` holding word `w i` from the origin, heads
  at the origin, empty output.
* `Turing.Cfg.ofWords_state`, `_inputPos`, `_workTapePos`, `_output` — the seam's fields beside
  `Turing.Cfg.ofWords_workTapes` (the ND inventory API, C1's pre-ship inventory, 2026-10-17).
* `Turing.splitAtLastTrue` — strip a marker suffix: the prefix before the
  last `true`, or `none` if the word is all `false` (the audited marker
  discipline of the Chapter-2 Exercise-2.1 construction).
* `Turing.solveSplit` — least solution `i ≤ n` of the padding length
  equation `i + C·(i+1)^e = n`, or `none` (the split-search discipline of
  the padding constructions).
* `Turing.incFixed_replicate_true_append`, `Turing.incFixed_eq_none_iff_replicate` — the
  increment's carry through a `true` prefix and its overflow criterion (CH34-D4).
* `Turing.incFixed` — little-endian fixed-width binary increment with
  explicit overflow (`none`), width preserved (the enumerator's counter
  discipline; width zero overflows immediately).

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§1.2: the k-tape machine model the
  seams are stated over.)
-/

namespace Turing

variable {k : ℕ} {State : Type*}

/-- The canonical seam configuration of the machine-construction library:
control at the anchor state `q`, input head at its initial position `1`,
work tape `i` holding the word `w i` written from the origin
(`Turing.FinTM.bufferTape`), every work head at the origin, and the output
empty. Loop-round and wrapper-entry contracts are stated as equations
between `runFrom` results and `ofWords` configurations; a body that owns
scratch tapes lists them with word `[]` on both sides of its contract
(body-restores-scratch, the frozen design decision 9.2). -/
def Cfg.ofWords {input : List Bool} (q : State) (w : Fin k → List Bool) :
    Cfg k Bool State input :=
  ⟨some q, 1, fun i => FinTM.bufferTape (w i), fun _ => 0, []⟩

/-- A machine's genuine initial configuration is the seam configuration at
its start state with every tape word empty: `Cfg.init` has blank tapes and
`Turing.FinTM.bufferTape [] = fun _ => none`. This is the lemma that lets a
combinator's startup phase begin from a seam rather than from a bespoke
initialization invariant. -/
lemma initCfg_ofWords (tm : MultiTapeTM k Bool State) (x : List Bool) :
    tm.initCfg x = Cfg.ofWords tm.q₀ (fun _ => []) := by
  simp only [MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Cfg.init, Cfg.ofWords, FinTM.bufferTape_nil]

/-- The seam words of a configuration are read back literally: at a seam,
work tape `i` holds exactly `w i` on cells `0, …, |w i| − 1` and blanks
elsewhere. Unfolds `Cfg.ofWords` for consumers that reason cell-wise. -/
lemma Cfg.ofWords_workTapes {input : List Bool} (q : State)
    (w : Fin k → List Bool) (i : Fin k) :
    (Cfg.ofWords (input := input) q w).workTapes i = FinTM.bufferTape (w i) :=
  rfl

/-- The seam's other fields (the ND inventory API, 2026-10-17; C1 wave 1's route inventory): the
state is `some q`, `(Cfg.ofWords q w).state = some q`. -/
theorem Cfg.ofWords_state {input : List Bool} (q : State) (w : Fin k → List Bool) :
    (Cfg.ofWords (input := input) q w).state = some q :=
  rfl

/-- At a seam the input head is at its initial position: `(Cfg.ofWords q w).inputPos = 1`. -/
theorem Cfg.ofWords_inputPos {input : List Bool} (q : State) (w : Fin k → List Bool) :
    (Cfg.ofWords (input := input) q w).inputPos = 1 :=
  rfl

/-- At a seam every work head is at the origin: `(Cfg.ofWords q w).workTapePos i = 0`. -/
theorem Cfg.ofWords_workTapePos {input : List Bool} (q : State) (w : Fin k → List Bool)
    (i : Fin k) : (Cfg.ofWords (input := input) q w).workTapePos i = 0 :=
  rfl

/-- At a seam the output is empty: `(Cfg.ofWords q w).output = []`. -/
theorem Cfg.ofWords_output {input : List Bool} (q : State) (w : Fin k → List Bool) :
    (Cfg.ofWords (input := input) q w).output = [] :=
  rfl

/-- Strip a marker suffix: the prefix of `v` before its **last** `true`, or
`none` when `v` is all `false`. This is the Chapter-2 Exercise-2.1 marker
discipline (split at the last `true`; an all-`false` certificate region is
a rejection), stated once as a pure function so that machine contracts and
the chapter-side semantic lemmas name the same operation. -/
def splitAtLastTrue (v : List Bool) : Option (List Bool) :=
  match v.reverse.dropWhile (fun b => !b) with
  | true :: rest => some rest.reverse
  | _ => none

/-- Least index `i ≤ n` solving the padding length equation
`i + C·(i+1)^e = n`, or `none` when no solution exists. Strict monotonicity
of `i ↦ i + C·(i+1)^e` makes the solution unique; the machine contract
`Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_splitSolve` performs this bounded search. -/
def solveSplit (C e n : ℕ) : Option ℕ :=
  (List.range (n + 1)).find? fun i => i + C * (i + 1) ^ e == n

/-- Little-endian fixed-width binary increment with explicit overflow:
`incFixed w` is the successor word of the same length, or `none` when `w`
is all `true` (overflow) — in particular width zero overflows immediately,
matching the enumerator's audited counter discipline. -/
def incFixed : List Bool → Option (List Bool)
  | [] => none
  | false :: rest => some (true :: rest)
  | true :: rest => (incFixed rest).map (false :: ·)

/-- The empty word overflows: `incFixed [] = none`. -/
theorem incFixed_nil : incFixed [] = none :=
  rfl

/-- A low `false` absorbs the carry: `incFixed (false :: w) = some (true :: w)`. -/
theorem incFixed_false_cons (w : List Bool) : incFixed (false :: w) = some (true :: w) :=
  rfl

/-- A low `true` passes the carry on: `incFixed (true :: w) = (incFixed w).map (false :: ·)`. -/
theorem incFixed_true_cons (w : List Bool) :
    incFixed (true :: w) = (incFixed w).map (false :: ·) :=
  rfl

/-- **The increment keeps the width:** `incFixed w = some v → |v| = |w|`.

**Proof sketch.** Induct on `w` through the three case equations: the empty word overflows, a
low `false` becomes `true`, and a low `true` becomes `false` before the incremented tail. -/
theorem incFixed_length {w v : List Bool} (h : incFixed w = some v) : v.length = w.length := by
  induction w generalizing v with
  | nil =>
    rw [incFixed_nil] at h
    exact absurd h (by simp)
  | cons b w ih =>
    cases b with
    | false =>
      rw [incFixed_false_cons, Option.some.injEq] at h
      subst v
      rfl
    | true =>
      rw [incFixed_true_cons] at h
      cases he : incFixed w with
      | none =>
        rw [he] at h
        exact absurd h (by simp)
      | some z =>
        rw [he, Option.map_some, Option.some.injEq] at h
        subst v
        rw [List.length_cons, List.length_cons, ih he]

/-- `Turing.incFixed` carries through a prefix of `true` bits: the prefix
`1ⁿ` becomes `0ⁿ` and the remainder `w` is incremented, the width is kept,
and the whole word overflows exactly when `w` does. Shared by the catalog's
increment routine and the `EXPCOM` deadline guard (CH34-D4).

**Proof sketch.** Induct on `n`. Each leading `true` is one step of the carry
clause of `incFixed`, which prepends one `false` to the incremented tail. -/
theorem incFixed_replicate_true_append (n : ℕ) (w : List Bool) :
    incFixed (List.replicate n true ++ w) =
      (incFixed w).map (List.replicate n false ++ ·) := by
  induction n with
  | zero => simp
  | succ n ih =>
    simp [List.replicate_succ, incFixed, ih, Option.map_map, Function.comp_def]

/-- **The overflow criterion of `Turing.incFixed`**: the increment overflows
exactly on the all-`true` word (the empty word included). The public home of
the criterion, promoted per the fills-6 request F6-1(e) (CH34-D4).

**Proof sketch.** Induct on `u`. The empty word overflows. A leading `false`
never overflows, and the word is then not all `true`. After a leading `true`,
the word overflows exactly when its tail does, and is all `true` exactly when
its tail is. -/
theorem incFixed_eq_none_iff_replicate (u : List Bool) :
    incFixed u = none ↔ u = List.replicate u.length true := by
  induction u with
  | nil => simp [incFixed]
  | cons b u ih =>
    cases b <;> simp [incFixed, ih, List.replicate_succ]

/-- **Emitter-increment vocabulary** (design §11): least
solution `i ≤ n` of the width-parametric split equation `i + f i = n`, or
`none` — the generalization of `Turing.solveSplit` from the hardwired
polynomial family to an arbitrary width function. At
`f = fun i => C * (i + 1) ^ e` this definitionally recovers
`solveSplit C e n`. Customers: the 3A-continuation's exponential padding
equation (through `computesFunInTime_splitSolveWith`) and later padding
arguments. No machine content: `List.range` search, first match. -/
def solveSplitWith (f : ℕ → ℕ) (n : ℕ) : Option ℕ :=
  (List.range (n + 1)).find? fun i => i + f i == n

/-- **Emitter-increment vocabulary** (design §11): split off
the leading unary token — the maximal `true`-prefix together with its
terminating `false` delimiter — returning the token and the remainder. A
word with no delimiter yields the whole word as an unterminated token with
empty remainder; the empty word yields two empty words; a leading `false`
is the length-zero token `[false]`. This operation consumes **unary
tokens** — the shared atom of the serialization grammars (unary indices
with terminators). It does not consume standalone single-bit markers or
polarity bits: `unaryTokenSplit [true, false, true] =
([true, false], [true])`, a terminated unary-one token, not a lone
`true` marker — scanners handle markers and polarity by their own
grammar states (emitter-infra round-1 audit, finding 4). Customers: the
3B continuation's streaming scanner, the Cook-Levin emitter's index
reads (4A), 4B's dual scanner. No machine content: structural recursion
on the word. -/
def unaryTokenSplit : List Bool → List Bool × List Bool
  | [] => ([], [])
  | false :: rest => ([false], rest)
  | true :: rest =>
    let (tok, r) := unaryTokenSplit rest
    (true :: tok, r)

end Turing

## ===== TCSlib/Complexity/TuringMachine/Build/Embed.lean =====

/-
