import Mathlib.Algebra.BigOperators.Field
import Mathlib.Algebra.Order.BigOperators.Group.Finset
import Mathlib.Data.Fintype.Prod
import Mathlib.Data.Real.Basic
import Mathlib.SetTheory.Cardinal.Finite
import Mathlib.Tactic.Linarith

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Uniform probability on finite types

Every probability in the concrete layer of the cryptography development is the
probability of an event under the uniform distribution on a finite type: inputs, keys
and coin strings are uniform, and an experiment's sample space is the product of their
types. So probabilities are exact counts, `uprob p = |{a | p a}| / |α|`, and
expectations are averages. Distributions that are not uniform arise as pushforwards
of uniform coins.

## Main definitions

* `uprob p`: the probability that a uniformly random element satisfies `p`.
* `uexp f`: the average of a real function over a finite type.

## Main results

* `uprob_nonneg`, `uprob_le_one`, `uprob_not`, `uprob_mono`, `uprob_or_le`,
  `uprob_exists_le`: basic laws and the union bound.
* `uprob_prod`: probability over a product is the average of the probabilities of
  the sections.
* `uprob_comp_equiv`: probability is invariant under relabelling by a bijection.
* `half_le_uprob_good`: the averaging argument — if an event has probability at least
  `ε`, then at least an `ε / 2` fraction of first coordinates have a section of
  probability at least `ε / 2`.
* `abs_sub_le_sum_hybrids`, `exists_hybrid_gap`: the hybrid argument for a chain of
  probabilities.

## References

* [Gar26] S. Garg, *A Course in Theory of Cryptography*, lecture notes, UC Berkeley,
  draft of 22 January 2026, §2.3 (Lemma 2.1) and §3.2 (proof of Lemma 3.3).
-/

namespace TCSlib.Cryptography

open Finset

variable {α β : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β]

/-- The probability that a uniformly random element of the finite type `α` satisfies `p`,
the number of elements satisfying `p` divided by the number of elements. -/
noncomputable def uprob (p : α → Prop) : ℝ :=
  (Nat.card {a // p a} : ℝ) / Fintype.card α

/-- The defining equation of `uprob`: the number of points satisfying `p` divided by the number
of points, `uprob p = Nat.card {a // p a} / Fintype.card α`. -/
theorem uprob_def (p : α → Prop) : uprob p = (Nat.card {a // p a} : ℝ) / Fintype.card α := rfl

/-- The average of a real function over the finite type `α`, its expectation under the
uniform distribution. -/
noncomputable def uexp (f : α → ℝ) : ℝ :=
  (∑ a, f a) / Fintype.card α

/-- The defining equation of `uexp`: the sum of the values divided by the number of points. -/
theorem uexp_def (f : α → ℝ) : uexp f = (∑ a, f a) / Fintype.card α := rfl

/-- With decidable `p`, the probability counts the elements of the filter. -/
theorem uprob_eq_card_filter (p : α → Prop) [DecidablePred p] :
    uprob p = ((univ.filter p).card : ℝ) / Fintype.card α := by
  rw [uprob, Nat.card_eq_fintype_card, Fintype.card_subtype]

/-- The probability of an event is the average of its indicator. -/
theorem uprob_eq_uexp (p : α → Prop) [DecidablePred p] :
    uprob p = uexp (fun a => if p a then (1 : ℝ) else 0) := by
  rw [uprob_eq_card_filter, uexp, Finset.sum_boole]

/-- Probabilities are nonnegative. -/
theorem uprob_nonneg (p : α → Prop) : 0 ≤ uprob p := by
  unfold uprob; positivity

/-- Probabilities are at most one. -/
theorem uprob_le_one (p : α → Prop) : uprob p ≤ 1 := by
  classical
  rw [uprob_eq_card_filter]
  exact div_le_one_of_le₀ (by exact_mod_cast card_le_univ _) (by positivity)

/-- The certain event has probability one on a nonempty type. -/
theorem uprob_true [Nonempty α] : uprob (fun _ : α => True) = 1 := by
  classical
  rw [uprob_eq_card_filter, filter_true, card_univ]
  exact div_self (Nat.cast_ne_zero.2 Fintype.card_ne_zero)

/-- The impossible event has probability zero. -/
theorem uprob_false : uprob (fun _ : α => False) = 0 := by
  classical
  rw [uprob_eq_card_filter, filter_false, card_empty, Nat.cast_zero, zero_div]

/-- The complement of an event has probability one minus its probability.

**Proof sketch.** The elements satisfying `p` and those satisfying `¬ p` partition `α`, so
their counts add up to `|α|`. -/
theorem uprob_not [Nonempty α] (p : α → Prop) : uprob (fun a => ¬ p a) = 1 - uprob p := by
  classical
  have hc : (Fintype.card α : ℝ) ≠ 0 := Nat.cast_ne_zero.2 Fintype.card_ne_zero
  have h := filter_card_add_filter_neg_card_eq_card (s := univ) p
  rw [card_univ] at h
  rw [uprob_eq_card_filter, uprob_eq_card_filter, eq_sub_iff_add_eq, ← add_div,
    div_eq_one_iff_eq hc]
  exact_mod_cast (by omega : (univ.filter fun a => ¬ p a).card + (univ.filter p).card =
    Fintype.card α)

/-- An event implied by another has at least its probability. -/
theorem uprob_mono {p q : α → Prop} (h : ∀ a, p a → q a) : uprob p ≤ uprob q := by
  classical
  rw [uprob_eq_card_filter, uprob_eq_card_filter]
  gcongr with a
  exact h a

/-- Union bound for two events. -/
theorem uprob_or_le (p q : α → Prop) : uprob (fun a => p a ∨ q a) ≤ uprob p + uprob q := by
  classical
  rw [uprob_eq_card_filter, uprob_eq_card_filter, uprob_eq_card_filter, ← add_div, filter_or]
  gcongr
  exact_mod_cast card_union_le _ _

/-- Union bound for finitely many events.

**Proof sketch.** The set where some `p i` holds is the union over `i ∈ s` of the sets
where `p i` holds, and the size of a union is at most the sum of the sizes. -/
theorem uprob_exists_le {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (p : ι → α → Prop) :
    uprob (fun a => ∃ i ∈ s, p i a) ≤ ∑ i ∈ s, uprob (p i) := by
  classical
  rw [uprob_eq_card_filter]
  simp_rw [uprob_eq_card_filter, ← sum_div]
  gcongr
  have : (univ.filter fun a => ∃ i ∈ s, p i a) = s.biUnion (fun i => univ.filter (p i)) := by
    ext a; simp
  rw [this]
  exact_mod_cast card_biUnion_le

/-- Probability over a product is the average over the first coordinate of the
probability of the section: Fubini for uniform distributions.

**Proof sketch.** Count the pairs satisfying `p` by first coordinate:
`|{z | p z}| / (|α| |β|) = (∑ a, |{b | p (a, b)}| / |β|) / |α|`. -/
theorem uprob_prod (p : α × β → Prop) :
    uprob p = uexp (fun a => uprob (fun b => p (a, b))) := by
  classical
  simp_rw [uexp, uprob_eq_card_filter, ← sum_div, div_div, Fintype.card_prod, Nat.cast_mul,
    mul_comm (Fintype.card β : ℝ)]
  congr 1
  simp_rw [card_filter]
  push_cast
  exact Fintype.sum_prod_type _

/-- Relabelling the sample space by a bijection preserves probabilities. In particular a
permutation of a uniform input is uniform. -/
theorem uprob_comp_equiv (e : α ≃ β) (p : β → Prop) : uprob (fun a => p (e a)) = uprob p := by
  rw [uprob, uprob, Nat.card_congr (e.subtypeEquiv (fun _ => Iff.rfl)),
    Fintype.card_congr e]

/-- An event depending only on the first coordinate has the same probability on the
product.

**Proof sketch.** By `uprob_prod`, the section at `a` is the certain or the impossible
event according to `p a`, so its probability is the indicator of `p a`, whose average
is `uprob p`. -/
theorem uprob_fst [Nonempty β] (p : α → Prop) : uprob (fun z : α × β => p z.1) = uprob p := by
  classical
  rw [uprob_prod, uprob_eq_uexp]
  congr 1
  funext a
  by_cases h : p a <;> simp [h, uprob_true, uprob_false]

/-- The averaging argument: if an event on `α × β` has probability at least `ε`, then
the first coordinates whose section has probability at least `ε / 2` have probability
at least `ε / 2`. [Gar26, Lemma 2.1].

**Proof sketch.** For `ε < 0` the claim is trivial, and for empty `α` both sides vanish.
Otherwise every section has probability at most `[a is good] + ε / 2`: a good `a` has
section probability at most `1`, a bad one below `ε / 2`. Averaging over `a` with Fubini
(`uprob_prod`) gives `ε ≤ uprob p ≤ Pr[good] + ε / 2`. -/
theorem half_le_uprob_good (p : α × β → Prop) {ε : ℝ} (h : ε ≤ uprob p) :
    ε / 2 ≤ uprob (fun a => ε / 2 ≤ uprob (fun b => p (a, b))) := by
  classical
  rcases lt_or_ge ε 0 with hε | hε
  · linarith [uprob_nonneg (fun a => ε / 2 ≤ uprob (fun b => p (a, b)))]
  rcases isEmpty_or_nonempty α with hα | hα
  · have : uprob p = 0 := by
      rw [uprob, Fintype.card_eq_zero, Nat.cast_zero, div_zero]
    linarith [uprob_nonneg (fun a => ε / 2 ≤ uprob (fun b => p (a, b)))]
  have hc : (0 : ℝ) < Fintype.card α := Nat.cast_pos.2 Fintype.card_pos
  rw [uprob_prod, uexp] at h
  rw [uprob_eq_uexp, uexp]
  have hpt : ∀ a, uprob (fun b => p (a, b)) ≤
      (if ε / 2 ≤ uprob (fun b => p (a, b)) then (1 : ℝ) else 0) + ε / 2 := by
    intro a
    split_ifs with hg
    · linarith [uprob_le_one (fun b => p (a, b))]
    · linarith
  have hsum := sum_le_sum (fun a (_ : a ∈ univ) => hpt a)
  rw [sum_add_distrib, sum_const, card_univ, nsmul_eq_mul] at hsum
  rw [le_div_iff₀ hc] at h ⊢
  linarith

/-- The hybrid argument, telescoping form: the gap between the ends of a chain is at
most the sum of the gaps between neighbours. [Gar26, proof of Lemma 3.3].

**Proof sketch.** Induction on `t` with the triangle inequality
`|P 0 - P (t+1)| ≤ |P 0 - P t| + |P t - P (t+1)|`. -/
theorem abs_sub_le_sum_hybrids (P : ℕ → ℝ) (t : ℕ) :
    |P 0 - P t| ≤ ∑ i ∈ range t, |P i - P (i + 1)| := by
  induction t with
  | zero => simp
  | succ t ih =>
    rw [sum_range_succ]
    exact (abs_sub_le _ _ _).trans (add_le_add_right ih _)

/-- The hybrid argument: in a chain of `t ≥ 1` steps some neighbouring pair is at least
a `1 / t` fraction of the end-to-end gap apart. [Gar26, proof of Lemma 3.3].

**Proof sketch.** Otherwise the telescoping bound gives a sum below `t · (gap / t)`. -/
theorem exists_hybrid_gap (P : ℕ → ℝ) {t : ℕ} (ht : 0 < t) :
    ∃ k < t, |P 0 - P t| / t ≤ |P k - P (k + 1)| := by
  by_contra hcon
  push_neg at hcon
  have hlt : ∑ i ∈ range t, |P i - P (i + 1)| < ∑ _i ∈ range t, |P 0 - P t| / t :=
    sum_lt_sum_of_nonempty (nonempty_range_iff.2 ht.ne') fun i hi => hcon i (mem_range.1 hi)
  have htR : (t : ℝ) ≠ 0 := Nat.cast_ne_zero.2 ht.ne'
  rw [sum_const, card_range, nsmul_eq_mul, mul_div_cancel₀ _ htR] at hlt
  linarith [abs_sub_le_sum_hybrids P t]

end TCSlib.Cryptography

import Mathlib.Data.Nat.Notation

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Oracle computations

The syntax of security games and protocols. An *oracle specification* names a family of oracles,
each with a type of queries and a type of answers. An *oracle computation* over it asks one
oracle a query, looks at the answer, chooses what to do next, and eventually returns a value. It
is the free monad over the specification: a well-founded tree (every run makes finitely many
queries) whose inner nodes are queries, with one subtree per possible answer. With finite answer
types, as for probabilistic computations, the tree is finite.

Everything else in the framework is built on this file:
- uniform sampling is one more oracle (`TCSlib.Cryptography.Games.Probability`);
- running a computation against implementations of its oracles is `simulate`
  (`TCSlib.Cryptography.Games.Simulate`);
- a two-party protocol is a pair of computations whose oracle is the message exchange
  (`TCSlib.Cryptography.Games.Protocols`).

With one oracle, an oracle computation is a `TCSlib.Cryptography.QueryTree` of the concrete
layer ([Gar26]); the bridge between the two is in the S2b layer.

## Main definitions

* `Games.OracleSpec ι`: a family of oracles named by `ι`.
* `Games.OracleComp spec α`: computations with access to the oracles of `spec`, returning an `α`;
  a `Monad` and a `LawfulMonad`.
* `Games.OracleComp.call i x`: ask oracle `i` the query `x` and return the answer.
* `Games.singleSpec I O`: one oracle (index `Unit`); its computations are the concrete layer's
  query trees.
* `Games.OracleSpec.add`: the disjoint union of two oracle families;
  `OracleComp.liftLeft`/`liftRight` run a computation over one part in the union.
* `Games.OracleComp.AllOutputs P c`: every possible output of `c` satisfies `P`.
* `Games.OracleComp.CostBoundedBy cost c q`: every run of `c` spends at most `q`, oracle `i`
  costing `cost i` per query (for example, 1 for the oracle under attack and 0 for coin draws).

## Main results

* `Games.OracleComp.instLawfulMonad`: the monad laws.
* `Games.OracleComp.CostBoundedBy.bind`: costs add under sequencing.
* `Games.OracleComp.costBoundedBy_liftLeft`, `costBoundedBy_liftRight`: lifting into a union of
  specifications keeps the cost.

## References

* [VCVio] D. Tuma and the VCVio contributors, *VCVio: machine-checked cryptographic proofs in
  Lean*, https://github.com/dtumad/VCV-io, commit 9054989327a7185ff19ef9ff0f119cccea479501
  (2026-11-04), Apache License 2.0. Design adapted (no code transcribed): oracle specifications
  indexed by a type of oracle names (`VCVio/OracleComp/OracleSpec.lean`), oracle computations as
  a free monad over them (`OracleComp.lean`, `OracleQuery.lean`), probabilistic computations as
  computations over the uniform-selection oracles (`OracleComp/ProbComp/Basic.lean`), and
  simulation of oracles by stateful handlers with query logging and composition (`SimSemantics/`,
  `SimSemantics/QueryImpl/Compose.lean`, `QueryTracking/LoggingOracle`).
* [Gar26] S. Garg, *A Course in Theory of Cryptography*, lecture notes, UC Berkeley, draft of
  22 January 2026, Definition 3.9 (oracle adversaries).
* [PS10] R. Pass, a. shelat, *A Course in Cryptography*, lecture notes, 3rd ed., January 2010,
  §3.8.1 (oracle machines).
-/

namespace TCSlib.Cryptography.Games

/-- A **family of oracles** named by `ι`: oracle `i` accepts queries in `dom i` and answers in
`rng i`. [VCVio, OracleComp/OracleSpec] -/
structure OracleSpec (ι : Type) where
  /-- The queries oracle `i` accepts. -/
  dom : ι → Type
  /-- The answers oracle `i` gives. -/
  rng : ι → Type

/-- **Oracle computations** over `spec` returning an `α`: either return a value, or ask oracle
`i` the query `x` and continue with `k` applied to the answer. This is the free monad over
`spec`; an oracle adversary of [Gar26, Definition 3.9] or [PS10, §3.8.1] with fixed coins is the
one-oracle case. [VCVio, OracleComp/OracleComp] -/
inductive OracleComp {ι : Type} (spec : OracleSpec ι) (α : Type) : Type where
  /-- Return `a` without further queries. -/
  | pure : α → OracleComp spec α
  /-- Ask oracle `i` the query `x`, and continue with `k` on the answer. -/
  | query (i : ι) (x : spec.dom i) (k : spec.rng i → OracleComp spec α) : OracleComp spec α

namespace OracleComp

variable {ι ι₁ ι₂ : Type} {spec : OracleSpec ι} {α β γ : Type}

/-- Sequencing: run `c`, then `f` on its result. Queries of `c` come first. -/
def bind : OracleComp spec α → (α → OracleComp spec β) → OracleComp spec β
  | .pure a, f => f a
  | .query i x k, f => .query i x (fun y => bind (k y) f)

instance : Monad (OracleComp spec) where
  pure := .pure
  bind := bind

/-- `>>=` is `OracleComp.bind`. -/
theorem bind_eq_bind (c : OracleComp spec α) (f : α → OracleComp spec β) :
    (c >>= f) = c.bind f := rfl

/-- `pure` is the constructor `OracleComp.pure`. -/
theorem pure_eq_pure (a : α) : (Pure.pure a : OracleComp spec α) = .pure a := rfl

/-- `<$>` is sequencing with a return. -/
theorem map_eq_bind (h : α → β) (c : OracleComp spec α) :
    (h <$> c) = c.bind (fun a => .pure (h a)) := rfl

/-- Returning first, then continuing, is continuing. -/
@[simp] theorem pure_bind (a : α) (f : α → OracleComp spec β) : (OracleComp.pure a).bind f = f a :=
  rfl

/-- A query followed by `f` is the query whose continuation is followed by `f`. -/
@[simp] theorem query_bind (i : ι) (x : spec.dom i) (k : spec.rng i → OracleComp spec α)
    (f : α → OracleComp spec β) :
    (OracleComp.query i x k).bind f = .query i x (fun y => (k y).bind f) := rfl

/-- Continuing with a return changes nothing. -/
@[simp] theorem bind_pure (c : OracleComp spec α) : c.bind .pure = c := by
  induction c with
  | pure a => rfl
  | query i x k ih => simp only [query_bind, ih]

/-- Sequencing is associative. -/
theorem bind_assoc (c : OracleComp spec α) (f : α → OracleComp spec β)
    (g : β → OracleComp spec γ) : (c.bind f).bind g = c.bind (fun a => (f a).bind g) := by
  induction c with
  | pure a => rfl
  | query i x k ih => simp only [query_bind, ih]

/-- The monad laws. -/
instance instLawfulMonad : LawfulMonad (OracleComp spec) :=
  LawfulMonad.mk' _
    (id_map := fun c => bind_pure c)
    (pure_bind := fun _ _ => rfl)
    (bind_assoc := fun c f g => bind_assoc c f g)

/-- Ask oracle `i` the query `x` and return the answer. -/
def call (i : ι) (x : spec.dom i) : OracleComp spec (spec.rng i) :=
  .query i x .pure

/-- Asking and then continuing with `f` is the query with continuation `f`. -/
@[simp] theorem call_bind (i : ι) (x : spec.dom i) (f : spec.rng i → OracleComp spec α) :
    (call i x).bind f = .query i x f := rfl

/-! ### Unions of oracle families -/

end OracleComp

/-- A single oracle with queries in `I` and answers in `O` (index type `Unit`). The concrete
layer's query trees are the computations over it (`TCSlib.Cryptography.QueryTree`). -/
abbrev singleSpec (I O : Type) : OracleSpec Unit := ⟨fun _ => I, fun _ => O⟩

/-- The single oracle of `singleSpec I O` takes queries in `I`. -/
theorem singleSpec_dom (I O : Type) (u : Unit) : (singleSpec I O).dom u = I := rfl

/-- The single oracle of `singleSpec I O` answers in `O`. -/
theorem singleSpec_rng (I O : Type) (u : Unit) : (singleSpec I O).rng u = O := rfl

/-- The **disjoint union** of two oracle families: oracle `.inl i` is oracle `i` of `s₁`, and
oracle `.inr j` is oracle `j` of `s₂`. [VCVio, OracleComp/OracleSpec] -/
abbrev OracleSpec.add {ι₁ ι₂ : Type} (s₁ : OracleSpec ι₁) (s₂ : OracleSpec ι₂) :
    OracleSpec (ι₁ ⊕ ι₂) :=
  ⟨Sum.elim s₁.dom s₂.dom, Sum.elim s₁.rng s₂.rng⟩

/-- The left oracles of the union have the queries of `s₁`: `(s₁.add s₂).dom (.inl i) = s₁.dom i`. -/
theorem OracleSpec.add_dom_inl {ι₁ ι₂ : Type} (s₁ : OracleSpec ι₁) (s₂ : OracleSpec ι₂) (i : ι₁) :
    (s₁.add s₂).dom (.inl i) = s₁.dom i := rfl

/-- The right oracles of the union have the queries of `s₂`: `(s₁.add s₂).dom (.inr j) = s₂.dom j`. -/
theorem OracleSpec.add_dom_inr {ι₁ ι₂ : Type} (s₁ : OracleSpec ι₁) (s₂ : OracleSpec ι₂) (j : ι₂) :
    (s₁.add s₂).dom (.inr j) = s₂.dom j := rfl

/-- The left oracles of the union have the answers of `s₁`: `(s₁.add s₂).rng (.inl i) = s₁.rng i`. -/
theorem OracleSpec.add_rng_inl {ι₁ ι₂ : Type} (s₁ : OracleSpec ι₁) (s₂ : OracleSpec ι₂) (i : ι₁) :
    (s₁.add s₂).rng (.inl i) = s₁.rng i := rfl

/-- The right oracles of the union have the answers of `s₂`: `(s₁.add s₂).rng (.inr j) = s₂.rng j`. -/
theorem OracleSpec.add_rng_inr {ι₁ ι₂ : Type} (s₁ : OracleSpec ι₁) (s₂ : OracleSpec ι₂) (j : ι₂) :
    (s₁.add s₂).rng (.inr j) = s₂.rng j := rfl

namespace OracleComp

variable {ι ι₁ ι₂ : Type} {α β : Type}

/-- Run a computation over `s₁` inside the union `s₁.add s₂`, asking only oracles of `s₁`. -/
def liftLeft {s₁ : OracleSpec ι₁} {s₂ : OracleSpec ι₂} :
    OracleComp s₁ α → OracleComp (s₁.add s₂) α
  | .pure a => .pure a
  | .query i x k => .query (.inl i) x (fun y => liftLeft (k y))

/-- Run a computation over `s₂` inside the union `s₁.add s₂`, asking only oracles of `s₂`. -/
def liftRight {s₁ : OracleSpec ι₁} {s₂ : OracleSpec ι₂} :
    OracleComp s₂ α → OracleComp (s₁.add s₂) α
  | .pure a => .pure a
  | .query j x k => .query (.inr j) x (fun y => liftRight (k y))

/-- Lifting commutes with sequencing. -/
theorem liftLeft_bind {s₁ : OracleSpec ι₁} {s₂ : OracleSpec ι₂} (c : OracleComp s₁ α)
    (f : α → OracleComp s₁ β) :
    (liftLeft (s₂ := s₂) (c.bind f)) = (liftLeft c).bind (fun a => liftLeft (f a)) := by
  induction c with
  | pure a => rfl
  | query i x k ih => simp only [query_bind, liftLeft, ih]

/-- Lifting commutes with sequencing. -/
theorem liftRight_bind {s₁ : OracleSpec ι₁} {s₂ : OracleSpec ι₂} (c : OracleComp s₂ α)
    (f : α → OracleComp s₂ β) :
    (liftRight (s₁ := s₁) (c.bind f)) = (liftRight c).bind (fun a => liftRight (f a)) := by
  induction c with
  | pure a => rfl
  | query j x k ih => simp only [query_bind, liftRight, ih]

/-! ### Query costs -/

variable {spec : OracleSpec ι₁}

/-- `c` is **cost-bounded by `q`**: along every run, the total cost of its queries, oracle `i`
costing `cost i` per query, is at most `q`. With `cost` equal to 1 on the oracle under attack and
0 elsewhere, this is "at most `q` queries to that oracle", the query bound of
[Gar26, Definition 3.9]. -/
def CostBoundedBy (cost : ι₁ → ℕ) : OracleComp spec α → ℕ → Prop
  | .pure _, _ => True
  | .query i _ k, q => cost i ≤ q ∧ ∀ y, CostBoundedBy cost (k y) (q - cost i)

/-- A return costs nothing. -/
@[simp] theorem costBoundedBy_pure (cost : ι₁ → ℕ) (a : α) (q : ℕ) :
    CostBoundedBy cost (OracleComp.pure (spec := spec) a) q :=
  trivial

/-- A query is within budget `q` exactly when its cost fits and every continuation fits in what
is left. -/
@[simp] theorem costBoundedBy_query (cost : ι₁ → ℕ) (i : ι₁) (x : spec.dom i)
    (k : spec.rng i → OracleComp spec α) (q : ℕ) :
    CostBoundedBy cost (OracleComp.query i x k) q ↔
      cost i ≤ q ∧ ∀ y, CostBoundedBy cost (k y) (q - cost i) :=
  Iff.rfl

/-- A larger budget is still a bound. -/
theorem CostBoundedBy.mono {cost : ι₁ → ℕ} {c : OracleComp spec α} {q q' : ℕ}
    (h : CostBoundedBy cost c q) (hq : q ≤ q') : CostBoundedBy cost c q' := by
  induction c generalizing q q' with
  | pure a => trivial
  | query i x k ih =>
    obtain ⟨hi, hk⟩ := h
    exact ⟨Nat.le_trans hi hq, fun y => ih y (hk y) (Nat.sub_le_sub_right hq _)⟩

/-- **Costs add under sequencing:** if `c` fits in `q₁` and every continuation `f a` fits in
`q₂`, then `c` followed by `f` fits in `q₁ + q₂`.

**Proof sketch.** Induction on `c`. At a query of cost `cost i ≤ q₁`, the continuation fits in
`q₁ - cost i` by hypothesis, so by induction it fits in `(q₁ - cost i) + q₂`, which is
`(q₁ + q₂) - cost i`. -/
theorem CostBoundedBy.bind {cost : ι₁ → ℕ} {c : OracleComp spec α} {f : α → OracleComp spec β}
    {q₁ q₂ : ℕ} (hc : CostBoundedBy cost c q₁) (hf : ∀ a, CostBoundedBy cost (f a) q₂) :
    CostBoundedBy cost (c.bind f) (q₁ + q₂) := by
  induction c generalizing q₁ with
  | pure a => exact (hf a).mono (Nat.le_add_left _ _)
  | query i x k ih =>
    obtain ⟨hi, hk⟩ := hc
    refine ⟨Nat.le_trans hi (Nat.le_add_right _ _), fun y => ?_⟩
    rw [Nat.sub_add_comm hi]
    exact ih y (hk y)

/-- Lifting into a union keeps the cost, when the union's cost agrees with the original on the
left part. -/
theorem costBoundedBy_liftLeft {s₂ : OracleSpec ι₂} {cost : ι₁ ⊕ ι₂ → ℕ} {c : OracleComp spec α}
    {q : ℕ} (h : CostBoundedBy (fun i => cost (.inl i)) c q) :
    CostBoundedBy cost (liftLeft (s₂ := s₂) c) q := by
  induction c generalizing q with
  | pure a => trivial
  | query i x k ih => exact ⟨h.1, fun y => ih y (h.2 y)⟩

/-- Lifting into a union keeps the cost, when the union's cost agrees with the original on the
right part. -/
theorem costBoundedBy_liftRight {s₁ : OracleSpec ι₂} {cost : ι₂ ⊕ ι₁ → ℕ}
    {c : OracleComp spec α} {q : ℕ} (h : CostBoundedBy (fun j => cost (.inr j)) c q) :
    CostBoundedBy cost (liftRight (s₁ := s₁) c) q := by
  induction c generalizing q with
  | pure a => trivial
  | query j x k ih => exact ⟨h.1, fun y => ih y (h.2 y)⟩

/-! ### Possible outputs -/

/-- **Every possible output** of `c` satisfies `P`: a return satisfies it, and every
continuation of a query does, whatever the answer. -/
def AllOutputs {spec : OracleSpec ι} (P : α → Prop) : OracleComp spec α → Prop
  | .pure a => P a
  | .query _ _ k => ∀ y, AllOutputs P (k y)

/-- The only possible output of a return is its value: `(pure a).AllOutputs P ↔ P a`. -/
theorem allOutputs_pure {spec : OracleSpec ι} {P : α → Prop} {a : α} :
    (OracleComp.pure (spec := spec) a).AllOutputs P ↔ P a :=
  Iff.rfl

/-- The possible outputs of a query are those of its continuations, whatever the answer:
`(query i x k).AllOutputs P ↔ ∀ y, (k y).AllOutputs P`. -/
theorem allOutputs_query {spec : OracleSpec ι} {P : α → Prop} {i : ι} {x : spec.dom i}
    {k : spec.rng i → OracleComp spec α} :
    (OracleComp.query i x k).AllOutputs P ↔ ∀ y, (k y).AllOutputs P :=
  Iff.rfl

/-- Every computation satisfies the trivial predicate at every possible output. -/
theorem allOutputs_true {spec : OracleSpec ι} (c : OracleComp spec α) :
    c.AllOutputs fun _ => True := by
  induction c with
  | pure a => trivial
  | query i x k ih => exact fun y => ih y

/-- `AllOutputs` is monotone in the predicate. -/
theorem AllOutputs.mono {spec : OracleSpec ι} {P Q : α → Prop} (hPQ : ∀ a, P a → Q a)
    {c : OracleComp spec α} (h : c.AllOutputs P) : c.AllOutputs Q := by
  induction c with
  | pure a => exact hPQ a h
  | query i x k ih => exact fun y => ih y (h y)

/-- Every possible output of `c` followed by `f` satisfies `Q` when every possible output `a`
of `c` satisfies `P` and every possible output of `f a` with `P a` satisfies `Q`. -/
theorem AllOutputs.bind {spec : OracleSpec ι} {P : α → Prop} {Q : β → Prop}
    {c : OracleComp spec α} {f : α → OracleComp spec β} (hc : c.AllOutputs P)
    (hf : ∀ a, P a → (f a).AllOutputs Q) : (c.bind f).AllOutputs Q := by
  induction c with
  | pure a => exact hf a hc
  | query i x k ih => exact fun y => ih y (hc y)

end OracleComp

end TCSlib.Cryptography.Games

/-

Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: TCSlib contributors

import TCSlib.Cryptography.Foundations.Probability
import Mathlib.GroupTheory.Index
import Mathlib.Logic.Equiv.Prod
import Mathlib.Tactic.FieldSimp
import Mathlib.Tactic.Linarith

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Expectations and uniform pushforwards

Toolkit for the Goldreich–Levin development: algebra of the uniform average `uexp`, and
maps that push the uniform distribution forward to the uniform distribution. Such maps
carry every probability and expectation unchanged, which is how all distributional
facts of the proof (a shifted query is uniform, two coordinates of a uniform tuple are
independent and uniform, a subset XOR of uniform strings is uniform) are expressed.

## Main definitions

* `PushesUniform π`: the pushforward of the uniform distribution along `π` is uniform.

## Main results

* `uexp_add`, `uexp_const_mul`, `uexp_sum`, `uexp_mono`, `uexp_prod`: linearity,
  monotonicity and Fubini for `uexp`.
* `uprob_prod_and`: independent events on a product multiply.
* `half_le_uprob_threshold`: if the average of a `[0, 1]`-valued function is at least
  `c + ε`, then the points where it is at least `c + ε / 2` have probability at least
  `ε / 2` (the "good set" argument of [Gar26, §2.5.1]).
* `pushesUniform_eval`, `pushesUniform_eval_pair`, `PushesUniform.prodMap`,
  `pushesUniform_of_surjective`: coordinates and pairs of coordinates of a uniform
  tuple, products, and surjective additive homomorphisms push uniform to uniform.
* `pushesUniform_restrict`: restricting a uniform table along an injection gives a uniform
  table.

## References

* [Gar26] S. Garg, *A Course in Theory of Cryptography*, lecture notes, UC Berkeley,
  draft of 22 January 2026, §2.5.1.
-/

namespace TCSlib.Cryptography.HardcoreBit

open Finset TCSlib.Cryptography

variable {Ω Ω' α β γ δ : Type*} [Fintype Ω] [Fintype Ω'] [Fintype α] [Fintype β]
  [Fintype γ] [Fintype δ]

/-! ### Algebra of `uexp` -/

/-- The average of a sum is the sum of the averages. -/
theorem uexp_add (f g : Ω → ℝ) : uexp (fun ω => f ω + g ω) = uexp f + uexp g := by
  simp only [uexp, sum_add_distrib, add_div]

/-- The average of a difference is the difference of the averages. -/
theorem uexp_sub (f g : Ω → ℝ) : uexp (fun ω => f ω - g ω) = uexp f - uexp g := by
  simp only [uexp, sum_sub_distrib, sub_div]

/-- Constants factor out of an average. -/
theorem uexp_const_mul (c : ℝ) (f : Ω → ℝ) : uexp (fun ω => c * f ω) = c * uexp f := by
  simp only [uexp, ← mul_sum, mul_div_assoc]

/-- The average of a constant over a nonempty type is that constant. -/
theorem uexp_const [Nonempty Ω] (c : ℝ) : uexp (fun _ : Ω => c) = c := by
  have : (Fintype.card Ω : ℝ) ≠ 0 := by exact_mod_cast Fintype.card_ne_zero
  simp only [uexp, sum_const, card_univ, nsmul_eq_mul]
  field_simp

/-- The average of a finite sum of functions is the sum of their averages. -/
theorem uexp_sum {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (f : ι → Ω → ℝ) :
    uexp (fun ω => ∑ i ∈ s, f i ω) = ∑ i ∈ s, uexp (f i) := by
  simp only [uexp, ← sum_div]
  rw [sum_comm]

/-- Averages are monotone. -/
theorem uexp_mono {f g : Ω → ℝ} (h : ∀ ω, f ω ≤ g ω) : uexp f ≤ uexp g :=
  div_le_div_of_nonneg_right (sum_le_sum fun ω _ => h ω) (Nat.cast_nonneg _)

/-- Relabelling by a bijection preserves averages. -/
theorem uexp_comp_equiv (e : Ω ≃ α) (F : α → ℝ) : uexp (fun ω => F (e ω)) = uexp F := by
  simp only [uexp, Fintype.card_congr e]
  rw [Fintype.sum_equiv e _ _ (fun _ => rfl)]

/-- Fubini for averages: the average over a product is the average over the first
coordinate of the averages of the sections. -/
theorem uexp_prod (F : α × β → ℝ) : uexp F = uexp (fun a => uexp (fun b => F (a, b))) := by
  simp only [uexp, Fintype.card_prod, Fintype.sum_prod_type, ← sum_div, Nat.cast_mul, div_div,
    mul_comm]

/-- A function of the first coordinate has the same average on the product. -/
theorem uexp_fst [Nonempty β] (F : α → ℝ) : uexp (fun z : α × β => F z.1) = uexp F := by
  rw [uexp_prod]
  simp only [uexp_const]

/-- The probability of an event is the average of its indicator (decidability supplied
classically). -/
theorem uprob_eq_uexp_ite (p : Ω → Prop) [DecidablePred p] :
    uprob p = uexp (fun ω => if p ω then (1 : ℝ) else 0) :=
  uprob_eq_uexp p

/-- An event of probability one holds everywhere. -/
theorem forall_of_uprob_eq_one {p : Ω → Prop} (h : uprob p = 1) (ω : Ω) : p ω := by
  classical
  rw [uprob_eq_card_filter] at h
  have hc : (Fintype.card Ω : ℝ) ≠ 0 := by
    intro h0; rw [h0, div_zero] at h; exact zero_ne_one h
  have hcard : (univ.filter p).card = Fintype.card Ω := by
    have := (div_eq_one_iff_eq hc).1 h
    exact_mod_cast this
  have := Finset.eq_univ_of_card _ hcard
  have hω : ω ∈ univ.filter p := by rw [this]; exact mem_univ ω
  exact (mem_filter.1 hω).2

/-- An event that holds everywhere on a nonempty type has probability one. -/
theorem uprob_eq_one_of_forall [Nonempty Ω] {p : Ω → Prop} (h : ∀ ω, p ω) : uprob p = 1 := by
  have : p = fun _ => True := funext fun ω => propext ⟨fun _ => trivial, fun _ => h ω⟩
  rw [this, uprob_true]

/-- Independent events on a product: the probability that the first coordinate satisfies
`p` and the second satisfies `q` is the product of the probabilities. -/
theorem uprob_prod_and (p : α → Prop) (q : β → Prop) :
    uprob (fun z : α × β => p z.1 ∧ q z.2) = uprob p * uprob q := by
  classical
  rw [uprob_prod, uprob_eq_uexp_ite p, mul_comm, ← uexp_const_mul]
  congr 1
  funext a
  by_cases ha : p a
  · simp only [ha, true_and, if_true, mul_one]
  · simp only [ha, false_and, if_false, mul_zero]
    exact uprob_false

/-- If a function is at least `b` on an event and nonnegative everywhere, its average is
at least `b` times the probability of the event. -/
theorem uprob_mul_le_uexp {G : Ω → Prop} {q : Ω → ℝ} {b : ℝ} (hq : ∀ ω, 0 ≤ q ω)
    (hG : ∀ ω, G ω → b ≤ q ω) : uprob G * b ≤ uexp q := by
  classical
  rw [uprob_eq_uexp_ite G, mul_comm, ← uexp_const_mul]
  refine uexp_mono fun ω => ?_
  by_cases h : G ω
  · simpa [h] using hG ω h
  · simpa [h] using hq ω

/-- The good-set argument: if a `[0, 1]`-valued function has average at least `c + ε`,
with `c, ε ≥ 0`, then the points where it is at least `c + ε / 2` have probability at
least `ε / 2`. [Gar26, §2.5.1], the claim `Pr[x ∈ G] ≥ ε(n) / 2` (stated there for
`c = 3/4` and, "with an identical argument", for `c = 1/2`).

**Proof sketch.** Bound the function by `1` on the good set and by `c + ε / 2` off it:
its average is at most `Pr[G] + c + ε / 2`, so `Pr[G] ≥ ε / 2`. -/
theorem half_le_uprob_threshold [Nonempty α] (q : α → ℝ) (hq : ∀ a, q a ≤ 1) {c ε : ℝ}
    (hc : 0 ≤ c) (hε : 0 ≤ ε) (h : c + ε ≤ uexp q) :
    ε / 2 ≤ uprob (fun a => c + ε / 2 ≤ q a) := by
  classical
  have hpt : ∀ a, q a ≤ (if c + ε / 2 ≤ q a then (1 : ℝ) else 0) + (c + ε / 2) := by
    intro a
    by_cases ha : c + ε / 2 ≤ q a
    · simp only [ha, if_true]; linarith [hq a]
    · simp only [ha, if_false, zero_add]; linarith
  have h1 := uexp_mono hpt
  rw [uexp_add, uexp_const, ← uprob_eq_uexp_ite] at h1
  linarith

/-! ### Maps pushing uniform to uniform -/

/-- The map `π` pushes the uniform distribution on `Ω` forward to the uniform distribution
on `γ`: every average over `γ` equals the average of its composite with `π`. -/
def PushesUniform (π : Ω → γ) : Prop :=
  ∀ F : γ → ℝ, uexp (fun ω => F (π ω)) = uexp F

/-- The defining property of `PushesUniform`: `PushesUniform π` iff
`uexp (F ∘ π) = uexp F` for every `F : γ → ℝ`. -/
theorem pushesUniform_iff (π : Ω → γ) :
    PushesUniform π ↔ ∀ F : γ → ℝ, uexp (fun ω => F (π ω)) = uexp F := Iff.rfl

/-- A map pushing uniform to uniform preserves the probability of every event. -/
theorem PushesUniform.uprob_eq {π : Ω → γ} (h : PushesUniform π) (p : γ → Prop) :
    uprob (fun ω => p (π ω)) = uprob p := by
  classical
  rw [uprob_eq_uexp_ite, uprob_eq_uexp_ite]
  exact h (fun c => if p c then 1 else 0)

/-- Maps pushing uniform to uniform compose. -/
theorem PushesUniform.comp {π : Ω → γ} {σ : γ → δ} (hπ : PushesUniform π)
    (hσ : PushesUniform σ) : PushesUniform (fun ω => σ (π ω)) := fun F => by
  rw [hπ (fun c => F (σ c)), hσ F]

/-- A bijection pushes uniform to uniform. -/
theorem pushesUniform_equiv (e : Ω ≃ γ) : PushesUniform e := uexp_comp_equiv e

/-- The identity pushes uniform to uniform. -/
theorem pushesUniform_id : PushesUniform (fun ω : Ω => ω) := fun _ => rfl

/-- Translation `a ↦ a + e` in a finite additive group pushes uniform to uniform. -/
theorem pushesUniform_add_right {G : Type*} [AddGroup G] [Fintype G] (e : G) :
    PushesUniform (fun a : G => a + e) :=
  pushesUniform_equiv (Equiv.addRight e)

/-- The first projection pushes uniform to uniform. -/
theorem pushesUniform_fst [Nonempty β] : PushesUniform (Prod.fst : α × β → α) := uexp_fst

/-- The second projection pushes uniform to uniform. -/
theorem pushesUniform_snd [Nonempty α] : PushesUniform (Prod.snd : α × β → β) :=
  (pushesUniform_equiv (Equiv.prodComm α β)).comp pushesUniform_fst

/-- **Restricting a uniform table along an injection gives a uniform table**: for an injective
`r : J → I`, the map `R ↦ R ∘ r` pushes the uniform distribution on `I → O` to the uniform
distribution on `J → O`.

**Proof sketch.** Split `I` into the image of `r` and its complement (`Equiv.ofInjective`,
`Equiv.Set.sumCompl`). A table is the pair of its two restrictions (`Equiv.sumArrowEquivProdArrow`),
and `R ∘ r` is the first one (`pushesUniform_equiv`, `pushesUniform_fst`). -/
theorem pushesUniform_restrict {I J O : Type*} [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I] [Fintype J]
    [DecidableEq J] [Fintype O] [Nonempty O] {r : J → I} (hr : Function.Injective r) :
    PushesUniform (fun R : I → O => fun j => R (r j)) := by
  classical
  let e₁ : J ⊕ ((Set.range r)ᶜ : Set I) ≃ I :=
    (Equiv.sumCongr (Equiv.ofInjective r hr) (Equiv.refl _)).trans
      (Equiv.Set.sumCompl (Set.range r))
  let e : (I → O) ≃ (J → O) × (((Set.range r)ᶜ : Set I) → O) :=
    (Equiv.arrowCongr e₁.symm (Equiv.refl O)).trans (Equiv.sumArrowEquivProdArrow _ _ _)
  have he : (fun R : I → O => fun j => R (r j)) = fun R => (e R).1 := by
    funext R j
    have h1 : e₁ (Sum.inl j) = r j := rfl
    show R (r j) = R (e₁ (Sum.inl j))
    rw [h1]
  rw [he]
  exact (pushesUniform_equiv e).comp pushesUniform_fst

/-- A product of maps pushing uniform to uniform pushes uniform to uniform: the
coordinates of a uniform pair are independent.

**Proof sketch.** Fubini over `Ω × Ω'`, push the inner average along the second map,
then the outer one along the first, and Fubini back. -/
theorem PushesUniform.prodMap {π₁ : Ω → γ} {π₂ : Ω' → δ} (h₁ : PushesUniform π₁)
    (h₂ : PushesUniform π₂) : PushesUniform (fun z : Ω × Ω' => (π₁ z.1, π₂ z.2)) := fun F => by
  rw [uexp_prod, uexp_prod F]
  have h : ∀ a, uexp (fun b => F (π₁ a, π₂ b)) = uexp (fun d => F (π₁ a, d)) :=
    fun a => h₂ (fun d => F (π₁ a, d))
  exact (congrArg uexp (funext h)).trans (h₁ (fun c => uexp fun d => F (c, d)))

/-- Evaluating a uniform function `ι → γ` at a point gives a uniform value. -/
theorem pushesUniform_eval {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (i : ι) :
    PushesUniform (fun ω : ι → γ => ω i) := by
  rcases isEmpty_or_nonempty γ with hγ | hγ
  · intro F
    haveI : IsEmpty (ι → γ) := ⟨fun ω => hγ.false (ω i)⟩
    show uexp _ = uexp _
    simp only [uexp, univ_eq_empty, sum_empty, zero_div]
  · have h := (pushesUniform_equiv (Equiv.funSplitAt i γ)).comp
      (pushesUniform_fst (α := γ) (β := {j // j ≠ i} → γ))
    exact h

/-- Evaluating a uniform function `ι → γ` at two distinct points gives a uniform pair: the
coordinates of a uniform tuple are pairwise independent and uniform. -/
theorem pushesUniform_eval_pair {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {i j : ι}
    (hij : i ≠ j) : PushesUniform (fun ω : ι → γ => (ω i, ω j)) := by
  have h₂ : PushesUniform (fun z : γ × ({k // k ≠ i} → γ) => (z.1, z.2 ⟨j, hij.symm⟩)) :=
    (pushesUniform_equiv (Equiv.refl γ)).prodMap (pushesUniform_eval _)
  exact (pushesUniform_equiv (Equiv.funSplitAt i γ)).comp h₂

/-- A surjective homomorphism of finite additive groups pushes uniform to uniform: all its
fibres have the same size.

**Proof sketch.** Group the sum over the domain by fibres; every fibre has the size of the
kernel, so both the sum and the cardinality of the domain pick up the same factor. -/
theorem pushesUniform_of_surjective {G H : Type*} [AddGroup G] [AddGroup H] [Fintype G]
    [Fintype H] (φ : G →+ H) (hφ : Function.Surjective φ) : PushesUniform φ := by
  classical
  intro F
  have hfib : ∀ h : H, #{g | φ g = h} = #{g | φ g = 0} := fun h =>
    AddMonoidHom.card_fiber_eq_of_mem_range φ (hφ h) ⟨0, map_zero φ⟩
  have hsum : ∑ g, F (φ g) = (#{g | φ g = 0} : ℝ) * ∑ h, F h := by
    rw [← Finset.sum_fiberwise' univ φ F, mul_sum]
    refine sum_congr rfl fun h _ => ?_
    rw [sum_const, nsmul_eq_mul, hfib]
  have hcard : Fintype.card G = #{g | φ g = 0} * Fintype.card H := by
    rw [← card_univ, card_eq_sum_card_fiberwise (f := φ) (t := univ) (fun _ _ => mem_univ _)]
    simp only [hfib, sum_const, card_univ, smul_eq_mul, mul_comm]
  have hpos : (#{g | φ g = 0} : ℝ) ≠ 0 := by
    have : (0 : G) ∈ ({g | φ g = 0} : Finset G) := by simp
    exact_mod_cast (Finset.card_pos.2 ⟨0, this⟩).ne'
  simp only [uexp, hsum, hcard, Nat.cast_mul]
  rw [mul_div_mul_left _ _ hpos]

end TCSlib.Cryptography.HardcoreBit

## ===== TCSlib/Cryptography/HardcoreBit/GoldreichLevin.lean =====

/-
Copyright (c) 2026 TCSlib contributors. All rights reserved.
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: TCSlib contributors
-/
import TCSlib.Cryptography.HardcoreBit.InnerProduct
import TCSlib.Cryptography.HardcoreBit.PairwiseIndependence

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Goldreich–Levin: the general case (prediction at least `1/2 + ε`)

[Gar26, Theorem 2.3, real case]: if `A` predicts `⟨x, r⟩` from `f(x) ‖ r` with
probability at least `1/2 + ε`, the inverter of [Gar26, Figure 2.5] inverts
`g(x, r) = f(x) ‖ r`. It samples `k` strings `s_ℓ` and guesses `k` bits `b_ℓ` (meant to
be `⟨x, s_ℓ⟩`); for each bit `i` and each nonempty `L ⊆ [k]` it forms the trial
`B_L ⊕ A(f(x) ‖ S_L ⊕ eᵢ)` with `S_L = ⊕_{j ∈ L} s_j`, `B_L = ⊕_{j ∈ L} b_j`, and
takes the majority over `L`. All guesses are right with probability `2^{-k}`, and then
the trials are pairwise independent, so Chebyshev applies.

Deviations from the source.
* The source ranges over all `L ⊆ [log T]`, including `L = ∅`, where `S_∅ = 0` is not
  uniform and the trial `A(f(x) ‖ eᵢ)` has no guaranteed success probability. Only the
  `2^k - 1` nonempty subsets are used.
* `k` (the source's `log T`) is an explicit natural number with the hypothesis
  `2 n ≤ ε² (2^k - 1)`, the role of `T = 2n / ε²`; the bound is `ε / (4 · 2^k)` in place
  of `(1/T) · (ε/2) · (1/2) = ε³/(8n)`. With `2^k ≤ 4n/ε²`, which a minimal `k` satisfies
  up to the rounding of `2n/ε² + 1` to a power of two, this is at least `ε³/(16 n)`
  (`invProb_guessInverter_cubic`).
* Each call to `A` uses fresh coins; independence across calls is part of the analysis.

## Main definitions

* `NESubset k`: the nonempty subsets of `Fin k`.
* `guessRecover A k`, `guessInverter A k`: the inverter of [Gar26, Figure 2.5].
* `idealRecover f A x`: the same procedure run with the correct guesses.

## Main results

* `guessRecover_correct_guess`: with correct guesses, `B_L = ⟨x, S_L⟩`.
* `uprob_idealRecover_ne_le`: for a good `x`, each majority is wrong with probability at
  most `1 / (ε² (2^k - 1))`.
* `invProb_guessInverter`: [Gar26, Theorem 2.3, real case].

## References

* [Gar26] S. Garg, *A Course in Theory of Cryptography*, lecture notes, UC Berkeley,
  draft of 22 January 2026, §2.5.1, Theorem 2.3 (real case) and Figure 2.5.
-/

namespace TCSlib.Cryptography.HardcoreBit

open Finset TCSlib.Cryptography

variable {n : ℕ} {β ρ : Type*} [Fintype ρ]

/-- The nonempty subsets `L` of `[k] = Fin k`, which index the trials of
[Gar26, Figure 2.5] (the source also uses `L = ∅`; see the module docstring). -/
abbrev NESubset (k : ℕ) : Type := {L : Finset (Fin k) // L.Nonempty}

/-- The coins of the inverter of [Gar26, Figure 2.5]: `k` strings `s_ℓ`, `k` guessed bits
`b_ℓ`, and a fresh coin string of `A` for each bit `i` and each nonempty `L`. -/
abbrev GuessCoins (n k : ℕ) (ρ : Type*) : Type _ :=
  (Fin k → Fin n → Bool) × (Fin k → Bool) × (Fin n → NESubset k → ρ)

/-- The recovery procedure of [Gar26, Figure 2.5]: bit `i` is the majority over nonempty
`L ⊆ [k]` of `B_L ⊕ A(y ‖ S_L ⊕ eᵢ)`, with `S_L = ⊕_{j ∈ L} s_j` and
`B_L = ⊕_{j ∈ L} b_j`. In total it makes `n (2^k - 1)` calls to `A`, samples `k` strings
of `n` bits, `k` bits and `n (2^k - 1)` coin strings, and computes the `2^k - 1` subset
XORs of strings and of bits, `n (2^k - 1)` further string and bit XORs, and `n`
majorities of `2^k - 1` bits. -/
def guessRecover (A : β × (Fin n → Bool) → ρ → Bool) (k : ℕ) (y : β)
    (c : GuessCoins n k ρ) : Fin n → Bool :=
  fun i => majority fun L : NESubset k =>
    subsetSum L.1 c.2.1 + A (y, subsetSum L.1 c.1 + Pi.single i true) (c.2.2 i L)

omit [Fintype ρ] in
/-- The defining equation of `guessRecover`: bit `i` is the majority over `L` of
`b_L ⊕ A(y, S_L ⊕ e_i)`. -/
theorem guessRecover_apply (A : β × (Fin n → Bool) → ρ → Bool) (k : ℕ) (y : β)
    (c : GuessCoins n k ρ) (i : Fin n) :
    guessRecover A k y c i = majority fun L : NESubset k =>
      subsetSum L.1 c.2.1 + A (y, subsetSum L.1 c.1 + Pi.single i true) (c.2.2 i L) := rfl

/-- The inverter of [Gar26, Figure 2.5]: on `f(x) ‖ r` it outputs
`guessRecover A k (f(x)) ‖ r`. -/
def guessInverter (A : β × (Fin n → Bool) → ρ → Bool) (k : ℕ) :
    β × (Fin n → Bool) → GuessCoins n k ρ → (Fin n → Bool) × (Fin n → Bool) :=
  glInverter (guessRecover A k)

omit [Fintype ρ] in
/-- The defining equation of `guessInverter`:
`guessInverter A k = glInverter (guessRecover A k)`. -/
theorem guessInverter_eq (A : β × (Fin n → Bool) → ρ → Bool) (k : ℕ) :
    guessInverter A k = glInverter (guessRecover A k) := rfl

/-- Reindexing the predictor's coins in `GuessCoins` along `e : ρ' ≃ ρ`. -/
def guessCoinsCongr {ρ' : Type*} (k : ℕ) (e : ρ' ≃ ρ) : GuessCoins n k ρ' ≃ GuessCoins n k ρ :=
  (Equiv.refl _).prodCongr
    ((Equiv.refl _).prodCongr (Equiv.piCongrRight fun _ => Equiv.piCongrRight fun _ => e))

omit [Fintype ρ] in
/-- The defining equation of `guessCoinsCongr`: it keeps `(s, b)` and applies `e` to every
predictor coin, `guessCoinsCongr k e (s, b, cs) = (s, b, fun i L => e (cs i L))`. -/
theorem guessCoinsCongr_apply {ρ' : Type*} (k : ℕ) (e : ρ' ≃ ρ) (c : GuessCoins n k ρ') :
    guessCoinsCongr k e c = (c.1, c.2.1, fun i L => e (c.2.2 i L)) := rfl

omit [Fintype ρ] in
/-- `guessRecover` with a predictor read through a coin bijection `e`: if `A' p c = A p (e c)`,
then `guessRecover A' k y c = guessRecover A k y (guessCoinsCongr k e c)`. -/
theorem guessRecover_coinsCongr {ρ' : Type*} (A : β × (Fin n → Bool) → ρ → Bool)
    (A' : β × (Fin n → Bool) → ρ' → Bool) (e : ρ' ≃ ρ) (h : ∀ p c, A' p c = A p (e c)) (k : ℕ)
    (y : β) (c : GuessCoins n k ρ') :
    guessRecover A' k y c = guessRecover A k y (guessCoinsCongr k e c) := by
  funext i
  rw [guessRecover_apply, guessRecover_apply, guessCoinsCongr_apply]
  simp only [h]

/-- The recovery procedure of [Gar26, Figure 2.5] for a known `x`, run with the correct
guesses `b_ℓ = ⟨x, s_ℓ⟩`: bit `i` is the majority over `L` of
`⟨x, S_L⟩ ⊕ A(f(x) ‖ S_L ⊕ eᵢ)`. An analysis device, not an algorithm. -/
def idealRecover (f : (Fin n → Bool) → β) (A : β × (Fin n → Bool) → ρ → Bool) {k : ℕ}
    (x : Fin n → Bool) (s : Fin k → Fin n → Bool) (cs : Fin n → NESubset k → ρ) :
    Fin n → Bool :=
  fun i => majority fun L : NESubset k =>
    ip x (subsetSum L.1 s) + A (f x, subsetSum L.1 s + Pi.single i true) (cs i L)

omit [Fintype ρ] in
/-- With the correct guesses `b_ℓ = ⟨x, s_ℓ⟩`, the guessed bits `B_L` equal `⟨x, S_L⟩`,
so the recovery procedure is `idealRecover`. [Gar26, §2.5.1, real case], the
computation `B(x, S_L) = B_L` under the event `F`. -/
theorem guessRecover_correct_guess (f : (Fin n → Bool) → β)
    (A : β × (Fin n → Bool) → ρ → Bool) {k : ℕ} (x : Fin n → Bool)
    (s : Fin k → Fin n → Bool) (cs : Fin n → NESubset k → ρ) :
    guessRecover A k (f x) (s, fun ℓ => ip x (s ℓ), cs) = idealRecover f A x s cs := by
  funext i
  simp only [guessRecover, idealRecover, subsetSum, ip_sum]

/-- For a good `x` (`secProb f A x ≥ 1/2 + ε/2`), each trial of the ideal procedure,
`⟨x, a⟩ ⊕ A(f(x) ‖ a ⊕ eᵢ)` for uniform `a` and coins, is right with probability at
least `1/2 + ε/2`. [Gar26, §2.5.1, real case].

**Proof sketch.** The trial equals `xᵢ` exactly when `A` is right on the query
`a ⊕ eᵢ`, since `⟨x, a ⊕ eᵢ⟩ = ⟨x, a⟩ ⊕ xᵢ`; and `a ⊕ eᵢ` is uniform. -/
theorem idealTrial_correct (f : (Fin n → Bool) → β) (A : β × (Fin n → Bool) → ρ → Bool)
    (x : Fin n → Bool) (i : Fin n) :
    uprob (fun z : (Fin n → Bool) × ρ =>
      ip x z.1 + A (f x, z.1 + Pi.single i true) z.2 = x i) = secProb f A x := by
  have hev : (fun z : (Fin n → Bool) × ρ =>
      ip x z.1 + A (f x, z.1 + Pi.single i true) z.2 = x i) =
      fun z => A (f x, z.1 + Pi.single i true) z.2 = ip x (z.1 + Pi.single i true) := by
    funext z
    rw [ip_add, ip_single]
    apply propext
    cases A (f x, z.1 + Pi.single i true) z.2 <;> cases ip x z.1 <;> cases x i <;> decide
  rw [hev]
  exact ((pushesUniform_xor (Pi.single i true)).prodMap
    (pushesUniform_id (Ω := ρ))).uprob_eq
    (fun z : (Fin n → Bool) × ρ => A (f x, z.1) z.2 = ip x z.1)

/-- For a good `x` (`secProb f A x ≥ 1/2 + ε/2`, `ε > 0`) and `k ≥ 1`, each majority of
the ideal procedure is wrong with probability at most `1 / (ε² (2^k - 1))`.
[Gar26, §2.5.1, real case], the bound `Pr[x'ᵢ ≠ xᵢ] ≤ 1/(4 (ε/2)² T)`.

**Proof sketch.** The trial for `L` is a function of `(S_L, cs i L)`. The subset sums over
nonempty `L` are pairwise uniform, and so are the coin strings `cs i L`; so the pairs are
pairwise uniform and the trials pairwise independent, each right with probability at
least `1/2 + ε/2`. Chebyshev over the `2^k - 1` trials with `δ = ε/2` gives the bound. -/
theorem uprob_idealRecover_ne_le [Nonempty ρ] (f : (Fin n → Bool) → β)
    (A : β × (Fin n → Bool) → ρ → Bool) {k : ℕ} (hk : 0 < k) (x : Fin n → Bool)
    (i : Fin n) {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) (hx : 1 / 2 + ε / 2 ≤ secProb f A x) :
    uprob (fun ω : (Fin k → Fin n → Bool) × (Fin n → NESubset k → ρ) =>
      idealRecover f A x ω.1 ω.2 i ≠ x i) ≤ 1 / (ε ^ 2 * ((2 : ℝ) ^ k - 1)) := by
  have hpu : PairwiseUniform (fun (L : NESubset k)
      (ω : (Fin k → Fin n → Bool) × (Fin n → NESubset k → ρ)) =>
      (subsetSum L.1 ω.1, ω.2 i L)) :=
    (pairwiseUniform_subsetSum (κ := Fin k) (G := Fin n → Bool)).prod
      ((pairwiseUniform_eval (ι := NESubset k) (γ := ρ)).comp_right (pushesUniform_eval i))
  let H : NESubset k → (Fin n → Bool) × ρ → Bool := fun _ z =>
    decide (ip x z.1 + A (f x, z.1 + Pi.single i true) z.2 = x i)
  have hY := hpu.pairwiseIndep H
  have hp : ∀ L : NESubset k, 1 / 2 + ε / 2 ≤
      uprob (fun ω : (Fin k → Fin n → Bool) × (Fin n → NESubset k → ρ) =>
        H L (subsetSum L.1 ω.1, ω.2 i L) = true) := by
    intro L
    rw [(hpu.marginal L).uprob_eq (fun z => H L z = true)]
    simpa only [H, decide_eq_true_eq, idealTrial_correct] using hx
  have hcard : Fintype.card (NESubset k) = 2 ^ k - 1 := by
    rw [card_nonempty_finset, Fintype.card_fin]
  have hm : 0 < Fintype.card (NESubset k) := by
    rw [hcard]
    have : 2 ≤ 2 ^ k := by
      calc 2 = 2 ^ 1 := by norm_num
        _ ≤ 2 ^ k := Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by norm_num) hk
    omega
  have hb := uprob_majority_fails_le hY (half_pos hε) hm hp
  have hcardR : (Fintype.card (NESubset k) : ℝ) = (2 : ℝ) ^ k - 1 := by
    rw [hcard, Nat.cast_sub (Nat.one_le_two_pow), Nat.cast_pow, Nat.cast_ofNat, Nat.cast_one]
  have hconst : 4 * (ε / 2) ^ 2 * (Fintype.card (NESubset k) : ℝ) =
      ε ^ 2 * ((2 : ℝ) ^ k - 1) := by
    rw [hcardR]; ring
  rw [hconst] at hb
  refine le_trans (uprob_mono fun ω hω => ?_) hb
  have := two_mul_card_le_of_majority_ne _ _ hω
  simpa only [H, decide_eq_true_eq] using this

/-- A uniform tuple of `k` bits equals a fixed one with probability `2^{-k}`: all `k`
guesses are right with probability `1 / 2^k`. [Gar26, §2.5.1, real case], `Pr[F]`. -/
theorem uprob_guess_eq {k : ℕ} (b₀ : Fin k → Bool) :
    uprob (fun b : Fin k → Bool => b = b₀) = 1 / 2 ^ k := by
  classical
  rw [uprob_eq_card_filter, filter_eq' univ b₀]
  simp

/-- For a good `x`, the guessing procedure recovers `x` with probability at least `2^{-k}`
times the probability that the ideal procedure does. [Gar26, §2.5.1, real case], the
factor `Pr[F]` in the final bound.

**Proof sketch.** Restrict to the event that all guesses are right, `b = (⟨x, s_ℓ⟩)_ℓ`,
where the procedure is the ideal one. The guesses are independent of `s` and of the coins,
so for each `s` this event and ideal success multiply, giving `2^{-k}` times the ideal
success probability. -/
theorem uprob_guessRecover_ge (f : (Fin n → Bool) → β) (A : β × (Fin n → Bool) → ρ → Bool)
    {k : ℕ} (x : Fin n → Bool) :
    1 / 2 ^ k * uprob (fun ω : (Fin k → Fin n → Bool) × (Fin n → NESubset k → ρ) =>
        idealRecover f A x ω.1 ω.2 = x) ≤
      uprob (fun c : GuessCoins n k ρ => guessRecover A k (f x) c = x) := by
  have hmono : uprob (fun c : GuessCoins n k ρ =>
      c.2.1 = (fun ℓ => ip x (c.1 ℓ)) ∧ idealRecover f A x c.1 c.2.2 = x) ≤
      uprob (fun c : GuessCoins n k ρ => guessRecover A k (f x) c = x) := by
    refine uprob_mono fun c hc => ?_
    obtain ⟨s, b, cs⟩ := c
    obtain ⟨hb, hc⟩ := hc
    simp only at hb hc ⊢
    rw [hb, guessRecover_correct_guess]
    exact hc
  refine le_trans (le_of_eq ?_) hmono
  rw [uprob_prod (fun c : GuessCoins n k ρ =>
      c.2.1 = (fun ℓ => ip x (c.1 ℓ)) ∧ idealRecover f A x c.1 c.2.2 = x),
    uprob_prod (fun ω : (Fin k → Fin n → Bool) × (Fin n → NESubset k → ρ) =>
      idealRecover f A x ω.1 ω.2 = x), ← uexp_const_mul]
  congr 1
  funext s
  have h := uprob_prod_and (fun b : Fin k → Bool => b = fun ℓ => ip x (s ℓ))
    (fun cs : Fin n → NESubset k → ρ => idealRecover f A x s cs = x)
  simp only at h ⊢
  rw [h, uprob_guess_eq]

/-- The general case of Goldreich–Levin: if `A` predicts `B(x, r) = ⟨x, r⟩` from
`g(x, r) = f(x) ‖ r` with probability at least `1/2 + ε`, `ε > 0`, and the number `k` of
guessed bits satisfies `2 n ≤ ε² (2^k - 1)`, then `guessInverter A k` inverts `g` with
probability at least `ε / (4 · 2^k)`. [Gar26, Theorem 2.3, real case]; the source's
`log T` with `T = 2n/ε²` is the explicit `k`, the trials range over the `2^k - 1`
nonempty subsets, and the source's bound `ε³/(8n) = (1/T)(ε/2)(1/2)` becomes
`2^{-k} (ε/2)(1/2)`.

**Proof sketch.** The good set `G = {x | Pr_r[E] ≥ 1/2 + ε/2}` has probability at least
`ε/2`. For `x ∈ G`, each of the `n` ideal majorities is wrong with probability at most
`1/(ε² (2^k - 1)) ≤ 1/(2n)`, so the ideal procedure recovers `x` with probability at
least `1/2`; the guesses are all right with probability `2^{-k}`, independently. -/
theorem invProb_guessInverter [Nonempty ρ] (f : (Fin n → Bool) → β)
    (A : β × (Fin n → Bool) → ρ → Bool) {k : ℕ} {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε)
    (hk : 2 * (n : ℝ) ≤ ε ^ 2 * ((2 : ℝ) ^ k - 1))
    (h : 1 / 2 + ε ≤ predProb (glPad f) glBit A) :
    ε / (4 * 2 ^ k) ≤ invProb (glPad f) (guessInverter A k) := by
  have hG := half_le_uprob_good f A (by norm_num) hε.le h
  have key := le_invProb_of_good f (guessRecover A k) hG
    (by positivity : (0 : ℝ) ≤ 1 / 2 ^ k * (1 / 2)) fun x hx => by
      refine le_trans ?_ (uprob_guessRecover_ge f A x)
      refine mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left ?_ (by positivity)
      refine le_trans ?_ (one_sub_sum_le_uprob_eq
        (fun ω : (Fin k → Fin n → Bool) × (Fin n → NESubset k → ρ) =>
          idealRecover f A x ω.1 ω.2) x)
      rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos n with hn | hn
      · subst hn; norm_num
      have hm : (0 : ℝ) < (2 : ℝ) ^ k - 1 := by
        have : (1 : ℝ) ≤ n := by exact_mod_cast hn
        nlinarith [sq_nonneg ε]
      have hk0 : 0 < k := by
        rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos k with h0 | h0
        · subst h0; norm_num at hm
        · exact h0
      have hsum : ∑ i : Fin n, uprob (fun ω : (Fin k → Fin n → Bool) ×
          (Fin n → NESubset k → ρ) => idealRecover f A x ω.1 ω.2 i ≠ x i) ≤
          ∑ _i : Fin n, 1 / (ε ^ 2 * ((2 : ℝ) ^ k - 1)) :=
        sum_le_sum fun i _ => uprob_idealRecover_ne_le f A hk0 x i hε hx
      rw [sum_const, card_univ, Fintype.card_fin, nsmul_eq_mul] at hsum
      have : (n : ℝ) * (1 / (ε ^ 2 * ((2 : ℝ) ^ k - 1))) ≤ 1 / 2 := by
        rw [mul_one_div, div_le_iff₀ (by positivity)]
        linarith
      linarith
  unfold guessInverter
  refine le_trans (le_of_eq ?_) key
  field_simp
  ring

/-- The general case in the source's cubic form: under the hypotheses of
`invProb_guessInverter` and `ε² 2^k ≤ 4 n` (so `k` is within one of the source's
`log(2n/ε²)`), the inversion probability is at least `ε³/(16 n)`. [Gar26, Theorem 2.3,
real case], whose bound is `ε³/(8n)` with the unrounded `T = 2n/ε²`; the factor 2 is the
cost of rounding to a power of two and of dropping `L = ∅`. -/
theorem invProb_guessInverter_cubic [Nonempty ρ] (f : (Fin n → Bool) → β)
    (A : β × (Fin n → Bool) → ρ → Bool) {k : ℕ} {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε)
    (hk : 2 * (n : ℝ) ≤ ε ^ 2 * ((2 : ℝ) ^ k - 1)) (hk' : ε ^ 2 * (2 : ℝ) ^ k ≤ 4 * n)
    (h : 1 / 2 + ε ≤ predProb (glPad f) glBit A) :
    ε ^ 3 / (16 * n) ≤ invProb (glPad f) (guessInverter A k) := by
  refine le_trans ?_ (invProb_guessInverter f A hε hk h)
  have hn : (0 : ℝ) < n := by
    by_contra hn
    push_neg at hn
    have h2k : (1 : ℝ) ≤ 2 ^ k := one_le_pow₀ (by norm_num)
    nlinarith [sq_nonneg ε, mul_pos hε hε]
  rw [div_le_div_iff₀ (by positivity) (by positivity)]
  nlinarith [mul_pos hε hε]

end TCSlib.Cryptography.HardcoreBit

import TCSlib.Cryptography.Foundations.Experiments
import TCSlib.Cryptography.HardcoreBit.Basic
import Mathlib.Algebra.Ring.BooleanRing

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# The Goldreich–Levin setting and the perfect predictor

The setting of [Gar26, Theorem 2.3]: from `f` on `n`-bit strings build
`g(x, r) = f(x) ‖ r` with the candidate hard-concentrate bit `B(x, r) = ⟨x, r⟩ mod 2`.
Bit strings are `Fin n → Bool`, and `Bool` carries Mathlib's Boolean-ring structure, in
which addition is XOR and multiplication is AND; so `s + t` is the bitwise XOR `s ⊕ t`
and `⟨x, r⟩ = ∑ᵢ xᵢ rᵢ` is the inner product mod 2.

This file sets up what the three cases of the proof share: inverters for `g` that keep
`r` and recover `x` from `f(x)` (`glInverter`), the reduction of the inversion probability
to the recovery probability (`le_invProb_of_good`), and the good set of inputs `x`
(`half_le_uprob_good`). It then proves the "super simple case": a perfect predictor
gives a perfect inverter.

## Main definitions

* `ip x r`: the inner product `⟨x, r⟩ mod 2`.
* `glPad f`: the function `g(x, r) = f(x) ‖ r`; `glBit`: the bit `B(x, r) = ⟨x, r⟩`.
* `glInverter R`: the inverter of `g` that outputs `R(f(x)) ‖ r` on `f(x) ‖ r`.
* `secProb f A x`: the probability, for fixed `x`, that `A` predicts `⟨x, r⟩` from
  `f(x) ‖ r` over uniform `r` and coins.
* `perfectInverter A`: the inverter of [Gar26, Figure 2.3].

## Main results

* `ip_add`, `ip_single`, `ip_sum`: linearity of the inner product, and
  `⟨x, eᵢ⟩ = xᵢ`; `pushesUniform_xor`: `a ⊕ e` is uniform for uniform `a`.
* `predProb_glPad_eq`: the prediction probability is the average of `secProb` over `x`.
* `half_le_uprob_good`: the good set has probability at least `ε / 2`.
* `le_invProb_of_good`: recovery bounds on a good set give inversion bounds.
* `invProb_perfectInverter`: [Gar26, Theorem 2.3, super simple case].

## References

* [Gar26] S. Garg, *A Course in Theory of Cryptography*, lecture notes, UC Berkeley,
  draft of 22 January 2026, §2.5.1, Theorem 2.3 and Figure 2.3.
-/

namespace TCSlib.Cryptography.HardcoreBit

open Finset TCSlib.Cryptography

variable {n : ℕ} {β γ ρ : Type*} [Fintype γ] [Fintype ρ]

/-! ### The inner product -/

/-- The inner product `⟨x, r⟩ = ∑ᵢ xᵢ rᵢ mod 2` of two bit strings, computed in the
Boolean ring `Bool` (XOR of the ANDs). [Gar26, Theorem 2.3], the bit `B(x, r)`. -/
def ip (x r : Fin n → Bool) : Bool := ∑ i, x i * r i

/-- The inner product is additive in its second argument: `⟨x, s ⊕ t⟩ = ⟨x, s⟩ ⊕ ⟨x, t⟩`. -/
theorem ip_add (x s t : Fin n → Bool) : ip x (s + t) = ip x s + ip x t := by
  simp only [ip, Pi.add_apply, mul_add, sum_add_distrib]

/-- The inner product with the unit vector `eᵢ` extracts the `i`-th bit: `⟨x, eᵢ⟩ = xᵢ`.
[Gar26, §2.5.1, super simple case]. -/
theorem ip_single (x : Fin n → Bool) (i : Fin n) : ip x (Pi.single i true) = x i := by
  simp only [ip]
  rw [sum_eq_single i]
  · simp only [Pi.single_eq_same]; exact mul_one _
  · intro j _ hj; simp only [Pi.single_eq_of_ne hj]; exact mul_zero _
  · intro h; exact absurd (mem_univ i) h

/-- The inner product with a sum of strings is the sum of the inner products:
`⟨x, ⊕_{j ∈ L} s_j⟩ = ⊕_{j ∈ L} ⟨x, s_j⟩`. [Gar26, §2.5.1, real case], the computation
`B(x, S_L) = ∑_{j ∈ L} B(x, s_j)`. -/
theorem ip_sum {κ : Type*} (x : Fin n → Bool) (L : Finset κ) (s : κ → Fin n → Bool) :
    ip x (∑ j ∈ L, s j) = ∑ j ∈ L, ip x (s j) := by
  simp only [ip, Finset.sum_apply, mul_sum]
  exact sum_comm

/-- XOR with a fixed string, `a ↦ a ⊕ e`, is a bijection of bit strings, so it maps a
uniform string to a uniform string. -/
theorem pushesUniform_xor (e : Fin n → Bool) : PushesUniform (fun a : Fin n → Bool => a + e) :=
  pushesUniform_equiv
    { toFun := fun a => a + e
      invFun := fun a => a + e
      left_inv := fun a => funext fun j => by
        simp only [Pi.add_apply]; cases a j <;> cases e j <;> rfl
      right_inv := fun a => funext fun j => by
        simp only [Pi.add_apply]; cases a j <;> cases e j <;> rfl }

/-! ### The function `g`, its bit, and inverters keeping `r` -/

/-- The function `g(x, r) = f(x) ‖ r` of [Gar26, Theorem 2.3]. -/
def glPad (f : (Fin n → Bool) → β) (z : (Fin n → Bool) × (Fin n → Bool)) :
    β × (Fin n → Bool) :=
  (f z.1, z.2)

/-- The defining equation of `glPad`: `glPad f (x, r) = (f x, r)`. -/
theorem glPad_apply (f : (Fin n → Bool) → β) (z : (Fin n → Bool) × (Fin n → Bool)) :
    glPad f z = (f z.1, z.2) := rfl

/-- The candidate hard-concentrate bit `B(x, r) = ⟨x, r⟩ mod 2` of [Gar26, Theorem 2.3]. -/
def glBit (z : (Fin n → Bool) × (Fin n → Bool)) : Bool := ip z.1 z.2

/-- The inverter of `g` built from a recovery procedure `R`: on `f(x) ‖ r` with coins `c`
it outputs `R(f(x), c) ‖ r`. All three inverters of [Gar26, §2.5.1] have this form. -/
def glInverter (R : β → γ → Fin n → Bool) (y : β × (Fin n → Bool)) (c : γ) :
    (Fin n → Bool) × (Fin n → Bool) :=
  (R y.1 c, y.2)

omit [Fintype γ] in
/-- The defining equation of `glInverter`: `glInverter R (y, r) c = (R y c, r)`. -/
theorem glInverter_apply (R : β → γ → Fin n → Bool) (y : β × (Fin n → Bool)) (c : γ) :
    glInverter R y c = (R y.1 c, y.2) := rfl

/-- The probability, for a fixed `x`, that the predictor `A` outputs `⟨x, r⟩` on
`f(x) ‖ r`, over uniform `r` and coins: the quantity `Pr_r[E]` defining the good set `G`
in [Gar26, §2.5.1]. -/
noncomputable def secProb (f : (Fin n → Bool) → β) (A : β × (Fin n → Bool) → ρ → Bool)
    (x : Fin n → Bool) : ℝ :=
  uprob fun z : (Fin n → Bool) × ρ => A (f x, z.1) z.2 = ip x z.1

/-- The prediction probability of `A` for the bit `B` of `g` is the average over `x` of the
probabilities `secProb f A x`. -/
theorem predProb_glPad_eq (f : (Fin n → Bool) → β) (A : β × (Fin n → Bool) → ρ → Bool) :
    predProb (glPad f) glBit A = uexp (secProb f A) := by
  unfold predProb secProb
  have h := uprob_prod
    (fun z : (Fin n → Bool) × ((Fin n → Bool) × ρ) => A (f z.1, z.2.1) z.2.2 = ip z.1 z.2.1)
  simp only at h
  rw [← h]
  exact uprob_comp_equiv (Equiv.prodAssoc _ _ _)
    (fun z : (Fin n → Bool) × ((Fin n → Bool) × ρ) => A (f z.1, z.2.1) z.2.2 = ip z.1 z.2.1)

/-- The good set is large: if `A` predicts `B` with probability at least `c + ε`
(`c, ε ≥ 0`), then `secProb f A x ≥ c + ε / 2` for a set of `x` of probability at least
`ε / 2`. [Gar26, §2.5.1], the claim `Pr[x ∈ G] ≥ ε(n)/2`, for `c = 3/4` (simple case) and
`c = 1/2` (real case). -/
theorem half_le_uprob_good (f : (Fin n → Bool) → β) (A : β × (Fin n → Bool) → ρ → Bool)
    {c ε : ℝ} (hc : 0 ≤ c) (hε : 0 ≤ ε) (h : c + ε ≤ predProb (glPad f) glBit A) :
    ε / 2 ≤ uprob (fun x => c + ε / 2 ≤ secProb f A x) := by
  rw [predProb_glPad_eq] at h
  exact half_le_uprob_threshold _ (fun x => uprob_le_one _) hc hε h

/-- Recovering `x` exactly inverts `g`: the inversion probability of `glInverter R` is at
least the probability that `R(f(x), c) = x` over uniform `x` and coins `c`. -/
theorem uprob_recover_le_invProb (f : (Fin n → Bool) → β) (R : β → γ → Fin n → Bool) :
    uprob (fun z : (Fin n → Bool) × γ => R (f z.1) z.2 = z.1) ≤
      invProb (glPad f) (glInverter R) := by
  let e : ((Fin n → Bool) × (Fin n → Bool)) × γ ≃ ((Fin n → Bool) × γ) × (Fin n → Bool) :=
    { toFun := fun w => ((w.1.1, w.2), w.1.2)
      invFun := fun z => ((z.1.1, z.2), z.1.2)
      left_inv := fun _ => rfl
      right_inv := fun _ => rfl }
  have h := uprob_comp_equiv e
    (fun z : ((Fin n → Bool) × γ) × (Fin n → Bool) => R (f z.1.1) z.1.2 = z.1.1)
  rw [uprob_fst (fun z : (Fin n → Bool) × γ => R (f z.1) z.2 = z.1)] at h
  rw [← h]
  refine uprob_mono fun w hw => ?_
  simp only [glPad, glInverter]
  simp only [e, Equiv.coe_fn_mk] at hw
  rw [hw]

/-- Inversion from recovery on a good set: if the good set `G` has probability at least
`a`, and for every `x ∈ G` the procedure `R` recovers `x` from `f(x)` with probability at
least `b ≥ 0`, then `glInverter R` inverts `g` with probability at least `a · b`.
[Gar26, §2.5.1], the final step `Pr[B inverts] ≥ Pr[x ∈ G] · Pr[x' = x | x ∈ G]` of the
simple and real cases.

**Proof sketch.** Bound the inversion probability below by the recovery probability,
split it over `x` (Fubini), and keep only the contribution of `x ∈ G`. -/
theorem le_invProb_of_good (f : (Fin n → Bool) → β) (R : β → γ → Fin n → Bool)
    {G : (Fin n → Bool) → Prop} {a b : ℝ} (hG : a ≤ uprob G) (hb : 0 ≤ b)
    (hR : ∀ x, G x → b ≤ uprob (fun c => R (f x) c = x)) :
    a * b ≤ invProb (glPad f) (glInverter R) := by
  refine le_trans ?_ (uprob_recover_le_invProb f R)
  rw [uprob_prod]
  exact (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hG hb).trans
    (uprob_mul_le_uexp (fun x => uprob_nonneg _) hR)

/-- Union bound over the bits: the probability of recovering all of `x` is at least one
minus the sum over `i` of the probabilities that bit `i` is wrong. -/
theorem one_sub_sum_le_uprob_eq [Nonempty γ] (R : γ → Fin n → Bool) (x : Fin n → Bool) :
    1 - ∑ i, uprob (fun c => R c i ≠ x i) ≤ uprob (fun c => R c = x) := by
  have h1 : uprob (fun c => ¬ R c = x) ≤ ∑ i, uprob (fun c => R c i ≠ x i) := by
    refine (uprob_mono fun c hc => ?_).trans (uprob_exists_le univ fun i c => R c i ≠ x i)
    by_contra h
    push_neg at h
    exact hc (funext fun i => h i (mem_univ i))
  rw [uprob_not] at h1
  linarith

/-! ### The super simple case -/

/-- The recovery procedure of [Gar26, Figure 2.3]: the `i`-th bit is `A(f(x) ‖ eᵢ)`, where
`eᵢ` is the `i`-th unit vector. It makes `n` calls to `A`, each with fresh coins `c i`,
and no other computation. -/
def perfectRecover (A : β × (Fin n → Bool) → ρ → Bool) (y : β) (c : Fin n → ρ) :
    Fin n → Bool :=
  fun i => A (y, Pi.single i true) (c i)

/-- The inverter of [Gar26, Figure 2.3]: on `f(x) ‖ r` it outputs
`A(f(x) ‖ e₁) ⋯ A(f(x) ‖ eₙ) ‖ r`, using `n` calls to `A` with fresh coins. -/
def perfectInverter (A : β × (Fin n → Bool) → ρ → Bool) :
    β × (Fin n → Bool) → (Fin n → ρ) → (Fin n → Bool) × (Fin n → Bool) :=
  glInverter (perfectRecover A)

omit [Fintype ρ] in
/-- The defining equation of `perfectInverter`:
`perfectInverter A = glInverter (perfectRecover A)`. -/
theorem perfectInverter_eq (A : β × (Fin n → Bool) → ρ → Bool) :
    perfectInverter A = glInverter (perfectRecover A) := rfl

/-- The super simple case of Goldreich–Levin: if `A` predicts `B(x, r) = ⟨x, r⟩` from
`g(x, r) = f(x) ‖ r` with probability `1`, then `perfectInverter A` inverts `g` with
probability `1`. [Gar26, Theorem 2.3, super simple case].

**Proof sketch.** Probability one on a finite space means `A` is right on every input and
every coin string, in particular on `f(x) ‖ eᵢ`, where the right answer is
`⟨x, eᵢ⟩ = xᵢ`. So the inverter recovers `x` exactly, always. -/
theorem invProb_perfectInverter (f : (Fin n → Bool) → β) (A : β × (Fin n → Bool) → ρ → Bool)
    (h : predProb (glPad f) glBit A = 1) : invProb (glPad f) (perfectInverter A) = 1 := by
  have hA := forall_of_uprob_eq_one h
  have hρ : Nonempty ρ := by
    by_contra hρ
    rw [not_nonempty_iff] at hρ
    have : uprob (fun z : ((Fin n → Bool) × (Fin n → Bool)) × ρ =>
        A (glPad f z.1) z.2 = glBit z.1) = 0 := by
      classical
      rw [uprob_eq_card_filter]; simp
    unfold predProb at h
    rw [this] at h
    exact zero_ne_one h
  refine le_antisymm (uprob_le_one _) ?_
  refine le_of_eq_of_le ?_ (uprob_recover_le_invProb f (perfectRecover A))
  refine (uprob_eq_one_of_forall fun z => funext fun i => ?_).symm
  have := hA ((z.1, Pi.single i true), z.2 i)
  simpa only [glPad, glBit, ip_single] using this

end TCSlib.Cryptography.HardcoreBit
