import TCSlib.Cryptography.Foundations.Experiments
import TCSlib.Cryptography.Games.OracleComp

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Adaptive oracle adversaries as query trees

An oracle adversary asks its oracle a question, looks at the answer, chooses the next
question, and finally outputs a value. At one fixed value of the security parameter such
an adversary (for a fixed coin string) is exactly a finite tree: a leaf carries the output,
and an inner node carries a query `x : I` and one subtree for each possible answer `o : O`.
The coins are a uniform element of a finite type `ρ`, so a randomized oracle adversary is a
function `ρ → QueryTree I O α`.

Running the adversary against an oracle `f : I → O` follows the path chosen by the
answers `f x`. The adversary makes at most `q` queries when every root-to-leaf path has at
most `q` inner nodes. The cost of a query in [Gar26, Definition 3.9] ("each call to that
function costs 1 unit of time") is accounted by this bound; running time otherwise is the
business of the asymptotic layer.

Answering the queries of one adversary by a computation that itself asks queries to a
second oracle (`simulate`) is the basic reduction step: the simulated tree makes the same
number of queries.

**One notion of oracle computation** (ruling of 2026-11-05, item F-1). A query tree *is* a
computation of the `Games` framework with one oracle: `QueryTree I O α` abbreviates
`Games.OracleComp (Games.singleSpec I O) α`, and `ret` and `query` are its two constructors (the
oracle index is the unit). Definitions by cases on `ret`/`query` are unchanged; proofs by
induction use `QueryTree.induct`. The links of `eval`, `BoundedBy` and `simulate` to the
framework's evaluation, query costs and simulation are in
`TCSlib.Cryptography.Games.Bridges.QueryTree`.

**Deviation:** query, answer and output types are in `Type` (universe 0), as the framework's are;
every use in [Gar26] and [PS10] is at `Type`.

## Main definitions

* `QueryTree I O α`: adaptive query trees with queries in `I`, answers in `O` and outputs
  in `α`: the one-oracle computations of the `Games` framework.
* `QueryTree.induct`: induction on query trees by their two constructors.
* `QueryTree.eval f t`: the output of `t` run against the oracle `f`.
* `QueryTree.BoundedBy t q`: every path of `t` makes at most `q` queries.
* `QueryTree.simulate π ans t`: answer each query `x` of `t` by asking `π x` to a new oracle
  and post-processing the answer with `ans x`.
* `OracleAdversary ρ I O`: randomized Boolean oracle adversaries with coins in `ρ`.
* `oracleDist A`: the adversary viewed as a distinguisher for oracles.

## Main results

* `QueryTree.eval_simulate`: running the simulated tree against `g` is running the
  original tree against the oracle `x ↦ ans x (g (π x))`.
* `QueryTree.BoundedBy.simulate`: simulation preserves the query bound.
* `QueryTree.BoundedBy.mono`: query bounds are monotone.

## References

* [Gar26] S. Garg, *A Course in Theory of Cryptography*, lecture notes, UC Berkeley,
  draft of 22 January 2026, Definition 3.9 (oracle adversaries).
* [VCVio] D. Tuma and the VCVio contributors, *VCVio: machine-checked cryptographic proofs in
  Lean*, https://github.com/dtumad/VCV-io, commit 9054989327a7185ff19ef9ff0f119cccea479501
  (2026-11-04), Apache License 2.0. Design adapted (no code transcribed): oracle computations as a
  free monad over an indexed oracle specification (`VCVio/OracleComp/OracleComp.lean`), here
  through `TCSlib.Cryptography.Games.OracleComp`.
-/

namespace TCSlib.Cryptography


/-- An adaptive oracle algorithm with queries in `I`, answers in `O` and output in `α`,
as a decision tree: `ret a` stops and outputs `a`, and `query x k` asks the oracle at `x`
and continues with the subtree `k o` for the answer `o`. This is the concrete form of an
oracle adversary with fixed coins [Gar26, Definition 3.9]: the one-oracle computation of the
`Games` framework. [VCVio, OracleComp/OracleComp] -/
abbrev QueryTree (I O α : Type) : Type := Games.OracleComp (Games.singleSpec I O) α

namespace QueryTree

variable {I O α I' O' : Type}

/-- Stop and output `a`. -/
@[match_pattern] abbrev ret (a : α) : QueryTree I O α := Games.OracleComp.pure a

/-- Ask the oracle at `x` and continue with `k` applied to the answer. -/
@[match_pattern] abbrev query (x : I) (k : O → QueryTree I O α) : QueryTree I O α :=
  Games.OracleComp.query () x k

/-- **Induction on query trees** by their two constructors: a property of leaves, and the step
from all the subtrees of a query to the query. Use it as `induction t using QueryTree.induct`. -/
@[elab_as_elim] def induct {motive : QueryTree I O α → Sort _} (ret : ∀ a, motive (ret a))
    (query : ∀ x k, (∀ o, motive (k o)) → motive (query x k)) : ∀ t, motive t
  | Games.OracleComp.pure a => ret a
  | Games.OracleComp.query () x k => query x k fun o => induct ret query (k o)

/-- `induct` computes on a leaf by its leaf case: `induct hret hquery (ret a) = hret a`. -/
theorem induct_ret {motive : QueryTree I O α → Sort _} (hret : ∀ a, motive (ret a))
    (hquery : ∀ x k, (∀ o, motive (k o)) → motive (query x k)) (a : α) :
    induct (motive := motive) hret hquery (ret a) = hret a :=
  rfl

/-- `induct` computes on a query node by its query case, applied to the inductions on the
subtrees: `induct hret hquery (query x k) = hquery x k (fun o => induct hret hquery (k o))`. -/
theorem induct_query {motive : QueryTree I O α → Sort _} (hret : ∀ a, motive (ret a))
    (hquery : ∀ x k, (∀ o, motive (k o)) → motive (query x k)) (x : I)
    (k : O → QueryTree I O α) :
    induct (motive := motive) hret hquery (query x k) =
      hquery x k fun o => induct (motive := motive) hret hquery (k o) :=
  rfl

/-- The output of the query tree `t` when every query `x` is answered by `f x`. -/
def eval (f : I → O) : QueryTree I O α → α
  | ret a => a
  | query x k => eval f (k (f x))

/-- A leaf outputs its value. -/
@[simp] theorem eval_ret (f : I → O) (a : α) : (ret a : QueryTree I O α).eval f = a := rfl

/-- A query node continues with the subtree for the oracle's answer. -/
@[simp] theorem eval_query (f : I → O) (x : I) (k : O → QueryTree I O α) :
    (query x k).eval f = (k (f x)).eval f := rfl

/-- The query tree `t` makes at most `q` oracle queries along every path: a leaf is
bounded by every `q`, and `query x k` is bounded by `q + 1` when every continuation `k o`
is bounded by `q`. -/
def BoundedBy : QueryTree I O α → ℕ → Prop
  | ret _, _ => True
  | query _ _, 0 => False
  | query _ k, q + 1 => ∀ o, BoundedBy (k o) q

/-- A leaf makes no queries. -/
@[simp] theorem boundedBy_ret (a : α) (q : ℕ) : (ret a : QueryTree I O α).BoundedBy q :=
  trivial

/-- A query node makes at least one query. -/
@[simp] theorem boundedBy_query_zero (x : I) (k : O → QueryTree I O α) :
    ¬ (query x k).BoundedBy 0 := id

/-- A query node makes at most `q + 1` queries iff every continuation makes at most
`q`. -/
@[simp] theorem boundedBy_query_succ (x : I) (k : O → QueryTree I O α) (q : ℕ) :
    (query x k).BoundedBy (q + 1) ↔ ∀ o, (k o).BoundedBy q := Iff.rfl

/-- A tree making at most `q` queries makes at most `q'` queries for every `q' ≥ q`. -/
theorem BoundedBy.mono {t : QueryTree I O α} {q q' : ℕ} (h : t.BoundedBy q)
    (hq : q ≤ q') : t.BoundedBy q' := by
  induction t using QueryTree.induct generalizing q q' with
  | ret a => trivial
  | query x k ih =>
    cases q with
    | zero => exact absurd h (boundedBy_query_zero x k)
    | succ q =>
      obtain ⟨q', rfl⟩ : ∃ q'', q' = q'' + 1 := ⟨q' - 1, by omega⟩
      exact fun o => ih o (h o) (by omega)

/-- Simulation of oracle queries: each query `x` of `t` is replaced by the query `π x` to a
new oracle with answers in `O'`, whose answer `o'` is turned into the answer `ans x o'` for
`t`. The simulated tree asks exactly one new query per original query. -/
def simulate (π : I → I') (ans : I → O' → O) : QueryTree I O α → QueryTree I' O' α
  | ret a => ret a
  | query x k => query (π x) (fun o' => simulate π ans (k (ans x o')))

/-- Simulating a leaf leaves it unchanged: `(ret a).simulate π ans = ret a`. -/
theorem simulate_ret (π : I → I') (ans : I → O' → O) (a : α) :
    (ret a : QueryTree I O α).simulate π ans = ret a :=
  rfl

/-- Simulating a query node asks `π x` and continues, on the answer `o'`, with the simulation of
the subtree for `ans x o'`:
`(query x k).simulate π ans = query (π x) (fun o' => (k (ans x o')).simulate π ans)`. -/
theorem simulate_query (π : I → I') (ans : I → O' → O) (x : I) (k : O → QueryTree I O α) :
    (query x k).simulate π ans = query (π x) (fun o' => (k (ans x o')).simulate π ans) :=
  rfl

/-- Running the simulated tree against `g` is running the original tree against the
oracle that answers `x` by `ans x (g (π x))`. -/
@[simp] theorem eval_simulate (π : I → I') (ans : I → O' → O) (g : I' → O')
    (t : QueryTree I O α) :
    (t.simulate π ans).eval g = t.eval (fun x => ans x (g (π x))) := by
  induction t using QueryTree.induct with
  | ret a => rfl
  | query x k ih => exact ih _

/-- Simulation does not increase the number of queries. -/
theorem BoundedBy.simulate {t : QueryTree I O α} {q : ℕ} (h : t.BoundedBy q)
    (π : I → I') (ans : I → O' → O) : (t.simulate π ans).BoundedBy q := by
  induction t using QueryTree.induct generalizing q with
  | ret a => trivial
  | query x k ih =>
    cases q with
    | zero => exact absurd h (boundedBy_query_zero x k)
    | succ q => exact fun o' => ih _ (h _)

end QueryTree

/-- A randomized Boolean oracle adversary with coins in `ρ`: for every coin string a query
tree with queries in `I`, answers in `O` and a one-bit output. [Gar26, Definition 3.9]
at one value of the security parameter; the input `1^n` is implicit in the fixed types,
and the coins are uniform over the finite type `ρ`. -/
abbrev OracleAdversary (ρ : Type*) (I O : Type) := ρ → QueryTree I O Bool

/-- The randomized oracle adversary `A` makes at most `q` queries on every coin string and
every path. -/
def OracleAdversary.BoundedBy {ρ : Type*} {I O : Type}
    (A : OracleAdversary ρ I O) (q : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ r, (A r).BoundedBy q

/-- `A` makes at most `q` queries iff the tree of every coin string does:
`A.BoundedBy q ↔ ∀ r, (A r).BoundedBy q`. -/
theorem OracleAdversary.boundedBy_iff {ρ : Type*} {I O : Type} (A : OracleAdversary ρ I O)
    (q : ℕ) : A.BoundedBy q ↔ ∀ r, (A r).BoundedBy q :=
  Iff.rfl

/-- The oracle adversary `A` as a distinguisher for oracles: on the oracle `f` and coins
`r` it outputs the result of running `A r` against `f`. With a sampler for the oracle,
`acceptProb` of this distinguisher is the probability `Pr[A^f = 1]` of
[Gar26, Definition 3.9]. -/
def oracleDist {ρ : Type*} {I O : Type} (A : OracleAdversary ρ I O) :
    (I → O) → ρ → Bool :=
  fun f r => (A r).eval f

/-- The distinguisher of `A` on the oracle `f` and coins `r` is the run of `A r` against `f`:
`oracleDist A f r = (A r).eval f`. -/
theorem oracleDist_apply {ρ : Type*} {I O : Type} (A : OracleAdversary ρ I O) (f : I → O)
    (r : ρ) : oracleDist A f r = (A r).eval f :=
  rfl

end TCSlib.Cryptography

## ===== TCSlib/Cryptography/Pseudorandom/Functions/SubHybrids.lean =====

/-
Copyright (c) 2026 TCSlib contributors. All rights reserved.
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: TCSlib contributors
-/
import TCSlib.Cryptography.Pseudorandom.Functions.LazySampling
import TCSlib.Cryptography.Pseudorandom.Functions.Defs

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Sub-hybrids: a table of PRG outputs against an adaptive adversary

This file isolates the inner hybrid argument of the GGM proof [Gar26, proof of
Theorem 3.3, "Sub-hybrids"]. Let `G : S → V` be a generator and consider an oracle
adversary `A` making at most `q` queries to a table `T : P → V`. In the *pseudorandom*
world the table is `G ∘ R` for a uniform `R : P → S`; in the *random* world it is a
uniform `T : P → V`. We bound the gap by `q` PRG distinguishing advantages.

The sub-hybrid `H_j` (`subHybridProb G A q j`) answers the queries lazily: the `k`-th
distinct query is answered by a uniform value of `V` if `k < j` and by `G` of a uniform
seed otherwise. So `H_0` is the pseudorandom world and `H_q` the random world, by lazy
sampling (`QueryTree.uprob_evalLazy`). The PRG distinguisher `tableDist G A q j` embeds
its challenge `z ∈ V` as the answer to the `j`-th distinct query; it accepts with the
probability of `H_j` when `z = G(s)` and with that of `H_{j+1}` when `z` is uniform.

**Deviation from the source.** [Gar26] defines `H_{i,j}` through a list `L` of prefixes,
which amounts to answering the first `j` *distinct* prefixes randomly, as here. The
argument then speaks of "the `(j*+1)`-th query", claims that it cannot repeat an earlier
prefix "because otherwise the hybrids would be identical" (not a valid inference: two
hybrids can differ although they agree on a particular event), and has the outer
adversary answer only that one query with its challenge, which leaves later queries with
the same prefix inconsistent with the challenge. Here the sub-hybrids are indexed by
distinct queries in order of first appearance, and the distinguisher answers *every*
query equal to the `j`-th distinct one with the challenge. A repeated query is then
simply answered by its recorded value, so no case split on repeats is needed, and the
distinguisher's runs coincide pointwise with those of the hybrids after relabelling one
uniform coordinate.

## Main definitions

* `subHybridStream G j W`, `subHybridProb G A q j`: the sub-hybrid `H_j`.
* `tableDist G A q j`: the PRG distinguisher embedding its challenge at the `j`-th
  distinct query.

## Main results

* `acceptProb_tableDist_prg`, `acceptProb_tableDist_uniform`: the distinguisher realises
  `H_j` and `H_{j+1}`.
* `subHybridProb_zero`, `subHybridProb_top`: the endpoints are the pseudorandom and the
  random table.
* `table_hybrid`: the gap between the two worlds is at most the sum over `j < q` of the
  distinguishing advantages of `tableDist G A q j`.

## References

* [Gar26] S. Garg, *A Course in Theory of Cryptography*, lecture notes, UC Berkeley,
  draft of 22 January 2026, §3.4.2, proof of Theorem 3.3 (sub-hybrids `H_{i,j}` and the
  outer adversary `B`), footnote 9 (lazy sampling).
-/

namespace TCSlib.Cryptography

open Function QueryTree

attribute [local irreducible] uprob acceptProb

variable {P S V : Type} {ρ : Type*} [Fintype P] [DecidableEq P] [Fintype S] [Nonempty S]
  [Fintype V] [Nonempty V] [Fintype ρ]

/-- The answer stream of the sub-hybrid `H_j` [Gar26, proof of Theorem 3.3]: the `k`-th
distinct query is answered by the uniform value `W.2 k` if `k < j` and by the generator
output `G (W.1 k)` on a uniform seed otherwise. -/
noncomputable def subHybridStream {q : ℕ} (G : S → V) (j : ℕ)
    (W : (Fin q → S) × (Fin q → V)) : ℕ → V :=
  fun k => if k < j then extendStream W.2 k else G (extendStream W.1 k)

/-- The oracle adversary `A` run with lazily sampled answers given by an answer stream. -/
def lazyDist (A : OracleAdversary ρ P V) : (ℕ → V) → ρ → Bool :=
  fun a r => (A r).evalLazy a []

omit [Fintype P] [Fintype V] [Nonempty V] [Fintype ρ] in
/-- On the answer stream `a` and coins `r`, `lazyDist A` is the lazy run of `A r` from the empty
list of distinct queries: `lazyDist A a r = (A r).evalLazy a []`. -/
theorem lazyDist_apply (A : OracleAdversary ρ P V) (a : ℕ → V) (r : ρ) :
    lazyDist A a r = (A r).evalLazy a [] :=
  rfl

/-- The probability that `A` accepts in the sub-hybrid `H_j`: `j` uniform values and
`q - j` generator outputs answer the distinct queries in order. [Gar26, proof of
Theorem 3.3, `H_{i,j}`] with the level `i` abstracted away; see the module docstring for
the indexing by distinct queries. -/
noncomputable def subHybridProb (G : S → V) (A : OracleAdversary ρ P V) (q j : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  acceptProb (subHybridStream (q := q) G j) (lazyDist A)

/-- The answer stream of the PRG distinguisher: as in `H_j`, except that the `j`-th
distinct query is answered by the challenge `z`. -/
noncomputable def challengeStream {q : ℕ} (G : S → V) (j : ℕ) (z : V)
    (W : (Fin q → S) × (Fin q → V)) : ℕ → V :=
  fun k => if k < j then extendStream W.2 k else if k = j then z else G (extendStream W.1 k)

/-- The PRG distinguisher built from the oracle adversary `A` [Gar26, proof of
Theorem 3.3, the outer adversary `B`]. On a challenge `z ∈ V` and coins
`((W₀, W₁), r)` with `W₀ : Fin q → S`, `W₁ : Fin q → V`, it runs `A` once on coins `r`,
answers the `k`-th distinct query by `W₁ k` if `k < j`, by `z` if `k = j`, and by
`G (W₀ k)` if `k > j`, and outputs what `A` outputs.

*Cost*, for `A` bounded by `q` queries (`OracleAdversary.BoundedBy`; the definition itself
runs any `A`). One run of `A`; at most `q` evaluations of `G`; `q` seeds and `q` values of
fresh randomness (lazy sampling, [Gar26, footnote 9]: no exponential table is sampled);
bookkeeping of the list of at most `q` distinct queries (membership and position
lookups). -/
noncomputable def tableDist (G : S → V) (A : OracleAdversary ρ P V) (q j : ℕ) :
    V → ((Fin q → S) × (Fin q → V)) × ρ → Bool :=
  fun z c => (A c.2).evalLazy (challengeStream G j z c.1) []

omit [Fintype P] in
/-- On a pseudorandom challenge `z = G s` the distinguisher `tableDist G A q j` accepts
exactly with the probability of the sub-hybrid `H_j`, for `j < q`.

**Proof sketch.** With `z = G s`, the challenge stream is the stream of `H_j` with the
seed table `W₀` overwritten at position `j` by `s`; overwriting one entry of a uniform
table by a uniform value leaves it uniform. -/
theorem acceptProb_tableDist_prg (G : S → V) (A : OracleAdversary ρ P V) {q j : ℕ}
    (hj : j < q) : acceptProb G (tableDist G A q j) = subHybridProb G A q j := by
  have hs : ∀ (s : S) (W : (Fin q → S) × (Fin q → V)),
      challengeStream G j (G s) W = subHybridStream G j (update W.1 ⟨j, hj⟩ s, W.2) := by
    intro s W; funext k
    unfold challengeStream subHybridStream
    by_cases h1 : k < j
    · simp [h1]
    · by_cases h2 : k = j
      · subst h2; simp only [lt_irrefl, if_false, if_true]
        exact congrArg G (extendStream_update_self W.1 ⟨k, hj⟩ s).symm
      · rw [if_neg h1, if_neg h1, if_neg h2, extendStream_update_of_ne _ _ _ h2]
  let E : (Fin q → S) → (Fin q → V) × ρ → Prop :=
    fun W₀ c => (A c.2).evalLazy (subHybridStream G j (W₀, c.1)) [] = true
  let e : S × ((Fin q → S) × ((Fin q → V) × ρ)) ≃ S × (((Fin q → S) × (Fin q → V)) × ρ) :=
    (Equiv.refl S).prodCongr (Equiv.prodAssoc _ _ _).symm
  have h1 : acceptProb G (tableDist G A q j) =
      uprob (fun z : S × ((Fin q → S) × ((Fin q → V) × ρ)) =>
        E (update z.2.1 ⟨j, hj⟩ z.1) z.2.2) := by
    rw [acceptProb_def, ← uprob_comp_equiv e
      (fun z : S × (((Fin q → S) × (Fin q → V)) × ρ) => tableDist G A q j (G z.1) z.2 = true)]
    exact uprob_congr fun z => iff_of_eq
      (congrArg (fun a => (A z.2.2.2).evalLazy a [] = true) (hs z.1 (z.2.1, z.2.2.1)))
  have h2 : subHybridProb G A q j = uprob (fun z : (Fin q → S) × ((Fin q → V) × ρ) => E z.1 z.2) := by
    rw [subHybridProb, acceptProb_def, ← uprob_comp_equiv (Equiv.prodAssoc _ _ _).symm
      (fun z : ((Fin q → S) × (Fin q → V)) × ρ => lazyDist A (subHybridStream G j z.1) z.2 = true)]
    rfl
  rw [h1, h2]
  exact uprob_update_absorb _ E

omit [Fintype P] in
/-- On a uniform challenge `z` the distinguisher `tableDist G A q j` accepts exactly
with the probability of the sub-hybrid `H_{j+1}`, for `j < q`.

**Proof sketch.** With `z` uniform, the challenge stream is the stream of `H_{j+1}` with
the uniform value table `W₁` overwritten at position `j` by `z`, which is again
uniform. -/
theorem acceptProb_tableDist_uniform (G : S → V) (A : OracleAdversary ρ P V) {q j : ℕ}
    (hj : j < q) :
    acceptProb (id : V → V) (tableDist G A q j) = subHybridProb G A q (j + 1) := by
  have hs : ∀ (z : V) (W : (Fin q → S) × (Fin q → V)),
      challengeStream G j z W = subHybridStream G (j + 1) (W.1, update W.2 ⟨j, hj⟩ z) := by
    intro z W; funext k
    unfold challengeStream subHybridStream
    by_cases h1 : k < j
    · rw [if_pos h1, if_pos (by omega), extendStream_update_of_ne _ _ _ (by simp; omega)]
    · by_cases h2 : k = j
      · subst h2; simp only [lt_irrefl, Nat.lt_succ_self, if_false, if_true]
        exact (extendStream_update_self W.2 ⟨k, hj⟩ z).symm
      · rw [if_neg h1, if_neg h2, if_neg (by omega)]
  let E : (Fin q → V) → (Fin q → S) × ρ → Prop :=
    fun W₁ c => (A c.2).evalLazy (subHybridStream G (j + 1) (c.1, W₁)) [] = true
  let e : V × ((Fin q → V) × ((Fin q → S) × ρ)) ≃ V × (((Fin q → S) × (Fin q → V)) × ρ) :=
    (Equiv.refl V).prodCongr
      { toFun := fun c => ((c.2.1, c.1), c.2.2)
        invFun := fun c => (c.1.2, (c.1.1, c.2))
        left_inv := fun _ => rfl
        right_inv := fun _ => rfl }
  let e' : (Fin q → V) × ((Fin q → S) × ρ) ≃ ((Fin q → S) × (Fin q → V)) × ρ :=
    { toFun := fun c => ((c.2.1, c.1), c.2.2)
      invFun := fun c => (c.1.2, (c.1.1, c.2))
      left_inv := fun _ => rfl
      right_inv := fun _ => rfl }
  have h1 : acceptProb (id : V → V) (tableDist G A q j) =
      uprob (fun z : V × ((Fin q → V) × ((Fin q → S) × ρ)) =>
        E (update z.2.1 ⟨j, hj⟩ z.1) z.2.2) := by
    rw [acceptProb_def, ← uprob_comp_equiv e
      (fun z : V × (((Fin q → S) × (Fin q → V)) × ρ) => tableDist G A q j (id z.1) z.2 = true)]
    exact uprob_congr fun z => iff_of_eq
      (congrArg (fun a => (A z.2.2.2).evalLazy a [] = true) (hs z.1 (z.2.2.1, z.2.1)))
  have h2 : subHybridProb G A q (j + 1) =
      uprob (fun z : (Fin q → V) × ((Fin q → S) × ρ) => E z.1 z.2) := by
    rw [subHybridProb, acceptProb_def, ← uprob_comp_equiv e'
      (fun z : ((Fin q → S) × (Fin q → V)) × ρ =>
        lazyDist A (subHybridStream G (j + 1) z.1) z.2 = true)]
    rfl
  rw [h1, h2]
  exact uprob_update_absorb _ E

/-- The sub-hybrid `H_0` is the pseudorandom table: for an adversary making at most `q`
queries, answering every distinct query by `G` of a fresh seed is the same as querying
`G ∘ R` for a uniform `R : P → S`. [Gar26, proof of Theorem 3.3, "`H_{i,0}` is the same
as `H_i`"].

**Proof sketch.** Condition on the adversary's coins; post-compose the tree's answers
with `G` and apply lazy sampling for seeds. -/
theorem subHybridProb_zero (G : S → V) (A : OracleAdversary ρ P V) {q : ℕ}
    (hA : A.BoundedBy q) :
    subHybridProb G A q 0 = acceptProb (fun R : P → S => G ∘ R) (oracleDist A) := by
  have h1 : subHybridProb G A q 0 = uprob (fun z : ρ × ((Fin q → S) × (Fin q → V)) =>
      ((A z.1).simulate id (fun _ => G)).evalLazy (extendStream z.2.1) [] = true) := by
    rw [subHybridProb, acceptProb_def]
    refine (uprob_prod_comm (fun W r => lazyDist A (subHybridStream G 0 W) r = true)).trans
      (uprob_congr fun z => iff_of_eq ?_)
    have hs : subHybridStream G 0 z.2 = G ∘ extendStream z.2.1 := by
      funext k; simp [subHybridStream]
    rw [lazyDist, hs, evalLazy_comp]
  have h2 : acceptProb (fun R : P → S => G ∘ R) (oracleDist A) =
      uprob (fun z : ρ × (P → S) => ((A z.1).simulate id (fun _ => G)).eval z.2 = true) := by
    rw [acceptProb_def]
    refine (uprob_prod_comm (fun R r => oracleDist A (G ∘ R) r = true)).trans
      (uprob_congr fun z => iff_of_eq ?_)
    rw [oracleDist_apply, eval_simulate]; rfl
  rw [h1, h2]
  refine uprob_sections_congr
    (fun r (W : (Fin q → S) × (Fin q → V)) =>
      ((A r).simulate id (fun _ => G)).evalLazy (extendStream W.1) [] = true)
    (fun r (R : P → S) => ((A r).simulate id (fun _ => G)).eval R = true) fun r => ?_
  exact (uprob_fst (fun W : Fin q → S =>
    ((A r).simulate id (fun _ => G)).evalLazy (extendStream W) [] = true)).trans
    (uprob_evalLazy (· = true) (((OracleAdversary.boundedBy_iff A q).1 hA r).simulate _ _))

/-- The sub-hybrid `H_q` is the random table: for an adversary making at most `q`
queries, all its distinct queries are answered by fresh uniform values, which is the same
as querying a uniform random function `P → V`. [Gar26, proof of Theorem 3.3, "`H_{i,q}`
is the same as `H_{i+1}`"].

**Proof sketch.** The adversary never reaches a `q`-th distinct query, so the stream of
`H_q` may be replaced by the uniform values alone; then condition on the coins and apply
lazy sampling. -/
theorem subHybridProb_top (G : S → V) (A : OracleAdversary ρ P V) {q : ℕ}
    (hA : A.BoundedBy q) :
    subHybridProb G A q q = acceptProb (randomFunction P V) (oracleDist A) := by
  have h1 : subHybridProb G A q q = uprob (fun z : ρ × ((Fin q → S) × (Fin q → V)) =>
      (A z.1).evalLazy (extendStream z.2.2) [] = true) := by
    rw [subHybridProb, acceptProb_def]
    refine (uprob_prod_comm (fun W r => lazyDist A (subHybridStream G q W) r = true)).trans
      (uprob_congr fun z => iff_of_eq ?_)
    rw [lazyDist]
    congr 1
    exact evalLazy_congr ((OracleAdversary.boundedBy_iff A q).1 hA z.1) [] fun k hk =>
      if_pos (by simpa using hk)
  have h2 : acceptProb (randomFunction P V) (oracleDist A) =
      uprob (fun z : ρ × (P → V) => (A z.1).eval z.2 = true) := by
    rw [acceptProb_def]
    simp only [oracleDist_apply, randomFunction_apply]
    exact uprob_prod_comm (fun T r => (A r).eval T = true)
  rw [h1, h2]
  refine uprob_sections_congr
    (fun r (W : (Fin q → S) × (Fin q → V)) => (A r).evalLazy (extendStream W.2) [] = true)
    (fun r (T : P → V) => (A r).eval T = true) fun r => ?_
  exact (uprob_snd (fun W : Fin q → V => (A r).evalLazy (extendStream W) [] = true)).trans
    (uprob_evalLazy (· = true) ((OracleAdversary.boundedBy_iff A q).1 hA r))

/-- **Sub-hybrid argument.** For an adversary making at most `q` queries to a table, the
gap between the pseudorandom table `G ∘ R` and a uniform table is at most the sum over
`j < q` of the PRG distinguishing advantages of `tableDist G A q j`, with `G` of a
uniform seed against a uniform element of `V`. [Gar26, proof of Theorem 3.3, sub-hybrids
`H_{i,0}, …, H_{i,q}` at one level], an exact inequality.

**Proof sketch.** The endpoints are `H_0` and `H_q`; telescope, and identify each
neighbouring gap `|H_j - H_{j+1}|` with the advantage of `tableDist G A q j`. -/
theorem table_hybrid (G : S → V) (A : OracleAdversary ρ P V) {q : ℕ} (hA : A.BoundedBy q) :
    |acceptProb (fun R : P → S => G ∘ R) (oracleDist A) -
        acceptProb (randomFunction P V) (oracleDist A)| ≤
      ∑ j : Fin q, distAdv G (id : V → V) (tableDist G A q j) := by
  rw [← subHybridProb_zero G A hA, ← subHybridProb_top G A hA]
  have key := abs_sub_le_sum_hybrids (fun j => subHybridProb G A q j) q
  have hsum : ∑ i ∈ Finset.range q, |subHybridProb G A q i - subHybridProb G A q (i + 1)| =
      ∑ j : Fin q, distAdv G (id : V → V) (tableDist G A q j) := by
    rw [Finset.sum_range (fun j => |subHybridProb G A q j - subHybridProb G A q (j + 1)|)]
    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun j _ => ?_
    have h1 := acceptProb_tableDist_prg G A j.isLt
    have h2 := acceptProb_tableDist_uniform G A j.isLt
    rw [distAdv_def, h1, h2]
  exact key.trans hsum.le

end TCSlib.Cryptography

## ===== TCSlib/Cryptography/Pseudorandom/GeneratorFromPermutation.lean =====

Authors: TCSlib contributors

import TCSlib.Cryptography.Pseudorandom.Generators

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# A pseudorandom generator from a one-way permutation

The concrete layer of [Gar26, §3.3.2]. For a permutation `f` and a bit `B(x, r)`, the
generator `G(x, r) = f(x) ‖ r ‖ B(x, r)` stretches its seed by one bit. If `B` is a
hard-concentrate bit for `g(x, r) = f(x) ‖ r`, then `G` is a pseudorandom generator
[Gar26, Theorem 3.2]. The concrete form: from any distinguisher `D` for `G` with
advantage `ε` we build an explicit predictor of `B(x, r)` from `f(x) ‖ r` that succeeds
with probability exactly `1/2 + ε`.

The bit `B` is arbitrary here: the theorem is the reduction, and hardness of `B` is an
assumption of the asymptotic statement. The inner-product bit of Goldreich–Levin
([Gar26, Theorem 2.3], Remark 3.1) is one instance. The domain of `f` and the type of `r`
are arbitrary finite types; `owpGenBits` and `exists_owpPredictorBits` specialize to bit
strings `{0,1}^n` and the output `{0,1}^{2n+1}`.

## Main definitions

* `owpGen f B`: the generator `G(x, r) = f(x) ‖ r ‖ B(x, r)` [Gar26, Construction 3.2].
* `owpPair f`: the function `g(x, r) = f(x) ‖ r` for which `B` is hard-concentrate.
* `owpGenNot f B`: the distribution `H_1' = f(x) ‖ r ‖ (1 - B(x, r))` of the proof.
* `owpPredictor D flip`: the predictor built from a distinguisher `D`.
* `owpGenBits`, `owpPredictorBits`: the bit-string versions.

## Main results

* `acceptProb_id_owp`: the uniform distribution is the even mixture of `H_0` and `H_1'`.
* `predProb_owpPredictor_false`, `predProb_owpPredictor_true`: the exact success
  probabilities of the predictor and of its flip.
* `exists_owpPredictor`: [Gar26, Theorem 3.2], a predictor with success `1/2 + ε`.
* `exists_owpPredictorBits`: the same on bit strings.

## References

* [Gar26] S. Garg, *A Course in Theory of Cryptography*, lecture notes, UC Berkeley,
  draft of 22 January 2026, §3.3.2 (Construction 3.2, Remark 3.1, Theorem 3.2) and
  Definition 2.3 (hard-concentrate bits).
-/

namespace TCSlib.Cryptography

open Finset

variable {α β ρ : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β] [Fintype ρ]

/-- The probability of an event on `Bool × γ` is the average of the probabilities of its
two sections. -/
theorem uprob_bool_prod {γ : Type*} [Fintype γ] (p : Bool × γ → Prop) :
    uprob p = (uprob (fun c => p (false, c)) + uprob (fun c => p (true, c))) / 2 := by
  rw [uprob_prod, uexp, Fintype.sum_bool, Fintype.card_bool]
  push_cast
  ring

/-- The generator of [Gar26, Construction 3.2]: `G(x, r) = f(x) ‖ r ‖ B(x, r)`, for a
permutation `f` of `α` and a bit `B` of `(x, r)`. -/
def owpGen (f : α ≃ α) (B : α × β → Bool) : α × β → α × β × Bool :=
  fun w => (f w.1, w.2, B w)

/-- The function `g(x, r) = f(x) ‖ r` of [Gar26, Construction 3.2], for which `B` is
assumed to be a hard-concentrate bit. -/
def owpPair (f : α ≃ α) : α × β → α × β :=
  fun w => (f w.1, w.2)

/-- The distribution `H_1' = f(x) ‖ r ‖ (1 - B(x, r))` of [Gar26, proof of Theorem 3.2]:
the generator with its last bit flipped. -/
def owpGenNot (f : α ≃ α) (B : α × β → Bool) : α × β → α × β × Bool :=
  fun w => (f w.1, w.2, !B w)

/-- The predictor of [Gar26, proof of Theorem 3.2] built from a distinguisher `D`: on
input `y = f(x) ‖ r`, draw a uniform bit `σ` and coins for `D`; output `σ` if
`D(y ‖ σ) = 1` and `1 - σ` otherwise. With `flip = true` the output is negated. It calls
`D` once and draws one extra uniform bit.

Deviation: [Gar26] assumes without loss of generality that
`Pr[D(H_0) = 1] - Pr[D(H_1') = 1]` is positive. The sign is not known to a uniform
reduction; here it is the parameter `flip` (non-uniform advice in the asymptotic layer),
and `predProb_owpPredictor_true` covers the negative sign. -/
def owpPredictor (D : α × β × Bool → ρ → Bool) (flip : Bool) : α × β → Bool × ρ → Bool :=
  fun y c => xor (if D (y.1, y.2, c.1) c.2 then c.1 else !c.1) flip

/-- The defining equation of `owpPredictor`:
`owpPredictor D flip y c = (if D(y, c₁; c₂) then c₁ else ¬c₁) ⊕ flip`. -/
theorem owpPredictor_apply (D : α × β × Bool → ρ → Bool) (flip : Bool) (y : α × β)
    (c : Bool × ρ) :
    owpPredictor D flip y c = xor (if D (y.1, y.2, c.1) c.2 then c.1 else !c.1) flip := rfl

/-- The uniform distribution on `α × β × Bool` is the even mixture of the generator's
output `H_0` and its flipped version `H_1'`: `Pr[D(U) = 1]` is the average of
`Pr[D(H_0) = 1]` and `Pr[D(H_1') = 1]`. [Gar26, proof of Theorem 3.2], the identities
`H_1 ≡ H_2` (because `f` is a permutation) and
`Pr[A(H_1) = 1] = ½ Pr[A(H_0) = 1] + ½ Pr[A(H_1') = 1]`.

**Proof sketch.** The map `(τ, x, r) ↦ (f(x), r, τ ⊕ B(x, r))` is a bijection, so the
uniform string is the image of uniform `(τ, x, r)`; split on the bit `τ`. -/
theorem acceptProb_id_owp [Nonempty ρ] (f : α ≃ α) (B : α × β → Bool)
    (D : α × β × Bool → ρ → Bool) :
    acceptProb (id : α × β × Bool → _) D =
      (acceptProb (owpGen f B) D + acceptProb (owpGenNot f B) D) / 2 := by
  let e : Bool × ((α × β) × ρ) ≃ (α × β × Bool) × ρ :=
    { toFun := fun v => ((f v.2.1.1, v.2.1.2, xor v.1 (B v.2.1)), v.2.2)
      invFun := fun z =>
        (xor z.1.2.2 (B (f.symm z.1.1, z.1.2.1)), ((f.symm z.1.1, z.1.2.1), z.2))
      left_inv := fun v => by simp
      right_inv := fun z => by simp }
  unfold acceptProb
  refine (uprob_eq_of_equiv e
    (p := fun v : Bool × ((α × β) × ρ) => D (f v.2.1.1, v.2.1.2, xor v.1 (B v.2.1)) v.2.2 = true)
    (q := fun z : (α × β × Bool) × ρ => D (id z.1) z.2 = true) fun _ => Iff.rfl).symm.trans ?_
  rw [uprob_bool_prod]
  simp only [Bool.false_xor, Bool.true_xor]
  rfl

/-- The predictor `owpPredictor D false` predicts `B(x, r)` from `f(x) ‖ r` with
probability exactly `1/2 + (Pr[D(H_0) = 1] - Pr[D(H_1') = 1]) / 2`. [Gar26, proof of
Theorem 3.2].

**Proof sketch.** Split on whether the random bit `σ` equals `B(x, r)`, each with
probability `1/2`: if it does, the predictor is right when `D(H_0)` accepts; if not, it
is right when `D(H_1')` rejects. -/
theorem predProb_owpPredictor_false [Nonempty ρ] [Nonempty α] [Nonempty β] (f : α ≃ α)
    (B : α × β → Bool) (D : α × β × Bool → ρ → Bool) :
    predProb (owpPair f) B (owpPredictor D false) =
      1 / 2 + (acceptProb (owpGen f B) D - acceptProb (owpGenNot f B) D) / 2 := by
  let e : Bool × ((α × β) × ρ) ≃ (α × β) × (Bool × ρ) :=
    { toFun := fun v => (v.2.1, (xor v.1 (B v.2.1), v.2.2))
      invFun := fun z => (xor z.2.1 (B z.1), (z.1, z.2.2))
      left_inv := fun v => by simp
      right_inv := fun z => by simp }
  unfold predProb
  refine (uprob_eq_of_equiv e
    (p := fun v => owpPredictor D false (owpPair f (e v).1) (e v).2 = B (e v).1)
    (q := fun z : (α × β) × (Bool × ρ) => owpPredictor D false (owpPair f z.1) z.2 = B z.1)
    fun _ => Iff.rfl).symm.trans ?_
  rw [uprob_bool_prod, show ∀ a b : ℝ, 1 / 2 + (a - b) / 2 = (a + (1 - b)) / 2 by
    intro a b; ring]
  congr 2
  · -- the random bit equals `B(x, r)`: the predictor is right when `D(H_0)` accepts
    unfold acceptProb
    congr 1
    funext c
    apply propext
    simp only [e, owpPredictor, owpPair, owpGen, Equiv.coe_fn_mk, Bool.false_xor,
      Bool.xor_false]
    cases D (f c.1.1, c.1.2, B c.1) c.2 <;> cases B c.1 <;> simp
  · -- the random bit is `1 - B(x, r)`: the predictor is right when `D(H_1')` rejects
    unfold acceptProb
    rw [← uprob_not]
    congr 1
    funext c
    apply propext
    simp only [e, owpPredictor, owpPair, owpGenNot, Equiv.coe_fn_mk, Bool.true_xor,
      Bool.xor_false]
    cases D (f c.1.1, c.1.2, !B c.1) c.2 <;> cases B c.1 <;> simp

/-- The flipped predictor `owpPredictor D true` predicts `B(x, r)` with probability
exactly `1/2 - (Pr[D(H_0) = 1] - Pr[D(H_1') = 1]) / 2`, the case of [Gar26, proof of
Theorem 3.2] that the source discards by symmetry.

**Proof sketch.** Its output is the negation of that of `owpPredictor D false`, so its
success probability is one minus that of `predProb_owpPredictor_false`. -/
theorem predProb_owpPredictor_true [Nonempty ρ] [Nonempty α] [Nonempty β] (f : α ≃ α)
    (B : α × β → Bool) (D : α × β × Bool → ρ → Bool) :
    predProb (owpPair f) B (owpPredictor D true) =
      1 / 2 - (acceptProb (owpGen f B) D - acceptProb (owpGenNot f B) D) / 2 := by
  have h : predProb (owpPair f) B (owpPredictor D true) =
      1 - predProb (owpPair f) B (owpPredictor D false) := by
    unfold predProb
    rw [← uprob_not]
    congr 1
    funext z
    apply propext
    simp only [owpPredictor, Bool.xor_true, Bool.xor_false]
    cases (if D ((owpPair f z.1).1, (owpPair f z.1).2, z.2.1) z.2.2 then z.2.1 else !z.2.1) <;>
      cases B z.1 <;> simp
  rw [h, predProb_owpPredictor_false]
  ring

/-- PRG from a one-way permutation, concrete form [Gar26, Theorem 3.2]: if `D`
distinguishes `G(x, r) = f(x) ‖ r ‖ B(x, r)` from uniform with advantage `ε`, then for one
choice of `flip` the predictor `owpPredictor D flip` predicts `B(x, r)` from
`f(x) ‖ r` with probability exactly `1/2 + ε`. So if `B` is a hard-concentrate bit for
`g(x, r) = f(x) ‖ r`, then `G` is a pseudorandom generator. Only bijectivity of `f` is
used, not its one-wayness (which is what makes hard-concentrate bits for `g` possible).

**Proof sketch.** By `acceptProb_id_owp`, `Pr[D(G) = 1] - Pr[D(U) = 1]` is half of
`Pr[D(H_0) = 1] - Pr[D(H_1') = 1]`. Take `flip = false` if this is nonnegative and
`flip = true` otherwise, and apply `predProb_owpPredictor_false` or
`predProb_owpPredictor_true`. -/
theorem exists_owpPredictor [Nonempty ρ] [Nonempty α] [Nonempty β] (f : α ≃ α)
    (B : α × β → Bool) (D : α × β × Bool → ρ → Bool) :
    ∃ flip : Bool, predProb (owpPair f) B (owpPredictor D flip) =
      1 / 2 + prgAdv (owpGen f B) D := by
  have hU := acceptProb_id_owp f B D
  unfold prgAdv distAdv
  rcases le_total 0 (acceptProb (owpGen f B) D - acceptProb (owpGenNot f B) D) with h | h
  · refine ⟨false, ?_⟩
    rw [predProb_owpPredictor_false, hU, abs_of_nonneg (by linarith)]
    ring
  · refine ⟨true, ?_⟩
    rw [predProb_owpPredictor_true, hU, abs_of_nonpos (by linarith)]
    ring

/-! ### Bit strings -/

/-- The encoding of `f(x) ‖ r ‖ b` as a string of length `2n + 1`, written `n + n + 1`. -/
def owpBitsEquiv (n : ℕ) : (Fin n → Bool) × (Fin n → Bool) × Bool ≃ (Fin (n + n + 1) → Bool) :=
  (Equiv.prodAssoc _ _ _).symm.trans
    (((Fin.appendEquiv n n).prodCongr (Equiv.refl Bool)).trans (Fin.succFunEquiv Bool _).symm)

/-- The generator of [Gar26, Construction 3.2] on bit strings:
`G : {0,1}^{2n} → {0,1}^{2n+1}`, `G(x, r) = f(x) ‖ r ‖ B(x, r)`, for a permutation `f` of
`{0,1}^n`, with the seed given as the pair `(x, r)`. -/
def owpGenBits {n : ℕ} (f : (Fin n → Bool) ≃ (Fin n → Bool))
    (B : (Fin n → Bool) × (Fin n → Bool) → Bool) :
    (Fin n → Bool) × (Fin n → Bool) → Fin (n + n + 1) → Bool :=
  fun w => owpBitsEquiv n (owpGen f B w)

/-- The predictor of [Gar26, proof of Theorem 3.2] for a distinguisher of `owpGenBits`:
`owpPredictor` run against `D` composed with the encoding of strings. Its cost is that of
`owpPredictor`. -/
def owpPredictorBits {n : ℕ} (D : (Fin (n + n + 1) → Bool) → ρ → Bool) (flip : Bool) :
    (Fin n → Bool) × (Fin n → Bool) → Bool × ρ → Bool :=
  owpPredictor (fun z r => D (owpBitsEquiv n z) r) flip

/-- PRG from a one-way permutation on bit strings [Gar26, Theorem 3.2]: a distinguisher
for `G(x, r) = f(x) ‖ r ‖ B(x, r) ∈ {0,1}^{2n+1}` with advantage `ε` yields, for one
choice of `flip`, a predictor of `B(x, r)` from `f(x) ‖ r` with success probability
exactly `1/2 + ε`. -/
theorem exists_owpPredictorBits [Nonempty ρ] {n : ℕ} (f : (Fin n → Bool) ≃ (Fin n → Bool))
    (B : (Fin n → Bool) × (Fin n → Bool) → Bool) (D : (Fin (n + n + 1) → Bool) → ρ → Bool) :
    ∃ flip : Bool, predProb (owpPair f) B (owpPredictorBits D flip) =
      1 / 2 + prgAdv (owpGenBits f B) D := by
  have h : prgAdv (owpGenBits f B) D = prgAdv (owpGen f B) (fun z r => D (owpBitsEquiv n z) r) :=
    prgAdv_comp_equiv (owpBitsEquiv n) (owpGen f B) D
  rw [h]
  exact exists_owpPredictor f B _

end TCSlib.Cryptography

/-

import TCSlib.Cryptography.Pseudorandom.Indistinguishability
import Mathlib.Data.Fin.Tuple.Basic
import Mathlib.Logic.Equiv.Fin.Basic
import Mathlib.Logic.Function.Iterate

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Pseudorandom generators and stretch extension

The concrete layer of [Gar26, §3.3 and §3.3.1]. A pseudorandom generator is a map `G`
from seeds to longer strings whose output on a uniform seed is computationally
indistinguishable from uniform; at one fixed value of the security parameter this is
measured by the advantage `prgAdv G D` of a distinguisher `D`.

The main result is the stretch extension of [Gar26, Theorem 3.1]: a generator `G` with
one bit of stretch, iterated `l` times, yields a generator `prgExt G l` with `l` bits of
stretch, and any distinguisher for `prgExt G l` with advantage `ε` turns into an explicit
distinguisher for `G` with advantage at least `ε / l`, via the source's hybrids.

The general statements use structured types: a one-bit-stretch generator is a map
`G : S → Bool × S` (the output bit and the next seed) on an arbitrary finite seed type `S`,
and the extension outputs `(Fin l → Bool) × S`. The bit-string statements are
`prgExtBits` and `exists_prgExtBitsRed_ge`, obtained by composing with the canonical
encodings `Fin (n + 1) → Bool ≃ Bool × (Fin n → Bool)` and
`(Fin l → Bool) × (Fin n → Bool) ≃ (Fin (l + n) → Bool)`.

## Main definitions

* `prgAdv G D`: the distinguishing advantage between `G` on a uniform seed and a uniform
  string [Gar26, Definition 3.5].
* `prgExt G l`: the iterated generator of [Gar26, Construction 3.1].
* `prgHybrid G l k`: the hybrid `H_k` of [Gar26, proof of Theorem 3.1].
* `prgExtRed G l k D`: the reduction at hybrid index `k`.
* `prgExtAvgRed G l D`: the reduction with a uniformly random hybrid index.
* `prgExtBits`, `prgExtBitsRed`: the bit-string versions.

## Main results

* `prgExt_succ`: the closed form of `prgExt` satisfies the recursion of the construction.
* `exists_prgExtRed_ge`: [Gar26, Theorem 3.1], some `k` has advantage `≥ ε / l`.
* `prgAdv_prgExtAvgRed`: the averaged reduction has advantage exactly `ε / l`.
* `exists_prgExtBitsRed_ge`: [Gar26, Theorem 3.1] on bit strings.

## References

* [Gar26] S. Garg, *A Course in Theory of Cryptography*, lecture notes, UC Berkeley,
  draft of 22 January 2026, §3.3 (Definition 3.5) and §3.3.1 (Construction 3.1,
  Theorem 3.1).
-/

namespace TCSlib.Cryptography

open Finset

variable {S σ ρ γ δ : Type*} [Fintype S] [Fintype σ] [Fintype ρ]

/-! ### Pseudorandom generators -/

/-- The PRG advantage of a distinguisher `D` against `G : σ → γ`: the distinguishing
advantage `|Pr[D(G(s)) = 1] - Pr[D(u) = 1]|` between the output of `G` on a uniform seed
`s` and a uniform element `u` of the output type. [Gar26, Definition 3.5], the condition
`U_{n+m} ≈ G(U_n)` at one value of the security parameter; `G` is a pseudorandom generator
when this advantage is negligible for every efficient `D`, which is stated in the
asymptotic layer. -/
noncomputable def prgAdv [Fintype γ] (G : σ → γ) (D : γ → ρ → Bool) : ℝ :=
  distAdv G (id : γ → γ) D

/-- The defining equation of `prgAdv`: `prgAdv G D = distAdv G id D`. -/
theorem prgAdv_eq [Fintype γ] (G : σ → γ) (D : γ → ρ → Bool) :
    prgAdv G D = distAdv G (id : γ → γ) D := rfl

/-- Re-encoding the output of a generator by a bijection `e` does not change PRG
advantages: the advantage of `D` against `e ∘ G` is that of `D ∘ e` against `G`. -/
theorem prgAdv_comp_equiv [Fintype γ] [Fintype δ] (e : γ ≃ δ) (G : σ → γ)
    (D : δ → ρ → Bool) :
    prgAdv (fun s => e (G s)) D = prgAdv G (fun z r => D (e z) r) := by
  unfold prgAdv distAdv
  rw [← acceptProb_comp_equiv e (id : δ → δ) D]
  rfl

/-! ### Stretch extension -/

/-- The seed update of a one-bit-stretch generator `G : S → Bool × S`: the next seed
`S_i` in `(σ_i, S_i) := G(S_{i-1})`. -/
def prgStep (G : S → Bool × S) : S → S :=
  fun s => (G s).2

/-- The stretch extension of a one-bit-stretch generator [Gar26, Construction 3.1]: from
the seed `S_0`, set `(σ_i, S_i) := G(S_{i-1})` for `i = 1, …, l` and output
`σ_1 σ_2 ⋯ σ_l S_l`. In closed form, with `S_i` the `i`-th iterate of the seed update,
the output bit at (0-indexed) position `i` is the bit of `G(S_i)` and the final seed is
`S_l`; `prgExt_succ` is the recursion of the construction. -/
def prgExt (G : S → Bool × S) (l : ℕ) : S → (Fin l → Bool) × S :=
  fun s => (fun i => (G ((prgStep G)^[i] s)).1, (prgStep G)^[l] s)

omit [Fintype S] in
/-- The stretch extension unrolls one step: `prgExt G (l + 1)` outputs the bit of `G s`
followed by `prgExt G l` on the next seed. [Gar26, Construction 3.1]. -/
theorem prgExt_succ (G : S → Bool × S) (l : ℕ) (s : S) :
    prgExt G (l + 1) s =
      (Fin.cons (G s).1 (prgExt G l (G s).2).1, (prgExt G l (G s).2).2) := by
  refine Prod.ext ?_ ?_
  · funext i
    cases i using Fin.cases with
    | zero => simp [prgExt]
    | succ i => simp [prgExt, Function.iterate_succ_apply, prgStep]
  · simp [prgExt, Function.iterate_succ_apply, prgStep]

/-- The hybrid `H_k` of [Gar26, proof of Theorem 3.1]: the first `k` output bits are
uniform (the first component of the seed), and the remaining `l - k` bits and the final
seed are produced by iterating `G` from a uniform seed `S_k` (the second component).
Seeds are `(Fin l → Bool) × S` for every `k`, the bits beyond the first `k` being ignored,
so that all hybrids share one seed space. -/
def prgHybrid (G : S → Bool × S) (l k : ℕ) : (Fin l → Bool) × S → (Fin l → Bool) × S :=
  fun v => (fun i => if (i : ℕ) < k then v.1 i else (G ((prgStep G)^[i - k] v.2)).1,
    (prgStep G)^[l - k] v.2)

/-- The stretch-extension reduction at hybrid index `k` [Gar26, proof of Theorem 3.1]: on
input `T = (σ, S) ∈ Bool × S`, it draws `k` uniform bits `σ_1, …, σ_k`, takes
`(σ_{k+1}, S_{k+1}) := T`, iterates `G` for the remaining `l - k - 1` steps and calls `D`
once on `σ_1 ⋯ σ_l S_l`. It makes `l - k - 1` calls to `G` and one call to `D`, and draws
`l` uniform bits of which it uses `k`. -/
def prgExtRed (G : S → Bool × S) (l k : ℕ) (D : (Fin l → Bool) × S → ρ → Bool) :
    Bool × S → (Fin l → Bool) × ρ → Bool :=
  fun T c => D (fun i => if (i : ℕ) < k then c.1 i else if (i : ℕ) = k then T.1
    else (G ((prgStep G)^[i - k - 1] T.2)).1, (prgStep G)^[l - k - 1] T.2) c.2

/-- The zeroth hybrid is the stretch extension on a uniform seed: `H_0 ≡ F`. -/
theorem acceptProb_prgHybrid_zero (G : S → Bool × S) (l : ℕ)
    (D : (Fin l → Bool) × S → ρ → Bool) :
    acceptProb (prgHybrid G l 0) D = acceptProb (prgExt G l) D := by
  have h : prgHybrid G l 0 = fun v => prgExt G l v.2 := by
    funext v
    simp [prgHybrid, prgExt]
  rw [h, acceptProb_snd]

/-- The `l`-th hybrid is uniform: `H_l ≡ U_{n+l}`. -/
theorem acceptProb_prgHybrid_self (G : S → Bool × S) (l : ℕ)
    (D : (Fin l → Bool) × S → ρ → Bool) :
    acceptProb (prgHybrid G l l) D = acceptProb (id : (Fin l → Bool) × S → _) D := by
  have h : prgHybrid G l l = id := by
    funext v
    simp [prgHybrid]
  rw [h]

/-- On an output of `G`, the hybrid-`k` reduction simulates the hybrid `H_k`.

**Proof sketch.** With `T = G(S_k)`, the bit at position `k` is the bit of `G(S_k)` and
later bits and the final seed come from iterating `G` from the seed of `G(S_k)`, which
is one more iteration from `S_k`. -/
theorem acceptProb_prgExtRed_left (G : S → Bool × S) {l k : ℕ} (hk : k < l)
    (D : (Fin l → Bool) × S → ρ → Bool) :
    acceptProb G (prgExtRed G l k D) = acceptProb (prgHybrid G l k) D := by
  refine (acceptProb_bind G (fun (T : Bool × S) (u : Fin l → Bool) =>
    ((fun i : Fin l => if (i : ℕ) < k then u i else if (i : ℕ) = k then T.1
      else (G ((prgStep G)^[i - k - 1] T.2)).1), (prgStep G)^[l - k - 1] T.2)) D).trans ?_
  refine Eq.trans ?_ (acceptProb_comp_equiv (Equiv.prodComm _ _) (prgHybrid G l k) D)
  congr 1
  funext w
  have hstep : ∀ m, (prgStep G)^[m] (G w.1).2 = (prgStep G)^[m + 1] w.1 := fun m => by
    rw [Function.iterate_succ_apply]; rfl
  refine Prod.ext ?_ ?_
  · funext i
    simp only [prgHybrid, Equiv.prodComm_apply, Prod.fst_swap, Prod.snd_swap]
    rcases lt_trichotomy (i : ℕ) k with h | h | h
    · simp [h]
    · simp [h]
    · simp only [not_lt.mpr h.le, h.ne', if_false, hstep]
      congr 3
      omega
  · simp only [prgHybrid, Equiv.prodComm_apply, Prod.fst_swap, Prod.snd_swap, hstep]
    congr 1
    omega

/-- On a uniform input, the hybrid-`k` reduction simulates the hybrid `H_{k+1}`.

**Proof sketch.** The uniform input bit plays the role of the uniform bit at position
`k`; overwriting the unused uniform bit at position `k` with it keeps the bits uniform,
and the uniform input seed is `S_{k+1}`. -/
theorem acceptProb_prgExtRed_right (G : S → Bool × S) {l k : ℕ} (hk : k < l)
    (D : (Fin l → Bool) × S → ρ → Bool) :
    acceptProb (id : Bool × S → _) (prgExtRed G l k D) =
      acceptProb (prgHybrid G l (k + 1)) D := by
  let e : (Bool × S) × (Fin l → Bool) ≃ Bool × ((Fin l → Bool) × S) :=
    { toFun := fun w => (w.1.1, (w.2, w.1.2)), invFun := fun v => ((v.1, v.2.2), v.2.1),
      left_inv := fun _ => rfl, right_inv := fun _ => rfl }
  refine (acceptProb_bind (id : Bool × S → _) (fun (T : Bool × S) (u : Fin l → Bool) =>
    ((fun i : Fin l => if (i : ℕ) < k then u i else if (i : ℕ) = k then T.1
      else (G ((prgStep G)^[i - k - 1] T.2)).1), (prgStep G)^[l - k - 1] T.2)) D).trans ?_
  refine Eq.trans ?_ ((acceptProb_comp_equiv e _ D).trans
    (acceptProb_update (ρ := ρ) (⟨k, hk⟩ : Fin l)
      (fun u (s : S) => prgHybrid G l (k + 1) (u, s)) D))
  congr 1
  funext w
  refine Prod.ext ?_ ?_
  · funext i
    simp only [e, prgHybrid, Function.update_apply, Fin.ext_iff, Equiv.coe_fn_mk, id]
    rcases lt_trichotomy (i : ℕ) k with h | h | h
    · simp [h, Nat.lt_succ_of_lt h, h.ne]
    · simp [h]
    · simp only [not_lt.mpr h.le, h.ne', if_false, not_lt.mpr (Nat.succ_le_of_lt h)]
      congr 3
  · simp only [e, prgHybrid, Equiv.coe_fn_mk, id]
    congr 1

/-- Stretch extension, concrete form [Gar26, Theorem 3.1]: if `D` distinguishes the
`l`-fold extension `prgExt G l` (with `l ≥ 1`) from uniform with advantage `ε`, then for
some hybrid index `k < l` the reduction `prgExtRed G l k D` distinguishes `G` from uniform
with advantage at least `ε / l`.

Deviation: [Gar26] writes the reduction's advantage as the signed difference
`Pr[B(G(U_n)) = 1] - Pr[B(U_{n+1}) = 1]` and then equates it with `|ε_k - ε_{k+1}|`;
the formal statement uses absolute values throughout.

**Proof sketch.** The reduction at `k` accepts outputs of `G` and uniform strings with
the acceptance probabilities of `H_k` and `H_{k+1}`; `H_0` is the extension and `H_l` is
uniform, and some neighbouring pair of hybrids is `ε / l` apart. -/
theorem exists_prgExtRed_ge (G : S → Bool × S) {l : ℕ} (hl : 0 < l)
    (D : (Fin l → Bool) × S → ρ → Bool) :
    ∃ k < l, prgAdv (prgExt G l) D / l ≤ prgAdv G (prgExtRed G l k D) := by
  obtain ⟨k, hk, hgap⟩ := exists_hybrid_gap (fun i => acceptProb (prgHybrid G l i) D) hl
  refine ⟨k, hk, ?_⟩
  unfold prgAdv distAdv
  rw [acceptProb_prgExtRed_left G hk, acceptProb_prgExtRed_right G hk,
    ← acceptProb_prgHybrid_zero G, ← acceptProb_prgHybrid_self G]
  exact hgap

/-- The uniform stretch-extension reduction: draw the hybrid index `k < l` uniformly at
random and run `prgExtRed G l k D`. It calls `D` once and `G` at most `l - 1` times. -/
def prgExtAvgRed (G : S → Bool × S) (l : ℕ) (D : (Fin l → Bool) × S → ρ → Bool) :
    Bool × S → Fin l × ((Fin l → Bool) × ρ) → Bool :=
  mixDist fun k : Fin l => prgExtRed G l k D

/-- Stretch extension with a uniform reduction: the reduction with a random hybrid index
has advantage against `G` exactly `ε / l`, where `ε` is the advantage of `D` against
`prgExt G l`. [Gar26, Theorem 3.1].

**Proof sketch.** Average the identities of `acceptProb_prgExtRed_left` and
`acceptProb_prgExtRed_right` over `k`; the differences telescope. -/
theorem prgAdv_prgExtAvgRed (G : S → Bool × S) (l : ℕ)
    (D : (Fin l → Bool) × S → ρ → Bool) :
    prgAdv G (prgExtAvgRed G l D) = prgAdv (prgExt G l) D / l := by
  rw [prgAdv, prgExtAvgRed, distAdv_mixDist_eq G _ _ (fun i => acceptProb (prgHybrid G l i) D)
    (fun k => acceptProb_prgExtRed_left G k.isLt D)
    (fun k => acceptProb_prgExtRed_right G k.isLt D), prgAdv, distAdv,
    acceptProb_prgHybrid_zero, acceptProb_prgHybrid_self]

/-! ### Bit strings -/

/-- The stretch extension on bit strings [Gar26, Construction 3.1]: for
`G : {0,1}^n → {0,1}^{n+1}`, read `G(s)` as its first bit and the remaining `n` bits,
iterate `l` times and output the `l` bits followed by the final seed, a string of length
`l + n`. -/
def prgExtBits {n : ℕ} (G : (Fin n → Bool) → Fin (n + 1) → Bool) (l : ℕ) :
    (Fin n → Bool) → Fin (l + n) → Bool :=
  fun s => Fin.appendEquiv l n
    (prgExt (fun s => (Fin.consEquiv fun _ => Bool).symm (G s)) l s)

/-- The bit-string stretch-extension reduction at hybrid index `k`: split the input
`T ∈ {0,1}^{n+1}` into its first bit and the rest, and run `prgExtRed` against the
distinguisher that reads the pair `(σ_1 ⋯ σ_l, S_l)` as the string `σ_1 ⋯ σ_l S_l`. Its
cost is that of `prgExtRed`. -/
def prgExtBitsRed {n : ℕ} (G : (Fin n → Bool) → Fin (n + 1) → Bool) (l k : ℕ)
    (D : (Fin (l + n) → Bool) → ρ → Bool) : (Fin (n + 1) → Bool) → (Fin l → Bool) × ρ → Bool :=
  fun T c => prgExtRed (fun s => (Fin.consEquiv fun _ => Bool).symm (G s)) l k
    (fun z r => D (Fin.appendEquiv l n z) r) ((Fin.consEquiv fun _ => Bool).symm T) c

/-- Stretch extension on bit strings [Gar26, Theorem 3.1]: if `D` distinguishes
`prgExtBits G l` (with `l ≥ 1`) from uniform `l + n`-bit strings with advantage `ε`, then
for some `k < l` the reduction `prgExtBitsRed G l k D` distinguishes `G` from uniform
`n + 1`-bit strings with advantage at least `ε / l`. The output length is written
`l + n` (bits before seed) where the source writes `n + l`. -/
theorem exists_prgExtBitsRed_ge {n : ℕ} (G : (Fin n → Bool) → Fin (n + 1) → Bool)
    {l : ℕ} (hl : 0 < l) (D : (Fin (l + n) → Bool) → ρ → Bool) :
    ∃ k < l, prgAdv (prgExtBits G l) D / l ≤ prgAdv G (prgExtBitsRed G l k D) := by
  obtain ⟨k, hk, h⟩ := exists_prgExtRed_ge (fun s => (Fin.consEquiv fun _ => Bool).symm (G s))
    hl (fun z r => D (Fin.appendEquiv l n z) r)
  refine ⟨k, hk, ?_⟩
  unfold prgExtBits
  rw [prgAdv_comp_equiv]
  rw [prgAdv_comp_equiv] at h
  exact h

end TCSlib.Cryptography

## ===== TCSlib/Cryptography/Pseudorandom/Indistinguishability.lean =====

/-
Copyright (c) 2026 TCSlib contributors. All rights reserved.
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: TCSlib contributors
-/
import TCSlib.Cryptography.Foundations.Experiments

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Computational indistinguishability: the sunglass and multicopy lemmas

The concrete layer of [Gar26, §3.2]. Distributions are samplers `X : σ → γ` from uniform
seeds, distinguishers are functions `D : γ → ρ → Bool` of a sample and uniform coins, and
`distAdv X Y D` is the advantage `|Pr[D(X) = 1] - Pr[D(Y) = 1]|`. Each lemma of the source
is stated as an explicit reduction: from a distinguisher `D` for the derived pair we build a
distinguisher for `X` and `Y` and prove an exact relation between the advantages. The
asymptotic statements ("if `X ≈ Y` then ...") follow once the reductions are shown to be
efficient, which is the job of the asymptotic layer.

Besides the two lemmas, the file provides the reseeding toolkit used by all reductions in
the pseudorandomness development: invariance of acceptance probabilities under bijections
of the seed space, under unused seed coordinates, and under moving a reduction's private
coins into the sampler; plus the *index-mixing* distinguisher that picks a hybrid index
uniformly at random, which turns the hybrid argument into a uniform reduction.

## Main definitions

* `pushSampler P X`: the sampler of `P(X)` for a randomized post-processing map `P`.
* `sunglassRed P D`: the distinguisher `D ∘ P` for `X` and `Y`.
* `mixDist D`: run `D k` for a uniformly random index `k`.
* `copies t X`: `t` independent copies of `X`.
* `multicopyHybrid X Y t k`: the hybrid `(Y, …, Y, X, …, X)` with `k` copies of `Y`.
* `multicopyRed X Y t k D`: the hybrid-`k` distinguisher for one copy.
* `multicopyAvgRed X Y t D`: the same with a uniformly random `k`.

## Main results

* `uprob_eq_of_equiv`, `acceptProb_fst`, `acceptProb_snd`,
  `acceptProb_bind`, `acceptProb_update`: reseeding.
* `distAdv_mixDist_eq`: the averaged hybrid argument.
* `distAdv_sunglassRed`: [Gar26, Lemma 3.2], with equal advantage.
* `exists_multicopyRed_ge`: [Gar26, Lemma 3.3], some `k` has advantage `≥ ε / t`.
* `distAdv_multicopyAvgRed`: the averaged reduction has advantage exactly `ε / t`.

## References

* [Gar26] S. Garg, *A Course in Theory of Cryptography*, lecture notes, UC Berkeley,
  draft of 22 January 2026, §3.2 (Definition 3.4, Lemmas 3.2 and 3.3).
-/

namespace TCSlib.Cryptography

open Finset

variable {σ τ κ ρ ι γ δ : Type*} [Fintype σ] [Fintype τ] [Fintype κ] [Fintype ρ]

/-! ### Reseeding -/

/-- Two events that correspond under a bijection of the sample spaces have the same
probability: if `p a` holds exactly when `q (e a)` does, then `Pr[p] = Pr[q]`. -/
theorem uprob_eq_of_equiv {α β : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β] (e : α ≃ β)
    {p : α → Prop} {q : β → Prop} (h : ∀ a, p a ↔ q (e a)) : uprob p = uprob q := by
  rw [← uprob_comp_equiv e q]
  congr 1
  funext a
  exact propext (h a)

/-- A seed coordinate that the sampler ignores does not change acceptance probabilities:
sampling `X` from the first coordinate of a uniform pair is sampling `X`. -/
theorem acceptProb_fst [Nonempty τ] (X : σ → γ) (D : γ → ρ → Bool) :
    acceptProb (fun z : σ × τ => X z.1) D = acceptProb X D := by
  let e : (σ × τ) × ρ ≃ (σ × ρ) × τ :=
    { toFun := fun w => ((w.1.1, w.2), w.1.2), invFun := fun z => ((z.1.1, z.2), z.1.2),
      left_inv := fun _ => rfl, right_inv := fun _ => rfl }
  unfold acceptProb
  exact (uprob_eq_of_equiv e (q := fun w : (σ × ρ) × τ => D (X w.1.1) w.1.2 = true)
    fun _ => Iff.rfl).trans (uprob_fst (fun y : σ × ρ => D (X y.1) y.2 = true))

/-- As `acceptProb_fst`, for an ignored first seed coordinate. -/
theorem acceptProb_snd [Nonempty τ] (X : σ → γ) (D : γ → ρ → Bool) :
    acceptProb (fun z : τ × σ => X z.2) D = acceptProb X D :=
  (acceptProb_comp_equiv (Equiv.prodComm τ σ) (fun z : σ × τ => X z.1) D).trans
    (acceptProb_fst X D)

/-- Moving coins into the sampler: a distinguisher that first draws private coins `c` and
feeds `P z c` to `D` accepts a sample of `X` with the probability that `D` accepts a sample
of the composite sampler `(s, c) ↦ P (X s) c`. -/
theorem acceptProb_bind (X : σ → γ) (P : γ → κ → δ) (D : δ → ρ → Bool) :
    acceptProb X (fun z (c : κ × ρ) => D (P z c.1) c.2) =
      acceptProb (fun s : σ × κ => P (X s.1) s.2) D :=
  uprob_eq_of_equiv (Equiv.prodAssoc σ κ ρ).symm fun _ => Iff.rfl

/-- Overwriting one coordinate of a uniform tuple with an independent uniform value leaves
the tuple uniform: a sampler fed `update u k x` for uniform `x` and `u` accepts with the
same probability as one fed `u`.

**Proof sketch.** The map `(x, u) ↦ (update u k x, u k)` is a bijection, and the sampler
ignores the second component of its image. -/
theorem acceptProb_update [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype ι] [Nonempty σ] (k : ι)
    (Z : (ι → σ) → τ → γ) (D : γ → ρ → Bool) :
    acceptProb (fun w : σ × ((ι → σ) × τ) => Z (Function.update w.2.1 k w.1) w.2.2) D =
      acceptProb (fun v : (ι → σ) × τ => Z v.1 v.2) D := by
  let e : σ × ((ι → σ) × τ) ≃ ((ι → σ) × τ) × σ :=
    { toFun := fun w => ((Function.update w.2.1 k w.1, w.2.2), w.2.1 k)
      invFun := fun v => (v.1.1 k, (Function.update v.1.1 k v.2, v.1.2))
      left_inv := fun w => by ext <;> simp
      right_inv := fun v => by ext <;> simp }
  rw [← acceptProb_fst (τ := σ) (fun v : (ι → σ) × τ => Z v.1 v.2) D]
  exact acceptProb_comp_equiv e (fun w : ((ι → σ) × τ) × σ => Z w.1.1 w.1.2) D

/-! ### The sunglass lemma -/

/-- The sampler of the post-processed distribution `P(X)`: draw a seed `s` of `X` and coins
`c` of `P`, output `P (X s) c`. -/
def pushSampler (P : γ → κ → δ) (X : σ → γ) : σ × κ → δ :=
  fun s => P (X s.1) s.2

/-- The sunglass reduction [Gar26, proof of Lemma 3.2]: from a distinguisher `D` of
`P(X)` and `P(Y)`, the distinguisher `D ∘ P` of `X` and `Y`. On input `z` it draws coins
for `P`, runs `P` once on `z`, and calls `D` once on the result with `D`'s own coins. -/
def sunglassRed (P : γ → κ → δ) (D : δ → ρ → Bool) : γ → κ × ρ → Bool :=
  fun z c => D (P z c.1) c.2

/-- The sunglass lemma, concrete form [Gar26, Lemma 3.2]: the distinguisher `D ∘ P` has
exactly the advantage between `X` and `Y` that `D` has between `P(X)` and `P(Y)`. The
post-processing `P` may be randomized, with coins from `κ`. -/
theorem distAdv_sunglassRed (P : γ → κ → δ) (X : σ → γ) (Y : τ → γ)
    (D : δ → ρ → Bool) :
    distAdv X Y (sunglassRed P D) = distAdv (pushSampler P X) (pushSampler P Y) D := by
  unfold distAdv sunglassRed pushSampler
  rw [acceptProb_bind, acceptProb_bind]

/-- The sunglass lemma for a deterministic post-processing map `P`: the distinguisher
`D ∘ P` has the advantage between `X` and `Y` that `D` has between `P ∘ X` and `P ∘ Y`.
[Gar26, Lemma 3.2]. -/
theorem distAdv_comp (P : γ → δ) (X : σ → γ) (Y : τ → γ) (D : δ → ρ → Bool) :
    distAdv X Y (fun z r => D (P z) r) = distAdv (fun s => P (X s)) (fun s => P (Y s)) D :=
  rfl

/-! ### Mixing over an index -/

/-- The distinguisher that draws an index `k` uniformly at random and runs `D k`. In a
hybrid argument this is the uniform reduction: it does not need to know the good hybrid
index. -/
def mixDist (D : ι → γ → ρ → Bool) : γ → ι × ρ → Bool :=
  fun z c => D c.1 z c.2

/-- The acceptance probability of the mixed distinguisher is the average over `k` of the
acceptance probabilities of the `D k`. -/
theorem acceptProb_mixDist [Fintype ι] (X : σ → γ) (D : ι → γ → ρ → Bool) :
    acceptProb X (mixDist D) = uexp fun k => acceptProb X (D k) := by
  let e : σ × (ι × ρ) ≃ ι × (σ × ρ) :=
    { toFun := fun w => (w.2.1, (w.1, w.2.2)), invFun := fun v => (v.2.1, (v.1, v.2.2)),
      left_inv := fun _ => rfl, right_inv := fun _ => rfl }
  unfold acceptProb mixDist
  exact (uprob_eq_of_equiv e (q := fun w : ι × (σ × ρ) => D w.1 (X w.2.1) w.2.2 = true)
    fun _ => Iff.rfl).trans (uprob_prod _)

/-- The averaged hybrid argument: if `D k` accepts `X` with probability `P k` and `Y` with
probability `P (k + 1)` for each `k < t`, then the mixed distinguisher has advantage exactly
`|P 0 - P t| / t`. [Gar26, proof of Lemma 3.3], uniform version.

**Proof sketch.** The difference of the averages is the average of the differences, which
telescopes to `(P 0 - P t) / t`. -/
theorem distAdv_mixDist_eq {t : ℕ} (X : σ → γ) (Y : τ → γ) (D : Fin t → γ → ρ → Bool)
    (P : ℕ → ℝ) (hX : ∀ k : Fin t, acceptProb X (D k) = P k)
    (hY : ∀ k : Fin t, acceptProb Y (D k) = P (k + 1)) :
    distAdv X Y (mixDist D) = |P 0 - P t| / t := by
  unfold distAdv
  rw [acceptProb_mixDist, acceptProb_mixDist]
  simp only [hX, hY, uexp, Fintype.card_fin]
  rw [← sub_div, ← Finset.sum_sub_distrib,
    Fin.sum_univ_eq_sum_range (fun i => P i - P (i + 1)), Finset.sum_range_sub', abs_div,
    Nat.abs_cast]

/-! ### The multicopy lemma -/

/-- The `t`-product of a sampler: `t` independent copies of `X`, sampled from `t`
independent seeds. [Gar26, Lemma 3.3]. -/
def copies (t : ℕ) (X : σ → γ) : (Fin t → σ) → Fin t → γ :=
  fun s i => X (s i)

/-- The `k`-th hybrid of the multicopy lemma: the first `k` coordinates are copies of `Y`,
the remaining `t - k` copies of `X`, all independent. [Gar26, proof of Lemma 3.3], the
hybrid `H_n^{(k,t)} = (Y^{(1)}, …, Y^{(k)}, X^{(k+1)}, …, X^{(t)})`. -/
def multicopyHybrid (X : σ → γ) (Y : τ → γ) (t k : ℕ) :
    (Fin t → σ) × (Fin t → τ) → Fin t → γ :=
  fun s i => if (i : ℕ) < k then Y (s.2 i) else X (s.1 i)

/-- The multicopy reduction at hybrid index `k` [Gar26, proof of Lemma 3.3]: on input `z`,
sample `k` copies of `Y` and `t - k - 1` copies of `X`, place `z` at position `k`
(0-indexed), and call `D` once on the resulting tuple. It uses `t - 1` calls to the
samplers of `X` and `Y` (it draws seeds for all `t` positions and ignores two of them);
this is where efficient samplability of `X` and `Y` is used.

Deviation: [Gar26] writes `B(Z) = A(X_1, …, X_{k-1}, Z, Y_{k+1}, …, Y_t)`, with copies of
`X` before `Z` and copies of `Y` after; that does not match its own hybrids, which put the
copies of `Y` first. Here the order matches the hybrids. -/
def multicopyRed (X : σ → γ) (Y : τ → γ) (t k : ℕ) (D : (Fin t → γ) → ρ → Bool) :
    γ → ((Fin t → σ) × (Fin t → τ)) × ρ → Bool :=
  fun z c => D (fun i => if (i : ℕ) < k then Y (c.1.2 i) else if (i : ℕ) = k then z
    else X (c.1.1 i)) c.2

/-- The zeroth hybrid is the `t`-product of `X`. -/
theorem acceptProb_multicopyHybrid_zero [Nonempty τ] (X : σ → γ) (Y : τ → γ) (t : ℕ)
    (D : (Fin t → γ) → ρ → Bool) :
    acceptProb (multicopyHybrid X Y t 0) D = acceptProb (copies t X) D := by
  have h : multicopyHybrid X Y t 0 = fun s => copies t X s.1 := by
    funext s i
    simp [multicopyHybrid, copies]
  rw [h, acceptProb_fst]

/-- The `t`-th hybrid is the `t`-product of `Y`. -/
theorem acceptProb_multicopyHybrid_self [Nonempty σ] (X : σ → γ) (Y : τ → γ) (t : ℕ)
    (D : (Fin t → γ) → ρ → Bool) :
    acceptProb (multicopyHybrid X Y t t) D = acceptProb (copies t Y) D := by
  have h : multicopyHybrid X Y t t = fun s => copies t Y s.2 := by
    funext s i
    simp [multicopyHybrid, copies]
  rw [h, acceptProb_snd]

/-- On a sample of `X`, the hybrid-`k` reduction simulates the `k`-th hybrid for `D`.

**Proof sketch.** Its input is placed at position `k`, which in the `k`-th hybrid holds a
copy of `X`; overwriting the ignored seed at position `k` with the input's seed leaves the
seed tuple uniform. -/
theorem acceptProb_multicopyRed_left [Nonempty σ] (X : σ → γ) (Y : τ → γ) {t k : ℕ}
    (hk : k < t) (D : (Fin t → γ) → ρ → Bool) :
    acceptProb X (multicopyRed X Y t k D) = acceptProb (multicopyHybrid X Y t k) D := by
  refine (acceptProb_bind X (fun z (s : (Fin t → σ) × (Fin t → τ)) (i : Fin t) =>
    if (i : ℕ) < k then Y (s.2 i) else if (i : ℕ) = k then z else X (s.1 i)) D).trans ?_
  refine Eq.trans ?_ (acceptProb_update (ρ := ρ) (⟨k, hk⟩ : Fin t)
    (fun u (s' : Fin t → τ) => multicopyHybrid X Y t k (u, s')) D)
  congr 1
  funext w i
  simp only [multicopyHybrid, Function.update_apply, Fin.ext_iff]
  rcases lt_trichotomy (i : ℕ) k with h | h | h
  · simp [h]
  · simp [h]
  · simp [h.ne', not_lt.mpr h.le]

/-- On a sample of `Y`, the hybrid-`k` reduction simulates the `(k + 1)`-th hybrid for `D`.

**Proof sketch.** As in `acceptProb_multicopyRed_left`: position `k` holds a copy of `Y` in
the `(k + 1)`-th hybrid. -/
theorem acceptProb_multicopyRed_right [Nonempty τ] (X : σ → γ) (Y : τ → γ) {t k : ℕ}
    (hk : k < t) (D : (Fin t → γ) → ρ → Bool) :
    acceptProb Y (multicopyRed X Y t k D) = acceptProb (multicopyHybrid X Y t (k + 1)) D := by
  let e : τ × ((Fin t → σ) × (Fin t → τ)) ≃ τ × ((Fin t → τ) × (Fin t → σ)) :=
    (Equiv.refl τ).prodCongr (Equiv.prodComm _ _)
  refine (acceptProb_bind Y (fun z (s : (Fin t → σ) × (Fin t → τ)) (i : Fin t) =>
    if (i : ℕ) < k then Y (s.2 i) else if (i : ℕ) = k then z else X (s.1 i)) D).trans ?_
  refine Eq.trans ?_ ((acceptProb_comp_equiv e _ D).trans
    ((acceptProb_update (ρ := ρ) (⟨k, hk⟩ : Fin t)
      (fun u (s : Fin t → σ) => multicopyHybrid X Y t (k + 1) (s, u)) D).trans
    (acceptProb_comp_equiv (Equiv.prodComm _ _) (multicopyHybrid X Y t (k + 1)) D)))
  congr 1
  funext w i
  simp only [e, multicopyHybrid, Function.update_apply, Fin.ext_iff, Equiv.prodCongr_apply,
    Equiv.coe_refl, Equiv.prodComm_apply, Prod.map, Prod.fst_swap, Prod.snd_swap, id]
  rcases lt_trichotomy (i : ℕ) k with h | h | h
  · simp [h, Nat.lt_succ_of_lt h, h.ne]
  · simp [h]
  · simp [h.ne', not_lt.mpr h.le, not_lt.mpr (Nat.succ_le_of_lt h)]

/-- The multicopy lemma, concrete form [Gar26, Lemma 3.3]: if `D` distinguishes `t ≥ 1`
independent copies of `X` from `t` independent copies of `Y` with advantage `ε`, then for
some hybrid index `k < t` the reduction `multicopyRed X Y t k D` distinguishes one copy with
advantage at least `ε / t`. The index `k` is the non-uniform choice of the source
(footnote 2); `distAdv_multicopyAvgRed` removes it.

**Proof sketch.** The reduction at `k` accepts `X` and `Y` with the acceptance
probabilities of hybrids `k` and `k + 1`; the end hybrids are the two `t`-products, and
some neighbouring pair of hybrids is `ε / t` apart. -/
theorem exists_multicopyRed_ge [Nonempty σ] [Nonempty τ] (X : σ → γ) (Y : τ → γ) {t : ℕ}
    (ht : 0 < t) (D : (Fin t → γ) → ρ → Bool) :
    ∃ k < t, distAdv (copies t X) (copies t Y) D / t ≤ distAdv X Y (multicopyRed X Y t k D) := by
  obtain ⟨k, hk, hgap⟩ :=
    exists_hybrid_gap (fun i => acceptProb (multicopyHybrid X Y t i) D) ht
  refine ⟨k, hk, ?_⟩
  unfold distAdv
  rw [acceptProb_multicopyRed_left X Y hk, acceptProb_multicopyRed_right X Y hk,
    ← acceptProb_multicopyHybrid_zero X Y, ← acceptProb_multicopyHybrid_self X Y]
  exact hgap

/-- The uniform multicopy reduction: draw the hybrid index `k < t` uniformly at random and
run `multicopyRed X Y t k D`. It calls `D` once and the samplers `t - 1` times. -/
def multicopyAvgRed (X : σ → γ) (Y : τ → γ) (t : ℕ) (D : (Fin t → γ) → ρ → Bool) :
    γ → Fin t × (((Fin t → σ) × (Fin t → τ)) × ρ) → Bool :=
  mixDist fun k : Fin t => multicopyRed X Y t k D

/-- The multicopy lemma with a uniform reduction: the reduction with a random hybrid index
has advantage exactly `ε / t`, where `ε` is the advantage of `D` on the `t`-products.
[Gar26, Lemma 3.3].

**Proof sketch.** Average the identities of `acceptProb_multicopyRed_left` and
`acceptProb_multicopyRed_right` over `k`; the differences telescope. -/
theorem distAdv_multicopyAvgRed [Nonempty σ] [Nonempty τ] (X : σ → γ) (Y : τ → γ) (t : ℕ)
    (D : (Fin t → γ) → ρ → Bool) :
    distAdv X Y (multicopyAvgRed X Y t D) = distAdv (copies t X) (copies t Y) D / t := by
  rw [multicopyAvgRed, distAdv_mixDist_eq X Y _ (fun i => acceptProb (multicopyHybrid X Y t i) D)
    (fun k => acceptProb_multicopyRed_left X Y k.isLt D)
    (fun k => acceptProb_multicopyRed_right X Y k.isLt D), distAdv,
    acceptProb_multicopyHybrid_zero, acceptProb_multicopyHybrid_self]

end TCSlib.Cryptography

/-!
# Randomness, learning and derandomization

The definitions, constructions and theorem statements of [PS10, Chapter 8].
The individual modules record deviations, proof sketches and outstanding admissions.

## Main definitions

See the definitions and construction modules listed below.

## Main results

See the theorem statements and correctness results in the constituent modules.

## Contents

* `Extraction` — unbiased extraction from a biased source.
* `Learning` — the Occam bound in the PAC layer.
* `BPPBridge` — the public bridge from BPP computations to distinguishers.
* `Derandomization` — learning and derandomization statements.

/-
Copyright (c) 2026 TCSlib contributors. All rights reserved.
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
